It reminds people that God is fully aware of all actions, and that divine justice will ultimately prevail, both in this life and in the hereafter.
orig: ثم أنتم هؤلاء تقتلون أنفسكم وتخرجون فريقا منكم من ديارهم تظاهرون عليهم بالإثم والعدوان وإن يأتوكم أسارى تفادوهم وهو محرم عليكم إخراجهم أفتؤمنون ببعض الكتاب وتكفرون ببعض فما جزاء من يفعل ذلك منكم إلا خزي في الحياة الدنيا ويوم القيامة يردون إلى أشد العذاب وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Those are the ones who have purchased the worldly life at the cost of the Hereafter; so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be aided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of prioritizing materialistic and transient aspects of the worldly life over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. It serves as a stern warning that those who make such choices trade away something of infinite value (the afterlife) for something fleeting and insignificant in comparison (worldly gains). Consequently, their actions result in severe and unrelenting punishment, as they have willingly forsaken the ultimate salvation for temporary pleasures. This verse underscores the importance of aligning one's actions with eternal truths rather than short-lived worldly gains.
orig: أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And indeed, We gave Moses the Scripture and followed up after him with messengers. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit. So whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant. Thus, some (messengers) you denied, and others you killed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and seriousness of God's message to humanity, delivered through a succession of prophets. It highlights human resistance to divine guidance, particularly when it contradicts personal desires or societal norms. The mention of specific prophets like Moses and Jesus underscores the significance of their roles in guiding people and the divine support they received, illustrated here as Jesus being aided by the Holy Spirit. This verse is a critique of the arrogance and rejection faced by prophets when they present truth and commandments that are unpalatable to their people. It points out the tragic responses of denial and violence directed towards these messengers, reflecting on the moral failures and the consequences of turning away from divine guidance.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب وقفينا من بعده بالرسل وآتينا عيسى ابن مريم البينات وأيدناه بروح القدس أفكلما جاءكم رسول بما لا تهوى أنفسكم استكبرتم ففريقا كذبتم وفريقا تقتلون

translation: And they say, 'Our hearts are wrapped (in coverings).' But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is what they believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hardened state of the hearts of some individuals who, out of arrogance or ignorance, claim that their hearts are inaccessible to faith. The phrase 'Our hearts are wrapped' metaphorically signifies their deliberate shutting off from divine guidance. The subsequent divine curse mentioned is a consequence of their persistent disbelief and rejection of faith, emphasizing that such obstinacy leads to spiritual deprivation and a profound detachment from truth. Hence, their capacity to believe and embrace faith is minimal, illustrating a spiritual malaise rooted in self-imposed isolation from divine guidance.
orig: وقالوا قلوبنا غلف بل لعنهم الله بكفرهم فقليلا ما يؤمنون

translation: And when there came to them a Book from Allah confirming what was with them - although beforehand they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved - but then when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony and tragedy of rejection by those who were initially optimistic and expectant of divine guidance. It reflects on the human tendency to reject truth when it finally manifests, especially if it challenges existing beliefs or comes in an unexpected form. The verse underscores the severe consequences of such denial, particularly when it contradicts prior acknowledgment or anticipation of the truth. It serves as a warning about the dangers of hypocrisy, stubbornness, and the self-destructive path of rejecting divine guidance after recognizing it.
orig: ولما جاءهم كتاب من عند الله مصدق لما معهم وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به فلعنة الله على الكافرين

translation: How wretched is that for which they sold themselves, that they should disbelieve in what Allah has revealed out of envy that Allah should send down His favor upon whom He wills from among His servants. So they incurred wrath upon wrath, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences of rejecting divine guidance out of jealousy or envy towards others who are favored by God. It emphasizes that such rejection is akin to selling one's soul for a miserable return. The phrase 'wrath upon wrath' underscores the accumulation of divine displeasure that results from persistent disbelief and the grave consequences that follow. The final part of the verse serves as a stern warning about the ignominious punishment awaiting those who persist in disbelief and reject the divine blessings bestowed upon others.
orig: بئسما اشتروا به أنفسهم أن يكفروا بما أنزل الله بغيا أن ينزل الله من فضله على من يشاء من عباده فباءوا بغضب على غضب وللكافرين عذاب مهين

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Believe in what Allah has revealed,' they say, 'We believe only in what was revealed to us.' And they reject anything beyond that, even though it is the truth confirming what is with them. Say, 'Why then have you killed the prophets of Allah before, if you are believers?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the stubbornness and selective belief shown by certain groups, who choose to only accept divine revelations that were specifically revealed to their own community, disregarding subsequent truths revealed to other prophets. The challenge to their actions in killing prophets, despite professing faith, underscores a profound hypocrisy and the inconsistency between their claimed beliefs and actual actions. This asks the reader to reflect on the integrity of their faith, urging a comprehensive acceptance of all divine messages as a cohesive, confirmed truth rather than fragmenting belief to suit personal or communal biases.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم آمنوا بما أنزل الله قالوا نؤمن بما أنزل علينا ويكفرون بما وراءه وهو الحق مصدقا لما معهم قل فلم تقتلون أنبياء الله من قبل إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, Moses came to you with clear proofs, then you took the calf [for worship] after him, while you were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a reproach to the people who were given direct evidence of divine truth through Prophet Moses, yet chose to deviate by worshipping the golden calf, an act of grave injustice and deviation from monotheistic faith. It underscores the human tendency to stray from the path of righteousness despite clear signs and guidance, reflecting on the theme of accountability and the consequences of disregarding the divine commandments.
orig: ولقد جاءكم موسى بالبينات ثم اتخذتم العجل من بعده وأنتم ظالمون

translation: And [recall] when We took your covenant and raised above you the Mount [saying], 'Hold firmly to what We have given you and listen.' They said, 'We hear and we disobey.' And [mention] their hearts absorbed [the worship of] the calf because of their disbelief. Say, 'Evil is it that your faith orders you, if you are indeed believers.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the incident of the Israelites at Mount Sinai, focusing on their failure to uphold the covenant with God despite the clear signs and divine commandments. It highlights the gravity of their disobedience and their inclination towards idolatry despite receiving direct guidance. The mention of 'their hearts absorbed the calf' underscores the deep-rooted nature of their defiance and the extent to which idolatry had tainted their spiritual integrity. This verse serves as a stark rebuke of insincere faith that outwardly professes belief but inwardly harbors rebellion and disbelief. It calls for a reflection on the authenticity and commitment of one's faith, stressing that true belief demands obedience and an unwavering adherence to divine commands.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واسمعوا قالوا سمعنا وعصينا وأشربوا في قلوبهم العجل بكفرهم قل بئسما يأمركم به إيمانكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Say, 'If the abode of the Hereafter with Allah is exclusively for you apart from all other people, then wish for death if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse challenges those who claim exclusive access to divine favor and the rewards of the Hereafter, highlighting the discrepancy between their claims and their actions. By prompting them to wish for death, it underscores the notion that true conviction in their privileged status should lead to a desire to hasten towards these promised rewards. The rhetorical use of challenging their readiness to die is a means to expose the insincerity or uncertainty in their claims. It serves as a critique of hypocrisy and false piety, reminding all believers to align their convictions with genuine faith and readiness to meet God.
orig: قل إن كانت لكم الدار الآخرة عند الله خالصة من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forth, and Allah is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitable consequences of one's actions, particularly highlighting the remorse or reluctance that wrongdoers feel towards the outcomes of their misdeeds. It suggests a deep-seated aversion to facing the repercussions of their actions, a sentiment rooted in the awareness of their wrongdoing. The mention of Allah’s omniscience serves as a reminder of divine justice and underscores that no deed, good or bad, escapes His notice. It is a call to self-awareness and moral accountability in human conduct.
orig: ولن يتمنوه أبدا بما قدمت أيديهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: And you will surely find them the most eager of people for life, even more than those who associate others with Allah. One of them wishes that he could live a thousand years, but it would not remove him from the punishment to live that long. And Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense attachment to worldly life and the fear of death found among certain people, particularly those who have strayed from monotheistic beliefs. It suggests that even if such individuals were granted a long life of a thousand years, it would not spare them from the divine punishment awaiting them in the afterlife. Their desire for extended life reflects a deep-seated fear of facing the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes God's omniscience, indicating that no matter how much one may wish to avoid accountability through extended worldly life, God is fully aware of all human deeds and no one can escape His justice.
orig: ولتجدنهم أحرص الناس على حياة ومن الذين أشركوا يود أحدهم لو يعمر ألف سنة وما هو بمزحزحه من العذاب أن يعمر والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - for indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by permission of Allah, confirming that which was before it and guidance and good tidings for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the angel Gabriel as a messenger of divine revelation, trusted by God to deliver His words accurately to the Prophet Muhammad. The mention of Gabriel specifically counters any accusations or distrust aimed at this angel by skeptics who may not understand his role or deny his importance in the heavenly scheme. Moreover, the verse asserts the continuity and confirmation of previous scriptures, indicating that the revelations brought by Gabriel are part of a divine tradition of guidance and glad tidings, aimed specifically at enriching the faith and knowledge of the believers.
orig: قل من كان عدوا لجبريل فإنه نزله على قلبك بإذن الله مصدقا لما بين يديه وهدى وبشرى للمؤمنين

translation: Whoever is an enemy to Allah, His angels, His messengers, Gabriel, and Michael, then indeed, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of opposing divine guidance and messengers. It clarifies that hostility towards divine entities, such as Allah, angels like Gabriel and Michael, and the prophets, is tantamount to aligning oneself against the essence of faith itself. Such opposition is not merely a personal stance but sets one on a path directly antagonistic to divine will, meriting opposition from Allah in return. This serves as a stern warning against the rejection of spiritual truths and the figures who are entrusted with their conveyance to humanity. It accentuates the interconnectedness of faith in Allah with respect for His messengers and angels, highlighting that disbelief in one aspect implies a rejection of the whole system of divine guidance.
orig: من كان عدوا لله وملائكته ورسله وجبريل وميكال فإن الله عدو للكافرين

translation: And indeed, We have sent down to you clear verses, and none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and evident nature of the revelations sent by God, which are meant to guide and enlighten. The assertion that only the 'defiantly disobedient' reject these signs suggests that disbelief is not due to ambiguity in the messages, but rather a deliberate choice stemming from disobedience and moral defiance. This highlights the intrinsic connection between ethical conduct and spiritual understanding, underlining that stubborn refusal to accept divine guidance is rooted in moral and spiritual defiance rather than intellectual inability or misunderstanding.
orig: ولقد أنزلنا إليك آيات بينات وما يكفر بها إلا الفاسقون

translation: And whenever they make a covenant, a group among them throws it away, but most of them do not believe.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of faithlessness and inconsistency in upholding commitments among some people. It highlights the human propensity to disregard solemn promises and implies a deeper spiritual ailment: a lack of true faith. The Quran often connects the adherence to covenants with righteousness and faith, suggesting that violation of agreements reflects not just a legal failure but a moral failing. The phrase 'most of them do not believe' underlines that true faith requires more than superficial acknowledgment; it demands steadfast adherence to one's word and obligations.
orig: أوكلما عاهدوا عهدا نبذه فريق منهم بل أكثرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah, confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of Allah behind their backs as if they did not know.
interpretation: This verse criticizes a segment of the religious community that received earlier scriptures, presumably the Jews and Christians, for their response to the arrival of a new Messenger, Muhammad, who confirmed the teachings they already possessed. Despite the affirmation of their own teachings, they disregarded and rejected the message of the Qur'an. The metaphor of throwing the Book behind their backs symbolizes their deliberate ignorance and rejection of the divine guidance they had previously valued and professed to uphold.
orig: ولما جاءهم رسول من عند الله مصدق لما معهم نبذ فريق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب كتاب الله وراء ظهورهم كأنهم لا يعلمون

translation: And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and what was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. Yet, these two did not teach anyone without saying, 'We are a trial, so do not disbelieve.' From them, people learned what might cause separation between a person and his spouse. But they could harm no one except with Allah's permission. And they learned what harmed them and did not benefit them. And indeed, they knew that whoever purchased it would have no share in the Hereafter. And how terrible was what they sold themselves for, if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse underscores the dangers and immorality associated with engaging in practices that have deviant origins, particularly highlighting the susceptibility of humans to be influenced by malevolent forces under the guise of gaining power or control. The story of Solomon, who is exonerated here of practicing magic, illustrates a clear distinction between divine wisdom and malevolent magic. The mention of Harut and Marut serves as a warning about the seductive nature of magic, which, while apparently alluring because it can provide immediate effects like causing division between loved ones, ultimately leads to spiritual ruin and a disconnection from divine guidance. The verse cautions against the pursuit of harmful knowledge that leads to eternal loss, underlining the broader Islamic ethics of seeking knowledge that is beneficial, elevating, and rooted in righteousness. Additionally, it reinforces the belief in divine sovereignty; even when humans err, harm cannot transpire without divine permission, which embeds trials within a framework of divine justice and the human capacity for choice.
orig: واتبعوا ما تتلو الشياطين على ملك سليمان وما كفر سليمان ولكن الشياطين كفروا يعلمون الناس السحر وما أنزل على الملكين ببابل هاروت وماروت وما يعلمان من أحد حتى يقولا إنما نحن فتنة فلا تكفر فيتعلمون منهما ما يفرقون به بين المرء وزوجه وما هم بضارين به من أحد إلا بإذن الله ويتعلمون ما يضرهم ولا ينفعهم ولقد علموا لمن اشتراه ما له في الآخرة من خلاق ولبئس ما شروا به أنفسهم لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And if they had believed and feared Allah, there would have been a reward from Allah far better, if only they had known.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and piety in attaining divine rewards. It suggests that belief in Allah and living a life in accordance with His commandments bring about rewards that are far superior to worldly gains. The phrase 'if only they had known' highlights the idea of regret over missed spiritual opportunities due to lack of faith and awareness of the true benefits of a God-conscious life.
orig: ولو أنهم آمنوا واتقوا لمثوبة من عند الله خير لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: O you who have believed, do not say 'Ra'ina' but say 'Unzurna' and listen, and for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of choosing words carefully to avoid misunderstandings or offensive implications, particularly in religious and interfaith contexts. It instructs believers to use clear and considerate language when communicating, especially in prayer or religious discourse. The verse also serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief, underscoring the idea that faith and obedience to divine guidance are crucial for avoiding divine retribution.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقولوا راعنا وقولوا انظرنا واسمعوا وللكافرين عذاب أليم

translation: Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists wish not that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. But Allah selects for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine selection and grace. It reflects the idea that divine blessings and mercy are not distributed based on human desires or prejudices, but are a matter of God's sovereign choice. The disbelievers' unwillingness to wish good for the believers highlights the contrast between human envy or hostility and God’s impartial and generous dispensation of mercy. The reference to God’s “great bounty” underscores the limitless and unbounded nature of His grace, available to whomever He chooses, regardless of human expectations or societal boundaries.
orig: ما يود الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب ولا المشركين أن ينزل عليكم من خير من ربكم والله يختص برحمته من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: We do not abolish a verse or cause it to be forgotten except that We bring forth better than it or similar to it. Do you not know that Allah is over all things competent?
interpretation: This verse addresses the concept of 'Naskh' or abrogation in the Quranic context. It highlights Allah's sovereign authority to amend or replace His previous commandments. The verse reassures that any change or forgetfulness initiated by Allah in the scripture is purposeful and brings something superior or equivalent in benefit and wisdom. It underscores the completeness and perfection of divine wisdom and power, emphasizing that Allah’s decisions are always in the best interest of humanity, tailored to their needs and circumstances over time.
orig: ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها نأت بخير منها أو مثلها ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and that you have no protector or helper besides Allah?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and authority of Allah over all creation, highlighting the futility of seeking protection or assistance from any source other than Allah. It reminds believers of their complete dependence on Allah and encourages them to seek refuge in Him alone, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid, the oneness of Allah.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Or do you wish to ask your messenger as Moses was asked before? And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly strayed from the even way.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, cautioning them against the attitude of excessive questioning and skepticism towards their prophet, similar to the behavior displayed by previous communities, such as the followers of Moses. It emphasizes that questioning the directives and wisdom of the prophet, as the followers of Moses did, is indicative of a lack of faith and trust in divine guidance. The verse warns that substituting belief with disbelief, through such actions, leads one away from the correct and balanced path of righteousness, implying a serious deviation from sincere faith. Thus, it stresses the importance of steadfast faith and trust in the guidance provided by the prophets.
orig: أم تريدون أن تسألوا رسولكم كما سئل موسى من قبل ومن يتبدل الكفر بالإيمان فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back to disbelief after you have believed, out of envy from themselves even after the truth has become clear to them. So pardon and overlook until Allah delivers His command. Indeed, Allah is capable of all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenges posed by external envy and hostility towards believers' faith, particularly from those who recognize the truth but reject it due to their prejudices. It advises believers to respond to such hostility with forgiveness and patience, emphasizing the importance of maintaining moral high ground and leaving judgment to Allah. This instructs not only to preserve personal peace but also to uphold the principles of justice and mercy, reaffirming Allah's omnipotence and ultimate authority over all affairs.
orig: ود كثير من أهل الكتاب لو يردونكم من بعد إيمانكم كفارا حسدا من عند أنفسهم من بعد ما تبين لهم الحق فاعفوا واصفحوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah, and whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of performing acts of worship, specifically prayer and almsgiving, as essential practices for spiritual growth and purification. It underscores a profound spiritual principle: the good deeds we perform in this world, done sincerely for the sake of Allah, are not lost but preserved and rewarded in the Hereafter. Allah's omniscience is highlighted, reminding believers that nothing escapes His watchful eye, thus motivating them to live righteously and act conscientiously at all times.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله إن الله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And they said, 'None shall enter Paradise unless he be a Jew or a Christian.' These are their vain desires. Say, 'Produce your proof if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse challenges exclusivist beliefs regarding salvation held by some religious groups. It criticizes the notion that heaven is reserved for specific communities and insists on a more inclusive view of divine mercy. The demand for proof serves as a call for critical examination of one's religious claims and emphasizes the importance of evidence in matters of faith. It underscores the idea that claims about ultimate truths, like salvation, should be substantiated rather than merely asserted.
orig: وقالوا لن يدخل الجنة إلا من كان هودا أو نصارى تلك أمانيهم قل هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good, for him there is his reward with his Lord, and there shall be no fear upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual and psychological tranquility granted to those who sincerely devote themselves to God and perform good deeds. It underlines the concept of 'Ihsan' or excellence in faith and actions, suggesting that such individuals are in a harmonious state, filled with inner peace, knowing their rewards are preserved with their Lord. The assurance of 'no fear' and 'no grief' signifies a state of ultimate security and contentment in this life and the hereafter, relieving them from the common human fears of the unknown future and the regret of past actions.
orig: بلى من أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن فله أجره عند ربه ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And the Jews said, 'The Christians have no basis,' and the Christians said, 'The Jews have no basis,' while they both recite the Scripture. Likewise, those who do not know said similar things. So, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of sectarian disputes and emphasizes that true judgment regarding religious truths will only be established by Allah on the Day of Judgment. It criticizes the baseless claims made by religious communities against one another and underlines the commonality of their reliance on scripture, suggesting a misguided approach in their contention. Ultimately, this verse calls for humility and the recognition that ultimate knowledge and judgment rest with Allah alone, discouraging division and encouraging unity and tolerance among different faith groups.
orig: وقالت اليهود ليست النصارى على شيء وقالت النصارى ليست اليهود على شيء وهم يتلون الكتاب كذلك قال الذين لا يعلمون مثل قولهم فالله يحكم بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And who is more unjust than those who prevent the name of Allah from being mentioned in His mosques and strive towards their ruin? Those individuals should not enter them except in fear; for them in this world is disgrace, and in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe wrongdoing of those who obstruct religious practices and damage places of worship. It underscores the sanctity of mosques as spaces dedicated to the remembrance and worship of Allah. The punishment mentioned serves both as a worldly consequence (disgrace) and a spiritual consequence (great punishment in the Hereafter), highlighting the gravity of such actions both in temporal and eternal dimensions. The condition of entering mosques 'in fear' suggests that violators are aware of their transgressions, facing both immediate societal repercussions and divine accountability.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها أولئك ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين لهم في الدنيا خزي ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: To Allah belong the east and the west, so wherever you turn, there is the face of Allah. Indeed, Allah is all-encompassing, all-knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah. It teaches that God's presence is not confined to any specific direction or location; rather, He encompasses all directions, reinforcing the concept that God is universally accessible to all believers, regardless of their physical orientation. The phrase 'the face of Allah' symbolizes His essence and presence everywhere. The attributes 'all-encompassing' and 'all-knowing' emphasize His infinite capacity and awareness, affirming that human actions and intentions are always within His purview.
orig: ولله المشرق والمغرب فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله إن الله واسع عليم

translation: And they say, 'Allah has taken a son.' Exalted is He! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and uniqueness of Allah, rejecting any human-like attributions such as paternity which are incompatible with His divine nature. It underscores that everything in the universe is under His dominion and authority, and that all creations are in a state of submission to His will, continuously glorifying Him and adhering to His commands.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الله ولدا سبحانه بل له ما في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون

translation: Originator of the heavens and the earth. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute creative power and authority of God, who effortlessly brings about whatever He wills. By mentioning His command 'Be,' the verse highlights the immediacy and ease with which God's will is executed, reflecting His omnipotence. The reference to God as the 'Originator' of the heavens and the earth further establishes His role as the ultimate source of all existence, underscoring the concept of divine creation without any need for pre-existing materials or external assistance. This serves as a reminder of God's sovereignty over all creation and His capability to enact His will without limitation.
orig: بديع السماوات والأرض وإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And those who do not know say, 'Why does not Allah speak to us or there come to us a sign?' Thus spoke those before them in a similar manner; their hearts are alike. We have certainly made clear the signs for a people who are certain.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism and demands for direct divine interaction or miraculous signs, similar to those made by previous generations. It highlights a pattern of doubt and disbelief that transcends time, suggesting that such attitudes are rooted in the hearts of the individuals rather than in the absence of divine communication. The verse emphasizes that God has indeed provided ample evidence and signs of His existence and will, but only those who have certainty in their faith can truly comprehend and appreciate these signs. The comparison between past and present skeptics serves to underscore the repetitive nature of such demands and the unchanged human disposition towards skepticism, while emphasizing the idea that divine wisdom and signs are perceptible and meaningful primarily to those who earnestly seek and hold firm faith.
orig: وقال الذين لا يعلمون لولا يكلمنا الله أو تأتينا آية كذلك قال الذين من قبلهم مثل قولهم تشابهت قلوبهم قد بينا الآيات لقوم يوقنون

translation: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And do not ask about the companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the profound responsibility and mission of the Prophet Muhammad as both a bearer of good news and a herald of warning, emphasizing the truthfulness of his message. It also serves as a reminder of the stark realities of accountability in the afterlife, delineating a clear boundary between those on the path of righteousness and the 'companions of the Hellfire.' The directive for the Prophet not to inquire about the latter group highlights the inevitability and severity of divine justice, suggesting that once judgment is passed, those who are condemned are no longer the focus for mercy or intercession.
orig: إنا أرسلناك بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا ولا تسأل عن أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And the Jews and the Christians will never be pleased with you until you follow their religions. Say, 'Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [true] guidance.' And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would have against Allah neither protector nor helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea of steadfastness in faith and warns against compromising one's beliefs to seek approval from others, particularly from followers of different faith traditions. It reinforces the concept that divine guidance supersedes all other influences and advises against deviating from this path once one has acquired true knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder of the potential spiritual consequences of replacing divine guidance with human desires or societal pressures.
orig: ولن ترضى عنك اليهود ولا النصارى حتى تتبع ملتهم قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم بعد الذي جاءك من العلم ما لك من الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book recite it with its true recital. They [are the ones who] believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it - those are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of engaging with the divine scriptures in a manner that reflects their true purpose and essence. It distinguishes between those who sincerely embrace and follow the teachings of the scripture, acknowledging their true value, and those who reject or disregard its guidance. The verse points out that genuine belief and adherence to the scripture are the markers of spiritual success, whereas disbelief and neglect are paths to loss and failure in the spiritual realm. This delineation serves as both encouragement to follow the scripture faithfully and a warning about the consequences of turning away from it.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يتلونه حق تلاوته أولئك يؤمنون به ومن يكفر به فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique position and responsibility of the Children of Israel, reminding them of the special favors and status granted by God. The mention of God's favors is an invocation to acknowledge His blessings, express gratitude, and adhere to the obligations that come with being the chosen community. By stating that they were preferred 'over the worlds', it highlights their distinct role and the divine expectations from them to uphold and spread the principles of righteousness and justice. This serves not just as a reminder of their privileged status, but also as a call to moral and spiritual accountability.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأني فضلتكم على العالمين

translation: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, nor will any compensation be accepted from it, nor will any intercession benefit it, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the solemnity and seriousness of the Day of Judgment, a time when individual accountability is paramount. Each person is solely responsible for their actions, and no external influence or assistance can alter their divine judgment. The denial of intercession and help underscores the concept of absolute justice on that day, where each soul reaps the consequences of their worldly deeds without any proxies or mitigation.
orig: واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ولا يقبل منها عدل ولا تنفعها شفاعة ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And [mention] when Abraham was tried by his Lord with commands and he fulfilled them. [Allah] said, 'Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people.' Abraham said, 'And of my descendants?' [Allah] replied, 'My covenant does not include the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of divine testing and reward. Abraham's obedience to God's commands exemplifies the quintessential submission required from believers. His successful completion of these tests leads to God's promise of making him a leader, suggesting that spiritual leadership is contingent upon moral and spiritual integrity. However, the dialogue between Abraham and God highlights a critical caveat—divine promises and leadership are not automatically inherited. They are instead conditional, particularly excluding those who commit injustices. This underscores a key Islamic principle that accountability and righteousness are necessary for attaining and maintaining favor in the eyes of God.
orig: وإذ ابتلى إبراهيم ربه بكلمات فأتمهن قال إني جاعلك للناس إماما قال ومن ذريتي قال لا ينال عهدي الظالمين

translation: And [mention] when We made the House a place of return for the people and a place of security and take, from the standing place of Abraham, a place of prayer; and We charged Abraham and Ishmael, [saying], 'Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who seclude themselves [for prayer] and those who bow and prostrate [in prayer].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the sanctity and the central role of the Kaaba as a spiritual hub for Muslims. It emphasizes the Kaaba as a place of universal gathering, where believers find solace and peace, symbolizing unity and harmony among them. The reference to the standing place of Abraham as a place of prayer underscores the importance of following the traditions and footsteps of the prophets. The command given to Abraham and Ishmael to purify the Kaaba serves as a profound indication of the continuous spiritual cleansing and devotion required in maintaining the sanctity of the holy places. This purification is not merely physical, but extends to ensuring that the acts of worship performed there are sincere and devoted, catering to the spiritual needs of the worshippers who engage in various forms of devotion such as Tawaf, prayer, and prostration.
orig: وإذ جعلنا البيت مثابة للناس وأمنا واتخذوا من مقام إبراهيم مصلى وعهدنا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل أن طهرا بيتي للطائفين والعاكفين والركع السجود

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits—those of them who believe in Allah and the Last Day.' He said, 'And whoever disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little while, then I will compel him to the torment of the Fire, and what a miserable destination.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep concern of Prophet Abraham for the spiritual and physical well-being of the inhabitants of the city (which is Mecca). His prayer illustrates the interconnection between faith and divine sustenance, emphasizing that true security and provision are linked with belief in God and the Day of Judgment. The response from God highlights the temporality of worldly pleasures for those who deny the faith, underscoring the ultimate reality of eternal accountability and the severe consequences of disbelief. It's a profound reminder of the temporary nature of this life compared to the perpetuity of the hereafter, and the pivotal role of faith in determining one's ultimate fate.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب اجعل هذا بلدا آمنا وارزق أهله من الثمرات من آمن منهم بالله واليوم الآخر قال ومن كفر فأمتعه قليلا ثم أضطره إلى عذاب النار وبئس المصير

translation: And [mention] when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House and [with him] Ishmael, [saying], 'Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and humility in acts of worship and devotion. Abraham and Ishmael, while engaged in the physically and spiritually significant act of building the Kaaba, seek acceptance of their efforts from God, acknowledging His omnipotence and omniscience. Their prayer exemplifies a profound spirituality, showing that even in great acts of devotion, the focus should remain on divine acceptance and recognition of human limitations. The verse teaches believers the value of humility and the importance of direct communication with God in seeking His approval for their deeds.
orig: وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت وإسماعيل ربنا تقبل منا إنك أنت السميع العليم

translation: Our Lord, make us Muslims devoted to You, and from our descendants a Muslim nation devoted to You. Show us our rituals and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication that reflects a deep desire for guidance and steadfastness in faith, not just for oneself but also for future generations. It highlights the importance of maintaining a continuous community of believers who adhere faithfully to their religious duties and rituals. Furthermore, the plea for God to show the correct practices ('our rituals') and to accept repentance underscores the human need for divine direction and forgiveness. This verse emphasizes God's qualities as Merciful and Accepting of repentance, reassuring believers of God's compassion and readiness to forgive, which motivates a sincere commitment to worship and moral conduct.
orig: ربنا واجعلنا مسلمين لك ومن ذريتنا أمة مسلمة لك وأرنا مناسكنا وتب علينا إنك أنت التواب الرحيم

translation: Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from themselves, who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them; indeed, You are the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of divine guidance through a Messenger who arises from within the community itself, underscoring the concepts of relatability and familiarity. The roles of the Messenger include recitation of divine revelations, imparting knowledge of the scriptures, teaching wisdom, and purifying the community spiritually. The mention of God's attributes, 'the Almighty, the Wise', highlights that the empowerment and success of this Messenger are by divine decree, reflecting God's ultimate authority and profound wisdom in nurturing and guiding His creation.
orig: ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم يتلو عليهم آياتك ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة ويزكيهم إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: And who would be averse to the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself? We had certainly chosen him in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the folly and imprudence of turning away from the monotheistic and righteous path exemplified by Prophet Abraham. It highlights Abraham’s distinction both in this life and the afterlife as chosen and righteous, implying that diverging from his example is inherently self-destructive and misguided. The verse reaffirms the eternal value and correctness of following Abraham's model of faith, stressing that deviation from this path is equivalent to rejecting wisdom and righteousness.
orig: ومن يرغب عن ملة إبراهيم إلا من سفه نفسه ولقد اصطفيناه في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: When his Lord said to him, 'Submit,' he said, 'I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound obedience and submission of a faithful believer to the will of God. It emphasizes the importance of unwavering faith and total surrender to God's commands. The reference to 'Lord of the worlds' underlines God's sovereignty over the entire universe, reinforcing the belief in His ultimate authority and benevolence. The response of the believer in this context signifies a deep, personal commitment to uphold divine commandments, serving as a model for others in the expression of true devotion and submission to the Creator.
orig: إذ قال له ربه أسلم قال أسلمت لرب العالمين

translation: And Abraham enjoined his sons with this, as did Jacob, saying, 'O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you the religion, so do not die except as Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith and the continuity of monotheistic belief across generations. It highlights how patriarchs like Abraham and Jacob not only practiced their faith but also strongly encouraged their descendants to maintain the same level of commitment to monotheism. The directive to remain Muslims until death signifies the lifelong dedication required in the worship and obedience of Allah. It underscores the notion that the true faith in God, as chosen by Allah, is not merely a part of life but a commitment that spans entire lifetimes, meant to be upheld passionately until one's last breath.
orig: ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه ويعقوب يا بني إن الله اصطفى لكم الدين فلا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون

translation: Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, 'What will you worship after me?' They said, 'We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac, one God, and to Him we are submissive.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a legacy of monotheistic faith across generations. It highlights how Jacob, on his deathbed, sought reassurance about the continuity of worship of the One God, reflecting a concern for spiritual continuity beyond his life. His sons' response reinforces the central Islamic principle of Tawhid, the oneness of God, linking their faith back to their forefathers. This passage underlines the virtue of submission to God's will, and the responsibility of each generation to uphold and transmit the true belief in God’s oneness and sovereignty.
orig: أم كنتم شهداء إذ حضر يعقوب الموت إذ قال لبنيه ما تعبدون من بعدي قالوا نعبد إلهك وإله آبائك إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق إلها واحدا ونحن له مسلمون

translation: That is a community that has passed. Theirs is what they earned, and yours is what you earn, and you will not be questioned about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual responsibility in matters of deeds and consequences. It underscores a fundamental principle in Islamic ethics wherein each person is accountable for their own actions rather than being burdened by the deeds of predecessors. The verse also signifies the transition between different communities or generations, affirming that every community is judged by its own deeds and not by the actions of those who came before them. This offers a clear directive to focus on one's personal moral and spiritual development without being unduly influenced by the historical deeds of others.
orig: تلك أمة قد خلت لها ما كسبت ولكم ما كسبتم ولا تسألون عما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they said, 'Be Jews or Christians, then you will be guided.' Say, 'Rather, [we follow] the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the Qur'anic theme of returning to the pure monotheistic faith exemplified by Abraham, who is honored as a paragon of unwavering devotion to the one God, undiluted by the polytheistic practices ubiquitous in his era. The verse critiques the assertion that salvation can only be attained through conversion to Judaism or Christianity, emphasizing instead a return to the original monotheistic 'millah' (faith community) of Abraham, which transcends sectarian labels. It delineates Islam's identity as deeply rooted in primordial monotheism, highlighting its universalistic ethos and its critique of religious exclusivism.
orig: وقالوا كونوا هودا أو نصارى تهتدوا قل بل ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Say, 'We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and what Moses and Jesus and the prophets were given from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and respecting the continuity and unity of divine revelation across different prophets in the history of monotheistic religions. It instructs believers to affirm their belief not only in their own scriptures but also in the revelations given to previous prophets, thus promoting a sense of continuity and solidarity among believers of different faiths. The refusal to distinguish between prophets underscores the belief in the singular source and purpose of their missions, revealing a fundamental principle of inclusivity and universalism in the Islamic faith. It calls for a holistic acceptance of all messengers and their teachings as integral to the divine will, fostering an atmosphere of respect and unity among the followers of different prophets.
orig: قولوا آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وما أنزل إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وما أوتي موسى وعيسى وما أوتي النبيون من ربهم لا نفرق بين أحد منهم ونحن له مسلمون

translation: So if they believe in what you believe, then they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, then they are only in dissension, and Allah will suffice you against them. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity in faith and the power of true guidance, which comes from believing in the same core principles as taught by the Quran and the Prophet Muhammad. It reassures the believers that following the path of true faith inherently leads to righteousness and guidance. The latter part of the verse addresses the scenario of rejection and opposition, indicating that such division is a departure from the truth. It also offers comfort and support to the believers, affirming that Allah is aware of all situations and will provide for and protect the faithful, alleviating the need for them to worry about opposition. This serves to strengthen the resolve and patience of believers, reminding them of Allah's omnipotence and omniscience.
orig: فإن آمنوا بمثل ما آمنتم به فقد اهتدوا وإن تولوا فإنما هم في شقاق فسيكفيكهم الله وهو السميع العليم

translation: The dye of Allah, and who is better than Allah in dye? And we are His worshippers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of the natural disposition (fitrah) towards which Allah has created humans. It metaphorically refers to this intrinsic nature as a 'dye' or color that is perfect and unchangeable, symbolizing how deeply the essence of faith is embedded in human nature. The rhetorical question 'who is better than Allah in dye?' emphasizes that no influence or alteration is superior to the innate disposition placed by Allah. The declaration 'we are His worshippers' reaffirms commitment to maintaining this pure state of being by adhering faithfully to His guidance and commands.
orig: صبغة الله ومن أحسن من الله صبغة ونحن له عابدون

translation: Say, 'Do you dispute with us about Allah while He is our Lord and your Lord? And for us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds, and we are sincere to Him.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the concept of religious dispute, emphasizing the futility of arguing over the shared belief in God's lordship. It acknowledges that each group (believers and opponents) is responsible for their own actions, suggesting that accountability is personal and tied to one's deeds. The insistence on sincerity indicates that genuine faith is characterized by an exclusive commitment to God without compromise, underscoring a central tenet of Islamic monotheism where the purity of one's intention and devotion to God is paramount.
orig: قل أتحاجوننا في الله وهو ربنا وربكم ولنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم ونحن له مخلصون

translation: Or do you say that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes were Jews or Christians? Say, 'Do you know better or does Allah?' And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from Allah? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse challenges the assertions some people make regarding the religious affiliations of the patriarchs and prophets before the advent of Islam, suggesting the absurdity of anachronistically labeling these figures as adherents of Judaism or Christianity, which were formalized after their times. It critiques those who claim to know more about divine matters than God Himself, emphasizing human fallibility and divine omniscience. The reference to concealing testimony highlights the severity of denying or hiding the truth of God’s revelations, indicating that such acts are not only unjust but are under constant divine scrutiny. This implies that true accountability and judgment come from God, who is fully aware of all human actions and intentions.
orig: أم تقولون إن إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط كانوا هودا أو نصارى قل أأنتم أعلم أم الله ومن أظلم ممن كتم شهادة عنده من الله وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: That is a nation that has passed away; they will have what they earned, and you will have what you earn. And you will not be questioned about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the intrinsic justice and individual accountability in divine judgment. Every community and individual is responsible for their own actions and will be judged accordingly. The past communities have received their due based on their deeds, just as present and future communities will. This principle underscores the importance of personal responsibility in the eyes of God, urging individuals to focus on their own actions rather than concerning themselves with the deeds of those who have passed away.
orig: تلك أمة قد خلت لها ما كسبت ولكم ما كسبتم ولا تسألون عما كانوا يعملون

translation: The foolish among the people will say, 'What has turned them away from their qibla [prayer direction], which they used to face?' Say, 'To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the criticism and confusion among some people regarding the change of the qibla from Jerusalem to Mecca. It underscores the absolute authority and sovereignty of Allah over all directions. The essential message is that the legitimacy of worship does not depend on the direction one faces but on the obedience to the divine command. The verse highlights that guidance comes only from Allah, who directs believers towards the right path, irrespective of geographical orientations, and that human understanding is limited and subject to divine will.
orig: سيقول السفهاء من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها قل لله المشرق والمغرب يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. And We did not make the direction that you used to face except that We might distinguish who follows the Messenger from who turns back on his heels. And indeed it was a big thing except for those whom Allah guided. And Allah would not let your faith be wasted; indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful towards people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the centrality of moderation and balance in the Muslim community, defining them as a 'middle nation'. The selection of the Muslim community as witnesses over humanity highlights their role in demonstrating ethical and moral conduct, as well as adhering to divine guidance symbolized by the Prophet, who is also a witness over them. The reference to the change in prayer direction (Qibla) serves as a test from Allah to distinguish true adherents of the Prophet's teachings from those who might falter in their faith. This test is acknowledged as difficult, but it's mentioned that those whom Allah has guided will find it manageable. The verse reassures believers that their previous devotions have not been in vain despite the change in the direction of prayer, with Allah's attributes of kindness and mercy underscoring His constant support and care for humanity.
orig: وكذلك جعلناكم أمة وسطا لتكونوا شهداء على الناس ويكون الرسول عليكم شهيدا وما جعلنا القبلة التي كنت عليها إلا لنعلم من يتبع الرسول ممن ينقلب على عقبيه وإن كانت لكبيرة إلا على الذين هدى الله وما كان الله ليضيع إيمانكم إن الله بالناس لرءوف رحيم

translation: We see the turning of your face towards the sky, so We shall indeed turn you to a direction that pleases you. Therefore, turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces towards it. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the compassion and responsiveness of Allah to the desires and comforts of His believers, exemplified by the changing of the prayer direction (Qibla) to something that holds deep significance and connection for the Prophet Muhammad and his followers. It underscores a transition not only in physical orientation but in spiritual and communal identity towards the Kaaba in Mecca, which is central to Islamic faith. Additionally, it asserts the acknowledgement and validation of the new direction by people of earlier revelations, strengthening the universal and inclusive message of Islam. It also serves to remind that Allah is all-knowing and observes all actions, encouraging accountability and sincerity in religious practice.
orig: قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم وما الله بغافل عما يعملون

translation: And if you were to bring to those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your Qiblah; nor will you be a follower of their Qiblah; nor are some of them followers of the other's Qiblah. And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, then you would surely be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in one's own religious principles in the face of opposition or differing opinions. It teaches that truth and guidance are not necessarily about consensus or mutual agreement, but about adherence to divine revelation, which might not align with the inclinations or traditions of others. The mention of not following others' desires after receiving knowledge reinforces the idea that divine knowledge should take precedence over cultural or societal norms, and that deviation from this after knowing the truth equates to injustice against oneself.
orig: ولئن أتيت الذين أوتوا الكتاب بكل آية ما تبعوا قبلتك وما أنت بتابع قبلتهم وما بعضهم بتابع قبلة بعض ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم من بعد ما جاءك من العلم إنك إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their own sons. But indeed a party of them conceal the truth while they know it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clear recognition and undeniable understanding that the people of the scripture (the Jews and Christians) have of the truth and prophecies in their own revelations regarding the advent of Prophet Muhammad and the veracity of the Islamic teachings. Despite their clear understanding, comparable to a parent's recognition of their own child, there remains a group among them who, driven by various motives such as pride, envy, or fear of losing authority, consciously choose to conceal and suppress this truth.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine truth originating from God, underscoring its ultimate and unquestionable nature. Believers are urged to embrace this truth wholeheartedly and avoid falling into skepticism or doubt about the messages and guidance provided by God. This exhortation serves to strengthen faith and encourage trust in the divine providence, steering individuals away from uncertainty and wavering belief, which can lead to spiritual and moral instability.
orig: الحق من ربك فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: For each [community], there is a direction toward which it faces. So race to [all that is] good. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you forth [for judgement] all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the diversity of religious and spiritual orientations that different communities might have, likening them to different directions they face. Regardless of these differences, the central message is a universal call to strive for goodness and virtuous deeds, highlighting the transient nature of worldly existence and the inevitability of divine accountability. It serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the ultimate gathering of all humanity for judgement, urging individuals to transcend petty differences and compete in acts of righteousness and moral integrity.
orig: ولكل وجهة هو موليها فاستبقوا الخيرات أين ما تكونوا يأت بكم الله جميعا إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And from wherever you go out, turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque; and indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, and Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a spiritual orientation towards the Sacred Mosque in Mecca in all aspects of life, symbolizing unity and a singular direction in the worship of Allah. It reassures the believers of the divine origin of their practices and reinforces the omniscience of Allah, affirming that all actions are observed by Him. This serves to remind the faithful of the constant presence of divine oversight and the importance of sincerity in their actions.
orig: ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وإنه للحق من ربك وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: And from wherever you set out, turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces towards it so that people will have no argument against you, except for those who wrong themselves. Fear them not, but fear Me; and that I may complete My blessings upon you, and that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity and directionality in ritual prayer for Muslims, highlighting the Qibla, towards the Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Haram), as a focal point to unify the believers. The instruction to face the Qibla serves not only as a religious directive but also an assertion of Islamic identity and communal cohesion. This alignment symbolizes submission to one divine authority and a rejection of division. The reference to people having no argument against the believers implies maintaining religious practices fervently and without contradiction, thereby protecting the community from criticism or negative influence. The call to fear God rather than people reaffirms the priority of divine commands and accountability. By adhering to this directive, believers are promised the completion of God's blessings and proper guidance, implying spiritual growth and favor. This guidance is contingent upon obedience and dedication to prescribed religious practices, serving as a means to achieving spiritual enlightenment and divine favor.
orig: ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره لئلا يكون للناس عليكم حجة إلا الذين ظلموا منهم فلا تخشوهم واخشوني ولأتم نعمتي عليكم ولعلكم تهتدون

translation: Just as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves, reciting Our verses to you and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you that which you did not know
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and guidance Allah bestows upon humanity by sending prophets who are from among the people themselves, thus making them relatable and effective as teachers. The messenger’s role is multifaceted: reciting the divine revelations, purifying the believers by guiding them to moral and spiritual purity, educating them about the scripture (the Quran) and imparting wisdom, which together cultivate a deep, holistic understanding of the religion and its application in daily life. The verse also highlights the element of enlightenment, where the messenger reveals knowledge previously unknown to the people, thereby expanding their horizons and deepening their comprehension of the divine will and the workings of the world.
orig: كما أرسلنا فيكم رسولا منكم يتلو عليكم آياتنا ويزكيكم ويعلمكم الكتاب والحكمة ويعلمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون

translation: So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reciprocal relationship between human beings and God, highlighting the importance of remembrance and gratitude. When individuals remember and mention God in their daily lives, God acknowledges them in return. The act of remembrance is linked to an attitude of gratitude, suggesting that being mindful of God's presence and favors should naturally lead to thankfulness. The directive to avoid denial of God underlines the necessity of maintaining faith and not rejecting the blessings and guidance that God provides. Overall, this verse serves as a reminder of the spiritual obligations individuals hold and the divine response that their actions provoke.
orig: فاذكروني أذكركم واشكروا لي ولا تكفرون

translation: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and prayer as means to seek divine assistance in times of trial and hardship. It reassures believers that Allah's support and companionship are assured for those who remain steadfast and maintain their prayers, reflecting a relationship where perseverance in faith yields divine proximity and favor.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا استعينوا بالصبر والصلاة إن الله مع الصابرين

translation: And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, 'They are dead.' Rather, they are alive, but you perceive it not.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual continuity and honor given to martyrs in Islam. It suggests that those who sacrifice their lives for the sake of their faith in Allah obtain a form of life that transcends ordinary human understanding. While they may appear dead to the worldly observer, they are alive in a way that is not perceivable through ordinary sensory experiences. This life is of a higher, spiritual nature, indicating a special state of existence that is both a reward and a testament to their faith and sacrifice.
orig: ولا تقولوا لمن يقتل في سبيل الله أموات بل أحياء ولكن لا تشعرون

translation: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitable trials and difficulties that believers will face in their lives, which serve as tests of faith and endurance. The specific challenges mentioned — fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives, and fruits — represent both physical and emotional hardships. The mention of 'giving good tidings to the patient' underscores the virtue and reward of patience in the face of adversity, reassuring believers that their perseverance in maintaining faith and trust in God during these trials will lead to spiritual growth and divine compensation.
orig: ولنبلونكم بشيء من الخوف والجوع ونقص من الأموال والأنفس والثمرات وبشر الصابرين

translation: Those who, when disaster strikes them, say, 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound acceptance and submission to Allah's will during times of suffering or loss. By declaring their belonging to Allah and acknowledging their eventual return to Him, it reflects a mindset of patience, resilience, and unwavering faith in the divine plan. This proclamation serves as a reminder to maintain a calm and composed demeanor, trusting in Allah's wisdom and mercy, even in the face of adversity.
orig: الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة قالوا إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون

translation: Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and it is those who are the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special stature of certain individuals who have received blessings and mercy from God due to their adherence to His guidance. It signifies that divine favor is contingent upon one's alignment with spiritual and moral correctness as ordained in Islamic teachings. The phrase 'rightly guided' encapsulates the idea of living a life in accordance with divine will, suggesting that true success and spiritual enlightenment are the rewards for such guidance.
orig: أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون

translation: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs 'Umrah, there is no blame on him for walking between them. And whoever voluntarily does good - indeed, Allah is Appreciative and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of As-Safa and Al-Marwah in the Islamic tradition as they are marked as symbols of Allah. It suggests a flexibility in religious rites, showing that the act of performing Sa'i (walking between these two hills) during Hajj or 'Umrah is not obligatory but rather permissible. The latter part of the verse highlights Allah's recognition and valuation of voluntary good deeds, reinforcing the principle that Allah is aware of and values the intentions and actions of believers.
orig: إن الصفا والمروة من شعائر الله فمن حج البيت أو اعتمر فلا جناح عليه أن يطوف بهما ومن تطوع خيرا فإن الله شاكر عليم

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We have made it clear for the people in the Scripture - those are cursed by Allah and cursed by those who curse.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the grave wrongdoing of concealing or suppressing religious truths and guidance that have been clearly revealed in the sacred scriptures. It underscores the moral obligation of believers to share and disseminate divine guidance for the benefit of all humanity. Those who choose to hide this knowledge out of self-interest or malice are subject to divine condemnation and also face rejection from the community of believers who uphold truth and justice. The verse serves as a stern warning about the consequences of withholding spiritual and moral guidance that is intended to be universally accessible to aid human understanding and moral development.
orig: إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزلنا من البينات والهدى من بعد ما بيناه للناس في الكتاب أولئك يلعنهم الله ويلعنهم اللاعنون

translation: Except those who repent, amend [their conduct], and make clear [their sincerity], for them I will accept their repentance, and I am the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the infinite mercy and forgiveness of God towards those who sincerely repent, rectify their actions, and openly demonstrate their commitment to righteousness. It emphasizes the importance of not only seeking forgiveness through repentance but also coupling it with concrete actions that reflect genuine change. Moreover, declaring one's sincerity serves as a testament to their honest intent, inviting divine forgiveness. The attributes of God as the Accepting of Repentance and the Merciful highlight His readiness to forgive and His compassion towards those who turn back to Him with a true heart.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا وبينوا فأولئك أتوب عليهم وأنا التواب الرحيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, upon them is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences facing those who persist in disbelief until death, highlighting their alienation not only from divine mercy but also from the goodwill of celestial beings and humanity at large. It underscores the gravity of dying in a state of rejection of faith, presenting it as a position that not only distances one from God but also places them under a universal condemnation that spans both the divine and human realms.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وماتوا وهم كفار أولئك عليهم لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين

translation: They will abide therein forever, neither will the punishment be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and permanence of punishment for those who persist in disbelief and die without repenting. It underscores the concept of divine justice, wherein those who reject faith and continue in their transgressions will face unrelenting consequences in the hereafter. The absence of any reduction or pause in their suffering highlights the critical importance of faith and repentance in one’s earthly life to avoid such an eternal fate.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And your God is One God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute oneness of God, known as Tawheed. It reinforces that God alone is worthy of worship and is the sole creator and sustainer of the universe. The attributes 'the Most Merciful' and 'the Most Compassionate' highlight God’s infinite mercy and compassion towards all creatures, which is central to His divine nature. This serves not only as a theological statement but also as a call for believers to trust and seek refuge in God's mercy and compassion throughout their lives.
orig: وإلهكم إله واحد لا إله إلا هو الرحمن الرحيم

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah has sent down from the sky of water, thereby reviving the earth after its death and scattering in it from every creature, and the directing of the winds and the clouds controlled between the heaven and the earth, are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reflections on natural phenomena as signs of divine power and wisdom, intended to inspire contemplation and understanding in those who are thoughtful. The orderly patterns and systems observed in the universe, from celestial objects to ecological cycles, are presented as evidence of an intelligent design, meant to benefit humanity and to prompt human beings to reflect on their creator. It underscores the interconnectivity of natural elements and their purposeful orchestration to sustain life, pointing towards a deliberate and beneficial creation that aligns with human intellect and understanding.
orig: إن في خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار والفلك التي تجري في البحر بما ينفع الناس وما أنزل الله من السماء من ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها وبث فيها من كل دابة وتصريف الرياح والسحاب المسخر بين السماء والأرض لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And among the people are those who take besides Allah rivals, loving them as they should love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah. And if only those who have wronged would see, when they see the punishment, that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of true allegiance and love that should be directed solely towards Allah, highlighting the mistake of idolizing others alongside Him. Believers are described as having an intense, unrivaled love for Allah, implying their understanding and appreciation of His supremacy. Additionally, the verse serves as a warning to those who err by associating partners with Allah, indicating that they will recognize Allah's sole sovereignty and severe retribution only when faced with the reality of divine punishment. This revelation aims to awaken the importance of monotheism and the consequences of idolatry.
orig: ومن الناس من يتخذ من دون الله أندادا يحبونهم كحب الله والذين آمنوا أشد حبا لله ولو يرى الذين ظلموا إذ يرون العذاب أن القوة لله جميعا وأن الله شديد العذاب

translation: When those who were followed disown those who followed them, and they see the punishment, and all ties with them are cut off,
interpretation: This verse highlights the Day of Judgment where there will be a clear separation between leaders of misguidance and their followers. It illustrates the ultimate accountability, where each individual will face the consequences of their choices independently. Leaders will disassociate themselves from their followers to save themselves, revealing the selfish nature of wrongful leadership and misguided allegiance. The mention of seeing the punishment and the severing of all ties emphasizes the reality of consequences and the dissolution of worldly relationships that were based on falsehood. It serves as a stern reminder of the importance of personal responsibility and the futility of relying on others for spiritual salvation.
orig: إذ تبرأ الذين اتبعوا من الذين اتبعوا ورأوا العذاب وتقطعت بهم الأسباب

translation: And those who followed will say, 'If only we had another chance, we would disown them as they have disowned us.' Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they will not be out of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of bad influence and the importance of personal responsibility. Those who followed the misguiders in life express a futile wish for another chance to rectify their mistakes, illustrating the irrevocable nature of their decisions on Judgment Day. Their regrets are a reflection of their realization of their wrongdoings, highlighted by Allah showing them their deeds. The verse serves as a stern warning that following others into sin without personal discernment leads to eternal regret and punishment, emphasizing the eternal consequences of earthly actions.
orig: وقال الذين اتبعوا لو أن لنا كرة فنتبرأ منهم كما تبرءوا منا كذلك يريهم الله أعمالهم حسرات عليهم وما هم بخارجين من النار

translation: O mankind, eat from whatever is on earth [that is] lawful and good and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming what is permissible and wholesome, drawing attention to the moral and spiritual implications of our dietary choices. It warns against the influence of Satan, who seeks to lead humanity astray from divine guidance. The mention of 'lawful and good' signifies that adherence to divine commandments in food consumption not only fulfills legal aspects but also ethical ones, promoting a pure, healthy lifestyle that aligns with spiritual purity. Following this path is juxtaposed against following Satan, who represents the forces leading to moral and spiritual corruption. Thus, the choice of what one consumes is also a reflection of one's broader ethical and spiritual orientation.
orig: يا أيها الناس كلوا مما في الأرض حلالا طيبا ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: He only commands you to evil and indecency, and to say about Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against following the incitements of Satan, who endeavors to lead humans into committing immoral and vile acts. Further, it cautions against making false statements concerning Allah, emphasizing the gravity of speaking without knowledge about divine matters. This teaches the importance of basing one’s actions and beliefs on informed understanding and righteousness.
orig: إنما يأمركم بالسوء والفحشاء وأن تقولوا على الله ما لا تعلمون
