interpretation: This verse underscores the severe spiritual and moral consequences of exploiting orphans by unlawfully consuming their wealth. It uses powerful imagery to equate such actions with ingesting fire, highlighting both the self-destructive nature of this sin and the intense suffering it will lead to in the hereafter. The metaphor of fire in the belly conveys the torment and guilt that will consume the individual from within, while the reference to burning in a blazing fire illustrates the grave punishment awaiting them, underscoring the profound ethical imperative to protect the vulnerable and uphold justice.
orig: إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما إنما يأكلون في بطونهم نارا وسيصلون سعيرا

translation: Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male, the equivalent of the portion of two females. If the children are all females, and there are two or more, they will have two-thirds of what he leaves behind. If there is only one, she will have half. For his parents, to each one of them, one-sixth of what he leaves if he has a child. If he has no child, and his parents are his heirs, then for his mother is one-third. If he has siblings, then for his mother is one-sixth, after any bequest he may have made or debt. Your parents and your children, you do not know which of them are more beneficial to you. These are obligations from Allah; indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines specific directives regarding inheritance, emphasizing the structured approach Islam takes in financial matters after one's death to ensure equitable distribution among heirs. The portions allocated to male and female children illustrate a balancing mechanism taking into consideration their different financial responsibilities in society. The stipulations for parents and the conditional changes based on the presence of children or siblings show a flexible consideration of family dynamics. The closing part of the verse highlights the divine wisdom behind these injunctions and reminds believers of the unknowable nature of which familial relationships will prove most beneficial in the long term, thus justifying the divinely ordained shares to prevent disputes and ensure justice.
orig: يوصيكم الله في أولادكم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين فإن كن نساء فوق اثنتين فلهن ثلثا ما ترك وإن كانت واحدة فلها النصف ولأبويه لكل واحد منهما السدس مما ترك إن كان له ولد فإن لم يكن له ولد وورثه أبواه فلأمه الثلث فإن كان له إخوة فلأمه السدس من بعد وصية يوصي بها أو دين آباؤكم وأبناؤكم لا تدرون أيهم أقرب لكم نفعا فريضة من الله إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And for you is half of what your wives leave if they have no child; but if they have a child, then for you is one-fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they [may have] made or debt. And for them is one-fourth of what you leave if you have no child; but if you have a child, then for them is one-eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you [may have] made or debt. And if a man or a woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants but has a brother or a sister, then for each one of them is a sixth. But if they are more than that, they share a third, after any bequest that was made or debt, as long as there is no harm [caused]. [This is] an ordinance from Allah, and Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse outlines detailed inheritance laws, emphasizing fairness and the orderly distribution of assets among heirs in an Islamic context. It establishes specific shares based on the presence of children and other relatives, ensuring financial security and duty to family after one's death. The stipulations regarding bequests and debts before distribution safeguard personal wishes and financial obligations. The verse highlights divine wisdom and patience, showing Allah's comprehensive knowledge of human needs and His merciful approach in guiding them through the specifics of inheritance law, which balances individual rights with the collective well-being of the family and society.
orig: ولكم نصف ما ترك أزواجكم إن لم يكن لهن ولد فإن كان لهن ولد فلكم الربع مما تركن من بعد وصية يوصين بها أو دين ولهن الربع مما تركتم إن لم يكن لكم ولد فإن كان لكم ولد فلهن الثمن مما تركتم من بعد وصية توصون بها أو دين وإن كان رجل يورث كلالة أو امرأة وله أخ أو أخت فلكل واحد منهما السدس فإن كانوا أكثر من ذلك فهم شركاء في الثلث من بعد وصية يوصى بها أو دين غير مضار وصية من الله والله عليم حليم

translation: These are the limits set by Allah, and whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and that is the great triumph.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the divine boundaries established by Allah, highlighting obedience to Allah and His Messenger as vital for attaining eternal success and fulfillment. It promises a reward in the form of eternal paradise characterized by lush gardens with rivers—a symbol of peace, abundance, and divine pleasure. The phrase 'great triumph' underscores the ultimate value and significance of this eternal reward compared to worldly gains, suggesting that true success lies in the eternal life hereafter rather than the temporary world.
orig: تلك حدود الله ومن يطع الله ورسوله يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him into a Fire, abiding therein, and he will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of disobedience to Allah and His Messenger, and the act of exceeding the set boundaries or limits of conduct prescribed in Islam. It warns that such transgressions lead not merely to temporary discomfort or worldly consequences, but to eternal damnation in the hereafter, specifically in the form of enduring the fire of hell. Moreover, the punishment described is not only painful but also humiliating, indicating a degradation not just of the physical but perhaps also of the moral and spiritual stature of the transgressor. This serves as a stern reminder of the gravity of obedience in Islamic ethics and the ultimate accountability before God.
orig: ومن يعص الله ورسوله ويتعد حدوده يدخله نارا خالدا فيها وله عذاب مهين

translation: And those of your women who commit illegal sexual intercourse, take the testimony of four from among you against them; and if they testify, confine them to the houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them another way.
interpretation: This verse outlines the prescribed procedure and consequences when dealing with accusations of sexual immorality among women in a social and judicial context. It underscores the necessity of substantial evidence, represented by the testimony of four witnesses, reflecting the Quran's emphasis on justice and the prevention of wrongful accusations. The confinement of the accused, pending death or divine intervention, points towards a combination of both punishment and the potential for repentance and rehabilitation within an Islamic framework. This approach is indicative of the balance Islam seeks between upholding moral laws and providing avenues for mercy, stressing the importance of a supportive and corrective community environment rather than one solely focused on punitive measures.
orig: واللاتي يأتين الفاحشة من نسائكم فاستشهدوا عليهن أربعة منكم فإن شهدوا فأمسكوهن في البيوت حتى يتوفاهن الموت أو يجعل الله لهن سبيلا

translation: And the two who commit it among you, punish them both. But if they repent and amend, then turn away from them; indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and accountability within the community, balanced with mercy and the opportunity for redemption. It addresses the response to wrongful actions, advocating initially for a measure of punitive action to underscore the seriousness of the offense. However, it crucially pivots to highlight the transformative power of repentance and reform. By allowing for forgiveness upon genuine change, the verse promotes a compassionate societal ethos, reflecting Allah's own attributes of mercy and forgiveness, thus encouraging a community governed by both justice and compassion.
orig: واللذان يأتيانها منكم فآذوهما فإن تابا وأصلحا فأعرضوا عنهما إن الله كان توابا رحيما

translation: Repentance with Allah is only for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon thereafter; it is they to whom Allah will turn in mercy, and Allah is All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse imparts the forgiving nature of Allah towards those who commit sins out of ignorance, yet swiftly seek repentance upon realizing their error. It accentuates Allah’s readiness to forgive and the profound mercy He extends to the repentant, provided their contrition is immediate and sincere. This stipulation of timely repentance underscores the significance of prompt rectification of one's mistakes in the Islamic faith, advocating for self-awareness and swift actions to amend wrongs. The attributes of Allah as 'All-Knowing' and 'Wise' at the end serve as a reaffirmation that Allah’s judgments are incredibly profound and based on complete understanding of human contexts and motivations, embodying perfect wisdom in forgiving those sincerely remorseful.
orig: إنما التوبة على الله للذين يعملون السوء بجهالة ثم يتوبون من قريب فأولئك يتوب الله عليهم وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And repentance is not for those who continue to do evil deeds, until death approaches one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I repent now,' nor for those who die while they are disbelievers. For them, We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity in repentance and underscores that it should be carried out before one's death is imminent. It criticizes those who live a life of sin and only decide to repent when faced with death, suggesting that such last-minute repentance is often insincere and thus unacceptable. The verse serves as a warning that true repentance should come from a genuine realization and transformation during one's lifetime, rather than as a desperate attempt to avoid punishment at the end. Additionally, it highlights the consequences for those who die in a state of disbelief, indicating a deliberate choice against faith, which leads to a promised painful retribution.
orig: وليست التوبة للذين يعملون السيئات حتى إذا حضر أحدهم الموت قال إني تبت الآن ولا الذين يموتون وهم كفار أولئك أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما

translation: O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will. Nor should you constrain them in order to take away part of what you have given them, unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. For if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike something in which Allah has placed much good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principles of justice, kindness, and respect in marital relationships. It specifically denounces the pre-Islamic practice of inheriting women against their will, advocating for women's autonomy and rights. The mention of not constraining women to reclaim dowries unless in cases of clear immorality underscores the importance of fairness and the conditions under which marital disputes should be addressed. The directive to live with wives kindly reflects the broader Islamic ethos of compassion and benevolence in familial interactions, even in instances of personal discontent. The final part of the verse encourages believers to remain patient and open-minded, highlighting that what may initially appear undesirable in a spouse could possess hidden virtues or beneficial aspects ordained by Allah, hence promoting a mindset of looking beyond surface-level judgments and fostering enduring relationships.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يحل لكم أن ترثوا النساء كرها ولا تعضلوهن لتذهبوا ببعض ما آتيتموهن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة وعاشروهن بالمعروف فإن كرهتموهن فعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا ويجعل الله فيه خيرا كثيرا

translation: And if you desire to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a great amount (a qintar), do not take back anything from it. Would you take it on false charges and manifest sin?
interpretation: This verse underscores the ethical and moral standards expected in the context of marital relationships, particularly in the scenario of divorce and remarriage. It addresses the inequity and impropriety of reclaiming a significant marital gift if one decides to divorce and marry another. The verse reinforces the sanctity of marriage and the seriousness of financial dealings within it, calling attention to the wrongful nature and clear sinfulness of falsifying reasons to reclaim gifts given in the context of marriage. It emphasizes fairness, accountability, and the avoidance of deceit in handling marital transitions.
orig: وإن أردتم استبدال زوج مكان زوج وآتيتم إحداهن قنطارا فلا تأخذوا منه شيئا أتأخذونه بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: And how could you take it back while you have gone in unto each other, and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity and serious nature of marital commitments. The reference to mutually entering into physical and emotional unions underscores the deep connection formed through marriage, which is not to be taken lightly. The 'solemn covenant' refers to the marriage contract, which is a serious, binding agreement in the sight of God. This covenant demands faithfulness and responsibility, and its violation through separation or divorce is not something to be done capriciously. The verse prompts believers to reflect on the gravity of marital vows and the ethical responsibility to maintain and honor such bonds.
orig: وكيف تأخذونه وقد أفضى بعضكم إلى بعض وأخذن منكم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred. Indeed, it is an indecency, and hateful, and an evil way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prohibition of incestuous relationships, particularly marrying women who were previously married to one's father, solidifying the moral and social boundaries within family structures in Islam. It underscores the view of such unions as morally reprehensible and socially unacceptable. It highlights a commitment to ethical conduct and the importance of maintaining dignified and respectful familial relationships, underscoring that deviation from these prescribed codes is not only a moral aberration but also a deviation from the righteous path.
orig: ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم من النساء إلا ما قد سلف إنه كان فاحشة ومقتا وساء سبيلا

translation: Forbidden to you are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your father's sisters, your mother's sisters, your brother's daughters, your sister's daughters, your foster mothers who nursed you, your foster sisters, your wives' mothers, and your step-daughters under your guardianship born of your wives unto whom you have gone in, but if you have not gone in unto them, there is no sin on you, and the wives of your sons who (spring) from your own loins, and that you take in marriage two sisters simultaneously, except for what has already occurred. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse delineates the bounds of lawful matrimonial relations in Islam, emphasizing the sanctity of familial bonds. It establishes a clear prohibition against marriages with close relatives, defining specific degrees of blood relations and milk kinship where marriage is considered incestuous and thus impermissible. The inclusion of step-daughters and daughters-in-law reinforces the ethical obligation to maintain chastity and honor within the extended family structure. The allowance for past occurrences indicates Allah's forgiving nature towards previous transgressions under ignorance before this revelation. This directive not only guards against genetic complications attributed to close kin marriages but also reinforces social norms that respect family boundaries and relationships.
orig: حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم وبناتكم وأخواتكم وعماتكم وخالاتكم وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت وأمهاتكم اللاتي أرضعنكم وأخواتكم من الرضاعة وأمهات نسائكم وربائبكم اللاتي في حجوركم من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن فإن لم تكونوا دخلتم بهن فلا جناح عليكم وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين إلا ما قد سلف إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And also prohibited are women already married, except those whom your right hands possess. This has been decreed by Allah upon you. Moreover, lawful for you are all others beyond these, provided that you seek them with your wealth in a lawful marriage, not committing fornication. So those whom you enjoy from them, give them their required due as an obligation. And there is no sin upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation. Indeed, Allah is always All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines the ethical and lawful framework for marital and sexual relationships in Islam. It emphasizes the sanctity of marriage and prohibits the involvement with married women unless they are captives who have different considerations under Islamic law. The text encourages seeking relationships based on mutual respect and lawful terms, rather than on mere sexual gratification. It affirms the necessity of providing mahr (a mandatory marital gift) to women as their right. The verse also hints at flexibility and personal discretion in adjusting the conditions of a marriage contract after fulfilling the primary obligations, underlining the importance of mutual consent and justice in personal relationships. Further, it reflects God's comprehensive knowledge and wisdom, guiding believers to maintain high moral standards in personal interactions.
orig: والمحصنات من النساء إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم كتاب الله عليكم وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم أن تبتغوا بأموالكم محصنين غير مسافحين فما استمتعتم به منهن فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة ولا جناح عليكم فيما تراضيتم به من بعد الفريضة إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And those among you who cannot afford to marry free believing women may marry from your believing maids whom your right hands possess. And Allah knows best about your faith, you [believers] are one from another. Marry them with the permission of their guardians and give them their due compensation justly, they should be chaste, not committing illicit sex, nor taking secret lovers. Once they are protected [in marriage], if they commit any open immorality, they shall receive half the punishment prescribed for free women. This [permission to marry slave women] is for the one among you who fears hardship [in maintaining chastity], but it is better for you to be patient. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the social and economic realities faced by early Muslim believers, emphasizing practical solutions within a spiritual framework. It acknowledges the financial difficulties some men may face in marrying free believing women and provides an alternative by allowing marriage to believing maids, thereby ensuring that moral and societal duties are met even in strained circumstances. This regulation also underscores the importance of consent from guardians and the provision of fair treatment and compensation to these women, emphasizing their dignity and rights within the marriage. The mention of reduced penalties for certain transgressions serves not only as a legal measure but also subtly underscores the importance of mercy and understanding in dealing with individuals' faults. The final encouragement towards patience hints at the superior moral value of restraint and the benefits of enduring hardships, aligning this with God's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, thus promoting a compassionate societal outlook.
orig: ومن لم يستطع منكم طولا أن ينكح المحصنات المؤمنات فمن ما ملكت أيمانكم من فتياتكم المؤمنات والله أعلم بإيمانكم بعضكم من بعض فانكحوهن بإذن أهلهن وآتوهن أجورهن بالمعروف محصنات غير مسافحات ولا متخذات أخدان فإذا أحصن فإن أتين بفاحشة فعليهن نصف ما على المحصنات من العذاب ذلك لمن خشي العنت منكم وأن تصبروا خير لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah intends to clarify things for you and guide you to the practices of those before you and to accept your repentance. And Allah is All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the benevolence and mercy of Allah, who seeks to enlighten and guide His followers by providing clarity and connection to the righteous practices of those who came before, thereby underscoring the continuity and consistency in divine guidance across generations. It also accentuates Allah's forgiveness, highlighting His readiness to accept repentance from His believers. The attributes of Allah being 'All-Knowing' and 'Wise' reassure the believers of the perfect wisdom and knowledge underlying divine commands and guidance.
orig: يريد الله ليبين لكم ويهديكم سنن الذين من قبلكم ويتوب عليكم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And Allah wishes to accept your repentance, but those who follow their passions want you to digress greatly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine will of God (Allah) to grant forgiveness and accept the repentance of individuals seeking it sincerely. It underscores God's inherent mercy and readiness to forgive, contrasting it with the intent of those driven by their desires. The latter group is described as wishing for others to stray significantly from the righteous path. This implies a spiritual struggle where believers must resist external temptations and inclinations towards excess, holding firm to the guidance and forgiveness offered by God.
orig: والله يريد أن يتوب عليكم ويريد الذين يتبعون الشهوات أن تميلوا ميلا عظيما

translation: Allah intends to lighten your burden, for man was created weak.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the compassionate and merciful nature of God, who understands the inherent weaknesses and limitations of human beings. It suggests that God’s commandments and laws are designed with the recognition of human frailty in mind, aiming to alleviate burdens rather than impose undue hardships. This compassionate approach by God serves as a reminder of the need for humans to also be understanding and forgiving towards themselves and others, recognizing and accommodating each other’s vulnerabilities.
orig: يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, except it be through trade mutually agreed upon among you, and do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah is to you ever Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of ethical conduct and mutual consent in financial transactions among believers. It cautions against the unjust consumption of wealth, promoting fairness and honesty in trade. Furthermore, it warns against self-destructive behaviors, and underscores the principle of mercy that Allah extends to the believers, encouraging them to mirror this mercy in their interactions with each other.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل إلا أن تكون تجارة عن تراض منكم ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم إن الله كان بكم رحيما

translation: And whoever does that in aggression and injustice, then We will drive him into a Fire, and this is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences that await those who commit acts of aggression and injustice. It underscores the principle that such actions are abhorrent and punishable by severe penalties in the hereafter, specifically the torment of the Fire. The phrase 'and this is easy for Allah' highlights God's absolute power and authority, affirming that nothing is beyond His capability, including the enactment of divine justice. This serves as a stern warning against wrongdoing and an admonition to adhere to moral and just behaviors.
orig: ومن يفعل ذلك عدوانا وظلما فسوف نصليه نارا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your lesser sins and admit you to a noble entrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of God towards His followers who consciously avoid committing major sins, recognizing human vulnerability to smaller errors. It assures believers that abstaining from significant wrongdoing, specifically those actions explicitly prohibited, will not only lead to the expiation of their minor sins but also secure them an honorable place in the hereafter. This encapsulates the concept of God’s grace in rewarding sincere efforts to live a morally upright life, promoting a balance between God's justice and mercy.
orig: إن تجتنبوا كبائر ما تنهون عنه نكفر عنكم سيئاتكم وندخلكم مدخلا كريما

translation: And do not wish for the things in which Allah has made some of you to excel others. For men there is a reward for what they have earned, and for women there is a reward for what they have earned. And ask Allah of His bounty. Indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of contentment and the recognition of individual merits and responsibilities. It discourages envy or covetousness over the divine favors and opportunities granted uniquely to others, affirming that both men and women are rewarded according to their own deeds and efforts. The verse encourages believers to seek Allah's bounty through rightful means instead of desiring what others have been given, highlighting Allah's omniscience and the concept that He distributes roles, responsibilities, and blessings among individuals according to His infinite wisdom.
orig: ولا تتمنوا ما فضل الله به بعضكم على بعض للرجال نصيب مما اكتسبوا وللنساء نصيب مما اكتسبن واسألوا الله من فضله إن الله كان بكل شيء عليما

translation: And for everyone, we have appointed heirs for what parents and close relatives leave behind, and also those to whom you have pledged your oaths, so give them their share. Indeed, Allah is a witness over everything.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of justice and fulfilling duties in the distribution of an inheritance. It emphasizes that one must adhere to the divinely ordained guidelines for inheritance, acknowledging not only biological kinship but also legally or morally bound relationships that are established through oaths. This demonstrates the comprehensive and inclusive nature of Islamic law, which aims to protect the rights of all related parties and ensure fair treatment. Additionally, by affirming that Allah is a witness to all actions, the verse reinforces the ethical and spiritual responsibility to adhere strictly to these guidelines, as ultimately, everyone is accountable to Allah for their actions.
orig: ولكل جعلنا موالي مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون والذين عقدت أيمانكم فآتوهم نصيبهم إن الله كان على كل شيء شهيدا

translation: Men are the protectors and maintainers of women because Allah has made some of them to excel others and because they spend from their means. Therefore, righteous women are devoutly obedient and guard in the husband's absence what Allah would have them guard. But those [wives] from whom you fear arrogance - [first] advise them; [then if they persist], forsake them in bed; and [finally], strike them. But if they obey you [once more], seek not against them means [of annoyance]. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand.
interpretation: This verse addresses the social and marital responsibilities between men and women, emphasizing a hierarchical but responsible relationship. Men are assigned the role of protectors and maintainers, not merely as a privilege, but tied to their financial obligations and the spiritual and moral accountability they hold. Women are encouraged to be obedient and guard their chastity and the family's private matters in their husband's absence. The verse also outlines a progressive form of conflict resolution in marital disputes, encouraging patience, communication, and progressive measures before considering physical reprimand, which has been subject to extensive interpretative scrutiny and various contextual limitations by Islamic scholars. It also reaffirms the need for mutual respect and love within the framework set by Allah, highlighting the divine oversight in all affairs, thus guiding believers to maintain harmony and respect within marriages.
orig: الرجال قوامون على النساء بما فضل الله بعضهم على بعض وبما أنفقوا من أموالهم فالصالحات قانتات حافظات للغيب بما حفظ الله واللاتي تخافون نشوزهن فعظوهن واهجروهن في المضاجع واضربوهن فإن أطعنكم فلا تبغوا عليهن سبيلا إن الله كان عليا كبيرا

translation: And if you fear dissension between the two, send an arbitrator from his people and an arbitrator from her people. If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will cause it between them. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing, Aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of mediation and external intervention in resolving marital disputes. It underscores the role of neutral and respected persons from both sides of the family in facilitating communication and understanding, with the ultimate goal of reconciliation if both parties are genuinely inclined. It also reflects the divine support for such endeavors and highlights Allah's comprehensive knowledge and awareness of all human affairs, ensuring that the outcomes are aligned with divine wisdom and justice.
orig: وإن خفتم شقاق بينهما فابعثوا حكما من أهله وحكما من أهلها إن يريدا إصلاحا يوفق الله بينهما إن الله كان عليما خبيرا

translation: And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor, the neighbor farther away, the companion at your side, the traveler, and what your right hands possess. Indeed, Allah does not love those who are self-deluding and boastful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism, urging believers to worship only Allah and shun all forms of idolatry. It underscores the significance of ethical conduct towards not only one's parents but also a wide circle of social relations, highlighting compassion and responsibility towards relatives, orphans, the needy, neighbors, companions, and travelers. The verse portrays these social responsibilities as intrinsic elements of faith which reflect the believer's commitment to God's commands. Moreover, the text criticizes arrogance and boastfulness, advocating for humility and sincerity as vital qualities of a true believer, indicating that these ethical behaviors are closely watched by Allah, who favors the humble and sincere over the proud.
orig: واعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا وبذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين والجار ذي القربى والجار الجنب والصاحب بالجنب وابن السبيل وما ملكت أيمانكم إن الله لا يحب من كان مختالا فخورا

translation: Those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness upon people, and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the moral failing of miserliness, particularly in those who not only practice it but also encourage others to do the same. It underscores the egregiousness of concealing and hoarding the bounty provided by Allah, which should ideally be shared and distributed amongst the community for the common good. By linking these actions with a 'humiliating punishment', the verse serves as a stark warning, emphasizing that such behavior is not only socially harmful but also spiritually detrimental, leading ultimately to disgrace and punishment in the hereafter. This stresses the importance of generosity and transparency as virtues that align with divine principles, fostering a just and caring society.
orig: الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل ويكتمون ما آتاهم الله من فضله وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who spend their money to be seen by people and do not believe in Allah nor the Last Day; and he to whom Satan is a companion, then evil is he as a companion.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy of those who perform acts of charity merely for societal recognition and praise, rather than out of genuine faith and devotion to God. It criticizes their lack of belief in the core tenets of Islam, such as the existence of Allah and the Day of Judgment. The association with Satan highlights the moral and spiritual peril of allowing one's actions to be guided by insincerity and the desire for worldly appreciation, as opposed to divine guidance. The evil companion (Satan) symbolizes the perpetuation of deceit and moral corruption, influencing the individual away from the path of truth and righteousness.
orig: والذين ينفقون أموالهم رئاء الناس ولا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ومن يكن الشيطان له قرينا فساء قرينا

translation: And what would it cost them had they believed in Allah and the Last Day, and spent out of what Allah had provided for them? And Allah is ever All-Knowing of them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith in Allah and the Day of Judgment. It questions the reluctance or hesitation people might have towards adopting these beliefs and contributing charitably from the sustenance provided by Allah. The rhetorical question posed suggests that such actions should be natural and beneficial, rather than burdensome. The assertion that Allah is All-Knowing serves to remind believers that their actions and intentions are always under divine scrutiny, encouraging them to align their behaviors with Islamic teachings.
orig: وماذا عليهم لو آمنوا بالله واليوم الآخر وأنفقوا مما رزقهم الله وكان الله بهم عليما

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom; and if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice and mercy of Allah. It assures that Allah is impeccably just in His judgments, not letting even the smallest act of injustice occur. Every action, no matter how minor, is accounted for. Moreover, the verse highlights Allah's generosity in rewarding good deeds. Not only are good actions recognized, but they are also rewarded manifold, reflecting the boundless grace and benevolence of Allah. The mention of 'a great reward' signifies that the blessings from Allah are immensely substantial and beyond ordinary human expectations.
orig: إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما

translation: So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you (O Muhammad) as a witness over these?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significant role of Prophet Muhammad as a universal witness on the Day of Judgment. It underscores the accountability of each person, as every community will have witnesses presented, validating the deeds done in their lifetimes. Prophet Muhammad's role as a witness highlights his central and pivotal position in the divine plan, bearing testimony to the adherence or deviation from God's guidance by all of humanity. The verse serves as a reminder of the seriousness of the Day of Judgment and the comprehensive justice that will be served.
orig: فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا

translation: On that day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish the earth could swallow them, and they will not be able to hide any story from Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound regret and despair that disbelievers and those who disobeyed the Messenger will experience on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the inevitability of divine accountability where every deed and thought will be exposed before Allah. The imagery of wishing the earth could swallow them underscores the depth of their shame and fear, illustrating the overwhelming nature of facing the consequences of one’s actions. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience and faith in avoiding such a fate.
orig: يومئذ يود الذين كفروا وعصوا الرسول لو تسوى بهم الأرض ولا يكتمون الله حديثا

translation: O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying, nor while in a state of impurity—except when traveling on the road—until you have washed. And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from relieving himself, or you have touched women and find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands. Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of purity and consciousness in the performance of prayers, highlighting that one must be in a clear state of mind and physically clean to stand before God. It underlines the flexibility in religious practices under certain conditions, such as illness or lack of water, showing God's mercy and understanding of human circumstances. This adaptability ensures that all believers are able to maintain their spiritual duties without being excessively burdened by their physical situations.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى حتى تعلموا ما تقولون ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل حتى تغتسلوا وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم إن الله كان عفوا غفورا

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, purchasing error and wishing that you would lose the way?
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and corruption among some of those who have been entrusted with divine scripture. Instead of adhering to its truthful teachings, they misuse their knowledge, engaging in actions that lead both themselves and others astray from the right path. The verse serves as a warning to be vigilant and discerning about false guidance, even when it appears to come from authoritative sources. It emphasizes the tragic irony that despite the privilege of receiving guidance, some twist it for personal gain or misguided purposes.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يشترون الضلالة ويريدون أن تضلوا السبيل

translation: And Allah is most knowing of your enemies; and sufficient is Allah as an ally, and sufficient is Allah as a helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah concerning the adversaries of the believers. It reassures the faithful that Allah is fully aware of those who oppose them and their intentions. The verse also serves to comfort and empower the believers, conveying that Allah alone is enough of a protector and supporter against any hostility they face. By repeating 'sufficient is Allah', it underscores the completeness and perfection of Allah's support, negating the need for believers to seek protection or assistance from any other source. This can inspire trust and reliance solely on divine support in all adversarial circumstances.
orig: والله أعلم بأعدائكم وكفى بالله وليا وكفى بالله نصيرا

translation: Among those who are Jews, there are some who distort words from their [proper] usages and say, 'We hear and disobey' and 'Hear but be not heard' and 'Ra'ina,' twisting their tongues and defaming the religion. And if they had said [instead], 'We hear and we obey,' and 'Hear,' and 'Look at us,' it would have been better for them, and more proper; but Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse addresses the behavior of certain individuals among the Jewish community who deliberately misinterpret and manipulate religious texts and directives. This misconduct includes misquoting or misrepresenting words and showing a disrespectful attitude towards religious authority, symbolized by their saying 'We hear and disobey.' The act of twisting their tongues and uttering disdainful remarks directly assaults the integrity of the divine religion. The verse underscores the consequences of such defiance and deliberate disbelief—divine curse and exclusion from faith—with only a small number continuing in genuine belief. The alternative, positive behaviors of compliance and respect towards divine commands are highlighted as yielding better outcomes both in moral alignment and in relation with God. Thus, the verse serves both as a criticism of hypocrisy and deceit in religious observance and a call towards sincerity and obedience.
orig: من الذين هادوا يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه ويقولون سمعنا وعصينا واسمع غير مسمع وراعنا ليا بألسنتهم وطعنا في الدين ولو أنهم قالوا سمعنا وأطعنا واسمع وانظرنا لكان خيرا لهم وأقوم ولكن لعنهم الله بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا

translation: O you who have been given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their heels, or curse them as We cursed the companions of the Sabbath; and the command of Allah is always executed.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning and call to the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) to accept the Quran, which confirms the truths already present in their own scriptures. The call to believe is urgent, with the consequence of not doing so being severe: the potential of physical or spiritual distortion and a curse like that which befell previous communities who disobeyed God, such as those who violated the Sabbath. The reference to the irreversible execution of God's command serves as a reminder of His absolute authority and the inevitability of His decrees.
orig: يا أيها الذين أوتوا الكتاب آمنوا بما نزلنا مصدقا لما معكم من قبل أن نطمس وجوها فنردها على أدبارها أو نلعنهم كما لعنا أصحاب السبت وكان أمر الله مفعولا

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has fabricated a tremendous sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of shirk, or associating partners with Allah, which is deemed an unforgivable sin if one dies without repenting from it. However, sins other than shirk can be forgiven if Allah wills. This establishes a clear hierarchy in the seriousness of offenses, directly linking forgiveness to the notion of divine will while underscoring the ultimate moral and theological error represented by idolatry or polytheism. The phrase 'fabricated a tremendous sin' highlights the act of shirk as not only a sin but also a deeply wrongful creation of falsehood against the unity of Allah.
orig: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ومن يشرك بالله فقد افترى إثما عظيما

translation: Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves? Nay, but Allah purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged even as much as a thread inside a date seed.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine prerogative in judging human purity and righteousness. It criticizes individuals who self-righteously claim moral and spiritual superiority. The reminder that ultimate judgment and absolution rest solely with Allah serves as a caution against the human tendency to self-aggrandizement and arrogance. The emphasis on Allah's fairness reassures that no one will be wronged under His judgment, depicting His infinite justice even in minimal matters.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم بل الله يزكي من يشاء ولا يظلمون فتيلا

translation: See how they fabricate lies against Allah, and it is sufficient as a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe wrongdoing associated with attributing falsehoods to God, emphasizing the gravity of such actions. By stating that it is a 'manifest sin,' the verse underscores the clarity and obviousness of the transgression, signaling that such behavior is not only wrong but evidently so. It serves as a stern warning against the misrepresentation or distortion of divine attributes or commands, illustrating the ethical and moral decay involved in lying about what God has decreed or who God is. This can serve as a caution to maintain integrity and truthfulness in matters of faith and spirituality.
orig: انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب وكفى به إثما مبينا

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in superstition and false deities, and they say to those who disbelieve, 'These are more rightly guided than those who believe.'
interpretation: This verse criticizes individuals who, despite having received divine guidance through the scriptures, choose to believe in and uphold baseless superstitions and false deities over true divine teachings. Their actions include misguided assertions that disbelievers are better guided than believers, illustrating a profound deviation from their spiritual obligations and a fundamental misunderstanding of the essence of their faith. The verse highlights the danger of hypocrisy and the ease with which individuals may stray from true faith despite possessing knowledge of the scriptures. It serves as a caution against the betrayal of one's spiritual teachings and the moral and spiritual corruption that can arise from such betrayal.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يؤمنون بالجبت والطاغوت ويقولون للذين كفروا هؤلاء أهدى من الذين آمنوا سبيلا

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and he whom Allah curses, you will not find for him any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of earning Allah's curse through disobedience and wrongful actions. It highlights the hopelessness and isolation that befalls those who are cursed by Allah; they are left without any support or assistance. The verse serves as a solemn warning to adhere to righteous conduct and avoid behaviors that could lead to divine disfavor.
orig: أولئك الذين لعنهم الله ومن يلعن الله فلن تجد له نصيرا

translation: Or do they have a share of the dominion? If so, they would not give people even the smallest bit.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency and selfishness inherent in the attitude of those who challenge divine revelations or authority, suggesting that if such individuals were to possess power or a portion of divine sovereignty, they would be miserly and unjust, failing to distribute even the smallest benefits or privileges fairly among people. It underscores the flawed nature of human governance when devoid of divine guidance and the misguided sense of entitlement that some individuals might harbor.
orig: أم لهم نصيب من الملك فإذا لا يؤتون الناس نقيرا

translation: Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them from His bounty? Indeed, We have given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom and bestowed upon them a great kingdom.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of envy among people when observing the blessings endowed by Allah upon others. It underscores the notion that the distributions of blessings, be it in knowledge, wealth, or power, are divine choices meant to test individuals in different ways. The specific mention of the family of Abraham, who were granted scripture, wisdom, and a significant kingdom, serves as an example of such divinely ordained favor. This verse serves as a reminder to cherish what one has been given and to understand that material and spiritual blessings are ultimately tests of character and faith, implicating that one should focus on their own divine journey rather than harboring jealousy towards others.
orig: أم يحسدون الناس على ما آتاهم الله من فضله فقد آتينا آل إبراهيم الكتاب والحكمة وآتيناهم ملكا عظيما

translation: Among them are some who believe in it, and some of them who turn away from it, and Hell is sufficient as a blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the diversity of human responses to divine guidance, indicating that while some individuals accept and believe in the truth when it is presented to them, others consciously choose to reject and turn away from it. The reference to Hell as sufficient as a blaze underscores the severe consequences awaiting those who persistently deny the truth and disregard the warnings. It serves as a stern reminder of the ultimate justice and the serious repercussions of one's choices regarding faith and disbelief.
orig: فمنهم من آمن به ومنهم من صد عنه وكفى بجهنم سعيرا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our signs, we will roast them in a fire. Every time their skins are cooked through, we will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences that await those who reject divine guidance, expressed through the metaphor of fire, symbolizing severe punishment. The continual replacement of skins represents an unending cycle of suffering, underlining the gravity and perpetuity of their punishment for disbelieving. The final phrases highlight God's absolute power and wisdom, affirming that the prescribed punishments are both a display of His sovereignty and a reflection of divine justice.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بآياتنا سوف نصليهم نارا كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها ليذوقوا العذاب إن الله كان عزيزا حكيما

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. They will have therein purified spouses, and We will admit them to a pleasant shade.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the rewards awaiting those who uphold faith in God and engage in virtuous actions. It portrays the Islamic concept of paradise as an eternal abode of bliss, characterized by beautiful gardens with rivers, companionship with purified spouses, and comforting shade, symbolizing complete serenity and satisfaction. It underscores the idea of divine justice and the ultimate fulfillment of spiritual and physical desires in the hereafter for the righteous.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سندخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا لهم فيها أزواج مطهرة وندخلهم ظلا ظليلا

translation: Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice. Indeed, Allah is ever, to you, an excellent adviser. Indeed, Allah is Hearing, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the paramount importance of ethical conduct and fairness in all dealings and judgements. It highlights the divine command to responsibly return whatever has been entrusted to an individual to its rightful owner, reflecting the value of trustworthiness in Islam. Furthermore, it stresses the necessity of just and unbiased decision-making when resolving disputes among people, aligning with the broader Islamic principles of justice. The reference to Allah as both Hearing and Seeing serves as a reminder that God is aware of all actions and intentions, underlining the spiritual and moral accountability in adhering to these commands. This admonition is not merely legal or social, but deeply ethical, aimed at cultivating integrity and equity in personal and communal relations.
orig: إن الله يأمركم أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها وإذا حكمتم بين الناس أن تحكموا بالعدل إن الله نعما يعظكم به إن الله كان سميعا بصيرا

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. And if you dispute over anything, refer it back to Allah and the Messenger, if you truly believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is better and more suitable for final determination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and unity within the Muslim community. It instructs believers to follow Allah, the Prophet Muhammad, and those who hold authority among them, thus establishing a clear hierarchy and path for governance and conflict resolution. The directive to revert matters back to Allah and His Messenger in cases of dispute underscores the need to root decisions in divine guidance and prophetic tradition, highlighting the central role of Islamic teachings in resolving conflicts. This not only preserves social harmony but also ensures that resolutions align with religious principles, which the verse suggests is the most benevolent and just approach, especially in the context of belief in the afterlife and divine accountability.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول وأولي الأمر منكم فإن تنازعتم في شيء فردوه إلى الله والرسول إن كنتم تؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا

translation: Have you not seen those who claim to have believed in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you? They wish to refer legislation to Taghut, while they were commanded to reject it, and Satan wishes to lead them far astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and inconsistency in the behavior of certain individuals who profess faith in divine revelations, including the messages sent to Prophet Muhammad and previous prophets, yet paradoxically seek judgment from sources that are fundamentally opposed to divine principles. 'Taghut' here refers to anything that exceeds its rightful limits, particularly in terms of authority and governance, often being idols, tyrants, or oppressive systems. The verse criticizes those who turn to such forbidden sources for judgment or resolution, despite being explicitly instructed against it. This act not only violates their religious commitments but also exposes them to the risk of severe deviation influenced by Satan, who aims to lead them away from the path of righteousness. The verse serves as a stern warning against compromising one’s faith by embracing unjust and corrupt forces, underlining the importance of steadfastness and integrity in adhering to true Islamic teachings.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يزعمون أنهم آمنوا بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك يريدون أن يتحاكموا إلى الطاغوت وقد أمروا أن يكفروا به ويريد الشيطان أن يضلهم ضلالا بعيدا

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,' you see the hypocrites turning away from you in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristic behavior of hypocrites in their response to the divine command and the invitation to adhere to spiritual and moral guidance. Their aversion and refusal to come forward when called upon to engage with the revelations of Allah and the teachings of the Prophet demonstrate their internal conflict and lack of genuine faith. This turning away signifies not just a physical reluctance but a deeper, spiritual resistance to truth and righteousness, indicative of the hypocrisy that distances them from the essence of true belief and moral rectitude.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا إلى ما أنزل الله وإلى الرسول رأيت المنافقين يصدون عنك صدودا

translation: So how will it be when disaster strikes them because of what their hands have sent forth, and then they come to you swearing by Allah, 'We intended nothing but good and reconciliation'?
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to evade responsibility and justify one's actions after facing the consequences of their own misdeeds. It underscores the insincere repentance that often follows when individuals confront the outcomes of their wrongful actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of genuine accountability and the need for sincere intentions in one’s actions. It criticizes the superficiality of merely verbal repentance that lacks true remorse or the commitment to change. Ultimately, it calls for a deeper self-reflection and honesty in one's dealings and relationships.
orig: فكيف إذا أصابتهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم ثم جاءوك يحلفون بالله إن أردنا إلا إحسانا وتوفيقا

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts, so turn away from them, admonish them, and say to them a profound word in themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, particularly in understanding the inner states and intentions of individuals. It advises the Prophet Muhammad to not only ignore those whose hearts are insincere, but also to engage them with meaningful, impact-oriented advice aiming to reach deep into their conscience. The guidance provided combines both detachment and proactive correction, suggesting a balanced approach in dealing with those whose commitment might be wavering or hidden. The ultimate goal implied is to encourage self-reflection and internal correction among such individuals.
orig: أولئك الذين يعلم الله ما في قلوبهم فأعرض عنهم وعظهم وقل لهم في أنفسهم قولا بليغا

translation: And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by permission of Allah. And if, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the pivotal role of messengers in guiding humanity according to divine decree, underscoring their authority and the necessity of obedience to them as a path to God's mercy. It highlights the profound mercy of Allah, accessible through repentance and seeking forgiveness, particularly facilitated through the mediation of a messenger. The reference to coming to the messenger and seeking forgiveness illustrates the therapeutic and transformative potential of admitting wrongs and actively seeking to rectify them through divine guidance, reinforcing the themes of repentance and divine compassion.
orig: وما أرسلنا من رسول إلا ليطاع بإذن الله ولو أنهم إذ ظلموا أنفسهم جاءوك فاستغفروا الله واستغفر لهم الرسول لوجدوا الله توابا رحيما

translation: No, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you [Muhammad] judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided, and submit in [full, willing] submission.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the critical role of the prophet Muhammad in settling disputes among his followers as a test of their faith. True belief is characterized not only by accepting the prophet's judgment but also by embracing his decisions without any internal resistance, showing complete surrender to God's guidance as delivered through Muhammad. The verse underscores the integration of external submission to religious authority with internal acceptance, marking the coherence of belief and emotional acceptance as foundational to faith.
orig: فلا وربك لا يؤمنون حتى يحكموك فيما شجر بينهم ثم لا يجدوا في أنفسهم حرجا مما قضيت ويسلموا تسليما

translation: And if We had decreed upon them, 'Kill yourselves or leave your homes,' they would not have done it, except for a few of them. But if they had done what they were advised, it would have been better for them and a firmer position [for them in faith].
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine testing and the human response to challenging decrees. It highlights the hypothetical extremes to which obedience might be pushed and emphasizes that true faith is not merely about accepting easy ordinances but also about enduring hardship when it is commanded. This proves the sincerity of one’s faith and obedience to God. The verse also suggests that adherence to God’s commandments, regardless of their difficulty, not only solidifies one's faith but also leads to better outcomes both in this life and the hereafter.
orig: ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم أو اخرجوا من دياركم ما فعلوه إلا قليل منهم ولو أنهم فعلوا ما يوعظون به لكان خيرا لهم وأشد تثبيتا

translation: And indeed, We will give them a great reward from Us.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the promise of a significant and divine reward for those who fulfil certain conditions or meet specific criteria laid out by God. It speaks to the benevolence and generosity of God in rewarding faithfulness and righteous actions. The phrase 'from Us' highlights that the reward originates from the divine, underscoring its inestimable value and purity, unlike worldly gains which might be tarnished by imperfections. This divine reward is often understood in the context of the hereafter, where the true and ultimate compensation for earthly deeds will be granted. It reassures believers of the intrinsic value of their perseverance and moral conduct in accordance with God's commands, encouraging them to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: وإذا لآتيناهم من لدنا أجرا عظيما

translation: And We guided them to a straight path
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine guidance provided by God, leading individuals towards righteousness and moral rectitude, represented by 'the straight path'. It emphasizes the role of divine intervention in directing believers away from misguidance and towards a life of virtue and integrity. The path symbolizes both a spiritual journey and a moral code to adhere to, aiming for personal development and adherence to divine will.
orig: ولهديناهم صراطا مستقيما

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the value and reward of obedience to Allah and His Messenger. It illustrates that those who live in accordance with divine guidance are promised companionship in the afterlife with the most exalted groups of people: prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and the righteous. This companionship is not only a reward but also a reflection of their spiritual status and the high regard in which they are held by Allah. The reference to these esteemed groups serves as an inspiration for the believers to strive for righteousness and steadfastness in their faith, aiming to emulate such noble qualities in their own lives.
orig: ومن يطع الله والرسول فأولئك مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين وحسن أولئك رفيقا

translation: That is the grace from Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Knower.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless grace and blessings bestowed by Allah, emphasizing that Allah's knowledge is complete and encompasses everything. It suggests that divine grace is a gift independent of human actions, underscoring the omniscience of Allah, who is fully aware of all circumstances and intentions. The phrase accentuates reliance on Allah's wisdom and serves as a reminder of the profound understanding and awareness of Allah in every aspect of existence.
orig: ذلك الفضل من الله وكفى بالله عليما

translation: O you who have believed, take your precaution and either go forth in groups or go forth all together.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of vigilance and preparedness against potential threats or adversities. It calls believers to act wisely by securing their safety and stresses unity and collective action. Whether moving in smaller, more manageable groups or as a whole community, the emphasis is on the strategic and collaborative approach to dealing with challenges.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا خذوا حذركم فانفروا ثبات أو انفروا جميعا

translation: And indeed, among you is he who would linger behind; and if a disaster were to strike you, he would say, 'Allah has favored me in that I was not present with them.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the attitude of hypocrisy and the lack of genuine commitment among some individuals within the community. It highlights the behavior of those who hesitate to participate in collective obligations and efforts, particularly those involving risk or sacrifice. When others face difficulties or calamities, this type of person feels relief and even fortunate for not being involved, rather than feeling empathy or solidarity. The verse serves as a critique of self-centered attitudes and a call for sincere and supportive community involvement.
orig: وإن منكم لمن ليبطئن فإن أصابتكم مصيبة قال قد أنعم الله علي إذ لم أكن معهم شهيدا

translation: And if a bounty from Allah touches you, they will surely say as if there was no affection between you and them, 'Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I could have achieved a great success.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the fickleness and hypocrisy of human nature, particularly in relation to the fair-weather friends who show envy or regret when seeing others receive Allah’s blessings. It highlights the importance of sincerity in relationships and the danger of harboring selfish desires that surface when witnessing the success of others. The verse serves as a caution against the superficial loyalty which shifts based on personal gains, urging believers to maintain steadfastness and unity in the face of divine tests and blessings.
orig: ولئن أصابكم فضل من الله ليقولن كأن لم تكن بينكم وبينه مودة يا ليتني كنت معهم فأفوز فوزا عظيما

translation: Let those fight in the cause of Allah who sell the life of this world for the hereafter. And whoever fights in the cause of Allah, and is killed or achieves victory, We will grant him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving for spiritual and eternal gains over temporal, worldly ones. It particularly addresses those believers who are willing to forego the comforts or attachments of this life in pursuit of what lies in the hereafter, which is viewed in Islamic teachings as lasting and more significant. The mention of fighting in the cause of Allah symbolizes a struggle or jihad, primarily understood as fighting against evil, injustice, and oppression to establish peace and divine order. The reward mentioned for those who are killed or emerge victorious underscores the high regard Islam holds for sacrifices made in the name of faith, promising them divine compensation and eternal contentment, which is immeasurably greater than any worldly success or material gain.
orig: فليقاتل في سبيل الله الذين يشرون الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة ومن يقاتل في سبيل الله فيقتل أو يغلب فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the cause of Allah and [for] the oppressed among men, women, and children who say, 'Our Lord, take us out of this city of oppressive people and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper'?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral and religious duty of Muslims to stand up and fight against oppression, specifically in defense of vulnerable groups who are unjustly treated. It underscores the idea of divine support and guidance for those who strive to combat injustice, reaffirming the importance of seeking God's assistance in overcoming oppressive situations. The plea of the oppressed for a protector and a helper reflects their dependence on divine intervention to bring about justice and relief from persecution.
orig: وما لكم لا تقاتلون في سبيل الله والمستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان الذين يقولون ربنا أخرجنا من هذه القرية الظالم أهلها واجعل لنا من لدنك وليا واجعل لنا من لدنك نصيرا

translation: Those who believe fight in the way of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the way of Taghut (false deities). So fight against the allies of Satan. Indeed, the plot of Satan is weak.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual and moral dichotomy between those who align themselves with divine guidance and those who follow paths of falsehood and opposition to divine will. The term 'Taghut' represents any force or entity that exceeds its rightful bounds, often associated with tyranny or idolatry. Believers are called to actively resist and battle against the forces and influence of evil, represented here as the 'allies of Satan.' The assurance that 'the plot of Satan is weak' serves to remind believers of the inherent fragility of malevolent schemes when faced with the steadfastness of faith and righteous action. It is a call to confidence and resilience in the spiritual battle between good and evil, reinforcing the idea that truth and virtue, though challenged, are ultimately supported by the strength of divine assistance.
orig: الذين آمنوا يقاتلون في سبيل الله والذين كفروا يقاتلون في سبيل الطاغوت فقاتلوا أولياء الشيطان إن كيد الشيطان كان ضعيفا

translation: Have you not seen those who were told to restrain their hands, establish the prayer, and give Zakat? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a group of them feared people as they should fear Allah or even more. They said, 'Our Lord, why have You decreed upon us fighting? Would You not grant us respite until a near term?' Say, 'The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah; and you will not be wronged, [even] as much as a thread [inside a date seed].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrasts in human behavior and faith under different circumstances. Initially compliant in non-confrontational acts of worship, some individuals display fear and reluctance when faced with the greater challenge of combat, commanded by God. Their fear of people surpassing their fear of God is pointed out as an inconsistency. The divine response emphasizes the transitory nature of worldly life and assures that the real and lasting rewards are for those who piety governs in the Hereafter. The reassurance that the faithful will not be wronged, even minimally, underscores God's absolute justice and the moral imperative to stand firm in faith regardless of the trials faced.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين قيل لهم كفوا أيديكم وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فلما كتب عليهم القتال إذا فريق منهم يخشون الناس كخشية الله أو أشد خشية وقالوا ربنا لم كتبت علينا القتال لولا أخرتنا إلى أجل قريب قل متاع الدنيا قليل والآخرة خير لمن اتقى ولا تظلمون فتيلا

translation: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in fortified towers. And if good befalls them, they say, 'This is from Allah'; and if evil befalls them, they say, 'This is from you.' Say, 'All is from Allah.' But what is [the matter] with these people, that they are scarcely able to understand a statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate and inevitable nature of death, which transcends all human efforts to escape or fortify against it, illustrating human vulnerability and the futility of seeking absolute security. It also highlights the varying human responses to circumstances based on their perception of good or ill fortune, illustrating a deeper theological discourse about understanding everything as deriving from the divine will of Allah. The question posed at the end of the verse points to a spiritual and cognitive disconnect people may have in recognizing and accepting the comprehensive dominion and wisdom of Allah in all aspects of life, encouraging a more profound reflection on faith and submission to divine will.
orig: أينما تكونوا يدرككم الموت ولو كنتم في بروج مشيدة وإن تصبهم حسنة يقولوا هذه من عند الله وإن تصبهم سيئة يقولوا هذه من عندك قل كل من عند الله فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا

translation: Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself. And We have sent you to the people as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concepts of personal responsibility and divine attribution in the context of events that occur in one’s life. It underlines that all the good and blessings one receives are purely from the grace and mercy of Allah, highlighting the generosity and benevolence of God towards humanity. Conversely, when one faces hardships or misfortunes, these are often due to one's own actions, decisions, or negligence, suggesting a direct consequence of one's deeds. Furthermore, the verse reaffirms the prophetic mission of Muhammad as a messenger sent to guide mankind, with Allah alone as the ultimate witness to this truth. This serves both as a reminder of the accountability of the individual for their choices and as an affirmation of the role of divine guidance through the prophet in navigating the moral and spiritual challenges of life.
orig: ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك وأرسلناك للناس رسولا وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah; and whoever turns away, then We have not sent you as a guardian over them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to the Prophet Muhammad, which is equated with obedience to Allah Himself. It underscores the role of the Prophet as a conveyor of divine guidance rather than a controller of people's faith or actions. The statement that Muhammad is not sent as a 'guardian' over the disbelievers implies that his responsibility is to deliver the message, not to enforce belief or compliance. This reflects the principle of individual accountability in faith and reiterates the freedom of choice in Islam, where guidance is offered, but the choice to accept it rests with each individual.
orig: من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله ومن تولى فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا

translation: And they say, 'We obey,' but when they leave your presence, a group of them secretly conspires differently from what you say. And Allah records what they conceal. So turn away from them and trust in Allah. And Allah is sufficient as a Trustee.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and deceitful behavior of some individuals who outwardly express obedience and agreement but secretly hold and plot contrary intentions. It underscores God's omniscience in that He is aware of all hidden thoughts and conspiracies, suggesting that deceptive actions cannot escape divine scrutiny. The verse encourages turning away from such hypocritical individuals and placing trust solely in God, emphasizing His sufficiency as a protector and advocate for the righteous. This guidance invites believers to focus on sincerity in their actions and rely on God's justice rather than being perturbed by the duplicity of others.
orig: ويقولون طاعة فإذا برزوا من عندك بيت طائفة منهم غير الذي تقول والله يكتب ما يبيتون فأعرض عنهم وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an? If it had been from other than Allah, they would have found within it much contradiction.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of contemplation and understanding of the Qur'an, asserting its divine origin and consistency. It challenges skeptics by stating that if the Qur'an were authored by anyone other than God, there would be inconsistencies and contradictions within its text. The absence of such contradictions is presented as proof of its divine origin, encouraging believers and critics alike to deeply engage with and reflect on its messages.
orig: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

translation: And when there comes to them information about [public] security or fear, they spread it around. If only they had referred it back to the Messenger or to those of authority among them, those who [can] draw correct conclusions from it would have known it. But had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of responsible communication and verification in a community, especially concerning sensitive information related to security or fear. It criticizes the hastiness in spreading such news without proper discernment or consultation with knowledgeable authorities. The verse promotes the principle of returning matters to those who have expertise or official responsibility, highlighting that such an approach leads to sound judgments and prevents the spread of misinformation. It also emphasizes the pivotal role of divine grace and mercy in guiding human actions and protecting individuals from the influence of malevolent forces like Satan.
orig: وإذا جاءهم أمر من الأمن أو الخوف أذاعوا به ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لاتبعتم الشيطان إلا قليلا

translation: So fight in the way of Allah; you are not tasked except with yourself. And urge the believers on, perhaps Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve. And Allah is more severe in assault and more severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual duty of striving (Qital) for God's cause, focusing on one's own commitment without bearing the burden of others' responsibilities. It encourages motivating fellow believers to strengthen the community's resolve. The suggestion that Allah might restrain the aggressors serves as a reassurance of divine support against those who oppose the faith. The mention of Allah's unparalleled might and punitive capabilities serves both as a warning to the disbelievers and a comfort to the believers, affirming that ultimate justice and retribution are within God's sovereign power.
orig: فقاتل في سبيل الله لا تكلف إلا نفسك وحرض المؤمنين عسى الله أن يكف بأس الذين كفروا والله أشد بأسا وأشد تنكيلا

translation: Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share in it; and whoever intercedes for an evil cause will have a portion from it. And Allah is over all things a Maintainer.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral responsibility associated with intercession. Individuals who advocate or intervene on behalf of righteous deeds will partake in the merits and rewards of those deeds. Conversely, those who support or plead for wrongful acts will similarly share in the consequences and burdens of those acts. It also underscores the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah, affirming that He is aware of all matters and maintains justice, observing everyone’s actions and intents.
orig: من يشفع شفاعة حسنة يكن له نصيب منها ومن يشفع شفاعة سيئة يكن له كفل منها وكان الله على كل شيء مقيتا

translation: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with what is better than it or return it; indeed, Allah is ever an Accountant over everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responding to kindness and good manners with even greater kindness, or at least with the same level of courtesy. It highlights the principle of reciprocity and the value of elevating moral interactions between individuals. By instructing believers to improve upon or match a greeting, it fosters a culture of respect, graciousness, and positive communication. The mention of Allah being 'an Accountant over everything' serves as a reminder that all actions, no matter how small, are noted and accountable to God, underpinning the importance of ethical conduct in all interactions.
orig: وإذا حييتم بتحية فحيوا بأحسن منها أو ردوها إن الله كان على كل شيء حسيبا

translation: Allah, there is no deity except Him, will surely gather you for [the Day of] Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah, reiterating the core Islamic belief in monotheism. It assures believers of the inevitable Day of Resurrection, a fundamental aspect of Islamic eschatology, where all individuals will be gathered for judgment. The rhetorical question underscores the absolute truthfulness and trustworthiness of Allah's words, reinforcing the importance of relying on divine revelation for guidance and truth.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه ومن أصدق من الله حديثا

translation: So why are there two groups among you regarding the hypocrites, when Allah has cast them back for what they have earned? Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has led astray? And he whom Allah leads astray, you will not find for him a way.
interpretation: This verse addresses the internal divisions among believers concerning their treatment of hypocrites. It criticizes the believers who may feel sympathetic or inclined to defend the hypocrites, reminding them that these individuals have already been reprimanded by Allah due to their deeds. The verse reinforces the notion of divine justice — that the misguidance of the hypocrites is a result of their own actions and a divine decree, emphasizing that human efforts to guide those whom Allah has decided to mislead are ultimately futile.
