It serves as a reminder of Allah’s sovereignty and the boundaries of human influence in matters of divine will regarding guidance and misguidance.
orig: فما لكم في المنافقين فئتين والله أركسهم بما كسبوا أتريدون أن تهدوا من أضل الله ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: They wish that you should disbelieve as they disbelieve, so that you would be alike. Therefore, do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the way of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from among them any ally or helper.
interpretation: This verse addresses the relationship between believers and non-believers who are hostile towards the faith, indicating strict boundaries and actions to be taken against those who not only refuse to accept the faith but also wish harm upon the believers. The verse emphasizes the importance of loyalty and aligning with those who support one's faith journey, while advocating for a firm stance against those who pose a threat to the unity and safety of the believing community. It underscores the necessity of spiritual and moral integrity, urging believers to distance themselves from those who reject and actively oppose the divine path.
orig: ودوا لو تكفرون كما كفروا فتكونون سواء فلا تتخذوا منهم أولياء حتى يهاجروا في سبيل الله فإن تولوا فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث وجدتموهم ولا تتخذوا منهم وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: Except for those who seek refuge with a people between whom and you there is a covenant, or who come to you because their hearts are constrained from fighting you or fighting their own people. And if Allah had willed, He could have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. So if they withdraw from you and do not fight you, and offer you peace, then Allah has not made for you a cause [to fight] against them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principles of peace and non-aggression in Islam, particularly in the context of inter-group relations. It underscores the moral obligation to respect treaties and covenants and shows compassion towards those who, despite political or social pressures, choose not to engage in conflict due to moral or personal constraints. The directive from Allah to refrain from aggression against those who seek peace highlights the value placed on peaceful coexistence and the resolution of conflicts through non-violent means.
orig: إلا الذين يصلون إلى قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق أو جاءوكم حصرت صدورهم أن يقاتلوكم أو يقاتلوا قومهم ولو شاء الله لسلطهم عليكم فلقاتلوكم فإن اعتزلوكم فلم يقاتلوكم وألقوا إليكم السلم فما جعل الله لكم عليهم سبيلا

translation: You will find others who wish to ensure your safety and that of their people. Every time they are returned to temptation, they plunge into it. If they do not stay away from you, offer peace to you, and restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them. And those, We have given you clear authority over them.
interpretation: This verse discusses the complexities of alliances and confrontations involving groups with divided loyalties, particularly in a context of ongoing conflict or temptation. It highlights the necessity of discerning genuine intentions and ensuring one's own community's safety. The directive to act decisively against those who fail to demonstrate peaceable and cooperative intentions reflects a principle of self-preservation and justice, granted under divine mandate, to maintain order and protect the community from instability and betrayal.
orig: ستجدون آخرين يريدون أن يأمنوكم ويأمنوا قومهم كل ما ردوا إلى الفتنة أركسوا فيها فإن لم يعتزلوكم ويلقوا إليكم السلم ويكفوا أيديهم فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث ثقفتموهم وأولئكم جعلنا لكم عليهم سلطانا مبينا

translation: It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. Whoever kills a believer by mistake must free a believing slave and pay compensation to the family of the deceased unless they forgo it. If the victim is from a people who are your enemies and he was a believer, then [only] the freeing of a believing slave [is required]. If he belonged to a people with whom you have a treaty, then compensation must be paid to his family, and a believing slave must be freed. And if one cannot find [a slave to free], then [the killer must] fast two consecutive months as repentance to Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the sanctity of life in Islam and the serious consequences of taking a life, even unintentionally. It lays out a legal and moral framework for retribution and expiation, emphasizing accountability, restitution, and forgiveness. The stipulation of freeing a slave or fasting represents not only a means to expiate the guilt but also serves as a significant spiritual cleansing and personal transformation towards repentance. The differentiation in the directive based on the communal relationship between the offender and the victim highlights the influence of socio-political contexts on legal rulings. Ultimately, the verse affirms the omniscience and wisdom of Allah in guiding human interactions and promoting justice, mercy, and social harmony.
orig: وما كان لمؤمن أن يقتل مؤمنا إلا خطأ ومن قتل مؤمنا خطأ فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة ودية مسلمة إلى أهله إلا أن يصدقوا فإن كان من قوم عدو لكم وهو مؤمن فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة وإن كان من قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق فدية مسلمة إلى أهله وتحرير رقبة مؤمنة فمن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين توبة من الله وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and Allah has become angry with him and has cursed him and prepared for him a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of deliberately taking the life of a believer, equating such an action to the worst kind of transgression in Islamic teachings. The eternal abode in Hell, alongside the explicit anger, curse, and the prepared great punishment from Allah, underlines divine condemnation and the spiritual as well as moral decay inherent in committing such a sin. It serves as a stern warning against the gravity of murder within the Islamic ethical framework, illustrating that such acts irreparably sever one's relationship with the divine and the community.
orig: ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها وغضب الله عليه ولعنه وأعد له عذابا عظيما

translation: O you who have believed, when you go forth [to fight] in the cause of Allah, investigate; and do not say to one who gives you [a greeting of] peace, 'You are not a believer,' seeking the perishable goods of worldly life; for with Allah are much better gains. Before that, you also had been in such condition, but Allah bestowed His favor on you, so investigate. Indeed, Allah is ever with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fair and just conduct during conflict, particularly warning against unjust assumptions and judgments about others' faith based on superficial assessments. It instructs believers to prioritize ethical integrity and spiritual values over worldly gains. The verse also highlights God's mercy and the transformation of believers from past ignorance to awareness through divine guidance, urging them to exercise caution and thorough verification in their interactions. It ultimately underscores that God is fully aware of all actions, emphasizing accountability and the need for conscious, principled behavior.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ضربتم في سبيل الله فتبينوا ولا تقولوا لمن ألقى إليكم السلام لست مؤمنا تبتغون عرض الحياة الدنيا فعند الله مغانم كثيرة كذلك كنتم من قبل فمن الله عليكم فتبينوا إن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: Not equal are those believers remaining [at home]—other than the disabled—and the mujahideen, [who strive and fight] in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred the mujahideen through their wealth and their lives over those who remain [behind] by degrees. And to all Allah has promised the best [reward]. But Allah has preferred the mujahideen over those who remain behind with a great reward.
interpretation: This verse underscores the distinction in the eyes of Allah between believers who engage actively in struggle for the cause of Allah (mujahideen) and those who don't, albeit with an exemption for those unable to participate due to disabilities. It emphasizes that spiritual and moral merit, as well as the rewards from Allah, are greater for those who dedicate their wealth and their lives more directly to the pursuit of Islamic principles. The verse not only highlights the higher esteem and rewards allotted to the mujahideen but also reassures all believers of a promised reward, stressing the inclusive mercy of Allah while simultaneously encouraging active engagement in righteous struggle to attain a higher spiritual station.
orig: لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين غير أولي الضرر والمجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم فضل الله المجاهدين بأموالهم وأنفسهم على القاعدين درجة وكلا وعد الله الحسنى وفضل الله المجاهدين على القاعدين أجرا عظيما

translation: Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the depth of God's compassion and generosity. It suggests that believers can ascend through various degrees of spiritual and moral elevation, which are ultimately bestowed by God's grace. The mention of forgiveness and mercy highlights that despite human shortcomings, God's innate qualities include being forgiving and merciful, offering hope and a path to redemption for believers. This further reinforces the concept of an ever-compassionate God who is always ready to embrace and uplift the faithful, encouraging them to strive for better in the assurance of His benevolent nature.
orig: درجات منه ومغفرة ورحمة وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: Indeed, those whom the angels take [in death] while wronging themselves - the angels will say, 'In what [condition] were you?' They will say, 'We were oppressed in the land.' The angels will say, 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious enough for you to emigrate therein?' For those, their refuge will be Hell - and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability of individuals in situations where they have the option to make choices. It criticizes those who justify their wrong actions by claiming oppression or victimhood, yet they had the opportunity to emigrate or change their environment. The verse challenges the complacency in enduring injustice when there is a possibility for change, and it warns of severe consequences in the hereafter for failing to take initiative for one's own moral and spiritual liberation. It underlines the broadness of God's earth as a field of opportunities to seek justice and practice faith freely, highlighting that remaining in a compromising situation when alternatives exist is not justifiable.
orig: إن الذين توفاهم الملائكة ظالمي أنفسهم قالوا فيم كنتم قالوا كنا مستضعفين في الأرض قالوا ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها فأولئك مأواهم جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Except for the oppressed among men, women, and children who cannot devise a plan nor can find a way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the compassion and understanding of the divine towards those who are genuinely powerless and oppressed. It acknowledges the difficult circumstances of certain individuals—men, women, and children—who are incapacitated by their societal or physical limitations, rendering them unable to change their situation or escape their plight. The verse serves as a reminder of the responsibility of the more fortunate to recognize and alleviate the struggles of the less fortunate, emphasizing the importance of understanding, empathy, and active support towards those who are most vulnerable.
orig: إلا المستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان لا يستطيعون حيلة ولا يهتدون سبيلا

translation: So those, Allah may pardon them, and Allah is ever Pardoning, Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's boundless mercy and readiness to forgive. It suggests that even those who have erred have hope for forgiveness if they turn back to Allah. The attributes of Allah as 'Pardoning' and 'Forgiving' emphasize that divine mercy is not just occasional but a fundamental aspect of His nature, encouraging believers to seek forgiveness with hope and faith.
orig: فأولئك عسى الله أن يعفو عنهم وكان الله عفوا غفورا

translation: And whoever emigrates for the sake of Allah will find on the earth many havens and abundance, and whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become incumbent upon Allah. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and material rewards awaiting those who forsake their homes in pursuit of defending or promoting their faith. Emigration, in this context, is portrayed as a sacrificial act of deep faith that brings one closer to divine grace and mercy. The reference to 'finding many havens and abundance' on earth suggests that such a journey will not only lead to spiritual gains but also open up new opportunities and blessings in this life. The latter part of the verse reassures believers that if death meets them before reaching their goal, their effort is still recognized and rewarded by Allah, underlining His forgiving and merciful nature. This encapsulates the immense value and respect Islam places on the intent and efforts of its followers, encouraging them through both spiritual contentment and tangible support.
orig: ومن يهاجر في سبيل الله يجد في الأرض مراغما كثيرا وسعة ومن يخرج من بيته مهاجرا إلى الله ورسوله ثم يدركه الموت فقد وقع أجره على الله وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And when you travel through the land, there is no sin upon you if you shorten your prayers, if you fear that the disbelievers may put you in trial. Indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the flexibility and practicality of Islamic practices to accommodate the believers' circumstances, especially during travel or in times of insecurity and threat from hostile forces. It underscores the merciful aspect of Islamic law, which prioritizes the safety and well-being of individuals over strict ritual adherence when facing genuine threats. The reference to disbelievers as a 'clear enemy' contextualizes the concession, highlighting that this allowance is particularly relevant in situations of conflict or danger posed by those who oppose the faith.
orig: وإذا ضربتم في الأرض فليس عليكم جناح أن تقصروا من الصلاة إن خفتم أن يفتنكم الذين كفروا إن الكافرين كانوا لكم عدوا مبينا

translation: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you and take their arms. Then when they prostrate, let them be behind you and let another group come who have not prayed and let them pray with you and take care and their arms. Those who disbelieve would wish you to neglect your weapons and belongings so they could attack you in a single assault. And there is no sin on you if you have a hurt from rain or are ill, to lay down your arms, but take precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims on maintaining vigilance and security during times of conflict, even during prayer. It underscores the importance of communal prayer while also acknowledging the practical need to remain guarded against potential threats. The verse illustrates a balance between spiritual duties and practical security measures, suggesting that neglecting either could lead to detrimental consequences. Additionally, it emphasizes that in extraordinary circumstances, such as illness or adverse weather, concessions are allowed, highlighting the flexibility and compassion within Islamic law. The reference to a humiliating punishment for disbelievers serves as a stern warning against those who intend harm towards Muslims, reinforcing the theme of divine justice.
orig: وإذا كنت فيهم فأقمت لهم الصلاة فلتقم طائفة منهم معك وليأخذوا أسلحتهم فإذا سجدوا فليكونوا من ورائكم ولتأت طائفة أخرى لم يصلوا فليصلوا معك وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم ود الذين كفروا لو تغفلون عن أسلحتكم وأمتعتكم فيميلون عليكم ميلة واحدة ولا جناح عليكم إن كان بكم أذى من مطر أو كنتم مرضى أن تضعوا أسلحتكم وخذوا حذركم إن الله أعد للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah while standing, sitting, or [lying] on your sides. But once you are settled, then establish the prayer, for prayer is indeed a timed decree upon the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of constant remembrance of Allah, regardless of one's physical state, illustrating that one's connection with the Divine should not be limited to formal acts of worship such as prayer. It encourages a continuous, pervasive awareness of God throughout daily life. The verse also reinforces the obligation of prayer as a structured and scheduled duty for believers, highlighting it as a foundation of spiritual discipline and engagement with God.
orig: فإذا قضيتم الصلاة فاذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم فإذا اطمأننتم فأقيموا الصلاة إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا

translation: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy; if you are suffering pains, so are they, but you hope from Allah what they do not hope, and Allah is All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of resilience and perseverance in the face of adversity, particularly during conflicts. It acknowledges the shared human experience of pain and suffering, but highlights the distinct advantage of the believers: their hope and trust in Allah's support and wisdom, which their adversaries lack. This hope rooted in faith is portrayed as a strategic and psychological strength, reinforcing that the believers' endurance is supported by divine insight and foresight. Thus, believers are encouraged to remain steadfast and maintain their efforts in the struggle, motivated by their unique spiritual insight and the anticipation of divine justice and assistance.
orig: ولا تهنوا في ابتغاء القوم إن تكونوا تألمون فإنهم يألمون كما تألمون وترجون من الله ما لا يرجون وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility entrusted to the recipient of divine revelation, which is to exercise judgment among people based on the guidance provided by God. The criteria for judgment should align with divine principles, aiming to facilitate justice and fairness. Additionally, the verse advises the recipient to avoid siding with or supporting those who are deceitful or betray trust, highlighting the importance of integrity in leadership and judgement.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق لتحكم بين الناس بما أراك الله ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما

translation: And seek forgiveness from Allah; indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness for one's sins and mistakes, highlighting Allah's infinite mercy and compassion. It reassures believers that no matter the severity of the transgression, Allah's capacity for forgiveness is greater, encouraging them to turn back to Him in repentance and have hope in His mercy.
orig: واستغفر الله إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love anyone who is treacherous and sinful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of moral integrity and the consequences of self-deception. It discourages advocating for those who knowingly engage in wrongdoing, underlining that such behaviors are detestable to Allah. The warning against treachery and sin serves as a reminder of the divine expectation for humans to embody honesty and righteousness in their actions and relationships.
orig: ولا تجادل عن الذين يختانون أنفسهم إن الله لا يحب من كان خوانا أثيما

translation: They hide from people but not from Allah, and He is with them when they plot by night, saying things He does not approve of. And Allah completely encompasses what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah, highlighting the futility of attempting to conceal one's actions from Him. It suggests that human efforts to disguise their wrongful actions from others are in vain, as Allah is always aware of every deed and intention, regardless of human perception. The inclusion of nocturnal plotting underscores the theme of secrecy and the deliberate avoidance of moral behaviors that are pleasing to Allah. Ultimately, the verse serves as a reminder of Allah's encompassing knowledge and presence, advocating for sincerity and transparency in one's actions and intentions.
orig: يستخفون من الناس ولا يستخفون من الله وهو معهم إذ يبيتون ما لا يرضى من القول وكان الله بما يعملون محيطا

translation: There you are, those who argued on their behalf in this worldly life; but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their advocate?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of defending wrongful actions or individuals for personal or worldly gains, highlighting that such defenses will hold no value in the hereafter. On the Day of Judgment, no one can intercede or argue against Allah's decree, underscoring the absolute accountability and justice of God. It serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly allegiances compared to the eternal judgment of the hereafter.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء جادلتم عنهم في الحياة الدنيا فمن يجادل الله عنهم يوم القيامة أم من يكون عليهم وكيلا

translation: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards His creations. It underscores the principle that no matter the extent of sin or self-inflicted injustice, if one sincerely repents and seeks forgiveness from Allah, He is always ready to forgive and extend His mercy. This teaches that hope and redemption are always available, thus encouraging believers to return to the right path without despairing over their missteps.
orig: ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And whoever earns sin, he earns it only against himself, and Allah is All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability for one's actions, specifically in the context of committing sins. It suggests that the consequences of sinning are borne by the individual alone, highlighting the principles of justice and responsibility in Islamic ethics. Additionally, the mention of Allah being 'All-Knowing' and 'Wise' underlines the divine omniscience and wisdom, indicating that God’s judgments and the moral order of the universe are perfectly informed and executed.
orig: ومن يكسب إثما فإنما يكسبه على نفسه وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever commits a sin or a crime, then blames it on an innocent person, has indeed taken upon himself a manifest slander and a clear sin.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of false accusations and the moral burden it places on the accuser. It highlights the dual wrongdoing involved: committing an initial sin or crime, and then exacerbating it by wrongly assigning the blame to someone who is innocent. This act is described not only as unethical but also as a clear, undeniable sin in the eyes of God. The verse serves as a stern warning against the manipulation of truth and the unjust treatment of others, emphasizing accountability and the ethical imperative to own up to one's actions.
orig: ومن يكسب خطيئة أو إثما ثم يرم به بريئا فقد احتمل بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: And if not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, a group among them would have intended to mislead you, but they do not mislead except themselves, and they will not harm you in anything. And Allah has revealed to you the Book and Wisdom, and taught you what you did not know, and great is the grace of Allah upon you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the protective and guiding role of divine grace and mercy in shielding individuals from the ill intentions and deceit of others. It suggests that those who attempt to mislead are ultimately only deceiving themselves and cannot inflect true harm on the one who is under divine protection. The verse also highlights the profound blessings bestowed upon a person through divine revelation, encompassing sacred knowledge and wisdom that lead to a deeper understanding and spiritual growth. It underscores the magnitude of Allah’s grace in elevating an individual's status and knowledge beyond ordinary human capacity.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته لهمت طائفة منهم أن يضلوك وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يضرونك من شيء وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما

translation: There is no good in much of their private conversations unless someone urges charity, or that which is right, or conciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah, then We will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of positive and meaningful communications among people. It criticizes idle or harmful talk while promoting discussions aimed at charitable deeds, promoting ethical behavior, or reconciling differences among individuals. The encouragement to perform these virtuous acts is further enforced by the promise of a significant reward from Allah, highlighting that actions borne out of genuine intent to seek God's approval are highly valued. This underscores the ethical framework within which Muslims are urged to operate, promoting a society based on benevolence, moral rectitude, and harmony among its members.
orig: لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضات الله فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him, and follows a path other than that of the believers, We will entrust him to what he has turned to and lead him into Hell, and what an evil destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity and adherence to the prophetic teachings after the truth has been made clear. It warns against deviation from the established path of the believers, highlighting the severe consequences of choosing to follow paths that diverge from divine guidance. The reference to 'Hell' as a destination for those who oppose the Messenger and deviate from the community underscores the spiritual peril of such actions. This serves as a strong deterrent against dissent and promotes conformity to the collective wisdom and practices of the faithful, reinforcing the value of communal integrity in maintaining the purity of faith.
orig: ومن يشاقق الرسول من بعد ما تبين له الهدى ويتبع غير سبيل المؤمنين نوله ما تولى ونصله جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of shirk, or associating partners with Allah, which is considered the most severe and unforgivable sin if one dies without repenting from it. It highlights the uniqueness and singularity of Allah and underscores that attributing divinity or partnership to any other entity is a profound error. The verse also illustrates Allah's vast mercy, as He may forgive all other sins depending on His divine will and the repentance of the individual. Thus, the verse draws a clear line between the absolute prohibition of shirk and the potential for forgiveness for other sins, establishing a framework of both warning and hope.
orig: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ومن يشرك بالله فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, they invoke none other than female deities, and they invoke none but a rebellious devil.
interpretation: This verse highlights the folly of idolatry, showing that those who worship idols are essentially invoking beings with no divine power or authority. The reference to female deities underscores the cultural perceptions of the time regarding femininity and divinity, critiquing the arbitrariness of idol worship. Additionally, equating their invocation to calling upon a rebellious devil emphasizes the moral and spiritual danger of turning away from monotheistic worship, portraying such acts as aligning oneself with forces of chaos and disobedience against the divine order.
orig: إن يدعون من دونه إلا إناثا وإن يدعون إلا شيطانا مريدا

translation: Allah cursed him and he said: 'I will surely take an appointed portion from your servants.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the statement of Iblis (Satan) after being cursed by Allah for his arrogance and refusal to obey Allah's command. Satan's declaration to 'take an appointed portion from your servants' signifies his resolve to mislead and ensnare a portion of humanity into disobedience and sin. It suggests the perpetual struggle between human beings' divine guidance and satanic influences. The use of 'appointed portion' highlights the inevitability and preordained aspect of this conflict within the broader divine plan, yet it also underscores that not all humanity will succumb to his deception, indicating the existence of both guidance and misguidance as part of the human experience.
orig: لعنه الله وقال لأتخذن من عبادك نصيبا مفروضا

translation: And I will surely mislead them, and arouse in them sinful desires, and I will command them so they will slit the ears of cattle, and I will command them so they will alter the creation of Allah. And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has indeed suffered a manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse outlines the deceitful promises and actions of Satan, showing his intent to lead humans astray from the path of righteousness detailed by Allah. It reveals how Satan plans to corrupt humans by inciting them to modify and disrespect Allah's creations, including altering the natural state of animals, which is symbolized by the slitting of cattle's ears. This act not only represents physical alteration but also disobedience to the natural order established by Allah. The verse serves as a stark warning against following Satan's temptations and manipulations, emphasizing that doing so results in clear and severe loss, distancing oneself from Divine guidance and favor.
orig: ولأضلنهم ولأمنينهم ولآمرنهم فليبتكن آذان الأنعام ولآمرنهم فليغيرن خلق الله ومن يتخذ الشيطان وليا من دون الله فقد خسر خسرانا مبينا

translation: He promises them and fills them with desires, but Satan's promises are nothing but deception.
interpretation: This verse warns against the temptations and false promises of Satan, which lead individuals away from the truth and into deception. It highlights the nature of Satan's tactics, which are based on appealing to desires and creating false hopes. The ultimate purpose is to emphasize the deceit inherent in following these illusory promises, reminding believers to remain vigilant and steadfast in their faith to avoid such pitfalls.
orig: يعدهم ويمنيهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Those, their abode will be Hell, and they will find no escape from it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and permanence of the consequences for those who have chosen a path away from righteousness according to Islamic teachings. The reference to Hell as an 'abode' underscores its role as a final, unalterable state for the individuals described. The phrase 'no escape' further highlights the complete lack of alternatives available to them after judgment, stressing the importance of accountability and the enduring impact of one's choices in life.
orig: أولئك مأواهم جهنم ولا يجدون عنها محيصا

translation: And those who have believed and done righteous deeds, We shall admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. It is a promise of Allah in truth, and who is truer in speech than Allah?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound reward and eternal paradise that awaits those who hold firm in their faith and perform righteous actions. It underscores the concept of divine justice and recompense, providing believers with a motivation to maintain their ethical comportment and spiritual devotion. The mention of Allah's promise being true and the rhetorical question about the truthfulness of His speech serve to reinforce the certainty and magnitude of this reward, bolstering the believer's confidence in the divine covenant.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سندخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا وعد الله حقا ومن أصدق من الله قيلا

translation: It is not by your desires, nor the desires of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it and will not find, besides Allah, any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of accountability and justice in Islamic theology. It addresses both Muslims and the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), declaring that mere wishes or desires to be righteous are not enough; one must act righteously. The verse highlights that God's judgment is impartial and based on one's actions rather than one's affiliations or desires. Engaging in evil acts leads to recompense, and when facing divine judgment, no individual or entity can offer protection or assistance apart from Allah. This underscores the importance of personal responsibility and integrity in one's actions and serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability to God.
orig: ليس بأمانيكم ولا أماني أهل الكتاب من يعمل سوءا يجز به ولا يجد له من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: And whoever does good deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise and not be wronged even as much as the speck on a date seed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principles of equality, justice, and reward in the context of faith. It assures that gender does not influence the divine judgment of one's actions when paired with true belief. Both men and women are equally eligible for the rewards of their righteous actions, highlighting the inclusivity of divine mercy. Entry into Paradise is conditioned upon both faith and righteous actions, eliminating any form of discrimination. The phrase 'not be wronged even as much as the speck on a date seed' underscores the precise justice of God, where no good deed, no matter how small, goes unrewarded and no unfair treatment will occur.
orig: ومن يعمل من الصالحات من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون نقيرا

translation: And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah, and he is a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ideal qualities of a believer, highlighting the superiority of those who genuinely dedicate themselves to God, embodying righteousness and adhering faithfully to the monotheistic teachings of Abraham. It underscores the importance of submitting oneself wholly to the will of God, performing good deeds, and maintaining steadfastness in the pure faith exemplified by Abraham, who is shown as a model due to his close relationship with God, symbolized by his title as God's 'intimate friend'. This invites believers to strive for a deep, personal connection with God, rooted in sincerity, righteousness, and an unwavering commitment to the path shown by prophetic examples.
orig: ومن أحسن دينا ممن أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن واتبع ملة إبراهيم حنيفا واتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah encompasses everything.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all things in existence, both celestial and terrestrial. It highlights the concept of divine omnipresence and omniscience, affirming that Allah's knowledge and power extend over everything, thus advising believers to acknowledge His authority and submit to His will, reflecting the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and all-encompassing nature of Allah.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله بكل شيء محيطا

translation: And they ask you for a legal decision about women. Say: 'Allah advises you concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan girls whom you do not give what is prescribed for them, and yet you desire to marry them, and (concerning) the weak among children, and that you should deal justly with orphans. Whatever good you do, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of it.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and fairness, especially toward vulnerable groups such as orphan girls and weak children. It instructs that one must uphold the rights of these individuals strictly according to divine commandments, not exploiting their vulnerabilities for personal gain. The mention of Allah being 'ever Knowing' underscores the moral and spiritual accountability in every action, reminding believers that their deeds are always under divine scrutiny. The stress is on adhering to ethical principles, especially in upholding the rights of those who might not have the means to claim them themselves.
orig: ويستفتونك في النساء قل الله يفتيكم فيهن وما يتلى عليكم في الكتاب في يتامى النساء اللاتي لا تؤتونهن ما كتب لهن وترغبون أن تنكحوهن والمستضعفين من الولدان وأن تقوموا لليتامى بالقسط وما تفعلوا من خير فإن الله كان به عليما

translation: And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion, there is no sin upon them if they make terms of settlement between them - settlement is best. And present in [human] souls is stinginess. But if you do good and fear Allah - then indeed Allah is ever with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of resolving marital conflicts amicably. It addresses situations where a wife feels neglected or mistreated by her husband, advocating for reconciliation and compromise as the preferable solutions. The verse highlights an inherent human trait of selfishness, which can hinder reconciliation, but underscores that virtuous behavior—rooted in goodness and God-consciousness—should guide one's actions in marriage. This approach not only fosters a healthier relationship but also aligns with divine awareness and approval.
orig: وإن امرأة خافت من بعلها نشوزا أو إعراضا فلا جناح عليهما أن يصلحا بينهما صلحا والصلح خير وأحضرت الأنفس الشح وإن تحسنوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: And you will never be able to be fair and just among [your] women, even if it is your ardent desire, so do not incline completely [towards one] and leave another hanging [suspended]. And if you mend [your ways] and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the inherent difficulties men face in treating multiple wives with equal justice in emotions and provisions, emphasizing that complete equality is beyond human capability. It cautions men against favoritism that may harm another spouse, leaving her in a state of uncertainty, akin to being neither married nor divorced. The verse advises men to strive for reform and consciousness of God's commands, reassuring that with sincere efforts to adhere to fairness and piety, God's forgiveness and mercy encompass all shortcomings.
orig: ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء ولو حرصتم فلا تميلوا كل الميل فتذروها كالمعلقة وإن تصلحوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And if they separate, Allah will enrich each from His abundance, for Allah is all-Encompassing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the divine guidance and support that Allah provides in the event of a separation, such as a divorce. It emphasizes that even in moments of personal upheaval, God ensures that each individual will not be left in destitution but will be provided for from His vast reserves of provision and mercy. The attributes of Allah being 'all-Encompassing' and 'Wise' highlight that His decisions and the provisions He offers are both boundless and delivered with profound wisdom, tailored to the needs and betterment of each person. This assurance instills a sense of security and trust in God’s plan, encouraging believers to rely on His wisdom and benevolence in all circumstances.
orig: وإن يتفرقا يغن الله كلا من سعته وكان الله واسعا حكيما

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Indeed, We have instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and yourselves to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve, then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supremacy and ownership of Allah over all that exists in the heavens and the earth, reinforcing the notion of God's sovereignty and omnipotence. The instruction to fear Allah, which has been given to both previous recipients of divine scriptures and the audience of the Qur'an, underlines the continuity and universality of this divine command across different religious communities. The caution against disbelief serves to remind believers of the insignificance of their rebellion in the face of God's immense self-sufficiency and ownership. Allah's attributes of being Self-Sufficient (Ghani) and Praiseworthy (Hameed) are highlighted to underscore that Allah is beyond need of any of His creation and is worthy of all praise, regardless of human faith or disbelief. This verse overall calls for a conscious reverence and mindfulness of Allah's omnipresence and the eternal truth of His commandments.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ولقد وصينا الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم وإياكم أن اتقوا الله وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله غنيا حميدا

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over everything in the universe, both in the heavens and on the earth. It highlights Allah's power and ability to manage and govern the universe without the need for any assistance. Declaring that Allah is sufficient as a guardian and disposer of affairs reassures believers that they can trust Allah completely in managing all matters of existence, guiding their reliance solely on Him for their needs and protection.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you, O people, and bring others [in your place]. And Allah is fully capable of that.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over creation. It serves as a reminder to humanity of their replaceability and the transient nature of their existence on Earth. The assertion of Allah's capability to replace humans with others underscores the importance of humility and obedience to divine commands, as human beings are not indispensable. It reinforces the concept that God's will is paramount and can manifest in ways that might be beyond human understanding or expectation.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم أيها الناس ويأت بآخرين وكان الله على ذلك قديرا

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of God's sovereignty and benevolence, highlighting that both worldly gains and spiritual rewards are within His purview. It encourages believers to seek not only transient, worldly achievements but to be mindful of the eternal life hereafter. The mention of Allah being 'All-Hearing, All-Seeing' serves as a reminder of His omnipresence and omniscience, suggesting that He is aware of one's intentions and actions, and thus one should strive for sincerity in seeking rewards both in this life and the next.
orig: من كان يريد ثواب الدنيا فعند الله ثواب الدنيا والآخرة وكان الله سميعا بصيرا

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more deserving of both. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the paramount importance of justice in Islam, urging believers to uphold justice impartially, regardless of personal connections or the social status of those involved. It commands Muslims to display integrity by being fair witnesses for the sake of Allah, even if it means testifying against one's own interests or those of close kin. The verse warns against being swayed by desires that might compromise the fairness of one's judgment. It concludes by reminding that Allah is aware of all actions, serving as a stern reminder that no deed, whether good or bad, escapes His notice.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على أنفسكم أو الوالدين والأقربين إن يكن غنيا أو فقيرا فالله أولى بهما فلا تتبعوا الهوى أن تعدلوا وإن تلووا أو تعرضوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the book that He sent down to His Messenger and the scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of not just initial belief, but the continual deepening of faith in Allah, His messengers, and His scriptures. It emphasizes that belief should not be superficial or stagnant but should be reinforced and reaffirmed over time. The mention of belief in the previous scriptures alongside the Quran suggests the continuity and consistency of divine guidance throughout different prophetic eras. Disbelief in any fundamental aspect of Islam is portrayed as a deviation from the right path, leading one into profound error and misguidance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا آمنوا بالله ورسوله والكتاب الذي نزل على رسوله والكتاب الذي أنزل من قبل ومن يكفر بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who believed then disbelieved, then believed again and then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief, Allah is not to forgive them nor guide them to a path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity and repercussions of instability and repeated inconsistency in one’s faith. It underscores the divine displeasure towards those who oscillate frequently between belief and disbelief, specifically when such behavior escalates into a firm and increased rejection of faith. The refusal of forgiveness and guidance from Allah to such individuals highlights the critical importance of steadfastness in one’s belief and warns against taking faith lightly or treating it with fickleness. The passage serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of persistent disbelief after the reception of guidance.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم ازدادوا كفرا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم سبيلا

translation: Inform the hypocrites that they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses a stern warning to those who claim faith outwardly but inwardly contradict it through their actions and beliefs, known as hypocrites. The painful punishment signifies both the severity of their deceit and the consequential justice that aligns with their insincerity in faith. It underscores that true faith must resonate with both belief and action, warning against the dangers of duplicity in one's spiritual and communal life.
orig: بشر المنافقين بأن لهم عذابا أليما

translation: Those who take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers - do they seek honor, power, and glory with them? Indeed, all honor, power, and glory belong to Allah alone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of loyalty and alliance within the community of believers. It criticizes those who, driven by a desire for worldly honor or influence, choose to align themselves with disbelievers rather than fellow believers. The verse underscores a fundamental principle that true honor and power arise from adherence to divine guidance and not from worldly alliances. It serves as a reminder that any pursuit of power or status should not compromise one’s spiritual integrity and commitment to faith.
orig: الذين يتخذون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أيبتغون عندهم العزة فإن العزة لله جميعا

translation: And it has already been revealed to you in the Scripture that when you hear the verses of Allah being denied and ridiculed, do not sit with them until they engage in a talk other than that; indeed, you are then just like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers all together in Hell.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining the sanctity and respect for divine revelations. It instructs believers to distance themselves from environments where God's verses are treated with disbelief or ridicule. The directive serves as a protective measure to maintain one's faith and moral integrity. Associating with those who mock God's messages can spiritually degrade a believer to the level of the mockers. This distancing is not just a physical separation but a moral stand against actions and attitudes that belittle divine guidance. The warning of a collective punishment for hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell underscores the gravity of such actions and the finality of divine justice.
orig: وقد نزل عليكم في الكتاب أن إذا سمعتم آيات الله يكفر بها ويستهزأ بها فلا تقعدوا معهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره إنكم إذا مثلهم إن الله جامع المنافقين والكافرين في جهنم جميعا

translation: Those who wait to see what happens to you: if you receive a victory from Allah, they say, 'Were we not with you?' and if the unbelievers gain a share, they say, 'Did we not prevail over you and protect you from the believers?' So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never grant the unbelievers a way over the believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the insincerity and opportunistic behavior of certain individuals who oscillate in their allegiance based on the outcome of events. It highlights their duplicity in claiming solidarity with the believers when it is advantageous, and siding with the unbelievers when the circumstances favor them. This reflects a lack of true faith and commitment. The verse underscores that true justice will ultimately be served by Allah on the Day of Resurrection, reiterating the divine principle that the disbelievers will not triumph over the believers. This serves as both a reassurance to the faithful and a warning to the insincere, emphasizing the importance of steadfast faith and loyalty to the cause of truth.
orig: الذين يتربصون بكم فإن كان لكم فتح من الله قالوا ألم نكن معكم وإن كان للكافرين نصيب قالوا ألم نستحوذ عليكم ونمنعكم من المؤمنين فالله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة ولن يجعل الله للكافرين على المؤمنين سبيلا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites try to deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and hardly remembering Allah at all.
interpretation: This verse addresses the characteristics and spiritual consequences of hypocrisy, particularly within the context of religious observance. It emphasizes that hypocrites, who outwardly display faith but inwardly deny it, attempt to deceive God with their insincere worship. However, the irony lies in their own self-deception, as God is fully aware of their true intentions and thus, turns their deceit back onto them. The description of their prayer—performed lazily and for show—further illustrates their lack of genuine devotion. The superficiality of their actions, performed merely to gain approval from others rather than to honor God, highlights a profound spiritual emptiness and disconnection from the divine essence of worship. This serves as a warning to be sincere in one’s faith and actions, valuing authenticity over the perception of others.
orig: إن المنافقين يخادعون الله وهو خادعهم وإذا قاموا إلى الصلاة قاموا كسالى يراءون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا

translation: Wavering between them, belonging neither to these nor to those. And whomever Allah sends astray, for him you will not find a way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the state of indecision and uncertainty that afflicts some individuals who are unable to commit to a path of belief or disbelief. It portrays their dilemma, torn between different groups and unable to find a solid stance. The verse also conveys the profound Islamic belief in divine predestination: if Allah has determined that a person should be misguided, no human effort can guide them to the right path. This serves as a reminder of the omnipotence of Allah and the importance of seeking His guidance to remain steadfast in faith.
orig: مذبذبين بين ذلك لا إلى هؤلاء ولا إلى هؤلاء ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah against yourselves a clear authority?
interpretation: This verse advises believers to prefer forming alliances and bonds of friendship with fellow believers rather than with disbelievers. It warns against the consequences of aligning closely with those who reject faith, as such alliances may contradict the values and obligations of one's own faith, potentially giving clear justification for divine judgment or disapproval. The verse emphasizes loyalty and solidarity among the community of believers and discourages intimate relationships with those who could lead one away from the teachings and principles of Islam.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أتريدون أن تجعلوا لله عليكم سلطانا مبينا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will find no helper for them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences awaiting hypocrites in the afterlife, highlighting their placement in the most grievous levels of Hell due to their insincerity and duplicity in faith. The absence of any helper underscores their complete abandonment and the divine retribution for their betrayal of trust and genuine belief.
orig: إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار ولن تجد لهم نصيرا

translation: Except those who repent, mend their ways, hold firmly to Allah, and dedicate their religion to Allah, for they will be with the believers, and Allah will grant the believers a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of sincere repentance and reformation in one's actions and beliefs. It highlights the importance of steadfast faith and the dedication of one's religious practice solely to Allah. By aligning themselves with these virtues, repentant individuals are reassured of their place among the believers and the promise of a significant reward from Allah. The verse underlines the mercy of Allah and His readiness to forgive those who genuinely turn back to Him and strive to live righteously.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله فأولئك مع المؤمنين وسوف يؤت الله المؤمنين أجرا عظيما

translation: What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is Appreciative, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine attributes of mercy and omniscience. It suggests that God does not desire to punish people unnecessarily; rather, He values gratitude and faith. The mention of Allah as 'Appreciative' implies that He acknowledges and rewards the smallest acts of gratitude and faith from His servants. This serves as a motivation for believers to cultivate these qualities in their lives, aligning their actions with divine pleasure. The statement also underscores that God's actions are informed by complete knowledge, which assures that His judgments are always just and informed by a comprehensive understanding of all matters.
orig: ما يفعل الله بعذابكم إن شكرتم وآمنتم وكان الله شاكرا عليما

translation: Allah does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. And Allah is Hearing, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of restraint in speech and conduct, particularly in refraining from spreading negativity or evil unless one is genuinely wronged and is seeking justice. The mention of Allah being 'Hearing, Knowing' underscores the divine awareness of all human actions and intentions, suggesting that individuals should be mindful of their actions since nothing escapes divine scrutiny. This principle promotes a society where grievances are addressed legally and ethically, discouraging malicious or unnecessary harm through words.
orig: لا يحب الله الجهر بالسوء من القول إلا من ظلم وكان الله سميعا عليما

translation: Whether you show goodness openly, conceal it, or forgive an evil, indeed Allah is Pardoning and Powerful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and omnipotence of Allah in witnessing all human actions, whether they are done publicly or in private. It underscores the virtue of forgiving others and being good in various circumstances, highlighting both the capacity and the divine nature of forgiveness possessed by Allah. Encouraging believers to emulate these divine attributes, the verse serves as a reminder that Allah values benevolence and forgiveness, rewarding such behaviors with His infinite mercy and power.
orig: إن تبدوا خيرا أو تخفوه أو تعفوا عن سوء فإن الله كان عفوا قديرا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and want to make distinction between Allah and His messengers, saying, 'We believe in some and disbelieve in others,' and wish to adopt a way in-between.
interpretation: This verse addresses the inconsistency and selectivity in belief. It criticizes those who claim to follow a path of faith but deliberately choose to believe in only certain aspects or messengers while rejecting others. The verse highlights that true belief does not involve partial acceptance tailored to personal preferences or prejudices, but it requires a complete and unified acceptance of all divine revelations and messengers. The verse underscores the impossibility of being halfway between belief and disbelief, illuminating the notion that faith involves a comprehensive commitment rather than a selective approach.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بالله ورسله ويريدون أن يفرقوا بين الله ورسله ويقولون نؤمن ببعض ونكفر ببعض ويريدون أن يتخذوا بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: Those are the true disbelievers, and for the disbelievers We have prepared a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction between those who truly reject faith and those who believe. It addresses the consequences of willful disbelief, particularly highlighting the severity of the outcome that awaits disbelievers. The mention of 'humiliating punishment' underscores not just the physical aspect of the punishment, but also its moral and emotional dimensions, designed to reflect the gravity of their denial of faith. This serves as a stern warning to uphold truth and spiritual awareness, and illustrates the principle of divine justice in response to human choices and beliefs.
orig: أولئك هم الكافرون حقا وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who believed in Allah and His messengers and did not differentiate between any of them - those will be given their rewards, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of accepting all of Allah's messengers without discrimination. Belief should be consistent and all-encompassing regarding the messengers, recognizing that they all come from the same divine source and carry the same message of truth. It underscores the idea that such undivided belief aligns with Allah's will and leads to the bestowal of rewards. The mention of Allah being 'Forgiving' and 'Merciful' highlights His benevolent nature and reassures believers that even if they falter, Allah's mercy can encompass their shortcomings if they remain faithful to the core tenets of Islam, including equality among prophets.
orig: والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله ولم يفرقوا بين أحد منهم أولئك سوف يؤتيهم أجورهم وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from the heavens. They had indeed asked Moses for even greater than that, for they said, 'Show us Allah openly.' Then the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing. Afterward, they took the calf [for worship], even after clear signs had come to them; yet We forgave that and gave Moses a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse highlights the historical pattern of excessive demands and skepticism among the People of the Book towards their prophets, as well as indicating the severe consequences of their actions. It contrasts the divine response to their transgressions — a combination of punishment and mercy. The mention of 'clear authority' given to Moses underscores the divine support and legitimacy granted to prophets despite the challenges they face from their communities. This serves as a lesson on the importance of faith, the dangers of demanding signs beyond what God has provided, and the continuous mercy of God even when correcting His people.
orig: يسألك أهل الكتاب أن تنزل عليهم كتابا من السماء فقد سألوا موسى أكبر من ذلك فقالوا أرنا الله جهرة فأخذتهم الصاعقة بظلمهم ثم اتخذوا العجل من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات فعفونا عن ذلك وآتينا موسى سلطانا مبينا

translation: And We raised the Mount above them as per their covenant and said to them, 'Enter the gate prostrating' and We told them, 'Do not transgress on the Sabbath,' and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the seriousness with which God holds covenants and the consequences of not honoring them. The imagery of raising the Mount above the Israelites serves as a powerful reminder of God’s omnipotence and the gravity of their commitments. The command to enter the gate prostrating symbolizes humility and submission to God’s will, essential for honoring any covenant. The prohibition against transgressing on the Sabbath, which was a sign of their covenant, emphasizes the importance of obedience to divine law. The reference to a 'solemn covenant' underscores the depth and seriousness of the agreement between God and the Israelites, reminding believers of the importance of their commitments to God.
orig: ورفعنا فوقهم الطور بميثاقهم وقلنا لهم ادخلوا الباب سجدا وقلنا لهم لا تعدوا في السبت وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: So because of their breach of their covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets unjustly, and their saying, 'Our hearts are wrapped'—rather, Allah has set a seal upon them for their disbelief, so they believe not, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse admonishes a group for their continual disobedience and rejection of divine guidance, emphasizing the severe consequences of such actions. It points out their failure to uphold sacred agreements, their rejection of God’s signs, and their unjust actions, such as the killing of prophets. The reference to their claim of 'wrapped hearts' suggests an obstinate refusal to understand or believe, to which the verse responds by indicating that it is their own disbelief that has metaphorically sealed their hearts, limiting their capacity to accept faith. This sealing is positioned as a divine response to persistent disbelief, essentially marking a spiritual consequence to their actions. The mention of 'except for a few' implies that despite the widespread disbelief, there remains a small group within who still hold true to their faith, suggesting a glimmer of hope or redemption.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم وكفرهم بآيات الله وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق وقولهم قلوبنا غلف بل طبع الله عليها بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا

translation: And for their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander,
interpretation: This verse highlights the condemnation of those who falsely slandered Mary (Maryam) by accusing her of immorality. This accusation is considered a severe form of disbelief and injustice, emphasizing not only the sin of false accusation but also the broader societal impact of slander. It underscores the importance of maintaining integrity and truth in one's words and actions, and it serves as a reminder of the high esteem in which Mary is held in Islam.
orig: وبكفرهم وقولهم على مريم بهتانا عظيما

translation: And their saying, 'We have killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the messenger of Allah,' and they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption, and they did not kill him, certainly.
interpretation: This verse addresses and refutes the claim made by some groups that they killed Jesus Christ, the Messiah. It clarifies that Jesus was neither crucified nor killed as some believe, but rather, it appeared so to them, suggesting a divine intervention or illusion that misled the perpetrators. The verse emphasizes the uncertainty and baseless conjecture surrounding the circumstances of Jesus' end among those who argue about it, highlighting their reliance on assumptions rather than factual knowledge. It firmly states that the claims of Jesus’ death on the cross are definitively untrue, reaffirming the Islamic belief in Jesus' protection from such an end by God's command.
orig: وقولهم إنا قتلنا المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم وإن الذين اختلفوا فيه لفي شك منه ما لهم به من علم إلا اتباع الظن وما قتلوه يقينا

translation: But Allah raised him unto Himself, and Allah is All-Powerful, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and omnipotence of God, highlighting His authority and wisdom in dealing with His creations. It affirms the divine act of protecting and elevating a revered figure, underscoring the concept that God’s decisions are executed with both absolute power and profound wisdom. This notion invites believers to trust in God's overarching plan and His capacity to enact His will beyond human understanding or intervention.
orig: بل رفعه الله إليه وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: And there is none from the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitable acknowledgment of the truth concerning Jesus (Isa) by the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) before his death. It highlights a future event where every individual, prior to their demise, will accept the true message and prophethood of Jesus, reconciling their beliefs with the Islamic view. On the Day of Judgment, this acceptance will have significant implications, as Jesus will bear witness regarding their initial disbelief and eventual belief. This serves as a profound reminder of accountability and the ultimate knowledge of God surpassing human understanding and historical disputes over religious truths.
orig: وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته ويوم القيامة يكون عليهم شهيدا

translation: So due to the wrongdoing of the Jews, We made unlawful for them certain good things which had been lawful to them, and for their hindering of many from the way of Allah,
interpretation: This verse addresses the punitive measures taken by God in response to the transgressions committed by the Jewish community of that time. It highlights the concept of divine retribution, where worldly privileges and permissions were revoked as a direct consequence of their moral and spiritual misdeeds. Primarily, it serves as a cautionary note on the importance of adhering to divine guidance and the potential worldly consequences of deviating from God's commands. The essence lies in promoting justice and deterring behaviors that would impede spiritual growth or lead to communal harm.
orig: فبظلم من الذين هادوا حرمنا عليهم طيبات أحلت لهم وبصدهم عن سبيل الله كثيرا

translation: And they took usury, though they were forbidden from it, and consumed people's wealth unjustly, and for the disbelievers among them, We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the strict prohibition of usury in Islamic teachings, emphasizing its moral and societal implications. The act of consuming wealth unjustly, such as through usury, is depicted as a transgression against divine commandments and social ethics. The severe warning of a painful punishment for the disbelievers who engage in such practices reflects the emphasis on justice and fairness within the community, urging individuals to adhere to ethical financial dealings and to avoid exploitation. The verse serves as a strong deterrent against economic exploitation and stresses accountability in the hereafter.
orig: وأخذهم الربا وقد نهوا عنه وأكلهم أموال الناس بالباطل وأعتدنا للكافرين منهم عذابا أليما

translation: But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, and those who establish prayer and give zakat, and believe in Allah and the Last Day—these, We will give them a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction of those who are deeply grounded in spiritual and religious knowledge. Their faith is not merely superficial or ritualistic; it is informed by a profound understanding of the scriptures, including the revelations given to previous prophets and the revelation given to the Prophet Muhammad. Their faith is manifested actively through the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakat, signifying not just a personal belief but a commitment to societal and communal responsibilities. This combination of deep knowledge, coupled with practical application of faith through good deeds and a firm belief in the fundamental concepts of Islam, qualifies them for a significant reward from Allah. This reinforces the principle that true faith requires both understanding and action, rooted in the comprehensive teachings of Islam.
orig: لكن الراسخون في العلم منهم والمؤمنون يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك والمقيمين الصلاة والمؤتون الزكاة والمؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أولئك سنؤتيهم أجرا عظيما

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, as We revealed to Noah and the Prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and to David We gave the Psalms.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and universality of divine guidance through prophets across different eras and communities. It highlights the notion that God’s revelation is consistent and has been imparted to a succession of prophets, each receiving guidance suited to their respective communities and times. The specific mention of giving the Psalms to David signifies the variety in forms of revelation, which can include scriptures like the Psalms or the methodologies of other prophets. This continuity in divine instruction underlines the unity and cohesive message of monotheism, urging current and future generations to view their own prophetic guidance (in this context, the Qur'an revealed to Prophet Muhammad) as part of a long-standing divine tradition.
orig: إنا أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى نوح والنبيين من بعده وأوحينا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وعيسى وأيوب ويونس وهارون وسليمان وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: And messengers We have mentioned to you before, and messengers We have not mentioned to you; and Allah spoke to Moses directly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the diversity and breadth of God's communication with humanity. It acknowledges that there are many prophets and messengers, some of whom are known and mentioned in the scriptures, while others remain unmentioned. The specific reference to God speaking directly to Moses highlights a unique and special form of communication, illustrating that God has various methods and degrees of direct interaction with His prophets. This verse teaches us about the honor bestowed upon certain prophets and the importance of recognizing all of God's messengers, known or unknown, as integral to the divine plan of guiding humanity.
orig: ورسلا قد قصصناهم عليك من قبل ورسلا لم نقصصهم عليك وكلم الله موسى تكليما

translation: Messengers bearing good tidings and warnings so that mankind shall have no argument against Allah after the messengers; and Allah is Ever-Mighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grace and mercy of Allah in sending messengers to humanity. Their role is dual: to bring good news to those who believe and follow the righteous path, and to serve as warners to those who choose to disregard the divine guidance. The dispatch of messengers ensures that all human beings are given the necessary knowledge and warning about Allah’s commands, thus removing any excuse for ignorance on the Day of Judgment. Allah’s reference as 'Ever-Mighty, All-Wise' underscores His absolute authority and the profound wisdom in His plans, emphasizing that the sending of messengers is a well-considered act fulfilling His divine will.
orig: رسلا مبشرين ومنذرين لئلا يكون للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels also bear witness. And sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin and authenticity of the revelations received by the Prophet. It emphasizes that God, being All-Knowing, consciously and purposefully sent these messages. The reference to the angels as witnesses further strengthens the credibility and sanctity of the revelations. The phrase 'And sufficient is Allah as Witness' underscores that God's testimony alone is enough to validate the truth, making any additional verification unnecessary. This serves to reassure the Prophet and the believers of the unassailable truth and authority of the divine messages they have received.
orig: لكن الله يشهد بما أنزل إليك أنزله بعلمه والملائكة يشهدون وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and prevented others from the path of Allah have gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the grave spiritual condition of those who not only reject belief in Allah but also actively work to obstruct others from following His guidance. Their actions lead them to be severely misguided, distancing themselves from spiritual truth and the potential for divine mercy and guidance. The phrase 'gone far astray' suggests a profound deviation from the righteous path, implying that their behavior not only affects their spiritual journey but also potentially misleads others, multiplying the impact of their misguidance.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله قد ضلوا ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and commit injustice, Allah is not to forgive them nor to guide them to a path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of persisting in disbelief and injustice, highlighting that such actions estrange individuals from divine forgiveness and guidance. It underscores the inherent connection between one’s faith and moral conduct, and the ultimate divine rejection experienced by those who choose to live in denial of truth and equity. The mention of neither forgiveness nor guidance denotes a spiritual abandonment, serving as a stark warning about the spiritual perils of steadfast wrongdoing and disbelief.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وظلموا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم طريقا

translation: Except the path to Hell, wherein they will abide forever. And that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute authority and power of Allah in determining the fates of individuals based on their actions and beliefs. It emphasizes the notion of divine justice and the eternal consequences of one's earthly choices. The phrase 'that is easy for Allah' highlights the omnipotence of God, reflecting that the administration of cosmic justice is within His effortless capability. It serves as a solemn reminder of the ultimate accountability each soul must face and the unalterable reality of divine judgment.
orig: إلا طريق جهنم خالدين فيها أبدا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: O mankind, indeed the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe, it is better for you. But if you disbelieve, then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah is All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of accepting and believing in the message delivered by the Messenger, which originates from God. It underscores that faith in this truth is beneficial for humanity. Conversely, the verse highlights God's independence and sovereignty, affirming that His dominion encompasses everything in the universe regardless of human belief. The attributes of God's omniscience and wisdom emphasize that His decrees are made with complete knowledge and perfect judgment, signaling that the divine plan is not contingent on human acceptance but is focused on guiding them towards what is inherently good.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الرسول بالحق من ربكم فآمنوا خيرا لكم وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion or say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a spirit from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And do not say, 'Three'; desist - it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Scripture, advising them against exaggeration or deviation in matters of faith, particularly concerning the nature and status of Jesus Christ. It emphasizes that Jesus, despite his miraculous birth and exceptional qualities, is not divine but a prophet of God. The reference to 'not say, 'Three' directly confronts and corrects the doctrine of the Trinity, urging followers to recognize the strict monotheism that characterizes Islam. The assertion of God's uniqueness and transcendence serves to remind believers that associating partners with God contradicts the fundamental tenets of Islamic theology. The verse reinforces the sovereignty of God over all creation and establishes His sufficiency as a guardian and protector, stressing the need for absolute reliance on Him alone.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم ولا تقولوا على الله إلا الحق إنما المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم وروح منه فآمنوا بالله ورسله ولا تقولوا ثلاثة انتهوا خيرا لكم إنما الله إله واحد سبحانه أن يكون له ولد له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: The Messiah will not disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels nearest to Him. And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will gather them all to Himself.
