The verse highlights the limited understanding of the skeptics and underscores that the absence of signs is due to the wisdom of God and the spiritual blindness or ignorance of the people, rather than any inability on God's part.
orig: وقالوا لولا نزل عليه آية من ربه قل إن الله قادر على أن ينزل آية ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And there is no creature on the earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you. We have neglected nothing in the Book, then unto their Lord they will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound unity and similarity among all creations of God, emphasizing that every creature, whether on land or flying with wings, forms a community akin to human communities. It underscores the comprehensive and meticulous nature of God's creation, where nothing is overlooked or left out, as reinforced by the assertion that everything is recorded in the divine scripture. Additionally, the verse underscores the ultimate accountability and return of all creatures to God, reinforcing themes of resurrection and divine judgment.
orig: وما من دابة في الأرض ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه إلا أمم أمثالكم ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء ثم إلى ربهم يحشرون

translation: And those who deny Our signs are deaf and dumb, dwelling in darkness. Whomsoever Allah wills, He lets go astray, and whomsoever He wills, He places on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse underscores the profound effect of spiritual defiance against divine signs on a person's perceptual and cognitive faculties, symbolically rendering them 'deaf and dumb,' unable to perceive or articulate truth, and 'in darkness,' representing a state of ignorance and misguidance. The passage emphasizes the omnipotence of God in matters of guidance and misguidance, asserting that divine will is decisive in determining individual spiritual paths. It highlights the dichotomy between divine mercy and justice, illustrating that while guidance is a grace bestowed by God, straying from the right path is also a consequence aligned with divine wisdom, serving perhaps as a trial or a test of faith.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا صم وبكم في الظلمات من يشإ الله يضلله ومن يشأ يجعله على صراط مستقيم

translation: Say, 'Tell me, if Allah's punishment comes to you, or if the Hour arrives, would you call upon any other than Allah, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of true faith and reliance on Allah, especially in times of distress or at the approach of the Judgment Day. It challenges the sincerity of those who may worship or call upon others besides Allah during their daily lives. The verse serves as a reminder that in the ultimate trials of life and the hereafter, only Allah can provide salvation and relief. It underscores the futility of placing trust in other deities or entities and invites individuals to reflect on the authenticity of their faith and the consistency of their devotion.
orig: قل أرأيتكم إن أتاكم عذاب الله أو أتتكم الساعة أغير الله تدعون إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But it is Him you call upon, and He can remove what you call upon Him to remove, if He wills, and you forget what you associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and sole authority of God in answering prayers and alleviating distress. It serves as a reminder of human tendency to forget or overlook the shirk (associating partners with God) they commit in times of ease, yet in times of hardship, they instinctively recognize the oneness of God and direct their pleas solely towards Him. The conditional 'if He wills' indicates that God's will is paramount and He may choose to respond to prayers as a test or a lesson for the believers. This illustrates both the mercy and the absolute sovereignty of God in the affairs of humans.
orig: بل إياه تدعون فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء وتنسون ما تشركون

translation: And indeed, We sent (messengers) to nations before you, then seized them with misery and hardship, that they might implore (for mercy).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the recurring theme of divine testing and mercy in the Qur'an. It illustrates that the afflictions and difficulties experienced by previous nations were a part of God's plan to encourage repentance and humility among His people. The hardships were intended to turn people's hearts towards seeking forgiveness and re-establishing a humble relationship with God. It reflects on the idea that suffering can serve as a poignant reminder of human vulnerability and the need for divine guidance and mercy.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا إلى أمم من قبلك فأخذناهم بالبأساء والضراء لعلهم يتضرعون

translation: So why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts had hardened, and Satan made attractive to them what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights human nature in facing divine retribution. It explores the concept of spiritual insensitivity, where individuals fail to humble themselves and repent even when faced with adversity as a consequence of their deeds. This steadfastness is attributed to the hardening of the hearts, a metaphorical description of becoming insensitive to guidance and truth. Additionally, the verse delves into the deceptive role of Satan in beautifying wrongful deeds in the eyes of the wrongdoers, further deterring them from seeking forgiveness and persisting on their misguided path. It serves as a warning about the dangers of succumbing to such spiritual maladies and the manipulations of evil forces.
orig: فلولا إذ جاءهم بأسنا تضرعوا ولكن قست قلوبهم وزين لهم الشيطان ما كانوا يعملون

translation: So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything, until, when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and then they were in despair.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of forgetting spiritual guidance and indulging excessively in worldly pleasures. It serves as a warning that divine blessings can swiftly turn into trials if they lead to arrogance or negligence in duties towards God. The sudden seizing by God symbolizes the unpredictable nature of divine retribution, reminding believers to remain steadfast in their faith and gratitude, regardless of their circumstances.
orig: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون

translation: And He cut off the last remnant of the people who did wrong, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine retribution meted out to those who persist in wrongdoing and oppression. By stating that He 'cut off the last remnant', it implies the complete elimination or eradication of the evil-doers, signifying the thoroughness of divine justice. The subsequent praise of Allah as 'Lord of the worlds' underscores the universal sovereignty and moral authority of God, indicating that such divine actions are just and encompass all forms of existence. This serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability to God and reinforces the value of righteousness.
orig: فقطع دابر القوم الذين ظلموا والحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Say, 'Have you considered if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight and seal your hearts, who other than Allah could restore them?' See how We explain the signs, yet they turn away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over human faculties and existence. It challenges individuals to reflect on their dependency on Allah for their sensory and cognitive abilities. By posing a rhetorical question, the verse urges people to recognize that there is no deity other than Allah who has the capability to restore such essential functions once they are lost. The latter part of the verse criticizes the heedlessness of those who, despite clear signs and explanations provided, choose to ignore the truth and turn away from the path of understanding and belief.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أخذ الله سمعكم وأبصاركم وختم على قلوبكم من إله غير الله يأتيكم به انظر كيف نصرف الآيات ثم هم يصدفون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered if the punishment of Allah comes to you unexpectedly or openly, will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice of divine retribution, highlighting that it targets only those who engage in wrongdoing. The mention of punishment arriving 'unexpectedly or openly' serves as a reminder of the omnipresence of divine justice, which can manifest at any moment, either suddenly or evident to all. It underscores the accountability of human actions and serves as a warning to the unjust that their misdeeds align them with destruction, urging all to adhere to righteous conduct and uphold justice.
orig: قل أرأيتكم إن أتاكم عذاب الله بغتة أو جهرة هل يهلك إلا القوم الظالمون

translation: And We send not the messengers except as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and reforms, there shall be no fear upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the primary roles of messengers as conveyors of glad tidings and as warners, serving to guide humanity by delineating the pathway towards righteousness and cautioning against wrongdoing. The assurance provided to those who believe and mend their ways underscores a divine promise of spiritual security and emotional peace, suggesting that true faith accompanied by righteous actions shields an individual from fear and sorrow in this life and potentially in the hereafter.
orig: وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين ومنذرين فمن آمن وأصلح فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And those who denied Our signs, punishment will touch them because of their transgressions.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice and retribution. It warns that those who reject divine guidance and persist in wrongdoing will inevitably face consequences. The punishment is depicted as a direct result of their defiance and misconduct, serving as a deterrent and a reminder of the moral order established by divine law.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا يمسهم العذاب بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: Say, 'I do not tell you that I possess the treasures of God, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me.' Say, 'Are the blind and the seeing equal? Then do you not reflect?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of the Prophet Muhammad and underscores his role as a messenger who faithfully conveys divine revelation rather than possessing any divine powers or knowledge of the unseen himself. It reminds the followers to recognize the limitations of human beings and the importance of revelation in guiding human understanding. The comparison between the blind and the seeing serves as a metaphor for spiritual insight versus spiritual blindness, urging believers to contemplate and discern the truth with the aid of divine guidance.
orig: قل لا أقول لكم عندي خزائن الله ولا أعلم الغيب ولا أقول لكم إني ملك إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير أفلا تتفكرون

translation: And warn therewith those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, there being for them no protector or intercessor besides Him, so that they might become righteous.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of warning and reminding those who hold a reverent fear of the Day of Judgment, when all individuals will be assembled before God without any intermediaries or advocates. The emphasis is on the fact that God stands as the sole authority and protector on that definitive day, highlighting the absence of worldly relationships or objects of dependence that could alter one’s fate. The primary goal of this admonition is to instill righteousness and God-consciousness (taqwa) in individuals, encouraging them to live responsibly and ethically in alignment with divine commands so that they may attain success in the hereafter.
orig: وأنذر به الذين يخافون أن يحشروا إلى ربهم ليس لهم من دونه ولي ولا شفيع لعلهم يتقون

translation: And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for them in anything, nor are they accountable for you in anything. If you drive them away, you will be among the unjust.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of tolerance and inclusion within the Muslim community. It advises against judging or excluding individuals based on their social status or appearance, particularly those earnest in their devotion to God. The verse underscores that everyone is responsible for their own actions before God and warns against the injustice of dismissing or ostracizing believers who sincerely strive to connect with their Creator. The broader implication is a call for unity and compassion among believers, highlighting that piety and devotion are the true measures of a person's worth in the eyes of God.
orig: ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء وما من حسابك عليهم من شيء فتطردهم فتكون من الظالمين

translation: And thus We have made some of them a trial for others, that they might say, 'Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed His favors among us?' Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?
interpretation: This verse addresses the concept of divine trials and the human inclination to question God's distribution of favors and blessings among people. The scenario depicted involves individuals questioning why certain people are seemingly favored over others, suggesting a test of faith and perspective. It prompts believers to reflect on the deeper wisdom of God's choices and actions, underscoring that God, being All-Knowing, is aware of who truly harbors gratitude and who does not.
orig: وكذلك فتنا بعضهم ببعض ليقولوا أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا أليس الله بأعلم بالشاكرين

translation: And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, 'Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed mercy upon Himself, that any of you who does wrong out of ignorance and then repents after it and corrects himself, indeed, He is Forgiving, Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of greeting fellow believers with peace and highlights God's infinite mercy and forgiveness. It underscores that God has made a divine commitment to mercy, thus encouraging believers to constantly seek forgiveness and improve themselves. The verse reassures that errors committed out of ignorance can be rectified through repentance and righteous actions, affirming God's qualities as forgiving and merciful to those who sincerely turn back to Him.
orig: وإذا جاءك الذين يؤمنون بآياتنا فقل سلام عليكم كتب ربكم على نفسه الرحمة أنه من عمل منكم سوءا بجهالة ثم تاب من بعده وأصلح فأنه غفور رحيم

translation: And thus do We detail the verses so that the way of the criminals becomes clear.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the meticulous and clear exposition of divine messages, aiming to elucidate the path of wrongdoers. It suggests that the clarity of divine guidance serves both to instruct the righteous and expose the errant behaviors of those who choose to deviate from moral and spiritual truth. The verse underscores the purpose of divine scripture in distinguishing right from wrong, thereby offering humanity the tools to recognize and avoid the behaviors that lead to corruption and injustice.
orig: وكذلك نفصل الآيات ولتستبين سبيل المجرمين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah. Say, 'I do not follow your desires; indeed, I would then be astray, and I am not of the guided.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the rejection of idolatry, marking a clear boundary against following or adhering to the polytheistic beliefs and practices of others. The speaker is instructed to assert their commitment to the worship of Allah alone, distancing themselves from the influences of societal or cultural pressures that deviate from this path. The mention of not following the 'desires' of others highlights the danger of allowing personal or popular inclinations to dictate one's faith, stressing that true guidance is aligned with divine commandments rather than human whims. This is a declaration of spiritual independence and a firm stance on maintaining the purity of one's faith against external temptations or misguidance.
orig: قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله قل لا أتبع أهواءكم قد ضللت إذا وما أنا من المهتدين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and you have denied it. I do not possess what you are impatient for. Judgment belongs only to Allah; He declares the truth, and He is the best of deciders.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine guidance and the finality of God's judgment. The speaker (the Prophet Muhammad, in this context) asserts his clarity and certainty in the divine revelation he has received, contrasted with the disbelief of those who reject this message. It highlights that true judgment and the hastening of events are solely under God's control. The speaker disclaims any personal power to bring about the ultimate consequences that the disbelievers impatiently seek, thereby affirming that God is the ultimate arbiter of truth and the most just decider in disputes. This verse reassures believers to trust in God's timing and judgment, while also serving as a warning to the skeptics of divine justice.
orig: قل إني على بينة من ربي وكذبتم به ما عندي ما تستعجلون به إن الحكم إلا لله يقص الحق وهو خير الفاصلين

translation: Say, 'If I had that which you are hastening for, the matter would have been decided between you and me. And Allah knows best the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and the supreme authority of Allah in matters of justice and retribution. It suggests that human impatience and desire for immediate resolution or retribution is not aligned with the divine wisdom and timing. The verse reinforces the concept that Allah is the most knowledgeable about who is in the wrong and the ultimate arbiter in disputes. Therefore, humans should exercise patience and trust in Allah's judgment and timing, rather than hastily seeking resolutions based on their limited understanding and perspective.
orig: قل لو أن عندي ما تستعجلون به لقضي الأمر بيني وبينكم والله أعلم بالظالمين

translation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows whatever there is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And there is no grain in the darkness of the earth, nor any fresh or dry thing, but that it is written in a clear record.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute knowledge and control of God over all aspects of the universe, highlighting His omniscience and omnipotence. It illustrates that nothing, no matter how minute or hidden, escapes God's knowledge, underlining the comprehensive and detailed record of everything in existence, upheld by divine wisdom. This serves to reassure believers of God's meticulous care and governance of all creation, fostering a sense of trust and awe towards the divine.
orig: وعنده مفاتح الغيب لا يعلمها إلا هو ويعلم ما في البر والبحر وما تسقط من ورقة إلا يعلمها ولا حبة في ظلمات الأرض ولا رطب ولا يابس إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: And it is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day; then He revives you therein that a specified term may be fulfilled; then to Him will be your return, and then He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of God, underscoring that He is in control of life and death. The taking of souls at night reflects the concept of death or a state akin to it during sleep, while the revival each morning signifies a rebirth and the opportunity to fulfill our earthly roles and rectify previous actions until our destined time comes. Ultimately, everyone will return to God, who is fully aware of all human deeds, and each individual will be accountable for their actions in life. This accountability highlights the moral and ethical dimensions governing human conduct as per God’s divine justice.
orig: وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار ثم يبعثكم فيه ليقضى أجل مسمى ثم إليه مرجعكم ثم ينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And He is the Subduer above His servants, and He sends guardians over you, until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take his soul, and they do not fail in their duties.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and authority of God over all His creation, highlighting His supreme control and guardianship. It reflects the Islamic belief that God appoints angels as guardians over humans to watch over them throughout their lives. The moment of death is depicted as a precise and ordained event, where appointed angels (referred to as God's messengers) are responsible for taking the soul of the deceased at the exact decreed time, ensuring the divine will is carried out flawlessly and with precision. The phrase 'and they do not fail in their duties' underscores the infallibility and meticulousness of these divine agents in executing God's commands.
orig: وهو القاهر فوق عباده ويرسل عليكم حفظة حتى إذا جاء أحدكم الموت توفته رسلنا وهم لا يفرطون

translation: Then they will be returned to Allah, their true Master. Indeed, His is the judgment, and He is the swiftest of accountants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment where everyone will return to Allah, the ultimate authority and arbiter of all affairs. It highlights God's sovereignty and His capability to judge swiftly and justly, urging believers to remain conscious of their actions and their ultimate accountability before God.
orig: ثم ردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق ألا له الحكم وهو أسرع الحاسبين

translation: Say, 'Who rescues you from the darkness of the land and sea? You call upon Him pleading and in secret, saying, 'If He saves us from this, we will surely be among the grateful.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the inherent human reliance on the Divine, especially in times of severe distress and danger that appear in the unpredictable terrains of both land and sea. It highlights the natural inclination of people to turn to a higher power when faced with overwhelming adversity. The act of calling upon God 'pleading and in secret' denotes a sincere and personal plea for help, reflecting the vulnerability and desperation often felt in such situations. The conditional promise to be grateful upon deliverance illustrates the transactional nature of human gratitude which, ideally, should evolve into a constant state of thankfulness, recognizing divine benevolence in all circumstances.
orig: قل من ينجيكم من ظلمات البر والبحر تدعونه تضرعا وخفية لئن أنجانا من هذه لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: Say, 'Allah delivers you from it and from every distress, yet you associate others with Him.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the human tendency to seek divine assistance during times of hardship and distress, recognizing the omnipotence of Allah in delivering them from such situations. However, it also highlights a paradoxical behavior where, despite acknowledging and experiencing Allah's saving grace, individuals still engage in the act of shirk, or associating partners with Allah. This inconsistency is pointed out as a reminder of the importance of maintaining monotheism and sincere devotion exclusively to Allah, particularly when He has demonstrated His power and mercy.
orig: قل الله ينجيكم منها ومن كل كرب ثم أنتم تشركون

translation: Say, 'He is the One capable of sending a punishment upon you from above you or from beneath your feet, or of confounding you into factions and making you taste the violence of one another. See how We explain the signs, perhaps they might understand.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and authority of God over all creation, emphasizing His ability to administer justice in various forms, either through natural disasters from above or below, or through social and communal strife that leads to internal conflict. The mentioning of 'confounding you into factions' refers to a divine act of sorting people into groups based on their beliefs and actions, which could lead to discord as a form of trial or test. By explaining His signs in different ways, God aims to offer clarity and promote understanding among people, urging them to reflect on their actions and the world around them to gain wisdom and live righteously.
orig: قل هو القادر على أن يبعث عليكم عذابا من فوقكم أو من تحت أرجلكم أو يلبسكم شيعا ويذيق بعضكم بأس بعض انظر كيف نصرف الآيات لعلهم يفقهون

translation: And your people have denied it, though it is the truth. Say, 'I am not a guardian over you.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the notion of personal responsibility in accepting the truth. Despite the truth being clear and manifest, there are those who will deny it due to their biases or ignorance. The Prophet is instructed to clarify that his role is not to compel belief or act as a custodian over their faith and decisions; rather, his duty is to convey the message. The emphasis on not being a guardian highlights the freedom of individuals to make their own choices and underscores the principle that guidance is ultimately in the hands of God.
orig: وكذب به قومك وهو الحق قل لست عليكم بوكيل

translation: For every news, there is a fixed place, and you will soon know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the notion that every event or piece of news has a determined outcome or a place in the divine plan, which is not immediately apparent to humans. The phrase 'you will soon know' suggests that the ultimate wisdom or truth behind events will eventually be unveiled, encouraging patience and trust in the unfolding of God's will.
orig: لكل نبإ مستقر وسوف تعلمون

translation: And when you see those who engage in our verses [inappropriately], turn away from them until they engage in a different topic; and if Satan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the unjust people.
interpretation: This verse counsels the believer on how to handle encounters with those who disrespect or misuse the sacred texts. It emphasizes the importance of distancing oneself from negative or blasphemous discussions to preserve one's faith and peace of mind. The verse also acknowledges human forgetfulness and the influence of negative forces like Satan, but it reminds adherents to return to the right path promptly after realization. Ultimately, it stresses the importance of avoiding the company of those who persistently act unjustly and disrespectfully towards divine guidance.
orig: وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره وإما ينسينك الشيطان فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمين

translation: And there is no blame on those who are conscious of Allah regarding their account, but it serves as a reminder so perhaps they may remain conscious.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining consciousness of Allah (taqwa) as a protective shield. It suggests that those who uphold this consciousness are absolved from worry about their ultimate reckoning, as their mindful living aligns them with divine expectations. The purpose of reminders in the form of divine revelations or life experiences is to encourage and reinforce this consciousness, ensuring continual spiritual growth and adherence to the path of righteousness.
orig: وما على الذين يتقون من حسابهم من شيء ولكن ذكرى لعلهم يتقون

translation: And leave those who take their religion as a distraction and amusement and whom worldly life has deluded. Remind with it, lest a soul be doomed because of what it has earned. It will have no protector or intercessor besides Allah, and if it offers every compensation, it will not be accepted. Those are the ones who are doomed by what they have earned. For them is a drink of boiling water and painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dangers of treating religion superficially or as a mere formality, highlighting the perilous fate awaiting those who are preoccupied with worldly affairs and neglect their spiritual obligations. It cautions against allowing oneself to be deceived by the transient pleasures of the material world, warning that such negligence can lead to eternal ruin. The verse serves as a stark reminder that there is no escaping divine justice through worldly means or intercessions. Every soul is accountable for its actions, and disregard for one’s spiritual duties leads to severe, everlasting consequences. The specific mention of 'a drink of boiling water and painful punishment' underscores the intense suffering reserved for the disbelievers who reject the truth and persist in their heedlessness. This vivid portrayal is intended to awaken the heedless and encourage a life oriented towards spiritual accountability and the earnest observance of religious precepts.
orig: وذر الذين اتخذوا دينهم لعبا ولهوا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا وذكر به أن تبسل نفس بما كسبت ليس لها من دون الله ولي ولا شفيع وإن تعدل كل عدل لا يؤخذ منها أولئك الذين أبسلوا بما كسبوا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: Say, 'Shall we call upon others besides Allah, who can neither benefit nor harm us, and [shall we] turn back on our heels after Allah has guided us, like one whom the devils have enticed [to wander] upon the earth in confusion, having companions inviting him to guidance [saying], 'Come to us?' Say, 'Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [true] guidance; and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absurdity and danger of turning away from divine guidance after receiving it. It draws a vivid picture of a person who, despite having clear guidance, allows himself to be misled, wandering aimlessly and being called to guidance by his companions yet refusing to follow. It underscores the firm stance believers should take in recognizing that genuine guidance can only come from Allah, and that deviation from this guidance is akin to submitting oneself to chaos and misguidance, much like being manipulated by devils. The reinstruction to submit to "the Lord of the worlds" reinforces the universality and ultimate authority of Allah's command, establishing that rightful submission transcends any earthly temptation or confusion.
orig: قل أندعو من دون الله ما لا ينفعنا ولا يضرنا ونرد على أعقابنا بعد إذ هدانا الله كالذي استهوته الشياطين في الأرض حيران له أصحاب يدعونه إلى الهدى ائتنا قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى وأمرنا لنسلم لرب العالمين

translation: And establish prayer and fear Him, and it is He to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining regular prayer as a means of demonstrating obedience and reverence to God. The call to 'fear Him' highlights the need for mindfulness of God's omnipresence and omnipotence, fostering a sense of accountability in believers. The phrase 'it is He to whom you will be gathered' serves as a reminder of the afterlife, where all individuals will be brought before God for judgment. This gathering underscores the inevitability of divine accountability and encourages believers to align their actions in this world with the expectations of their faith, reinforcing the significance of both prayer and piety in leading a life that prepares one for the final assembly before God.
orig: وأن أقيموا الصلاة واتقوه وهو الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: And He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth, and on the day He says, 'Be,' and it is, His word is the truth, and to Him belongs the dominion on the day the trumpet is blown. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He is the Wise, the Aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of God over creation and existence. It declares God's ability to create with a command, illustrating His omnipotence and the fact that His will is executed without fail. The mention of the trumpet refers to the Day of Judgment, highlighting God's sovereignty on that decisive day. The attributes 'Knower of the unseen and the witnessed' and 'Wise, the Aware' underscore God’s comprehensive knowledge and wisdom, reinforcing that His judgments and decrees are informed by an all-encompassing understanding that transcends human perception.
orig: وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق ويوم يقول كن فيكون قوله الحق وله الملك يوم ينفخ في الصور عالم الغيب والشهادة وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said to his father Azar, 'Do you take idols as deities? Indeed, I see you and your people in manifest error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the courageous challenge Abraham posed to his father's idolatrous practices, underscoring a critical moment where he rejected the prevalent polytheistic beliefs of his society in favor of monotheism. Abraham's address to his father is emblematic of his pivotal role in calling people away from the worship of man-made idols to the worship of the one true God. This verse emphasizes the importance of critical thinking and spiritual awakening in recognizing and correcting misguided traditions and beliefs.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه آزر أتتخذ أصناما آلهة إني أراك وقومك في ضلال مبين

translation: And thus We showed Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and the earth so that he would be among the certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of direct inspiration and divine revelation to strengthen faith. By granting Prophet Abraham a profound vision of the universe, God aimed to deepen his understanding and certainty of the divine. This act of showing the divine kingdom serves as a means to fortify faith through experiential knowledge and spiritual insight, underscored by the universal lesson that true conviction often comes from personal understanding and spiritual experiences.
orig: وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين

translation: So when the night covered him, he saw a star. He said, 'This is my lord.' But when it set, he said, 'I love not those that set.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the journey of spiritual realization and the rejection of transient objects of worship. It illustrates the process of moving from initial confusion or misguidance to a profound understanding of the impermanence and unsuitability of finite entities as objects of ultimate allegiance. The setting of the star symbolizes the fleeting nature of all physical and worldly entities, prompting a rejection of such temporal things in favor of seeking the eternal and unchanging. This can be seen as an allegory for human realization of the need for an immutable and permanent source of guidance and worship, God.
orig: فلما جن عليه الليل رأى كوكبا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لا أحب الآفلين

translation: So when he saw the moon rising, he said, 'This is my Lord.' But when it set, he said, 'If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people gone astray.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the journey of spiritual searching and the recognition of the limitations of celestial bodies as divine entities. It reflects on human vulnerability to misguidance without divine guidance. The shifting focus from the moon as a potential object of worship to recognizing its transience emphasizes the need for a constant, unfaltering source of guidance, which is only fulfilled by the Eternal God. This narrative also serves as a critique of idolatry and demonstrates the evolution of monotheistic belief, stressing the importance of relying on God's guidance to avoid the pitfalls of uncertainty and misguidance.
orig: فلما رأى القمر بازغا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لئن لم يهدني ربي لأكونن من القوم الضالين

translation: So when he saw the sun rising, he said, 'This is my lord; this is greater.' But when it set, he said, 'O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with God.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the intellectual journey of a seeker of truth, symbolically using the sun as an object of false worship to demonstrate the folly of worshipping transient entities. The rising and setting of the sun illustrate the impermanence and limitations inherent in all parts of creation compared to the divine Creator, who is eternal, unchanging, and unparalleled. This story serves as a powerful argument against polytheism and invites reflection on the supremacy and uniqueness of God, encouraging adherents to disassociate from practices or beliefs that equate God with His creation. It underscores a return to pure monotheistic worship and acknowledges the inherent human ability to recognize and reject falsehood when seeking truth earnestly.
orig: فلما رأى الشمس بازغة قال هذا ربي هذا أكبر فلما أفلت قال يا قوم إني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Indeed, I have turned my face towards He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the speaker's commitment to monotheism, dedicating their worship and life's orientation purely towards Allah, the Creator of the universe. It signifies a conscious rejection of idolatry or polytheism, symbolizing a spiritual and ethical stance that is rooted in the recognition and affirmation of one supreme creator, Allah. The phrase 'inclining toward truth' reflects an inner disposition aimed at righteousness and integrity, illustrating a way of life that is aligned with the innate nature (fitrah) that Allah has instilled in all humans.
orig: إني وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السماوات والأرض حنيفا وما أنا من المشركين

translation: And he argued with his people, saying, 'Do you argue with me concerning Allah while He has guided me? I do not fear what you associate with Him except if my Lord wills something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then remember?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of arguing against divine guidance once bestowed. The speaker confidently asserts his guidance from Allah, signifying that no worldly power or opposing views can instill fear in him, except by divine will. It accentuates that Allah's knowledge transcends all, rendering human objections insignificant. Through invoking remembrance, it also calls for recognition of Allah's omnipotent wisdom and encourages trust and conformity to the divine guidance over human conjectures.
orig: وحاجه قومه قال أتحاجوني في الله وقد هدان ولا أخاف ما تشركون به إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا وسع ربي كل شيء علما أفلا تتذكرون

translation: And how should I fear what you associate [with Him] while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has not sent down to you any authority? Which of the two parties has more right to safety, if you should know?
interpretation: This verse challenges the perspective of those who attribute partners to Allah (polytheism) without any divine authority or evidence. It highlights a logical inconsistency in their beliefs and behavior, questioning why the prophet should fear their false gods when they themselves do not fear their act of associating partners with Allah, which is a grave sin. It prompts them to reflect on who truly deserves security: those who erroneously attribute partners to Allah, risking His wrath, or those who faithfully worship Him alone. The verse calls for introspection regarding the basis and consequences of one's beliefs, stressing the importance of adhering to divine guidance and the folly of unfounded religious practices.
orig: وكيف أخاف ما أشركتم ولا تخافون أنكم أشركتم بالله ما لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: Those who believed and did not mix their faith with injustice, those will have security, and they are rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of purity in one's faith by avoiding injustices or wrongdoing, which serves as a contaminant to belief. The assurance of 'security' and being 'rightly guided' is a divine promise to those who maintain their faith untainted by unjust acts. It underscores that true faith must be accompanied by upright moral conduct, and that the internal purity of faith ensures divine protection and spiritual guidance.
orig: الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم أولئك لهم الأمن وهم مهتدون

translation: And that was Our argument which We gave to Abraham against his people. We elevate whom We will in rank, for your Lord is Wise, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine practice of empowering individuals with wisdom and clear arguments to guide and lead their communities. In Abraham's case, it refers to the unique insights and reasoning capabilities conferred upon him by God to challenge the prevailing fallacies and to promote monotheism among his idolatrous people. The phrase about elevating ranks underlines that wisdom and knowledge are the criteria God uses to elevate individuals in spiritual and moral standing. It implies that divine wisdom and knowledge are bestowed according to God’s comprehensive understanding of every individual’s capacity and potential. Consequently, the elevation of a person by God also serves as a test for others in their response to truth and divine guidance communicated through the elevated individuals.
orig: وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه نرفع درجات من نشاء إن ربك حكيم عليم

translation: And We granted him Isaac and Jacob, each of them We guided, and Noah We guided before, and among his descendants, David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron, and thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of guidance and reward from God to those who are righteous and do good deeds. The lineage mentioned showcases a tradition of prophethood and wisdom, reflecting God's ongoing mercy and support for those who uphold moral values and strive toward spiritual excellence. It punctuates the idea that divine guidance is not random but a deliberate blessing bestowed upon those who contribute positively to their communities and uphold principles of faith. The mention of these prophets underlines the varied challenges they faced, yet they remained steadfast, setting an example of perseverance rewarded by divine favor. It also serves as a reminder to the believers that good deeds and righteousness have enduring rewards, both in this life and hereafter.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب كلا هدينا ونوحا هدينا من قبل ومن ذريته داوود وسليمان وأيوب ويوسف وموسى وهارون وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And Zechariah, and John, and Jesus, and Elias; each one was of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue and righteousness of these prophets, affirming that they were exemplary in their moral and spiritual conduct. It serves as a reminder to the reader of the high standards set by prophets who were favored by God due to their piety, obedience, and dedication to truth. The mention of each by name emphasizes their individual importance and the unique role each played in their respective communities. This verse motivates believers to aspire to emulate such qualities in their own lives.
orig: وزكريا ويحيى وعيسى وإلياس كل من الصالحين

translation: And [mention] Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot - and all [of them] We preferred over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction and honor bestowed by God upon these prophets, highlighting their elevated status and the preference God gave them over others. It serves as a reminder of their piety, dedication, and the special roles they played in their respective communities as bearers of divine guidance. The mention of 'over the worlds' signifies the universal importance and exemplary nature of their missions, transcending their immediate environments to offer lessons for all of humanity.
orig: وإسماعيل واليسع ويونس ولوطا وكلا فضلنا على العالمين

translation: And from their fathers, their descendants, and their brethren, We chose them and guided them unto a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine selection and guidance bestowed upon certain individuals from among their relatives and kin, signifying that Allah's guidance is not merely based on lineage or familial connections but on His divine will and choice. It signifies a spiritual lineage of piety and righteousness that transcends biological relationships, reinforcing the importance of adhering to the path of truth and righteousness as guided by Allah.
orig: ومن آبائهم وذرياتهم وإخوانهم واجتبيناهم وهديناهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills of His servants. And if they had associated others with Him, indeed their deeds would have become worthless.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah in guiding His servants, underlining that divine guidance is a gift bestowed according to His divine wisdom and will. The latter part of the verse serves as a stern warning against the sin of shirk (associating partners with Allah), illustrating that such an act nullifies the virtues and righteous deeds one may have accumulated. This underscores the core Islamic principle of monotheism and the severe spiritual consequences of deviating from this fundamental belief.
orig: ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء من عباده ولو أشركوا لحبط عنهم ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Those are the ones whom We gave the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood. But if these disbelieve in it, indeed, We have entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility and honour of receiving divine guidance through the Scriptures, wisdom, and prophethood. It stresses the continuity of God’s message despite the disbelief of some. If the primary recipients reject this guidance, God ensures its preservation and continuation through other people who value and uphold the truth. This verse highlights the universal and enduring nature of divine truth, which transcends individual or community neglect, illustrating that divine guidance is a trust offered to humanity, and those who forsake it will see others embrace and fulfill this noble duty.
orig: أولئك الذين آتيناهم الكتاب والحكم والنبوة فإن يكفر بها هؤلاء فقد وكلنا بها قوما ليسوا بها بكافرين

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, so follow their guidance. Say, 'I ask you not for it any reward; it is only a reminder to the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of those whom Allah has rightfully guided, suggesting the path laid out by the prophets and righteous individuals. It underscores the selflessness of the Messenger, who is instructed to inform the people that he seeks no personal gain or reward from conveying this message. The core of the message is universal, intended as a reminder to all of humanity and not limited to a specific group or time. Thus, it highlights the altruistic nature of prophetic missions where the primary goal is guidance and enlightenment of all beings without any worldly compensation.
orig: أولئك الذين هدى الله فبهداهم اقتده قل لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إن هو إلا ذكرى للعالمين

translation: And they did not estimate Allah with an estimation due to Him when they said, 'Allah has not sent down anything to any human being.' Say, 'Who then sent down the Book which Moses brought as a light and guidance to the people? You make it into sheets, revealing some and concealing much. And you were taught that which you knew not, neither you nor your fathers. Say, 'Allah,' then leave them in their engrossment playing.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the theme of divine revelation and human accountability in recognizing and respecting it. It criticizes those who underestimate God's power and role as a divine revealer, specifically addressing skeptics who deny that God communicates with humanity through prophets. By referencing the scripture given to Moses, the verse emphasizes the continuity and consistency of divine guidance, which serves both as enlightenment and instruction for righteous living. The mention of people manipulating these revelations (by selectively disclosing parts of the scriptures) underscores a breach of trust and a deviation from the intended purpose of these divinely revealed texts. The instruction to proclaim 'Allah' and then to leave the skeptics to their own devices highlights a strategy of disengagement from fruitless debates, suggesting a focus on personal conviction and the avoidance of prolonged confrontation with those who are insistently dismissive or playful about sacred matters.
orig: وما قدروا الله حق قدره إذ قالوا ما أنزل الله على بشر من شيء قل من أنزل الكتاب الذي جاء به موسى نورا وهدى للناس تجعلونه قراطيس تبدونها وتخفون كثيرا وعلمتم ما لم تعلموا أنتم ولا آباؤكم قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم يلعبون

translation: And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed and confirming what came before it, that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it. Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are diligent in their prayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine legitimacy and sanctity of the Qur'an, suggesting it is a continuation and affirmation of prior scriptures. It underlines the Qur'an's role as a guide and a warning to the people of Mecca ('the Mother of Cities') and the surrounding regions, signaling its importance in spreading the message of Islam broadly. The verse also makes a clear connection between belief in the Hereafter and the commitment to prayer, suggesting that true faith is reflected in a dedication to religious practices and an awareness of life beyond the physical world. This relationship is crucial as it highlights the comprehensive commitment expected of believers, encompassing both doctrinal belief and active practice.
orig: وهذا كتاب أنزلناه مبارك مصدق الذي بين يديه ولتنذر أم القرى ومن حولها والذين يؤمنون بالآخرة يؤمنون به وهم على صلاتهم يحافظون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or says, 'It has been revealed to me,' while nothing has been revealed to him, and one who says, 'I will bring down the same as Allah has sent down'? And if you could see when the wrongdoers are in the throes of death and the angels are extending their hands, [saying], 'Discharge your souls! Today you will be awarded the punishment of degradation for what you used to claim against Allah other than the truth, and for your being arrogant towards His signs.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the grievous sin of fabricating lies about divine revelation and the severe consequences that await those who arrogantly attribute false statements to God. It underscores the sanctity and the exclusivity of divine revelation, condemning those who falsely claim prophetic inspiration or equate their words with God’s commands. The imagery of death and retribution serves as a stark warning about the spiritual and moral responsibility of truthfulness in matters of faith and the humility required before God’s signs. This verse serves both as a deterrent against deceit in religious matters and an admonishment to all to regard the sacred texts and prophetic messages with sincerity and reverence.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو قال أوحي إلي ولم يوح إليه شيء ومن قال سأنزل مثل ما أنزل الله ولو ترى إذ الظالمون في غمرات الموت والملائكة باسطو أيديهم أخرجوا أنفسكم اليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تقولون على الله غير الحق وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون

translation: And indeed you have come to us individually, just as We created you the first time, and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you. We do not see with you your intercessors, whom you claimed were partners among you. Indeed, the ties between you have been severed, and what you used to claim has strayed from you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the notion of individual accountability on the Day of Judgment, where each person will stand alone before God, devoid of any worldly possessions or status that they had been given during their earthly life. It confronts the fallacy of relying on intercessors or partners in divinity, which some might have depended on rather than direct devotion to God. The verse starkly reminds that earthly claims and associations will hold no value in the afterlife, stressing the ultimate sovereignty and oneness of God and the dissolution of worldly relations and beliefs that are not in accordance with divine truth.
orig: ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة وتركتم ما خولناكم وراء ظهوركم وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء لقد تقطع بينكم وضل عنكم ما كنتم تزعمون

translation: Indeed, Allah is the Cleaver of grain and date seeds. He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living. That is Allah, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and continual creative activity of Allah, who is portrayed as having control over the transformation of states in the natural world. The process of bringing forth life from seemingly inert matter, like seeds, allegorically underscores the broader spiritual and existential realities that define human existence and the resurrection. It invites reflection on the cycles of life and death, suggesting that what appears to be an end or lifeless also contains the potential for new beginnings. The rhetorical question at the end challenges the audience to reconsider their perspectives and the possible illusions (delusions) that might mislead them from understanding the true essence and omnipotence of Allah.
orig: إن الله فالق الحب والنوى يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ذلكم الله فأنى تؤفكون

translation: The splitter of dawn, and He made the night a rest, and the sun and the moon a calculation. That is the determination of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the manifestation of God's precise and purposeful organization in nature. The splitting of dawn symbolizes the transition from darkness to light, signifying enlightenment and hope. The designation of night as a period of rest reflects the divine intent for renewal and peace. The sun and moon functioning as methods for keeping time emphasize the meticulous and mathematical order in the universe, facilitating human life and activities. This setup, decreed by God, who is characterized as both Almighty and All-Knowing, underscores His ultimate authority and omniscience, shaping a world governed by balance and wisdom.
orig: فالق الإصباح وجعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And it is He who made for you the stars, that you may be guided by them through the darkness of the land and the sea. We have detailed Our signs for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy and guidance towards humanity through the natural world, symbolized here by the stars which serve as navigational aids in times of darkness both on land and sea. The mention of the detailing of signs for those who 'know' implies that understanding and appreciating these signs requires a certain level of insight and wisdom, hinting at the deeper spiritual and existential guidance provided by God, beyond mere physical navigation.
orig: وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: And it is He who created you from a single soul, then [provided] a dwelling place and a depository. Indeed, We have detailed the signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and origin of all humans, deriving from one soul, highlighting God's power and wisdom in creation. It underscores the divine arrangement for human life, providing physical spaces (dwelling) and spiritual or moral receptacles (depository) to facilitate human existence. The mention of meticulously detailed signs serves as an invitation for contemplation and understanding, directed towards those who seek deeper insight into the nature of creation and their purpose in life.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأكم من نفس واحدة فمستقر ومستودع قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يفقهون

translation: And it is He who sends down water from the sky, and with it We brought forth vegetation of all things. From it We brought forth green crops from which We produce grains arraigned upon each other, and from the palm trees – from their pollen – dense clusters hanging low. And [We created] gardens of grapes, olives, and pomegranates, similar in kind yet varied in look. Observe their fruit when it bears and ripens. Indeed in that are signs for people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the miraculous and diverse manifestations of God's creation, reflecting His omnipotence and meticulous planning in the natural world. The detailed description of vegetation, crops, and fruits underscores the nurturing and sustaining role of water, sent by God, which symbolizes life and growth. The variations among similar species highlight the uniqueness crafted in each of God’s creations, encouraging humans to reflect on the diversity and precision in the universe. By inviting believers to observe the maturation of fruits, the verse encourages a contemplative appreciation of the cycles of growth and fruition, recognizing these processes as signs (miracles) of God’s existence, benevolence, and divine control over the universe, which should strengthen their faith and awe towards the Creator.
orig: وهو الذي أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به نبات كل شيء فأخرجنا منه خضرا نخرج منه حبا متراكبا ومن النخل من طلعها قنوان دانية وجنات من أعناب والزيتون والرمان مشتبها وغير متشابه انظروا إلى ثمره إذا أثمر وينعه إن في ذلكم لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And they assign to Allah partners - the jinn - and created them, and they invent for Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Exalted is He and high above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse is critically addressing the practices of associating partners with Allah, particularly focusing on the attribution of familial relations to the divine, an act considered gravely erroneous in Islamic theology. By mentioning 'without knowledge,' it emphasizes that such beliefs are baseless and not supported by divine revelation or truth. The phrase 'Exalted is He and high above what they describe' underlines the transcendent majesty and uniqueness of Allah, disassociating Him from human-like attributes and familial constructs that diminish His divine essence. The verse serves as a reminder of the core monotheistic principle in Islam, which strictly negates any form of polytheism or attributions that compromise the absolute oneness of Allah.
orig: وجعلوا لله شركاء الجن وخلقهم وخرقوا له بنين وبنات بغير علم سبحانه وتعالى عما يصفون

translation: Originator of the heavens and the earth, how could He have a child when He has no consort? He created all things, and He is all-knowing of everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique and incomparable nature of God, highlighting His absolute oneness and independence. It refutes any notions of God having physical human attributes, such as parenthood, which would suggest dependence or limitations. The reference to God as the creator of everything reinforces His omnipotence and omniscience, indicating that nothing occurs without His knowledge or outside His sovereign will. Overall, the verse asserts the transcendence and incomparability of God, challenging human tendencies to anthropomorphize the divine.
orig: بديع السماوات والأرض أنى يكون له ولد ولم تكن له صاحبة وخلق كل شيء وهو بكل شيء عليم

translation: That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him, and He is over all things a Trustee.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the foundational Islamic belief in the oneness and sovereignty of God (Allah). It underscores the unique status of Allah as the sole creator and sustainer of the universe, which establishes His exclusive right to worship. The reference to Allah as a 'Trustee' over everything reiterates His all-encompassing knowledge, power, and authority over all creation, and it reminds believers of the comprehensive and meticulous care with which He manages all affairs of the universe.
orig: ذلكم الله ربكم لا إله إلا هو خالق كل شيء فاعبدوه وهو على كل شيء وكيل

translation: No vision can grasp Him, but His grasp is over all vision; and He is the Subtle, the Aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and incomprehensibility of God. It conveys that God's essence and being are beyond human perception and understanding—no visual faculty can capture or encompass His nature. Despite this, God has complete awareness and perception of all things, indicating His omniscience. The attributes 'the Subtle' and 'the Aware' further highlight His gentle, yet profound, presence in everything and His exhaustive knowledge of all creation, manifesting His closeness to everything while being beyond physical senses.
orig: لا تدركه الأبصار وهو يدرك الأبصار وهو اللطيف الخبير

translation: There have indeed come to you insights from your Lord. So, whoever sees, it is for their own benefit; and whoever is blind, it is to their own detriment, and I am not a keeper over you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of individuals for their own actions, particularly in response to the divine guidance and insights provided by God. It underscores the concept that each person has the autonomy to accept or reject guidance, and the consequences of their choices directly impact their own souls. The Prophet's role is clarified as a messenger and deliverer of God's revelations, not as one who is charged with enforcing belief or overseeing the spiritual affairs of individuals. This highlights the essential Islamic teaching of personal accountability in matters of faith and righteousness.
orig: قد جاءكم بصائر من ربكم فمن أبصر فلنفسه ومن عمي فعليها وما أنا عليكم بحفيظ

translation: And thus We diversify the signs so that they may say, 'You have studied,' and so We may make it clear to a people who know.
interpretation: This verse underscores the purpose of diversification and varying presentation of divine signs and revelations to challenge the perceptions and provoke thought among people. It acknowledges the skepticism of the disbelievers who dismiss the Prophet's knowledge as mere study or learning from others, rather than as divine revelation. At the same time, it highlights the intent to clarify and elucidate these signs for those who genuinely seek knowledge and understand. Thus, the verse impresses upon the significance of wisdom, discernment, and the readiness to learn from divine signs among those who are intellectually and spiritually prepared.
orig: وكذلك نصرف الآيات وليقولوا درست ولنبينه لقوم يعلمون

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord, there is no deity except Him, and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in monotheistic belief, urging adherence to divine guidance while consciously ignoring and distancing oneself from those who associate partners with God. It highlights the exclusivity of God's sovereignty and the need for believers to focus on their spiritual journey without being influenced or swayed by practices and beliefs that contradict the essence of monotheism.
orig: اتبع ما أوحي إليك من ربك لا إله إلا هو وأعرض عن المشركين

translation: And if Allah had so willed, they would not have associated partners with Him; and We have not made you a guardian over them, nor are you a manager of their affairs.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine will and human autonomy in actions, highlighting that God’s will is supreme, and if He had willed, people would not commit the sin of associating partners with Him. However, the allowance of such actions without divine intervention indicates the freedom given to humans to make their own choices. Moreover, the verse serves to alleviate the burden of responsibility from the Prophet (or the addressed) by clarifying that his role is not to control or oversee the actions of the people, which emphasizes the principle that guidance is provided, but judgment and accountability are ultimately individual.
orig: ولو شاء الله ما أشركوا وما جعلناك عليهم حفيظا وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: And do not insult those they invoke other than Allah, lest they insult Allah in enmity without knowledge. Thus We have adorned for every community their deeds; then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining respect and refrainment from offensive speech towards those who follow different beliefs or deities. The instruction reflects a proactive approach to prevent reciprocal disrespect and potential defamation of divine entities due to ignorance or retaliation. It also sheds light on the principle of divine justice, highlighting that regardless of their beliefs and actions, all people will ultimately return to God, who will judge them based solely on their deeds. This underscores the theme of accountability and the transcendental surveillance of human actions, encouraging a conduct that promotes peace and mutual respect among diverse religious communities.
orig: ولا تسبوا الذين يدعون من دون الله فيسبوا الله عدوا بغير علم كذلك زينا لكل أمة عملهم ثم إلى ربهم مرجعهم فينبئهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say, 'The signs are only with Allah, and what will make you perceive that even if it came, they would not believe?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism and the conditional faith exhibited by some, who insist that they would believe if only a miraculous sign were shown to them. The verse highlights the futility of such demands, emphasizing that divine signs are under the sole discretion of Allah and that human understanding or readiness to believe might not necessarily change even if a sign is given. This response underscores the deeper issue of a hardened heart and a closed mind, which may not be receptive to guidance regardless of the evidence presented. It also serves as a reminder that genuine faith should not be contingent upon witnessing miracles but should be grounded in trusting Allah's wisdom and timing.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءتهم آية ليؤمنن بها قل إنما الآيات عند الله وما يشعركم أنها إذا جاءت لا يؤمنون

translation: And We overturn their hearts and their eyes, just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine response to persistent disbelief and rebellion against God's signs. When individuals repeatedly neglect or deny the truth after it has been made clear to them, their spiritual perception becomes obscured, symbolized here by the overturning of hearts and eyes. This metaphor suggests a deep disorientation or confusion in both their emotional and perceptual faculties, indicating a state where recognizing truth becomes increasingly difficult. The continuation of their wandering in transgression emphasizes that persisting in such a state after clear evidence has been presented leads to a self-imposed isolation from divine guidance, reinforcing their deviance and failure to see the path of righteousness.
orig: ونقلب أفئدتهم وأبصارهم كما لم يؤمنوا به أول مرة ونذرهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: Even if We had sent down angels to them, and the dead spoke to them, and We gathered everything before them, they would not believe unless Allah wills. But most of them are ignorant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound impact of divine will on human belief and highlights the limitations of signs and miracles in guiding those whose hearts are closed to faith. It suggests that belief in God is not merely a result of witnessing supernatural events or miracles, but rather is rooted in an openness to divine guidance, which itself is a grace bestowed by God. The term 'ignorant' here refers to a lack of understanding or awareness about the spiritual truth and divine guidance, rather than just lack of information or education.
orig: ولو أننا نزلنا إليهم الملائكة وكلمهم الموتى وحشرنا عليهم كل شيء قبلا ما كانوا ليؤمنوا إلا أن يشاء الله ولكن أكثرهم يجهلون

translation: And thus We have made for every prophet enemies - devils among mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another decorative speech in deception. But if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and what they invent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal challenge faced by prophets wherein they encounter opposition not just from humans but also from supernatural beings, the jinn. The 'decorative speech' refers to enticing but misleading arguments used to sway people from the truth. The passage underscores divine permission in these adversarial dynamics, suggesting that such challenges are part of a larger divine plan navigating free will and the testing of faith. It encourages disengagement from falsehood and focuses on upholding truth without being swayed by fabrications, regardless of their appeal or the stature of their proponents.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا شياطين الإنس والجن يوحي بعضهم إلى بعض زخرف القول غرورا ولو شاء ربك ما فعلوه فذرهم وما يفترون

translation: And so that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline towards it, and that they may be pleased with it, and commit what they are to commit.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the subtle ways in which disbelief can manifest in one's actions and inclinations. It suggests that those who deny the existence of an afterlife are prone to being swayed by falsehoods or inaccuracies, seeking satisfaction in them because these align with their worldly desires or preconceptions. The phrase 'commit what they are to commit' underscores that such individuals are likely to engage in actions that reflect their disbelief and lead them away from divine guidance and truth. This highlights the inherent risks in choosing a path based on denial of the ultimate accountability.
orig: ولتصغى إليه أفئدة الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وليرضوه وليقترفوا ما هم مقترفون

translation: Should I seek a judge other than Allah while it is He who has sent down to you the Book, explained in detail? Those to whom We gave the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supremacy and exclusivity of divine guidance through the Qur'an, which is portrayed as the ultimate and detailed source of truth and law. It underscores the need for believers to rely solely on God’s judgment and reject other sources that may lead to doubt. Additionally, it affirms the acknowledgment by the learned recipients of previous scriptures that the Qur'an is indeed from God and aligns with the truth. The verse admonishes believers against skepticism regarding the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an.
orig: أفغير الله أبتغي حكما وهو الذي أنزل إليكم الكتاب مفصلا والذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعلمون أنه منزل من ربك بالحق فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice. There is no altering His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute, unchangeable, and reliable nature of God's words, which are both truthful and just. It highlights the divine attributes of omniscience and omnipresence, suggesting that God's decrees are perfectly aligned with truth and fairness, and are beyond human modification or error. The characteristics of God being all-hearing and all-knowing reinforce His awareness and understanding of all matters, assuring believers of His perfect governance and oversight.
orig: وتمت كلمت ربك صدقا وعدلا لا مبدل لكلماته وهو السميع العليم

translation: And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah. They follow nothing but conjecture, and they do nothing but lie.
interpretation: This verse underscores the danger of following popular opinion or majority sentiment without critical evaluation, particularly when such views contradict divine guidance. It emphasizes that many people base their beliefs and actions on mere speculation and falsehoods rather than truth and divine instruction. The verse cautions against leaning on societal norms that deviate from spiritual and moral principles as dictated by Allah, highlighting the importance of maintaining integrity and adherence to one's faith amidst widespread misguidance.
orig: وإن تطع أكثر من في الأرض يضلوك عن سبيل الله إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of the guided ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of God, particularly in understanding the spiritual state and actions of human beings. It highlights that God is fully aware of those who deviate from the righteous path as well as those who remain steadfast in guidance. This serves as a reminder of God's surveillance and perfect knowledge of all human affairs, suggesting that divine justice is informed by complete and unerring awareness of each individual's circumstances and choices.
orig: إن ربك هو أعلم من يضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: So eat of that which Allah's name has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming only those foods on which the name of Allah has been invoked, which signifies the practice of eating halally slaughtered meat according to Islamic law. The condition 'if you are believers in His signs' connects the act of eating such foods to a demonstration of faith and acknowledgement of the signs and commandments of Allah. It underscores that abiding by the dietary laws prescribed in Islam is not merely a cultural norm but a manifestation of one's faith and obedience to divine law.
orig: فكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه إن كنتم بآياته مؤمنين

translation: And why should you not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, when He has explained to you in detail what is forbidden to you, except under compulsion of necessity? But indeed, many people mislead others with their desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is best aware of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to dietary laws prescribed in Islam, underscoring the necessity of invoking Allah's name on what is consumed. It highlights the distinction between lawful and forbidden foods, urging compliance unless dire circumstances intervene. The verse also critiques those who, driven by baseless personal desires, misguide others regarding these regulations. Allah's omniscience is affirmed, especially concerning those who transgress His commandments.
orig: وما لكم ألا تأكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه وقد فصل لكم ما حرم عليكم إلا ما اضطررتم إليه وإن كثيرا ليضلون بأهوائهم بغير علم إن ربك هو أعلم بالمعتدين

translation: And abandon what is outwardly of sin and what is inwardly of it. Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to perpetrate
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of refraining from all forms of sin, both visible and hidden. It highlights the comprehensive nature of accountability, where every action, whether public or private, is subject to divine scrutiny. The verse serves as a reminder that consequences are not limited to earthly reckonings but extend to divine justice, where individuals will be recompensed in accordance with the magnitude and nature of their actions. It stresses the moral responsibility of every individual to actively avoid sins and wrongful deeds as part of their spiritual and ethical development.
orig: وذروا ظاهر الإثم وباطنه إن الذين يكسبون الإثم سيجزون بما كانوا يقترفون

translation: And do not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for it is indeed disobedience. And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to argue with you; and if you obey them, then you are indeed associating others with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming only what is lawful and sanctified in Islam, specifically highlighting the necessity of mentioning Allah's name over food before consuming it. It underscores the spiritual implications of eating such food, equating its consumption without God’s name as an act of disobedience and deviation from the righteous path. This adherence to dietary laws is not merely about physical well-being but is deeply tied to the spiritual purity and obedience to God. The verse also warns against the influence of evil forces that seek to lead believers astray through debate and intellectual sophistry. The implication is that such forces aim to normalize and justify disobedience by making the unlawful appear lawful, leading to the sin of shirk, or associating partners with Allah. Thus, it stresses vigilance and discernment in both dietary practices and spiritual beliefs, aligning both with divine commands to maintain both personal integrity and communal harmony.
orig: ولا تأكلوا مما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه وإنه لفسق وإن الشياطين ليوحون إلى أوليائهم ليجادلوكم وإن أطعتموهم إنكم لمشركون

translation: Is he who was dead and We gave him life and made for him light by which to walk among the people like one who is in darkness, never to emerge from it? Thus it has been made attractive to the disbelievers what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse discusses the transformation of a person from a state of ignorance or disbelief (symbolized by death) to a state of guidance and enlightenment (symbolized by life and light). The light represents guidance that allows the person to navigate through life uprightly among others. The comparison made here emphasizes the marked difference between someone blessed with divine guidance and someone entrenched in spiritual darkness, indicative of disbelief, where they are unable to find their way out of their misconceptions and wrong actions. Thus, the verse highlights the beauty and value of divine guidance and the plight of those who remain in denial, for whom their wrong actions may seem appealing.
orig: أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها كذلك زين للكافرين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And thus We have placed in every town the greatest of its criminals to scheme therein, but they only scheme against themselves, and they do not perceive it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in allowing the persistence of evil and corruption within communities through their own worst elements. It serves as a reflection on the self-destructive nature of wickedness and deceit. Those who engage in corrupt and malicious acts are ultimately setting up their own downfall, even though they may be unaware of it. The verse also underscores a profound irony in the actions of the wicked: while they believe they are orchestrating harm against others, their actions are in fact a detriment to themselves. This can be viewed as a form of divine justice where evil doers are unwittingly trapped by the consequences of their own misconduct.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا في كل قرية أكابر مجرميها ليمكروا فيها وما يمكرون إلا بأنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: And when a sign comes to them, they say, 'We will not believe until we are given the same as what was given to the messengers of Allah.' Allah knows best where to place His message.
