orig: إن تستفتحوا فقد جاءكم الفتح وإن تنتهوا فهو خير لكم وإن تعودوا نعد ولن تغني عنكم فئتكم شيئا ولو كثرت وأن الله مع المؤمنين

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger and do not turn away from him while you hear.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of active and conscious obedience to God and His Messenger, emphasizing that true believers must adhere to divine guidance especially when they are aware of it and can comprehend the message. The instruction not to 'turn away' highlights the need for steadfastness and commitment in one's faith, particularly when one is not ignorant of the teachings. It is a call to prioritize divine commands over distractions or temptations that might lead one astray.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله ورسوله ولا تولوا عنه وأنتم تسمعون

translation: And do not be like those who say, 'We hear,' but they do not listen.
interpretation: This verse serves as a caution against hypocrisy and superficiality in faith. It criticizes those who profess to listen to guidance and truth but fail to internalize or act upon it. The emphasis is on the importance of sincere adherence to ethical and spiritual teachings, rather than mere verbal acknowledgment. It urges believers to genuinely engage with their faith and its teachings, ensuring that their actions reflect their words, promoting integrity and authenticity in the practice of religion.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين قالوا سمعنا وهم لا يسمعون

translation: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not use reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of using reason and understanding in one's life. It highlights that those who do not employ their faculties of reasoning are likened to the least favorable of creatures. The mention of being 'deaf' and 'dumb' may not necessarily refer to physical conditions but symbolically points to those who, despite having the capability, choose not to listen to guidance or articulate reason. It serves as a stark reminder of the value of intellect and comprehension in discerning truth and leading a responsible life in accordance with divine guidance.
orig: إن شر الدواب عند الله الصم البكم الذين لا يعقلون

translation: And if Allah had known any good in them, He would indeed have made them listen; and even if He had made them listen, they would still have turned away, obstinately persisting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that divine guidance is not arbitrarily withheld but is contingent upon the receptiveness and the inherent qualities of individuals. It suggests that merely receiving guidance is not sufficient if the disposition to accept and act on it is lacking. Those whose hearts are closed to guidance will resist it even if it is made accessible to them. The verse underlines the interplay between divine omniscience and human free will, underscoring a deeper philosophical assertion that guidance must be sought and welcomed, not just provided.
orig: ولو علم الله فيهم خيرا لأسمعهم ولو أسمعهم لتولوا وهم معرضون

translation: O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life; and know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart and that to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and responsiveness to divine guidance, symbolized through the call of Allah and His Messenger. It highlights that true life and vitality in one's existence come through following this guidance. The mention of Allah intervening between a man and his heart signifies that divine influence can redirect or influence one's intentions and feelings, reminding believers of the profound control and authority Allah holds over human inner affairs. The concluding part of the verse serves as a reminder of the afterlife, where all individuals will be accountable for their responses and actions in this world.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا استجيبوا لله وللرسول إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه وأنه إليه تحشرون

translation: And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively, and know that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being aware and cautious of societal or communal trials and tribulations that are not limited to the wrongdoers alone but can affect everyone. It serves as a reminder that the consequences of injustice or wrongdoing can extend beyond the perpetrators to the wider community. The verse also serves to remind individuals of the severity of Allah's punishment and the need for all to uphold justice and righteousness, thereby preventing any form of collective suffering due to the misdeeds of a few.
orig: واتقوا فتنة لا تصيبن الذين ظلموا منكم خاصة واعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب

translation: And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people might abduct you, but He sheltered you, supported you with His help, and provided you with good things that you might be thankful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the mercy and protection Allah extends to His believers in times of vulnerability and fear. It emphasizes the transformation from a state of weakness and fear to one of safety and strength through divine support. The provision of 'good things' is not only a reference to physical sustenance but also to spiritual blessings and well-being, cultivating an attitude of gratitude among the believers toward Allah. This narrative serves to remind the believers of their humble beginnings and the continuous support of Allah, encouraging them to maintain a grateful disposition for His ongoing favours and interventions in their lives.
orig: واذكروا إذ أنتم قليل مستضعفون في الأرض تخافون أن يتخطفكم الناس فآواكم وأيدكم بنصره ورزقكم من الطيبات لعلكم تشكرون

translation: O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know [the consequence].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of maintaining trustworthiness in all aspects of life, particularly in matters where God and His Messenger are involved. It underscores the moral and spiritual responsibility of believers to uphold integrity and to be conscious of their duties towards God, His Messenger, and the trusts (amana) they hold, which could range from secrets to responsibilities assigned to them. The phrase 'while you know' highlights the accountability of those who are aware of the implications of their actions and still choose to betray, thus deepening their sin. The verse serves as a stern reminder of the ethical framework within which believers are expected to operate, anchoring trust and honesty as foundational virtues in a faithful community.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تخونوا الله والرسول وتخونوا أماناتكم وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And know that your possessions and your children are but a trial and that Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient nature of worldly assets and familial relationships, reminding believers that these are tests of faith and devotion. It encourages the prioritization of spiritual growth and commitment to God, highlighting that true and lasting rewards are found with Allah, beyond the ephemeral temptations of earthly life.
orig: واعلموا أنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة وأن الله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion (to judge between right and wrong), and will expiate for you your sins, and forgive you; and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound spiritual and ethical rewards that come from fearing and being conscious of Allah. It suggests that true believers who live their lives in accordance with divine guidance are blessed with 'a criterion,' which refers to an innate ability to distinguish between truth and falsehood, a vital tool in navigating life's moral complexities. Furthermore, the verse underscores Allah's mercy and generosity, as He promises to cleanse believers of their sins and offer forgiveness. This is indicative of the transformative impact of piety on a believer's life, not only in ensuring moral clarity but also in securing divine forgiveness, thus leading to a life aligned with divine will and favor.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تتقوا الله يجعل لكم فرقانا ويكفر عنكم سيئاتكم ويغفر لكم والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you, or kill you, or expel you. And they plot and plan, and Allah also plans. And Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: This verse highlights the protective and supreme authority of Allah over human affairs. It reflects on the challenges and threats faced by the Prophet Muhammad from his opponents. Despite their plots to harm or thwart him, the verse reassures believers that Allah is in control and His plans are superior to those of humans. This assures believers of divine support and guidance in the face of opposition and adversity, emphasizing trust in Allah's wisdom and mastery over all situations.
orig: وإذ يمكر بك الذين كفروا ليثبتوك أو يقتلوك أو يخرجوك ويمكرون ويمكر الله والله خير الماكرين

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, 'We have heard [this]; if we wanted, we could say something like this. This is nothing but the legends of the former peoples.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the reaction of skeptics or disbelievers when they hear the Quranic verses. They dismiss them as mere stories or legends that have been passed down from previous generations. Their response reflects a closed mindset and an unwillingness to consider the divine origin of the Quran. The verse highlights their arrogance and the idea that they believe they possess the capability to produce similar words, underestimating the uniqueness and profoundness of the divine message. It serves as a critique of their superficial engagement with the text and their denial of its spiritual and moral depth.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا قالوا قد سمعنا لو نشاء لقلنا مثل هذا إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: And when they said, 'O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down stones upon us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stubbornness and disbelief of those who, despite being presented with the truth of the divine message, chose to challenge and mock God's revelations instead of reflecting on them. Their demand for stones to rain down or a painful punishment is an expression of their disbelief and resistance to faith, reflecting a provocative attitude towards divine guidance. It serves as a warning about the consequences of arrogance and rejecting truth when it is clearly presented.
orig: وإذ قالوا اللهم إن كان هذا هو الحق من عندك فأمطر علينا حجارة من السماء أو ائتنا بعذاب أليم

translation: And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor will He punish them while they seek forgiveness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and forbearance of Allah, emphasizing the protective presence of the Prophet Muhammad among his people and the power of seeking forgiveness. It underscores that divine punishment is withheld not only due to the sanctifying presence of a prophet but also due to the act of istighfar (seeking forgiveness). This reflects on the importance of communal righteousness and individual repentance in averting divine wrath, suggesting that mercy is profoundly tied to both the leaders' righteousness and the followers' sincere repentance.
orig: وما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم وما كان الله معذبهم وهم يستغفرون

translation: And why should Allah not punish them while they obstruct [people] from the Sacred Mosque, and they were not its guardians? Indeed, its guardians are only the righteous, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse stresses the divine rationale for potentially punishing those who hinder believers' access to the Sacred Mosque, underscoring that custodianship of such sacred sites is a responsibility reserved for those who uphold righteousness and piety. The verse highlights a disconnect between the self-appointed guardians and the truly deserving guardians as defined by their piety, suggesting a broader commentary on the misuse of religious authority and the ignorance that often accompanies wrongful claims to spiritual leadership.
orig: وما لهم ألا يعذبهم الله وهم يصدون عن المسجد الحرام وما كانوا أولياءه إن أولياؤه إلا المتقون ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands. So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the hollow and superficial rituals performed by the disbelievers at the sacred house (Kaaba). It highlights the lack of sincerity and true spiritual engagement in their actions, which were reduced to mere noise and physical gestures (whistling and clapping). The verse serves as a stern warning and a reminder of the consequences of disregarding true faith and the essence of worship. It underscores that divine retribution is a result of their disbelief and mockery of sincere religious practices.
orig: وما كان صلاتهم عند البيت إلا مكاء وتصدية فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [others] from the way of Allah. They will spend it, then it will become a source of regret for them, then they will be overcome, and those who disbelieved will be gathered to Hell.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility and eventual regret associated with using material wealth to oppose divine guidance. It serves as a cautionary reminder that worldly investments against spiritual truths not only fail but lead to profound remorse and ultimate defeat. The reference to gathering in Hell underscores the severe consequences awaiting those who persist in disbelief and work against the path decreed by Allah, highlighting the stark contrast between transient worldly gains and enduring spiritual outcomes.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ينفقون أموالهم ليصدوا عن سبيل الله فسينفقونها ثم تكون عليهم حسرة ثم يغلبون والذين كفروا إلى جهنم يحشرون

translation: So that Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good, and pile the wicked one upon another and place them all together in Hell. Those are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine process of separating the inherently evil from the inherently good among humans, demonstrating God's omniscient judgment. The wicked are not only distinguished but are also accumulated, signifying the magnitude of their stray from righteousness, leading to collective punishment. Their culmination in Hell underscores the severe consequences of their moral choices, illustrating the ultimate loss as being distanced from divine mercy.
orig: ليميز الله الخبيث من الطيب ويجعل الخبيث بعضه على بعض فيركمه جميعا فيجعله في جهنم أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Say to those who disbelieve, if they cease (from disbelief), their past will be forgiven; but if they revert, then the previous ways have already passed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine mercy and forgiveness, contingent upon the cessation of disbelief and the abandonment of previous rebellious behaviors. It underscores a pivotal Islamic theme: the opportunity for redemption and forgiveness from God if one turns away from disbelief and doubts towards faith and obedience. However, it also warns of the consequence of reverting to old ways, suggesting that the outcomes of such actions are as those experienced by past communities who persisted in disbelief and were then subject to divine justice.
orig: قل للذين كفروا إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف وإن يعودوا فقد مضت سنت الأولين

translation: And fight them until there is no fitnah (persecution) and the religion, all of it, is for Allah. And if they cease, then indeed, Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of religious persecution and the need to fight against it to ensure the freedom of worship and the establishment of monotheism. It instructs believers to combat forces that threaten the practice and prevalence of their faith until such threats are eliminated and the sovereignty of divine law is acknowledged universally. The cessation of opposition by adversaries prompts an end to hostility, emphasizing God’s continual awareness and judgment of all human actions.
orig: وقاتلوهم حتى لا تكون فتنة ويكون الدين كله لله فإن انتهوا فإن الله بما يعملون بصير

translation: And if they turn away, then know that Allah is your Protector – an excellent Protector and an excellent Helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unwavering support and protection Allah provides to believers, especially when they face opposition or abandonment from others. It highlights the supremacy of relying on Allah over all others, affirming that His guardianship and assistance are unparalleled and the most beneficial.
orig: وإن تولوا فاعلموا أن الله مولاكم نعم المولى ونعم النصير

translation: And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, then indeed, for Allah is one fifth of it and for the Messenger, for close relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the traveler, if you have believed in Allah and what We sent down to Our servant on the day of criterion - the day when the two forces met. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of equitable distribution of gains, particularly from war, underscoring the need for a system where resources are shared among various segments of society, including religious authorities, family, and those in need. It connects the legitimacy of this distribution directly to the faith of the believers in divine revelation and justice. Moreover, it highlights God's comprehensive power and authority, thus positioning this directive within the broader scheme of divine will and the cosmic order.
orig: واعلموا أنما غنمتم من شيء فأن لله خمسه وللرسول ولذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل إن كنتم آمنتم بالله وما أنزلنا على عبدنا يوم الفرقان يوم التقى الجمعان والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: When you were on the near bank, and they were on the far one, and the caravan was below you; and if you had made an appointment to meet, you would certainly have differed about the time of the meeting; but [it happened as it did] so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done. That those who were to perish might perish upon evidence, and those who were to live might live upon evidence. And indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the preordained nature of events where divine wisdom dictates outcomes beyond human control. It emphasizes that human plans are subject to Allah’s will, which ensures that every occurrence serves a greater purpose. This purpose includes distinguishing between those who uphold truth and righteousness and those who do not, based on clear evidence. The verse reinforces the idea of divine justice and omniscience, suggesting that Allah's decrees are based on all-encompassing knowledge and perfect listening, ensuring that reality unfolds in a manner that aligns with divine justice and wisdom.
orig: إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا وهم بالعدوة القصوى والركب أسفل منكم ولو تواعدتم لاختلفتم في الميعاد ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيى من حي عن بينة وإن الله لسميع عليم

translation: When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few; and had He shown them as many, you would surely have been discouraged, and you would surely have disputed in (making) the decision; but Allah saved (you). Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom and mercy of Allah in managing the perceptions and emotions of believers to maintain unity and resolve among them. It suggests that Allah's intervention in altering the vision of the believers, making a daunting enemy appear numerically smaller, prevented demoralization and internal conflict that could have arisen from perceiving overwhelming odds. The verse reinforces the theme that Allah is all-knowing and understands the deepest fears and inclinations of human hearts, thereby orchestrating events in such a way that serves a greater good and fulfills His divine plan while taking into account human psychological limitations.
orig: إذ يريكهم الله في منامك قليلا ولو أراكهم كثيرا لفشلتم ولتنازعتم في الأمر ولكن الله سلم إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And [remember] when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes and He made you [appear as] few in their eyes that Allah might accomplish a matter already destined. And to Allah, matters are returned.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the psychological aspects of warfare and the divine influence on human perceptions. It suggests that God can alter perceptions to influence the outcome of events, which underscores the principle that human efforts are intertwined with divine will. The mention of destiny ('a matter already destined') highlights the belief that certain events are preordained by God, irrespective of human actions. The phrase 'to Allah, matters are returned' reinforces the concept of divine sovereignty, emphasizing that the ultimate control over all affairs rests with God. Thus, the verse encourages believers to recognize the power of divine intervention and the predetermined nature of certain events, fostering reliance and trust in God's supreme authority.
orig: وإذ يريكموهم إذ التقيتم في أعينكم قليلا ويقللكم في أعينهم ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O you who have believed, when you encounter a group, stand firm and remember Allah much that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and the remembrance of Allah during challenging encounters or conflicts. It suggests that spiritual resilience and a constant mindfulness of the divine presence can significantly contribute to one's success. The call to 'remember Allah much' indicates that victory and prosperity are not merely achieved through physical or strategic prowess, but through spiritual endurance and integrity. The invocation of belief at the outset underscores that this directive is particularly significant for those who profess faith, linking their spiritual commitment directly to their earthly challenges and triumphs.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا لقيتم فئة فاثبتوا واذكروا الله كثيرا لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And obey Allah and His messenger, and do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength departs; and be patient, indeed Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity and obedience in achieving success. Disputes and disagreements among individuals can lead to a loss of collective strength and morale, which are crucial for overcoming challenges. It stresses the virtue of patience and reassures that perseverance is supported by divine accompaniment, suggesting that enduring difficulties while maintaining faith leads to spiritual and possibly material success.
orig: وأطيعوا الله ورسوله ولا تنازعوا فتفشلوا وتذهب ريحكم واصبروا إن الله مع الصابرين

translation: And do not be like those who left their homes arrogantly and to be seen by people and who hinder others from the path of Allah, for Allah encompasses all that they do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a caution against hypocrisy and arrogance. It criticizes those who act with the intention of being seen and praised by others, rather than seeking the pleasure of Allah. The act of leaving their homes arrogantly refers to actions done for show, rather than genuine commitment to faith. The reference to hindering others from the path of Allah indicates the negative influence these behaviors can have on the community and on individuals' spiritual journeys. The verse concludes with a reminder of Allah's omnipresence and omniscience, emphasizing that no action, however public or hidden, escapes His notice.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين خرجوا من ديارهم بطرا ورئاء الناس ويصدون عن سبيل الله والله بما يعملون محيط

translation: And when Satan made their deeds seem pleasing to them and said, 'No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am indeed your protector.' But when the two groups saw each other, he turned on his heels and said, 'I disavow you; indeed, I see what you do not see; indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in penalty.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deceptive nature of Satan and his tendency to abandon humans when they rely on his promises. It serves as a warning about the perils of succumbing to temptations that seem appealing but are ultimately harmful. The instance of Satan initially providing assurance and then distancing himself at a critical moment underscores his unreliability and the illusion of security he provides. Furthermore, it highlights the importance of vigilance and reliance on Allah’s guidance rather than being misled by false promises. Satan’s fear of Allah despite his rebellion is indicative of Allah’s omnipotence and the inevitable accountability that every being, including deceitful ones, must face.
orig: وإذ زين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم وقال لا غالب لكم اليوم من الناس وإني جار لكم فلما تراءت الفئتان نكص على عقبيه وقال إني بريء منكم إني أرى ما لا ترون إني أخاف الله والله شديد العقاب

translation: When the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease, say, 'These [believers] are deluded by their religion.' But whoever relies upon Allah, then indeed Allah is Mighty, Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the mockery and skepticism directed towards believers by hypocrites and those harboring doubts or corrupt intentions within their hearts. It underscores the superficial judgment and misunderstanding by the nonbelievers concerning the depth and sincerity of the believers' faith. Conversely, the verse reinforces the strength and prudence in wholly trusting Allah's wisdom and might. It reminds believers that reliance on Allah, despite external skepticism or internal trials, aligns them with divine strength and wisdom that surpasses human frailties and societal judgments.
orig: إذ يقول المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض غر هؤلاء دينهم ومن يتوكل على الله فإن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: And if you could see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved, striking their faces and their backs, saying, 'Taste the punishment of the burning fire.'
interpretation: This verse vividly illustrates the consequences that await those who deny the truth in the afterlife. The physical striking of the faces and backs by angels symbolizes the severe and unavoidable nature of divine retribution. This serves as a stern warning about the reality of the hereafter and the stark differences in outcomes based on one's beliefs and actions in this world. It emphasizes that the punishment of the disbelievers is both a physical and spiritual experience, meant to be a direct result of their denial and a manifestation of divine justice.
orig: ولو ترى إذ يتوفى الذين كفروا الملائكة يضربون وجوههم وأدبارهم وذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: That is because of what your hands have sent forth, and Allah is not unjust to the servants.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine justice and individual accountability. It suggests that the consequences or the situation one faces are a direct result of one's own actions. Allah, being supremely just, does not wrong His servants; instead, the outcomes they face are fair recompenses for their deeds. It serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and their repercussions, reinforcing the teaching that nothing unjust or arbitrary will be imposed by God, thereby emphasizing the moral responsibility of individuals to choose righteousness.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت أيديكم وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: Like the behavior of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they denied the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed, Allah is powerful, severe in punishment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of persistently denying and disregarding the signs and guidance of Allah, as exemplified by the people of Pharaoh and those before them. Their denial led to their downfall and serves as a stern warning about the might of Allah in dealing with persistent wrongdoers through severe punishment. It highlights the divine justice that holds accountable those who transgress the limits set by God, reaffirming the importance of respecting and adhering to divine guidance to avoid such severe repercussions.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كفروا بآيات الله فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم إن الله قوي شديد العقاب

translation: That is because Allah would not change a favor which He had bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves. And indeed, Allah is Hearing, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine consistency and human accountability. It suggests that God's blessings and favors to a community are stable and enduring, conditional primarily on the behavior and the inner state of the individuals within that community. The changing of divine favor is directly contingent upon the people's own transformation - specifically, a negative alteration in their spiritual or moral condition. This underscores a broader theological theme where human agency plays a crucial role in the continuation of divine grace. Moreover, the attributes of God as 'Hearing' and 'Knowing' highlight His intimate awareness of human conditions and actions, implying that nothing escapes His notice and that He responds justly based on comprehensive knowledge of all circumstances.
orig: ذلك بأن الله لم يك مغيرا نعمة أنعمها على قوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وأن الله سميع عليم

translation: Like the behavior of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, and We drowned the people of Pharaoh, and all of them were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of persistent denial and rejection of divine signs and guidance. It highlights a pattern observed in history, where civilizations that persistently engaged in wrongdoing, especially in the context of rejecting divine guidance, faced severe consequences. The reference to the destruction of such peoples serves as a warning that persistent injustice and denial of truth can lead to downfall and divine retribution. The drowning of Pharaoh’s people, a notable event in Islamic teachings, underlines the theme of accountability and the inevitable outcome of tyrannical behavior and oppression. It reminds the believers and readers about the importance of adhering to divine guidance and ethical conduct to avoid such fates.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كذبوا بآيات ربهم فأهلكناهم بذنوبهم وأغرقنا آل فرعون وكل كانوا ظالمين

translation: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who have disbelieved, and they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual and moral bankruptcy of those who persistently reject faith in God. It categorizes them as the lowest among creatures, not based on their physical nature, but due to their deliberate choice to deny the truth and their steadfast refusal to believe. The verse underscores the significance of faith in defining one's standing with God and hints at the profound spiritual consequences of disbelief.
orig: إن شر الدواب عند الله الذين كفروا فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Those with whom you made a pact, but they break their covenant every time and they do not fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring unfaithfulness and disregard for commitments by certain individuals or groups despite agreements made. It underscores their lack of reverence and fear of Allah, which is integral in maintaining trust and integrity in agreements. The emphasis on breaking pacts 'every time' indicates a habitual wrongdoing, suggesting a deep-seated moral corruption. This behavior is contrasted with the expected norm of honoring agreements, especially those sworn in the name of God, reflecting the values of trustworthiness and piety advocated in Islam.
orig: الذين عاهدت منهم ثم ينقضون عهدهم في كل مرة وهم لا يتقون

translation: And if you encounter them in battle, then scatter those behind them, so that perhaps they may remember.
interpretation: This verse underscores the strategy and psychological tactics in warfare, aiming to weaken the morale and coherence of the enemy. By targeting those in the rear and causing disorder, it may lead the enemy to reconsider their actions and the consequences of their aggression, potentially leading to introspection and a change in their conduct. The phrase 'so that perhaps they may remember' highlights the purpose of this action, which is not just military victory but also to instigate a moral and cognitive awakening among the adversaries.
orig: فإما تثقفنهم في الحرب فشرد بهم من خلفهم لعلهم يذكرون

translation: And if you fear betrayal from a people, then throw back to them [their treaty] on equal terms. Indeed, Allah does not love the traitors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of mutual trust and fairness in agreements, especially when there is a fear of betrayal. It exhorts believers to address their concerns by ending agreements in a just manner that reflects the terms initially agreed upon, thereby preserving their integrity and moral values. The verse also underscores that betrayal is deeply disliked by Allah, encouraging His followers to uphold honesty and reliability in all of their dealings.
orig: وإما تخافن من قوم خيانة فانبذ إليهم على سواء إن الله لا يحب الخائنين

translation: And let not those who disbelieve think they can outrun (Us). Indeed, they cannot escape.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that disbelievers should not be under the illusion that they can evade or outpace divine justice or the consequences of their disbelief. It serves as a reminder of the omnipotence and omnipresence of God, highlighting that no matter how much one might try to avoid accountability, escape from the divine reckoning is impossible. The verse reinforces the theme of accountability and the inevitable reality of divine justice.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا سبقوا إنهم لا يعجزون

translation: And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know but whom Allah knows. And whatever you spend in the cause of Allah will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being strategically and physically prepared in the face of adversaries to safeguard the community and uphold divine principles. It advocates for readiness, not just in direct confrontations but also in deterring potential unseen threats. The encouragement to mobilize resources underscores a proactive approach to security. Furthermore, the verse reassures that expenditures in the path of righteousness, such as for defense or community protection, are recognized and compensated by Allah, ensuring that justice prevails for those who act with integrity and in good faith.
orig: وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل ترهبون به عدو الله وعدوكم وآخرين من دونهم لا تعلمونهم الله يعلمهم وما تنفقوا من شيء في سبيل الله يوف إليكم وأنتم لا تظلمون

translation: And if they incline to peace, then incline to it [as well] and rely upon Allah; indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responding positively to initiatives for peace and reconciliation. By instructing to incline towards peace if the opposite party does so, it underlines the virtue of peace in Islam. Additionally, it reinforces the idea of trusting in Allah's wisdom and guidance, highlighting His attributes as All-Hearing and All-Knowing, implying that Allah is aware of all intentions and outcomes, and thus, one's reliance on Him should be complete and unwavering in the pursuit of peace.
orig: وإن جنحوا للسلم فاجنح لها وتوكل على الله إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is Allah. He it is Who supported you with His help and with the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reliance on divine support and the power of community, underscoring that God's assistance and the solidarity of fellow believers serve as the ultimate shield against deceit and harm. It reassures the believer that, in the face of adversities or deceitful intentions from others, they should find solace and strength in God's comprehensive protection and the support of the faithful community. This alliance, supernaturally bolstered and united by faith, is portrayed as an invincible force that should comfort and empower the believer.
orig: وإن يريدوا أن يخدعوك فإن حسبك الله هو الذي أيدك بنصره وبالمؤمنين

translation: And He united their hearts. If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have united their hearts, but Allah united them. Indeed, He is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the limits of human effort and material wealth in achieving unity and harmony among people. It highlights that true unity of hearts and deeper reconciliations are fundamentally the work of divine intervention. The reference to Allah’s attributes, 'Almighty' and 'All-Wise', at the end emphasizes that His actions are both powerful and guided by profound wisdom, suggesting that the unification of hearts is not only a display of His might but also a manifestation of His wise planning in creating social harmony and peace.
orig: وألف بين قلوبهم لو أنفقت ما في الأرض جميعا ما ألفت بين قلوبهم ولكن الله ألف بينهم إنه عزيز حكيم

translation: O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those who follow you among the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sufficiency of God's support for the Prophet Muhammad and his followers who are true believers. It reassures that divine assistance is adequate and serves as an affirmation of faith and trust in God's protection and provision. It underlines the idea that, despite any challenges or opposition, the adherence to faith in Allah and His guidance is all that the Prophet and his followers need to overcome obstacles and to sustain their spiritual and moral duties.
orig: يا أيها النبي حسبك الله ومن اتبعك من المؤمنين

translation: O Prophet, urge the believers to battle. If there are among you twenty steadfast, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are among you a hundred, they will overcome a thousand of those who have disbelieved because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of spiritual and moral strength in Islam, particularly in the context of battle. It highlights the idea that a smaller group of believers, who are steadfast and morally aligned with Islamic teachings, can achieve victory over a numerically superior enemy. This is attributed not only to their numbers but to their opponent's lack of understanding and spiritual insight. The verse signifies the importance of quality over quantity and underscores the power of faith and resilience in the face of adversity.
orig: يا أيها النبي حرض المؤمنين على القتال إن يكن منكم عشرون صابرون يغلبوا مائتين وإن يكن منكم مائة يغلبوا ألفا من الذين كفروا بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are among you a hundred who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred, and if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand, by Allah's permission. And Allah is with the steadfast.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's understanding and consideration of human frailty. It teaches that with divine support and steadfastness, a smaller group of committed individuals can overcome a numerically superior adversary. The numerical ratios underscore the power of divine assistance and the emphasis on quality over quantity. The presence of Allaah with those who are steadfast reassures believers that their perseverance in faith and endurance in challenges, both spiritual and worldly, are not in vain but are supported by divine presence and favor.
orig: الآن خفف الله عنكم وعلم أن فيكم ضعفا فإن يكن منكم مائة صابرة يغلبوا مائتين وإن يكن منكم ألف يغلبوا ألفين بإذن الله والله مع الصابرين

translation: It is not fitting for a prophet to have captives until he has triumphed thoroughly in the land. You desire the fleeting gains of this world, but Allah desires for you the Hereafter. And Allah is Mighty, Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the priorities and conduct expected of a prophet and his followers, concerning worldly gains versus spiritual goals. It suggests that engaging in premature actions for material gain, such as taking captives for ransom before achieving a decisive victory, is not in alignment with the higher ethical and spiritual objectives that a prophet is supposed to embody. It underscores a contrast between short-term worldly desires and the eternal, profound rewards of the Hereafter, encouraging a focus on spiritual victories and divine will. The attributes of Allah as 'Mighty' and 'Wise' reaffirm that His plans are grounded in immense power and deep wisdom, guiding believers to trust in divine judgment and seek the everlasting over the temporary.
orig: ما كان لنبي أن يكون له أسرى حتى يثخن في الأرض تريدون عرض الدنيا والله يريد الآخرة والله عزيز حكيم

translation: If not for a decree from Allah that preceded, you would have been touched by a great punishment for what you took.
interpretation: This verse underlines the concept of divine decree and mercy, emphasizing that the avoidance of a great punishment for certain actions is due to a prior decree by Allah. It suggests the protective nature of such decrees, highlighting Allah's mercy and the importance of divine guidance in shielding mankind from the consequences of their actions.
orig: لولا كتاب من الله سبق لمسكم فيما أخذتم عذاب عظيم

translation: So consume what you have gained, lawful and good, and fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of ethics and mindfulness in the consumption of goods and resources that one rightfully earns or acquires. It underscores that benefits derived from lawful means are not just permitted but should also be wholesome and pure. The directive to fear Allah serves as a reminder to maintain consciousness of divine laws and morality in all actions, assuring believers of Allah's forgiveness and mercy towards those who strive to live a virtuous and God-conscious life.
orig: فكلوا مما غنمتم حلالا طيبا واتقوا الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O Prophet, say to those in your captivity, if Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you something better than what has been taken from you, and He will forgive you; and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the merciful and forgiving nature of Allah towards captives who harbor goodness in their hearts. It suggests that divine assessment and reward are based on the internal moral state and intentions of individuals. The promise of receiving something better than what was lost not only refers to material compensation but also implies spiritual and emotional blessings, reinforcing the principle that divine justice transcends immediate circumstances. Forgiveness offered by Allah highlights the opportunity for redemption and transformation, signaling that past actions do not irrevocably determine one's fate if one turns towards goodness.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لمن في أيديكم من الأسرى إن يعلم الله في قلوبكم خيرا يؤتكم خيرا مما أخذ منكم ويغفر لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: And if they intend to betray you, then indeed they have betrayed Allah before, so He gave you power over them. And Allah is All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the recurrent theme of divine omniscience and wisdom, illustrating that Allah is fully aware of the intentions and actions of individuals. The betrayal referred to is not just a personal affront but a transgression against divine trust. By stating that God had previously been betrayed, it underscores the pattern of disloyalty among certain individuals and groups. The verse also highlights the concept of divine justice and support for those who are righteous and faithful, as expressed through the empowerment of the prophet over the betrayers. It serves as a reminder of the inevitable consequences of betrayal and reassurance that divine wisdom and knowledge encompass all human actions and intentions.
orig: وإن يريدوا خيانتك فقد خانوا الله من قبل فأمكن منهم والله عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and emigrated and fought with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who have given shelter and aid, they are allies of one another. But those who have believed and have not emigrated, you have no duty of protection towards them until they emigrate. And if they seek help from you in the religion, then it is your duty to help, except against a people with whom you have a treaty. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound bond and mutual obligations among Muslims who have fully committed to the cause of Islam through belief, emigration, and jihad (striving) in the way of Allah. It underscores the deep spiritual and practical alliance formed between those who have left their homes in pursuit of religious freedom and those who have assisted them. On the other hand, it delineates that while solidarity with all believers is a fundamental principle, the practical responsibilities, such as protection, extend only to those who actively engage in the communal struggle by emigrating. Moreover, it instructs that support should be extended to fellow believers in need unless such support conflicts with existing peace treaties, highlighting the importance of keeping agreements and fostering international relations built on trust. Through this, the verse also reinforces the characteristic of Allah as an all-seeing entity, aware of the actions of individuals, thus emphasizing accountability in adherents' actions towards one another and in diplomatic engagements.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله والذين آووا ونصروا أولئك بعضهم أولياء بعض والذين آمنوا ولم يهاجروا ما لكم من ولايتهم من شيء حتى يهاجروا وإن استنصروكم في الدين فعليكم النصر إلا على قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And those who disbelieve are allies of one another; if you do not do this, there will be fitnah (tribulation) on the earth and great corruption.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the solidarity among disbelievers to support each other in their disbelief, highlighting the natural tendency of like-minded individuals to form alliances. It serves as a warning to the believers about the potential consequences of failing to maintain unity and support among themselves. Lack of such solidarity among believers can lead to widespread tribulation and corruption in society, undermining the moral and social order established by the faith. This stresses the importance of unity and collective responsibility among the believers to uphold justice and prevent societal decay.
orig: والذين كفروا بعضهم أولياء بعض إلا تفعلوه تكن فتنة في الأرض وفساد كبير

translation: And those who believed, and emigrated, and strove in the way of Allah, and those who gave refuge and aid—those are the true believers. For them is forgiveness and a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significant virtues and rewards associated with true faith in Islam. It highlights the comprehensive nature of belief, which encompasses not just faith but also actionable commitments such as migration in the cause of Allah and active struggle (jihad), which here refers to striving for a righteous cause. It also underscores the importance of community support, as seen in providing refuge and assistance to fellow believers. The 'true believers' are depicted not just by their professed faith but by their actionable efforts and support for one another in righteousness. The promised rewards of forgiveness and 'noble provision' symbolize both spiritual and material blessings, emphasizing that true faith leads to spiritual cleansing and tangible bounties in life. This holistic approach underlines the idea that faith must be lived actively, combining individual duties with communal responsibilities and support.
orig: والذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله والذين آووا ونصروا أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: And those who believed afterwards, and emigrated and struggled alongside you, they are of you; and those of kinship, some of them are more entitled to others in the Book of Allah. Indeed, Allah is knowledgeable of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and bond within the Muslim community, especially highlighting the inclusion and importance of those who joined the faith later and participated actively in its struggles. It also underscores the principle of prioritizing familial ties as prescribed in the divine law, indicating that kinship holds significant legal and ethical importance in the structure of Muslim society. The verse reassures that Allah is fully aware of all circumstances and the intrinsic details of relationships and affiliations among individuals.
orig: والذين آمنوا من بعد وهاجروا وجاهدوا معكم فأولئك منكم وأولو الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض في كتاب الله إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: A declaration of disassociation from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you had made a treaty among the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse marks the severance of treaty obligations with certain polytheistic groups who had repeatedly breached their agreements. It underscores the importance of fidelity to treaties and agreements in Islam, indicating that such contracts are binding only so long as all parties uphold their terms. The proclamation is both a warning and a guideline that alliances with those who betray trust are not to be maintained. This directive emphasizes the necessity of mutual respect and integrity in maintaining peace and security, reminding believers to align their diplomatic practices with principles of justice and accountability.
orig: براءة من الله ورسوله إلى الذين عاهدتم من المشركين

translation: So travel freely throughout the land for four months and know that you cannot escape Allah and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine decree that grants a period of grace, emphasizing the inevitability of divine justice and reinforcing the idea that attempting to evade divine reckoning is futile. It serves as a warning to the disbelievers about their end and underscores Allah's omnipotence and the unavoidable nature of His judgment.
orig: فسيحوا في الأرض أربعة أشهر واعلموا أنكم غير معجزي الله وأن الله مخزي الكافرين

translation: And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that Allah is disassociated from the polytheists, and so is His Messenger. So if you repent, it is better for you, but if you turn away, then know that you cannot frustrate Allah. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the rejection of polytheism. It declares a clear and public disassociation from polytheists by Allah and His Messenger, which is announced during the significant occasion of the greater pilgrimage, underscoring the gravity of the announcement. The verse offers a choice to the listeners: to repent from polytheism which leads to betterment, indicating Allah’s mercy and willingness to forgive, or to persist in disbelief and face the inability to escape or frustrate Allah’s divine plan, culminating in a warning of inevitable painful retribution for continued disbelief. This demonstrates the principle of divine justice and the serious consequences of turning away from monotheistic belief.
orig: وأذان من الله ورسوله إلى الناس يوم الحج الأكبر أن الله بريء من المشركين ورسوله فإن تبتم فهو خير لكم وإن توليتم فاعلموا أنكم غير معجزي الله وبشر الذين كفروا بعذاب أليم

translation: Except for those among the polytheists with whom you have made a covenant, then they have not failed you in anything nor supported anyone against you. So fulfill their covenant until the term of their contract, for indeed, Allah loves the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding treaties and agreements, especially with those who, despite differing in faith, honor their commitments and do not act aggressively. It underscores the principle of integrity in dealings and reciprocal respect, reflecting that righteousness is not only about personal piety but also about just and fair interactions with others, irrespective of their religious beliefs. Furthermore, it highlights that Allah appreciates those who adhere to their ethical commitments, which is an integral aspect of righteousness.
orig: إلا الذين عاهدتم من المشركين ثم لم ينقصوكم شيئا ولم يظاهروا عليكم أحدا فأتموا إليهم عهدهم إلى مدتهم إن الله يحب المتقين

translation: So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, capture them and besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent, perform the prayer, and give zakah, then leave their way free. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines a conditional directive entailing actions to be taken concerning polytheists who break treaties. It emphasizes the importance of the sanctity of agreements and the severe consequences for their violation, indicative of the broader principle of justice in dealing with aggression and betrayal. However, the verse also underscores the propensity for mercy and forgiveness in the Islamic tradition, provided there is genuine repentance and a renewed commitment to the core tenets of faith and societal obligations.
orig: فإذا انسلخ الأشهر الحرم فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم وخذوهم واحصروهم واقعدوا لهم كل مرصد فإن تابوا وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فخلوا سبيلهم إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allah. Thereafter, convey him to his place of safety because they are a people who do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of compassion and protection towards those who are not believers in the Islamic faith. It advocates for providing a safe space for non-believers to learn about the message of Islam without coercion. The directive to ensure their safety until they are returned to a secure place highlights the principles of mercy and justice intrinsic to Islamic teachings, regardless of religious differences. It underscores that ignorance, not malice, often leads to disbelief, and therefore, it is the duty of Muslims to inform and protect rather than to condemn.
orig: وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله ثم أبلغه مأمنه ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعلمون

translation: How can there be a covenant for the polytheists in the sight of Allah and His Messenger, except for those you have made a covenant with at the Sacred Mosque? So long as they are true to you, remain true to them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honoring agreements made in good faith, even with those who do not share the same religious beliefs, as long as they uphold their part of the covenant. The specific reference to the Sacred Mosque underscores the solemnity and importance of such agreements made in a sacred context. The verse also highlights a general principle of reciprocity in relations and underscores the virtue of piety and righteousness in maintaining harmony and trust across diverse communities.
orig: كيف يكون للمشركين عهد عند الله وعند رسوله إلا الذين عاهدتم عند المسجد الحرام فما استقاموا لكم فاستقيموا لهم إن الله يحب المتقين

translation: How [will it be] when, if they gain dominance over you, they would not observe any tie or protection in regard to you? They would satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights themes of trust, integrity, and the true nature of individuals' commitment to moral and social bonds. It issues a cautionary note about placing reliance on those whose words are not backed by sincere intentions or moral earnestness. Specifically, it warns against those who may outwardly appear benign or trustworthy but fundamentally lack commitment to principles of decency and respect once they hold a position of power. It underscores the discrepancy between external expressions and internal moral alignment, cautioning that many may betray a righteous path, driven instead by their disobedience and ethical deviations.
orig: كيف وإن يظهروا عليكم لا يرقبوا فيكم إلا ولا ذمة يرضونكم بأفواههم وتأبى قلوبهم وأكثرهم فاسقون

translation: They purchased with the signs of Allah a small price and hindered (others) from His way. Indeed, what they did was evil.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of the moral and spiritual corruption of those who, driven by selfish and worldly gains, misuse or disregard divine teachings. It criticizes the actions of those who, for trivial material benefits, compromise on the principles and guidance provided by God, thereby not only going astray themselves but also leading others away from the righteous path. It emphasizes the enormity of wrongdoing when divine signs or messages, meant to guide humanity, are used as mere tools for short-sighted worldly achievements. The phrase 'a small price' underscores how insignificant and fleeting these worldly gains are compared to the enduring and profound value of spiritual integrity and truth. The verse serves as a stern warning against the consequences of such actions, illustrating how detrimental they are to one's spiritual wellbeing and to society as a whole.
orig: اشتروا بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا فصدوا عن سبيله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: They do not respect any covenant or promise made with a believer, and those are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral depravity of certain individuals who deliberately break or disregard the covenants and promises they make, particularly with believers. It underscores the seriousness with which betrayal or treachery, especially in matters of trust and agreement, is viewed in Islamic ethics. Such actions are firmly categorized as acts of transgression, indicating a deviation from justice, righteousness, and the path prescribed by God. This emphasis serves to caution believers about the presence and impact of untrustworthy individuals, and the need to remain vigilant and discerning in their interactions.
orig: لا يرقبون في مؤمن إلا ولا ذمة وأولئك هم المعتدون

translation: But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion; and We detail the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of repentance, prayers, and charity in defining who is part of the Muslim community. It outlines clear conditions under which those who may have erred can be reintegrated into the fold of Islam. Furthermore, the verse underscores the principle of inclusivity contingent upon adherence to key Islamic tenets. It also highlights that the Qur'an offers detailed guidance and is purposefully accessible to those who seek true understanding, illustrating how divine guidance caters to people equipped with knowledge and a willingness to learn.
orig: فإن تابوا وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فإخوانكم في الدين ونفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: And if they break their oaths after their covenant, and assail your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief, for they have no oaths; perhaps they will stop.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining religious and contractual integrity. It addresses the scenario where agreements or covenants made in good faith are broken, specifically mentioning those who not only breach their promises but also attack the religious foundations of others. The directive to confront, specifically, the leaders of such disbelief highlights a strategic approach to curtail not just individual transgressors but the sources of orchestrated efforts against faith. The ultimate hope expressed is for cessation of such hostilities and enmities, suggesting that the aim of confrontation is restoration of peace and proper order, rather than mere retaliation.
orig: وإن نكثوا أيمانهم من بعد عهدهم وطعنوا في دينكم فقاتلوا أئمة الكفر إنهم لا أيمان لهم لعلهم ينتهون

translation: Will you not fight against a people who have broken their oaths and plotted to expel the Messenger, and they attacked you first? Do you fear them? Allah is more deserving of your fear if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses believers, urging them to confront those who have violated sacred promises, specifically those who have conspired against the Prophet and initiated aggression. It emphasizes the importance of prioritizing fear and reverence for Allah over fear of other humans, especially in matters of justice and upholding divine commands. The verse strengthens the resolve of believers, reminding them of their duty to defend their community and principles of faith, reinforcing that their allegiance to Allah should supersede any worldly fears when confronting injustice and treachery.
orig: ألا تقاتلون قوما نكثوا أيمانهم وهموا بإخراج الرسول وهم بدءوكم أول مرة أتخشونهم فالله أحق أن تخشوه إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and disgrace them and give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a believing people.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine support and justice provided to the believers in their struggle against oppression. It emphasizes that the act of fighting against oppressors is not just a physical battle, but also a spiritual one, where God plays a direct role in punishing the wrongdoers, bringing disgrace upon them, and ultimately granting victory to the believers. The phrase 'heal the breasts of a believing people' metaphorically suggests the relief and spiritual satisfaction believers attain when justice prevails and tyranny is overcome. This verse thereby motivates and assures the faithful of God's presence in their righteous endeavors against injustice.
orig: قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم ويخزهم وينصركم عليهم ويشف صدور قوم مؤمنين

translation: And He removes the rage from their hearts. And Allah turns in mercy to whom He wills; and Allah is All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transformative power of divine grace in alleviating deep-seated anger and resentment from the believers' hearts. It underscores the role of God's will in granting repentance and mercy, suggesting that such divine qualities are selectively bestowed according to a wisdom that is beyond human understanding. This serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and wisdom in guiding human beings towards spiritual purification and emotional healing.
orig: ويذهب غيظ قلوبهم ويتوب الله على من يشاء والله عليم حكيم

translation: Or did you think that you would be left [as you are] and Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strive and do not take anyone other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as intimates? And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the notion of divine testing and distinction among the believers. It serves as a reminder that mere profession of faith is not enough; believers are expected to actively strive in their faith under the guidance of God, His Messenger, and the community of believers. It underscores the importance of loyalty and the avoidance of seeking support or guidance from those outside the fold of Islam. It also suggests that true striving in the way of Allah is under constant divine scrutiny, and only through sincere effort can the believers prove their true allegiance and potentially attain divine approval.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تتركوا ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ولم يتخذوا من دون الله ولا رسوله ولا المؤمنين وليجة والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while witnessing against themselves with disbelief. Those, their deeds have become worthless, and they will abide in the fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the incompatibility of maintaining a place of worship dedicated to Allah while simultaneously holding beliefs that contradict the fundamental tenets of Islam. The act of maintaining the mosque, while outwardly appearing devout, if coupled with disbelief, renders such actions null and void in the sight of Allah. The essence of this verse suggests that sincerity in belief is critical to the acceptance of one's religious duties and actions. The stark consequence mentioned for such contradiction between belief and action is eternal damnation, highlighting the severity with which Islam views polytheism and hypocrisy in religious practices.
orig: ما كان للمشركين أن يعمروا مساجد الله شاهدين على أنفسهم بالكفر أولئك حبطت أعمالهم وفي النار هم خالدون

translation: Only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, and establish prayer, and give Zakat, and fear none but Allah are those who are likely to be among the rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the characteristics of those who truly maintain and cherish the mosques of Allah. It highlights that such individuals are not merely caretakers of physical structures, but more fundamentally, they are devout believers who uphold key Islamic practices—faith in Allah and the Day of Judgement, regular observance of prayer, giving of obligatory charity (Zakat), and living a life of God-consciousness, fearing none but Allah. Their dedication to these principles is an indication of their spiritual guidance and their strong connection with their faith, projecting the mosque not just as a place of worship but as a center of a community embodying these values.
orig: إنما يعمر مساجد الله من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وأقام الصلاة وآتى الزكاة ولم يخش إلا الله فعسى أولئك أن يكونوا من المهتدين

translation: Do you consider the providing of water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque equal to the belief in Allah and the Last Day, and striving in the way of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah, and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse addresses the differences in acts of worship and service, emphasizing that internal belief and active striving in the path of Allah hold a higher spiritual and moral value than merely performing external caretaking duties, even if these duties are linked to sacred practices such as caring for pilgrims or maintaining a mosque. It underlines the notion that true faith involves a deep, personal commitment to the principles of Islam and active engagement in its struggles, beyond mere ritualistic or outward religious observances. The verse highlights that acts motivated by true faith and in pursuit of spiritual struggle are immensely more significant in the eyes of Allah, and it serves as a reminder that not all acts are of equal merit or influence on one’s spiritual standing. This differentiation also indicates that divine guidance and favor are reserved for those who earnestly seek justice and righteousness through their faith and actions, distancing from merely formalistic or superficial displays of religiosity.
orig: أجعلتم سقاية الحاج وعمارة المسجد الحرام كمن آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وجاهد في سبيل الله لا يستوون عند الله والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Those who believed and emigrated and fought for the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives are of higher degree in the sight of Allah, and those are the successful ones.
interpretation: This verse underscores the high status and ultimate success granted by Allah to those who not only hold faith but also physically and materially sacrifice for the divine cause. It emphasizes that true belief is manifest through significant, proactive engagement in striving for spiritual and communal goals, underlining a fusion of faith, action, and self-sacrifice that elevates one's standing before Allah and leads to ultimate success, both spiritually and eternally.
orig: الذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم أعظم درجة عند الله وأولئك هم الفائزون

translation: Their Lord gives them glad tidings of mercy from Him, and pleasure, and gardens for them wherein is enduring bliss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the compassionate and rewarding nature of God towards the faithful believers. It assures them of God's mercy, which encompasses forgiveness and benevolence, and His pleasure, indicating their actions and faith have found favor with Him. The reference to gardens symbolizes an eternal paradise promised to them, where they will experience everlasting happiness and bliss. This serves as both a reassurance and motivation for the believers to maintain their faith and righteousness in accordance with God's commands.
orig: يبشرهم ربهم برحمة منه ورضوان وجنات لهم فيها نعيم مقيم

translation: Abiding therein forever, indeed Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward that awaits the righteous in the hereafter. It highlights the perpetual blessings that believers will enjoy, underscoring the infinite grace and generosity of Allah. The phrase 'a great reward' serves to remind believers of the immense and incomparable benefits of adhering to divine guidance, encouraging steadfastness in faith and righteous actions.
orig: خالدين فيها أبدا إن الله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not take your fathers or your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over belief. And whoever of you does {that}, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing faith and allegiance to God over familial bonds if these relatives advocate disbelief. It underscores a fundamental Islamic principle that true loyalty must align with faith over social or blood ties. The verse warns against the spiritual danger and wrongful action of siding with one's family when they are in opposition to faith, identifying such a stance as oppressive or unjust.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا آباءكم وإخوانكم أولياء إن استحبوا الكفر على الإيمان ومن يتولهم منكم فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: Say, if your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your kindred, the wealth you have amassed, the commerce you fear may decline, and the dwellings you are pleased with, are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His path, then wait until Allah brings about His command, for Allah does not guide the disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the necessity of prioritizing devotion to Allah, His Messenger, and the cause of Islam above all worldly attachments and possessions. It warns that a failure to prioritize spiritual commitments over material or familial ties indicates a misalignment in the believer's values, which may lead to divine disapproval and a lack of spiritual guidance. The use of 'then wait until Allah brings about His command' suggests an impending divine decision or consequence for those whose hearts are not correctly aligned with the divine will, highlighting the serious repercussions of choosing worldly life over spiritual obligations.
orig: قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم وأزواجكم وعشيرتكم وأموال اقترفتموها وتجارة تخشون كسادها ومساكن ترضونها أحب إليكم من الله ورسوله وجهاد في سبيله فتربصوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: Allah has indeed helped you in many battlefields, and on the day of Hunayn, when you admired your own numbers, but they availed you nothing and the earth closed in on you despite its vastness; then you turned back, fleeing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of human vulnerability and the folly of overconfidence. It emphasizes that regardless of numerical strength or perceived power, success and protection ultimately come from Allah. The incident at Hunayn teaches humility, showing that reliance on mere numbers or resources can be misleading. True security comes from spiritual depth and reliance on divine guidance, rather than just physical or material means.
orig: لقد نصركم الله في مواطن كثيرة ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئا وضاقت عليكم الأرض بما رحبت ثم وليتم مدبرين

translation: Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down forces you did not see, and He punished those who disbelieved, and that is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support and reassurance granted by Allah to the Prophet and the believers during a time of adversity, emphasizing the unseen assistance that comes from faith in God. The tranquility sent by Allah reassures believers, strengthening their resolve and calming their hearts in the face of conflict or trials. Additionally, the reference to 'forces you did not see' suggests the presence of divine interventions or angels that support the believers in ways beyond human perception. The punishment of the disbelievers serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of denying faith and opposing divine truth. This verse serves to affirm the justice of divine retribution while comforting and encouraging the faithful, reinforcing the notion that ultimate victory and support belong to those who uphold their faith in the face of opposition.
orig: ثم أنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وأنزل جنودا لم تروها وعذب الذين كفروا وذلك جزاء الكافرين

translation: Then Allah forgives whom He wills after that, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's boundless mercy and forgiveness, emphasizing that even after disobedience, Allah offers the opportunity for repentance and forgiveness to those He chooses. It affirms the notion that divine forgiveness is not arbitrary but aligned with divine wisdom, providing hope and encouragement to seek repentance for one's misdeeds. The attributes of Allah being 'Forgiving' and 'Merciful' underscore the compassionate nature of divine justice, which is meant to rehabilitate rather than punish.
orig: ثم يتوب الله من بعد ذلك على من يشاء والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are impure, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs. And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of the Sacred Mosque by prohibiting the impure, represented by polytheists, from entering it after a specific time. This exclusion reflects the importance of maintaining the purity and sanctity of the worship space. The verse also addresses the concerns of the believers regarding economic hardship that might follow from enforcing this exclusion, reassuring them that Allah, with His infinite wisdom and knowledge, will provide for them if they obey His commands and have faith. Thus, the verse reinforces the principle of reliance on divine provision and encourages adherence to divine decrees, linking spiritual purity with divine support.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما المشركون نجس فلا يقربوا المسجد الحرام بعد عامهم هذا وإن خفتم عيلة فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله إن شاء إن الله عليم حكيم

translation: Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.
interpretation: This verse addresses a specific context where conflict arises between the Islamic community and certain non-Muslim communities referenced as 'those who were given the Scripture.' The command to 'fight' is contextual and contingent upon hostility arising from these groups against Muslims. It emphasizes enforcing a socio-political order where these groups, if they choose not to embrace Islam and continue in their original faith, must contribute to the Islamic state through a form of tax known as 'jizyah.' This tax is symbolic of a mutual acknowledgment and respect of a protective covenant. The stipulation for being humbled indicates a requirement for submission to the state's authority but does not imply degradation or loss of personal dignity. The overarching aim is to establish justice, peace, and secure coexistence within the state.
orig: قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ولا يحرمون ما حرم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

translation: And the Jews say, 'Ezra is the son of Allah,' and the Christians say, 'The Messiah is the son of Allah.' That is their statement from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse criticizes certain groups among the Jews and Christians for their beliefs about Ezra and Jesus, respectively, being the 'son of Allah,' highlighting that such beliefs are deviations from the monotheistic concept of God emphasized in Islam. The verse accuses these groups of echoing the words of earlier disbelievers, thus showing a continuity of disbelief across history. It reflects a strong disapproval of associating partners with Allah—a core tenet of Islamic faith known as Tawhid. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes the bewilderment over their state of delusion and deviation from monotheism.
orig: وقالت اليهود عزير ابن الله وقالت النصارى المسيح ابن الله ذلك قولهم بأفواههم يضاهئون قول الذين كفروا من قبل قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the critique of religious authority and idolatry. It addresses how certain religious leaders, scholars (ahbar), and monks (ruhban) have been improperly elevated to divine status amongst their followers, diverting worship away from the sole deity, Allah. This misplacement of devotion includes the veneration of the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, beyond his intended role. The verse underscores the central Islamic tenet of monotheism (Tawhid), which calls for worship directed exclusively towards the one true God, free from any association or partnership (Shirk) with other beings or figures. It serves as a reminder of the unique and unparalleled status of Allah, calling believers to maintain the purity of worship and uphold Islamic monotheistic principles.
orig: اتخذوا أحبارهم ورهبانهم أربابا من دون الله والمسيح ابن مريم وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا إلها واحدا لا إله إلا هو سبحانه عما يشركون

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it.
