orig: ما كان للنبي والذين آمنوا أن يستغفروا للمشركين ولو كانوا أولي قربى من بعد ما تبين لهم أنهم أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And Abraham's seeking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Abraham was tenderhearted and forbearing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep commitment to promises and moral integrity exhibited by Prophet Abraham. Originally, his plea for his father's forgiveness stemmed from a heartfelt promise, reflecting his truthful and sincere nature. However, upon realizing his father's staunch opposition to divine directives, Abraham adhered strictly to his ultimate commitment to God, distancing himself from anything that contradicted his faith. This teaches the importance of righteous commitments but emphasizes that one's devotion to God supersedes all earthly ties, especially when these ties are in conflict with divine commandments. Abraham's character as compassionate and patient underscores the importance of having a gentle heart but not at the expense of compromising on principled stances based on divine guidance.
orig: وما كان استغفار إبراهيم لأبيه إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه إن إبراهيم لأواه حليم

translation: And Allah would not let a people go astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid. Indeed, Allah is all-knowing of everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice and mercy of Allah. It reassures the believers that divine guidance, once granted, is sustained and clarified by Allah Himself. It highlights the importance of clear, divine communication indicating what is to be avoided in order to remain on the path of righteousness. The mention of Allah's omniscience underlines that His guidance and the subsequent obligations placed on the believers are always based on complete and perfect knowledge, ensuring fairness in divine judgment.
orig: وما كان الله ليضل قوما بعد إذ هداهم حتى يبين لهم ما يتقون إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Indeed, Allah is the Sovereign of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death. And you have, besides Allah, no protector and no helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah over all of creation, underscoring that He alone has the ultimate authority over life and death. The phrase highlights the futility of seeking protection or assistance from any source other than Allah, as He is the ultimate guardian and supporter. The verse is a reminder of the dependence of human beings on Allah's will and power, encouraging trust and reliance solely on Him.
orig: إن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يحيي ويميت وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Indeed, Allah has turned in mercy to the Prophet, the Muhajireen (emigrants), and the Ansar (helpers) who followed him in the time of hardship, after the hearts of a group of them had almost swerved; then He turned to them in mercy. Truly, He is to them Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mercy and forgiveness bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad, his followers who emigrated with him, and the helpers who supported them in Medina during times of difficulty. It addresses a moment of wavering faith among some of them under extreme pressure, yet underscores Allah’s boundless compassion by granting them repentance and reaffirming His benevolence. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's readiness to accept repentance and forgive His followers, emphasizing His attributes of kindness and mercy. It also underlines the importance of steadfastness and loyalty during challenging times and the spiritual rewards that follow such perseverance.
orig: لقد تاب الله على النبي والمهاجرين والأنصار الذين اتبعوه في ساعة العسرة من بعد ما كاد يزيغ قلوب فريق منهم ثم تاب عليهم إنه بهم رءوف رحيم

translation: And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind [in the battle of Tabuk] until, when the earth closed in on them despite its vastness and their souls constricted within them, and they realized that there was no refuge from Allah except in Him, then He turned to them so they could repent. Truly, Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards those who sincerely repent and turn back to Him, even after having initially failed or strayed. It highlights the psychological and emotional distress experienced by those who realize the gravity of turning away from divine commands, as well as the relief and redemption offered through genuine repentance. By illustrating Allah's willingness to accept repentance, it motivates believers to always seek God's forgiveness, no matter how dire or hopeless the situation may seem. The verse reassures that Allah's mercy encompasses all, and His forgiveness can be sought continuously, underscoring the boundless compassion inherent in the divine nature.
orig: وعلى الثلاثة الذين خلفوا حتى إذا ضاقت عليهم الأرض بما رحبت وضاقت عليهم أنفسهم وظنوا أن لا ملجأ من الله إلا إليه ثم تاب عليهم ليتوبوا إن الله هو التواب الرحيم

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with those who are true.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consciousness of God (taqwa) and integrity in the life of a believer. It encourages believers to maintain their duty to God and to align themselves with people who are truthful and honest. This alignment not only strengthens one's personal faith and moral compass but also builds a community based on trust and righteousness, which is vital for the spiritual health and societal welfare of the believers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وكونوا مع الصادقين

translation: It was not fitting for the people of Medina and the desert Arabs around them to stay behind from following the Messenger of Allah, nor to prefer their own selves over his sensibilities. This is because they neither experience thirst, nor fatigue, nor hunger in the cause of Allah, nor do they tread on any ground that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they inflict any harm upon an enemy, but a righteous deed is recorded for them. Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the emphasis on the communal obligation and commitment required from the believers, specifically the people of Medina and nearby desert Arabs, to support and follow the Prophet Muhammad in his endeavors. It underscores the moral and spiritual repercussions of their choice to participate or not in religious obligations or battles. Those who engage in striving for the cause of Allah are assured that even the smallest of their efforts will not go unnoticed and will be recorded as righteous deeds. This assurance is meant to motivate adherence to the Prophet's call and reinforce the value of self-sacrifice in the path of faith, providing an assurance that all such sacrifices have inherent value and divine acknowledgement, thereby deepening their faith and dedication to their spiritual responsibilities.
orig: ما كان لأهل المدينة ومن حولهم من الأعراب أن يتخلفوا عن رسول الله ولا يرغبوا بأنفسهم عن نفسه ذلك بأنهم لا يصيبهم ظمأ ولا نصب ولا مخمصة في سبيل الله ولا يطئون موطئا يغيظ الكفار ولا ينالون من عدو نيلا إلا كتب لهم به عمل صالح إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: And they do not spend any small or large amount, nor do they cross a valley, but that it is recorded for them, so that Allah may reward them with the best of what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive awareness and record-keeping of God regarding the deeds of individuals. Every act, no matter how minor or significant, as well as every challenge or hardship they overcome, is meticulously noted. This serves as an assurance that all their efforts and sacrifices in pursuit of righteousness will be recognized and rewarded by God, possibly even in ways that exceed their earthly deeds. It serves both as motivation to persist in good actions and reassurance that nothing righteous is overlooked by the Divine.
orig: ولا ينفقون نفقة صغيرة ولا كبيرة ولا يقطعون واديا إلا كتب لهم ليجزيهم الله أحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And it is not for the believers to go forth entirely [in battle]. But why should not a group from each of their sections go forth to gain understanding in religion and warn their people when they return to them, so that they may be cautious?
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of balance in communal obligations, emphasizing that not everyone is required to partake in every communal duty, such as battle. Instead, it is beneficial if some members from each group dedicate themselves to deepen their understanding of their faith. This deeper understanding equips them to educate and warn their communities, fostering a more informed and cautious society. It stresses the role of knowledge and awareness in safeguarding the community's spiritual and physical well-being.
orig: وما كان المؤمنون لينفروا كافة فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون

translation: O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers and let them find in you harshness. And know that Allah is with those who are righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the directive to the believers to defend their community against aggression from non-believers who are in close proximity. It instructs believers to adopt a firm stance in their defensive actions to effectively prevent and discourage future aggression. The verse further reassures them that in their adherence to righteousness and faith, they will have the support and guidance of Allah, reinforcing the importance of moral conduct even in confrontational scenarios.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قاتلوا الذين يلونكم من الكفار وليجدوا فيكم غلظة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: And when a surah is revealed, there are among them those who say, 'Which of you has this increased in faith?' As for those who have believed, it increases them in faith, and they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrasting reactions of different individuals upon receiving the revelations of the Quran. For true believers, each surah deepens their faith and brings them joy as it resonates with their existing belief and commitment to God, serving as both affirmation and inspiration. Conversely, the question posed by some about who has increased in faith after a surah’s revelation likely reflects skepticism or a challenge, indicating varying levels of belief and commitment among the listeners. This divergence in reactions also underscores the dynamic and impactful nature of the Quranic revelation, which not only affirms faith but also tests and differentiates among its adherents based on their spiritual openness and sincerity.
orig: وإذا ما أنزلت سورة فمنهم من يقول أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا فأما الذين آمنوا فزادتهم إيمانا وهم يستبشرون

translation: But as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has increased their defilement to their defilement, and they died while they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual state of those who harbor doubt or hypocrisy in their hearts. The 'disease' mentioned refers metaphorically to spiritual and moral corruption. The increase in their 'defilement' suggests that persisting in such a state only deepens one's distance from faith and truth. Ultimately, their demise in a state of disbelief signifies a spiritual failure and the grave consequences of nurturing such internal corruption instead of seeking healing through faith and righteous actions.
orig: وأما الذين في قلوبهم مرض فزادتهم رجسا إلى رجسهم وماتوا وهم كافرون

translation: Do they not see that they are tried every year once or twice yet they do not repent nor do they remember?
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurrent trials and tribulations that people face as a reminder or a test of their faith. Despite these repeated challenges, it points out human negligence in failing to turn back to God in repentance and mindfulness. The verse serves as both a criticism of such behavior and a caution, emphasizing the importance of recognizing divine signs, reflecting on one's actions, and maintaining a conscious relationship with the Creator.
orig: أولا يرون أنهم يفتنون في كل عام مرة أو مرتين ثم لا يتوبون ولا هم يذكرون

translation: And when a surah is revealed, some of them look at each other, asking, 'Does anyone see you?' Then they turn away. Allah has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of the hypocrites in the community who lack genuine faith. When they hear the revelations, instead of reflecting on their meaning and applying them, they are more concerned with whether others are observing their reactions, indicating their insincerity and desire to conceal their disbelief. Their turning away after questioning if they have been seen, symbolizes their detachment and rejection of the guidance offered by the revelations. Allah's turning their hearts away is a consequence of their deliberate choice to ignore the truth and persist in misunderstanding, demonstrating a divine justice that matches their inward disbelief and outward hypocrisy.
orig: وإذا ما أنزلت سورة نظر بعضهم إلى بعض هل يراكم من أحد ثم انصرفوا صرف الله قلوبهم بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer, [he is] eager for you and to the believers is kind and merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the deep empathy and concern that the Prophet Muhammad holds for his community. The expression 'from among yourselves' underscores his humanity and relatability, making it clear that he shares in the struggles and understands the pains of his followers. His distress over the suffering of his people and his eagerness for their well-being highlight his compassionate and merciful nature, which aligns with his role as a mercy to the believers. This description serves to strengthen the bond between the Prophet and his followers, encouraging them to appreciate and follow his guidance, knowing that it comes from a place of genuine care and divine wisdom.
orig: لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه ما عنتم حريص عليكم بالمؤمنين رءوف رحيم

translation: But if they turn away, say, 'God suffices me. There is no deity except Him. On Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reliance on God, especially in the face of rejection or adversity. It conveys a sense of unconditional trust and devotion to God, who is portrayed as the ultimate source of support and sovereignty. This reliance is not just a passive waiting but an active trust that involves recognizing God's omnipotence and the futility of placing similar trust in others. By referring to God as the 'Lord of the Great Throne', the verse also highlights His supreme authority and power, suggesting that His support is the most significant and effective that one can seek.
orig: فإن تولوا فقل حسبي الله لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وهو رب العرش العظيم

translation: Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book.
interpretation: This verse introduces a chapter of the Qur'an underscoring the divine nature of its messages, conveyed through clear and wise verses. It points to the Qur'an as not merely a text, but a profound source of wisdom, crafted with precision and purpose. The mention of 'Alif Lam Ra' could also allude to the mysterious and unique aspects of the Qur'anic revelation, inviting believers and thinkers to ponder deeply on its meanings and guidance.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب الحكيم

translation: Is it a wonder for people that We have sent revelation to a man from among them, saying, 'Warn mankind and give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a firm precedence of truth with their Lord'? The disbelievers say, 'Indeed, this is an obvious sorcerer.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief encountered by prophets when they conveyed divine revelations to their communities. It addresses the human tendency to doubt and reject the unfamiliar or miraculous, particularly when divine guidance comes through ordinary individuals from within their own community. The term 'obvious sorcerer' reflects the dismissive and derogatory attitudes of the disbelievers who could not reconcile the profound nature of the prophet's message with his familiar human origins. Furthermore, the verse underscores the reassurance provided to the believers, affirming that their faith and acknowledgement of the truth grants them a distinguished status in the sight of their Lord. It serves as both a consolation to the believers and a challenge to the skeptics, urging them to see beyond their prejudices and recognize the authenticity of the divine message.
orig: أكان للناس عجبا أن أوحينا إلى رجل منهم أن أنذر الناس وبشر الذين آمنوا أن لهم قدم صدق عند ربهم قال الكافرون إن هذا لساحر مبين

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne, managing the affairs; there is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Do you not then remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and omnipotence of Allah, illustrating His unparalleled ability to create and govern the universe. It underscores the concept of monotheism by affirming that Allah alone is worthy of worship. The reference to the six days of creation and His establishment above the Throne symbolizes His supreme authority and control over all matters. The mention of intercession only occurring with His permission highlights His ultimate judgment and reinforces the dependence of all creation on His will. This verse serves as a call to acknowledge Allah's omnipotence and to worship Him alone, inspiring believers to reflect on His greatness and their devotion to Him.
orig: إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش يدبر الأمر ما من شفيع إلا من بعد إذنه ذلكم الله ربكم فاعبدوه أفلا تذكرون

translation: To Him is your return, all of you. The promise of Allah is true. He begins creation; then He repeats it so that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice. And those who disbelieved, for them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of the return to Allah, underscoring the completeness and absoluteness of this return for all beings without exception. It asserts the truthfulness of Allah's promise regarding the lifecycle of creation and re-creation, serving as a mechanism to establish divine justice. The reward or punishment is dispensed based on one's faith and deeds, illustrating a direct correlation between earthly actions and eschatological outcomes. Reward for the believers and punishment for the disbelievers are explained not just as consequences, but as a rectification and continuity of the justice that governs the universe. This principle enforces the moral responsibility and accountability of individuals for their choice of belief and actions, highlighting the fairness of divine judgment.
orig: إليه مرجعكم جميعا وعد الله حقا إنه يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات بالقسط والذين كفروا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a reflected light and determined for it stages, that you may know the number of years and the account. Allah did not create this except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom and purpose behind the creation of celestial bodies like the sun and the moon. By designing the sun to serve as a source of light and warmth, and the moon to reflect the sun's light and follow precise lunar phases, God has provided humanity with a means to measure time and organize life appropriately. The meticulous structuring of these elements reflects the deliberate and truthful aspect of creation, underscoring that nothing God establishes is without profound significance and purpose. Furthermore, the verse invites those with knowledge to reflect on these signs as manifestations of God's majesty and precision in the universe.
orig: هو الذي جعل الشمس ضياء والقمر نورا وقدره منازل لتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب ما خلق الله ذلك إلا بالحق يفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day, and in what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth, are signs for a people who fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the existence of divine signs in the natural phenomena around us, specifically the cyclical patterns of night and day, and the broader creations in the heavens and earth. These signs are meant to serve as reminders of the omnipotence and meticulous design of Allah, geared towards those who have a consciousness and fear of Him. Such individuals are likely to reflect on these signs, recognizing them as indications of Allah's sovereignty and mastery, which in turn fosters a deeper sense of accountability and reverence towards the Creator.
orig: إن في اختلاف الليل والنهار وما خلق الله في السماوات والأرض لآيات لقوم يتقون

translation: Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us and are content with the life of this world, feeling secure therein, and those who are heedless of Our signs
interpretation: This verse highlights a spiritual disparity between those who are focused solely on the material aspects of this life and those who maintain a consciousness of a higher, spiritual reality. The emphasis on not expecting to meet God signifies a deep-rooted materialism and a lack of awareness or denial of the afterlife. It points to a complacency where individuals are so ensconced in their worldly lives that they negate or ignore the spiritual signs and guidance from God. This verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of the worldly life and warns against the neglect of one's spiritual obligations and the ultimate reality of the hereafter.
orig: إن الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها والذين هم عن آياتنا غافلون

translation: Those, their abode will be the Fire because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice in Islamic theology, where individuals face consequences directly tied to their actions. In this context, the 'Fire' represents Hell, a place of punishment for those who engage in misdeeds and immoral actions. The phrase 'because of what they used to earn' highlights the principle that people's actions in life are akin to earnings that they will eventually 'reap' in the Hereafter. This serves as a cautionary reminder that wrongful earnings in this world lead to grievous consequences in the life beyond.
orig: أولئك مأواهم النار بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - their Lord will guide them because of their faith. Beneath them rivers will flow in the Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine reward awaiting those who uphold their faith and engage in good deeds. It assures believers that their efforts and faith are recognized by God, who will guide them to spiritual and eternal bliss. The reference to rivers flowing in gardens symbolizes a state of perpetual peace, satisfaction, and joy. It highlights the link between faith-driven actions in this world and the divine guidance and rewards in the hereafter, promoting a life oriented towards spiritual fulfillment and moral integrity.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات يهديهم ربهم بإيمانهم تجري من تحتهم الأنهار في جنات النعيم

translation: Their declaration therein will be: 'Glory be to You, O Allah,' and their greeting therein will be: 'Peace.' And the last of their declaration will be: 'Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse beautifully portrays the state of the inhabitants of Paradise, emphasizing their continuous glorification and praise of Allah. It reflects a condition of eternal peace and contentment, underscoring the ultimate fulfillment and spiritual joy they experience. The repetition of glorification and greeting with 'peace' signifies a permanent departure from worldly sufferings and conflicts. The final statement, recognizing Allah as the Lord of all worlds, marks a recognition of His sovereignty and grace, encapsulating the gratitude and acknowledgment of His blessings that the dwellers of Paradise embody.
orig: دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم وتحيتهم فيها سلام وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: If Allah were to hasten for people the evil [they invoke] as He hastens for them the good, their term would have been ended for them. So We leave those who do not expect to meet Us wandering blindly in their transgression.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and patience of Allah towards humanity. It illustrates that if God expedited punishment for evil as quickly as He grants blessings for good deeds, many people would have already faced their demise. Instead, God in His infinite wisdom and mercy allows time for repentance and correction, giving individuals the opportunity to seek forgiveness and amend their ways. The latter part of the verse serves as a warning and a manifestation of the consequences faced by those who deny the existence of a final reckoning or meeting with God. Their denial leads them to persist in their wrongdoing and moral blindness, veering further away from the path of righteousness.
orig: ولو يعجل الله للناس الشر استعجالهم بالخير لقضي إليهم أجلهم فنذر الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us, whether lying on his side, sitting, or standing; but when We remove his adversity from him, he passes on as if he had never invoked Us for an adversity that touched him. Thus it has been made fair-seeming to the extravagant what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle nature of human beings when it comes to their relationship with divine guidance and assistance. It underscores that in times of hardship or distress, individuals are quick to turn to a higher power, praying and seeking relief in various postures of desperation. Yet, once the crisis is averted and the individual's situation improves, there is a tendency to forget or disregard the aid they once fervently sought, acting as if the despair was never a part of their lives. This behavior is particularly associated with those who are extravagant or excessive, suggesting that indulgence can cloud moral and spiritual judgement, making one less appreciative of the divine intervention in their times of need and more likely to revert to heedless ways.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان الضر دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما فلما كشفنا عنه ضره مر كأن لم يدعنا إلى ضر مسه كذلك زين للمسرفين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And indeed, We destroyed generations before you when they committed injustice, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine retribution that befalls communities or generations that engage in gross injustices despite receiving clear warnings and guidance from their prophets. The relentless rejection of truth and persistence in wrongdoing trigger a punitive response from God, illustrating the principle of accountability in the divine scheme. The historical reference serves as a stern reminder and warning to all subsequent generations about the consequences of ignoring divine guidance and persisting in criminal behavior.
orig: ولقد أهلكنا القرون من قبلكم لما ظلموا وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وما كانوا ليؤمنوا كذلك نجزي القوم المجرمين

translation: Then We made you successors upon the earth after them, to see how you would perform.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of human responsibility and stewardship on Earth. It suggests that humanity is appointed by God as successors or caretakers of the Earth, following those who came before. This appointment serves as a test to observe how well humans fulfill their duties and responsibilities in maintaining justice, upholding ethical values, and managing the world's resources. The phrase 'to see how you would perform' highlights that our actions on Earth are under divine scrutiny and will be judged accordingly. It emphasizes the transient nature of human authority and the ongoing divine oversight over human affairs.
orig: ثم جعلناكم خلائف في الأرض من بعدهم لننظر كيف تعملون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not look forward to meeting Us say, 'Bring a Qur'an other than this or change it.' Say, 'It is not for me to change it on my own. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the resistance and disbelief of those who reject the divine message, expressing their refusal to accept the Qur'an in its present form and demanding alterations that suit their desires. The response commanded to the Prophet underscores the principle that divine revelation is not subject to alteration by human whims. It reaffirms the Messenger's role as a mere conduit of God’s words, emphasizing his adherence to divine command and the fear of divine retribution that governs his obedience. This scenario demonstrates the challenge of conveying an unaltered truth in the face of skepticism and the critical role of submission to divine authority in maintaining the purity of the message.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ائت بقرآن غير هذا أو بدله قل ما يكون لي أن أبدله من تلقاء نفسي إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, 'If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you aware of it. And I had already resided among you for a lifetime before it. Then will you not reason?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of divine will in the transmission of the Qur'anic message and underscores the accountability of the recipients. The reference to the Prophet's long presence among his people before receiving revelation serves to remind his audience of his trustworthy character and consistent life. It argues that their familiarity with him should lead them to trust his message and use reason to understand the truth of the revelation rather than dismiss it.
orig: قل لو شاء الله ما تلوته عليكم ولا أدراكم به فقد لبثت فيكم عمرا من قبله أفلا تعقلون

translation: So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals do not prosper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of fabricating falsehoods about God or denying His divine signs, categorizing such acts as the pinnacle of injustice. It underscores the moral and spiritual corruption inherent in deceiving others about matters of faith, especially concerning the nature and commands of Allah. The verse further conveys a vivid warning that those who engage in such acts, labeled as criminals, will ultimately fail to achieve success or prosperity, highlighting the inevitable divine justice that counters acts of transgression and falsehood.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته إنه لا يفلح المجرمون

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them, and they say, 'These are our intercessors before Allah.' Say, 'Do you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?' Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the irrationality and futility of idolatry, pointing out the absurdity of worshiping beings or objects that have no power to harm or benefit. It critiques the notion of assigning partners or intercessors with Allah, highlighting that Allah is all-knowing and transcendent, perfectly aware of everything in the heavens and on the earth. Therefore, the idea that humans need to or can inform Allah about anything, or rely on intermediaries, contradicts His omnipotence and omniscience. The verse glorifies Allah, affirming His greatness and the purity of His uniqueness, rejecting any form of association (shirk) with Him.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا يضرهم ولا ينفعهم ويقولون هؤلاء شفعاؤنا عند الله قل أتنبئون الله بما لا يعلم في السماوات ولا في الأرض سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And mankind was not but a single community, then they differed; and if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them concerning that about which they differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inherent unity of humanity, indicating that all people originated from a singular community sharing common beliefs and values. Over time, differences emerged among them, leading to disputes and divisions. The verse also highlights the divine wisdom and patience; God's prior decree prevented immediate judgment on these disputes, allowing time for differences to unfold and perhaps resolve, reflecting a broader purpose and plan beyond human understanding. It points towards the importance of recognizing our shared origins while acknowledging and managing our differences with grace and patience, guided by divine timing and wisdom.
orig: وما كان الناس إلا أمة واحدة فاختلفوا ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم فيما فيه يختلفون

translation: And they say, 'Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'The unseen belongs only to Allah; so wait, indeed, I am with you among those who are waiting.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism and demand for miraculous evidence from those who doubt prophetic messages. The response instructed to the Prophet emphasizes that knowledge of the unseen, including when and how signs or miracles are manifested, is exclusively with Allah. It highlights the principle of patience and trust in divine wisdom and timing. The Prophet is instructed to align himself with the demanders in the act of waiting, demonstrating humility and shared anticipation for God's signs, thereby fostering a common ground of expectancy and watchfulness for divine intervention.
orig: ويقولون لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه فقل إنما الغيب لله فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: And when We let the people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, behold, they devise plots against Our signs. Say, 'Allah is swifter in planning.' Indeed, Our messengers record what you plot.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to turn away from spiritual and moral obligations when they experience ease after hardships. It criticizes those who respond to divine mercy and relief from difficulties with arrogance and rejection of divine signs. The verse serves as a warning against such behavior, emphasizing that Allah is aware of all schemes and responds more swiftly and justly than one can imagine. The mention of divine recorders underscores the accountability of individuals for their actions and intentions, reminding believers to maintain gratitude and obedience to God, regardless of their circumstances.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة من بعد ضراء مستهم إذا لهم مكر في آياتنا قل الله أسرع مكرا إن رسلنا يكتبون ما تمكرون

translation: It is He who transports you across land and sea until when you are on ships, and they sail with them with a favorable wind and they rejoice at it, then a stormy wind strikes them, and waves come to them from everywhere, and they think they are surrounded, they earnestly pray to Allah, dedicating their religion to Him: 'If You deliver us from this, we shall truly be of the grateful.'
interpretation: This verse vividly portrays the vulnerability and fluctuating fortunes of human beings, highlighting how swiftly their circumstances can change, especially in the face of nature's overwhelming force. It serves as a powerful reminder of human dependence on God's mercy and the intrinsic human tendency to turn to a higher power in times of desperation and crisis. This narrative encourages gratitude and humility, illustrating that joy and comfort can quickly turn into trials and that during such trials, individuals often rediscover and reaffirm their faith. The verse ultimately teaches that sincerity in faith and acknowledgement of one’s frailty before God can lead to salvation and gratitude.
orig: هو الذي يسيركم في البر والبحر حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم بريح طيبة وفرحوا بها جاءتها ريح عاصف وجاءهم الموج من كل مكان وظنوا أنهم أحيط بهم دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين لئن أنجيتنا من هذه لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: And when He saved them, behold, they rebelliously transgress on the earth without right. O mankind, your rebellion is only against yourselves, [a mere] enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us will be your return, and We will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ingratitude and waywardness of humans upon being delivered from hardships by God. Rather than showing humility and reform, they often return to unjust and oppressive behaviors. The verse serves as a poignant reminder that their rebellious actions primarily harm themselves, offering only temporary worldly benefits. Ultimately, everyone will return to God, who will hold them accountable for their deeds, reinforcing the principles of justice and divine reckoning. The underlying lesson is to remain mindful of one's actions and their long-term consequences, rather than being swayed by transient pleasures and gains.
orig: فلما أنجاهم إذا هم يبغون في الأرض بغير الحق يا أيها الناس إنما بغيكم على أنفسكم متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعكم فننبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: The example of worldly life is like water which We sent down from the sky; thus the earth's vegetation mingles with it, from which people and animals eat. Until, when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified, and its people think they have control over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, making it as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus We explain the signs in detail for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically compares the transient nature of worldly life to water that nourishes plants which are eventually destroyed. It highlights the illusion of control and permanence that humans often feel about their possessions and achievements. The suddenness with which God's decree can change the state of things serves as a reminder of the ultimate impermanence and unpredictability of worldly life. The verse calls on people to reflect on these truths, suggesting that a deeper understanding of life's fleeting nature can lead to more thoughtful and spiritually aligned living.
orig: إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض مما يأكل الناس والأنعام حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازينت وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها أتاها أمرنا ليلا أو نهارا فجعلناها حصيدا كأن لم تغن بالأمس كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And Allah invites to the abode of peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine call from Allah to humanity, inviting them towards 'Dar as-Salam', which metaphorically represents peace, safety, and eternal paradise. Furthermore, it emphasizes the sovereignty and wisdom of Allah in guiding whom He chooses to the 'straight path', symbolizing the correct and righteous way of living according to His will. This guidance is both a blessing and a mercy, indicating that true peace and ultimate success are through adherence to this divinely ordained path.
orig: والله يدعو إلى دار السلام ويهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: For those who have done good is the best [reward] and extra. No darkness will cover their faces, nor humiliation. Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the rewards awaiting those who commit to righteousness and moral excellence in their actions. The 'best [reward]' refers to the immense and perfect blessings of Paradise, while 'extra' signifies additional favors and joys that exceed basic expectations, highlighting the boundless generosity of God. The absence of darkness and humiliation on their faces symbolizes purity, dignity, and honor upheld in the hereafter, contrasting earthly life where faces can be marred by distress or shame. Finally, the eternal dwelling in Paradise reflects the ultimate fulfillment and permanent contentment granted to the virtuous.
orig: للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة ولا يرهق وجوههم قتر ولا ذلة أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And those who earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil deed is like it, and abasement will cover them. They have no protector against Allah. As if their faces are covered with pieces of the dark night. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of justice and retribution in the Hereafter, where individuals are held accountable for their actions. The punishment meted out is proportionate to the sins committed. The imagery of faces covered with darkness symbolizes the utter despair and humiliation that the wrongdoers will experience, underscored by the absolute absence of any divine protection against the consequences of their actions. The reference to eternal abode in the Fire serves as a stern warning about the enduring consequences of one's earthly deeds.
orig: والذين كسبوا السيئات جزاء سيئة بمثلها وترهقهم ذلة ما لهم من الله من عاصم كأنما أغشيت وجوههم قطعا من الليل مظلما أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And [mention] the Day when We will gather them all together; then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, 'Stay in your place, you and your 'partners.'' So We separated them, and their 'partners' will say, 'You did not worship us.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate accountability and the unveiling of truth in the Hereafter. It portrays the Day of Resurrection, where those who committed idolatry or polytheism will face the consequences of their beliefs. Allah will isolate them along with their presumed 'partners'—the deities or entities they wrongly worshipped. This separation serves to highlight the falsehood of their beliefs, as even their 'partners' in worship will deny being objects of worship. The verse emphasizes the emptiness and deception of associating partners with Allah, illustrating how these erroneous beliefs will inevitably lead to humiliation and self-reproach when the reality is laid bare.
orig: ويوم نحشرهم جميعا ثم نقول للذين أشركوا مكانكم أنتم وشركاؤكم فزيلنا بينهم وقال شركاؤهم ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون

translation: And sufficient is Allah as a Witness between us and you that we were indeed unaware of your worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of Allah as an omnipresent observer who is fully aware of the true state and intentions of all individuals. It addresses the distinction between the beliefs of the speaker and the addressed, highlighting a disassociation and unawareness of the customs or practices of the latter. It underscores the idea that true accountability and witness are ultimately with Allah, who comprehends all matters transparently, thereby nullifying any need for human validation or acknowledgment in matters of personal faith and worship.
orig: فكفى بالله شهيدا بيننا وبينكم إن كنا عن عبادتكم لغافلين

translation: There, every soul will be tested for what it has sent forth, and they will be returned to Allah, their true Master, and what they used to fabricate will vanish from them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability of every individual for their actions in this worldly life. It highlights the Day of Judgment as a moment of truth where every soul will confront the consequences of their past deeds, stripped of any falsehoods or illusions they harbored. The reference to Allah as the true Master underscores the return to the ultimate authority and dispeller of all fabrications and misguided beliefs that people might have clung to during their earthly lives. It serves as a reminder of the inevitable reality where worldly attachments and misconceptions will no longer hold sway, and every soul will face the ultimate truth.
orig: هنالك تبلو كل نفس ما أسلفت وردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight? And who brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living? And who manages all affairs?' They will surely say, 'Allah.' So say, 'Will you not then fear Him?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the extent of God's sovereignty and control over the universe and everything within it. It invites individuals to reflect on the source of their sustenance, the granting of their sensory capabilities, the cycle of life and death, and the orderly governance of all matters. By directing these questions, the verse emphasizes that these realities, recognized intuitively or through contemplation, should naturally lead to the acknowledgement of Allah as the supreme authority. The response expected (and given) rhetorically underscores a universal recognition of this divine authority. Following this acknowledgment, the call to fear God serves as an exhortation to revere Him, adhere to His commands, and refrain from disobedience, recognizing His omnipotence and the accountability of human actions in His sight.
orig: قل من يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أمن يملك السمع والأبصار ومن يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ومن يدبر الأمر فسيقولون الله فقل أفلا تتقون

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, the Truth. So what is there after Truth except error? How then are you turned away?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute and ultimate reality of Allah as the definitive truth, contrasting it with all that is false or erroneous. It underscores a rhetorical question about the nature of truth and falsity, suggesting that once the truth (which is represented by the existence and oneness of Allah) is known, any departure from this truth can only lead to misguidance or error. The verse also highlights human susceptibility to deviation from the truth despite clear evidence and logical reasoning, urging introspection and steadfastness in faith.
orig: فذلكم الله ربكم الحق فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال فأنى تصرفون

translation: Thus has the word of your Lord come into effect upon those who defiantly disobey, that they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and justice inherent in divine decree, particularly regarding those who persist in disobedience and sin. It reflects how the decree of God—once set upon individuals who continuously engage in defiant disobedience—determines that they will not believe. This consequence is portrayed not as an arbitrary punishment, but as a fitting result of their choice to forsake the guidance and paths laid out by God. The verse serves as a warning that persisting in sinful defiance can lead to the solidification of disbelief in one's heart, ultimately distancing the individual from divine mercy and guidance.
orig: كذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين فسقوا أنهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Say, is there any of your 'partners' who can begin creation and then repeat it? Say, 'Allah begins creation and then repeats it; then how are you deluded?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique power of Allah in initiating and recreating life, highlighting His sole authority and capability in matters of creation and resurrection. It challenges the believers to reflect on the impotence of idols or deities they may associate with Allah, urging them to recognize the futility of such beliefs and the deception involved in idolatry. By questioning the capability of their 'partners', it directs them towards the realization of the one true God's supremacy and the irrationality of attributing divine powers to others.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده قل الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Say, is there any of your partners who guide to the truth? Say, 'Allah guides to the truth. Is He then who guides to the truth more deserving to be followed, or one who does not guide unless he is guided? So what is wrong with you, how do you judge?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine guidance versus human or idolatrous guidance. It challenges the idea of associating partners with Allah in worship and guidance, positing that only Allah possesses the ultimate ability to guide to the truth. The rhetorical questions highlight the illogical nature of following those who themselves need guidance. It criticizes the judgments of those who choose lesser or misguided entities over the all-knowing Creator, urging reflection and correction of one's understanding and priorities in terms of guidance and following.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يهدي إلى الحق قل الله يهدي للحق أفمن يهدي إلى الحق أحق أن يتبع أمن لا يهدي إلا أن يهدى فما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: And most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Indeed, conjecture avails not against the truth at all. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to rely on assumptions and guesses rather than seeking the truth. It emphasizes that such conjectures hold no value in the face of definitive truth, which is known to Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is aware of all actions and intentions, guiding that reliance on speculation instead of divine guidance and factual knowledge leads to misguidance and does not benefit an individual in matters of truth and justice.
orig: وما يتبع أكثرهم إلا ظنا إن الظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا إن الله عليم بما يفعلون

translation: And this Qur'an could not have been fabricated by anyone besides Allah, but it is a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of the Scripture, about which there is no doubt, from the Lord of the Worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, asserting that it is not a human invention but a revelation from Allah. It highlights the Qur'an's role in affirming the truth found in earlier revelations and providing a clear and detailed exposition of spiritual principles that were previously obscured or unexplained. The declaration of the Qur'an’s authenticity is portrayed as irrefutable, emanating directly from the creator of the universe, thereby underscoring its universal significance and authority.
orig: وما كان هذا القرآن أن يفترى من دون الله ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented it'? Say, 'Bring a chapter like it, and call upon anyone you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse challenges the skeptics and critics of the Qur'an who accuse the Prophet Muhammad of fabricating the Qur'an. It throws down a gauntlet to produce even a single chapter that matches the linguistic eloquence, depth, and wisdom of the Qur'an, emphasizing the divine origin of the text. The challenge also underlines the inability of anyone besides Allah to produce such a work, thus reinforcing the authenticity of the Qur'an and the truthfulness of the Prophet's message.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بسورة مثله وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But they denied what they did not encompass with their knowledge, and its interpretation had not yet come to them. Similarly, those before them denied. See then what was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights human tendencies to dismiss or reject things beyond the scope of their understanding or knowledge. It reflects on the pattern of denial exhibited by communities through history when faced with truths that challenge their current beliefs or knowledge paradigms. It warns of the consequences faced by such deniers, emphasizing that ignorance and arrogance often lead to downfall. This can be seen as a caution against close-mindedness and the danger of judging matters without comprehensive understanding or patience for revealed truth.
orig: بل كذبوا بما لم يحيطوا بعلمه ولما يأتهم تأويله كذلك كذب الذين من قبلهم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And among them are those who believe in it and those who do not believe in it, and your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity of belief among people regarding divine revelations or religious truth. It acknowledges that belief is varied and that not everyone will accept spiritual or religious truths. Implicit in this is a reminder of God's omniscience, particularly in discerning the inner states and intentions of individuals. Those who reject faith after understanding it are often described as corrupters, as their rejection can lead to corruption in both belief systems and societal structures. This recognition serves to comfort the believers, affirming that ultimate judgment of integrity and corruption rests with God, not with human judgment.
orig: ومنهم من يؤمن به ومنهم من لا يؤمن به وربك أعلم بالمفسدين

translation: And if they deny you, say, 'For me is my work, and for you is your work. You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of personal responsibility and the distinct boundaries between the actions of individuals. It conveys that one should remain focused on their own duties and moral obligations, irrespective of others' acceptance or rejection of one's beliefs. The verse promotes a principle of mutual non-accountability in personal deeds, emphasizing that every person is independently responsible for their actions in the sight of God. It encourages maintaining personal integrity and detaching oneself from the judgments or misdeeds of others.
orig: وإن كذبوك فقل لي عملي ولكم عملكم أنتم بريئون مما أعمل وأنا بريء مما تعملون

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not understand?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitations of human influence and guidance. It suggests that despite the prophet's efforts to communicate and guide, there are individuals whose hearts and minds are closed, akin to the deaf who cannot hear. The verse underscores the idea that guidance ultimately comes from God, and not everyone will heed the message, particularly if they lack the capacity or willingness to understand.
orig: ومنهم من يستمعون إليك أفأنت تسمع الصم ولو كانوا لا يعقلون

translation: And among them are those who look at you. Can you guide the blind even though they cannot see?
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human capability in guiding those who are spiritually blind to the truth. It reflects on the Prophet Muhammad's role and suggests that guidance ultimately comes from God. Thus, regardless of the Prophet's efforts, without God's will to open someone's heart to faith, they will remain spiritually unseeing, just as the literally blind cannot see without divine intervention.
orig: ومنهم من ينظر إليك أفأنت تهدي العمي ولو كانوا لا يبصرون

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all, but the people wrong themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice and fairness of Allah, conveying that any suffering or injustice experienced by individuals is not inflicted by Allah but is a result of their own actions or the actions of others in society. It serves as a reminder of personal responsibility and the consequences of one's actions, urging self-reflection and accountability.
orig: إن الله لا يظلم الناس شيئا ولكن الناس أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And on the day He will gather them as if they had not stayed [in the world] except for an hour of the day, they will recognize each other. Indeed, those who denied the meeting with Allah have lost, and they were not guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fleeting nature of worldly life in contrast to the eternity of the Hereafter. It highlights that the Day of Judgment will make the extensive lives lived on earth seem incredibly short, as if they lasted only an hour, emphasizing the abrupt realization of their reality among people. Moreover, the verse serves as a stark warning to those who deny the existence or the meeting with Allah, illustrating that such denial leads to a profound loss. Their lack of guidance in the worldly life culminates in a disorienting moment of truth upon resurrection, emphasizing the importance of faith and righteous living in accordance with divine guidance.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم كأن لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من النهار يتعارفون بينهم قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: And whether We show you some of what We promise them or We take your soul, to Us is their return, and then Allah is witness over what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of Divine accountability and the ultimate return of all creation to Allah. It highlights that regardless of whether the Prophet Muhammad witnesses the fulfillment of divine promises or judgments in his lifetime or not, the ultimate control and knowledge of events rest with Allah. The verse also underscores Allah's omniscience, as He is aware of all actions and nothing escapes His observation. This serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly life and the certainty of divine justice.
orig: وإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا مرجعهم ثم الله شهيد على ما يفعلون

translation: And for every nation there is a messenger. So when their messenger comes, judgment is made among them with justice, and they are not wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal principle of divine justice and guidance. It underlines the idea that God, in His wisdom, has appointed messengers for every community and nation throughout history, ensuring that every group of people has access to His guidance. The arrival of these messengers is a pivotal moment where decisions are made fairly and justly based on divine laws, guaranteeing that no one is treated unjustly. This reflects the comprehensive mercy and fairness of God towards all of humanity, affirming that divine justice transcends cultural, temporal, and geographical boundaries. The assurance that 'they are not wronged' reinforces the concept of accountability and the protective nature of divine justice against any form of oppression or injustice.
orig: ولكل أمة رسول فإذا جاء رسولهم قضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And they say, 'When is this promise, if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: This verse reflects skepticism and impatience among those who doubt the veracity of the divine promises regarding the Day of Judgment. It highlights the challenge posed by disbelievers to the prophetic message, questioning the integrity and truthfulness of the prophets. The underlying theme is the testing of faith and the confrontation between belief and disbelief, prompting believers to steadfastly uphold their conviction in the truths that have been revealed to them.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'I have no power over harm or benefit to myself except as Allah wills. For every nation there is an appointed time; when their time comes, they cannot delay it for an hour, nor can they advance it.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound submission and reliance on Allah's will, highlighting the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all affairs. The human being, no matter their status or power, cannot alter predetermined events or the fixed time of their occurrence, which Allah has set for every nation and individual. This teaches believers to place their trust in Allah and to accept life's unfolding events with patience and humility, recognizing that everything occurs within the divine decree and wisdom.
orig: قل لا أملك لنفسي ضرا ولا نفعا إلا ما شاء الله لكل أمة أجل إذا جاء أجلهم فلا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if His punishment should come to you by night or by day, what exactly is it that the criminals are hastening for?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and unpredictability of divine punishment, serving as a warning to those who persist in wrongdoing. The rhetorical question posed by God through the Prophet highlights the irrationality and short-sightedness of those who actively seek out or rush towards sinful behavior, being oblivious to the severe consequences that might befall them suddenly, either during the night or day. It underscores the idea that no one can escape divine justice, and it prompts individuals to reflect on their actions and hasten towards repentance and rectification instead of persisting in their transgressions.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أتاكم عذابه بياتا أو نهارا ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون

translation: Do you then believe in it only after it has happened? Now, while you used to hasten it before.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who only affirm their belief in divine warnings and prophecies after witnessing the events unfold, despite previously being impatient for such occurrences. It highlights a weakness in faith and understanding, as true belief should be constant and unwavering, not conditional upon seeing the outcomes. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to trust in divine wisdom and timing, rather than demanding signs or rushing what has been foretold.
orig: أثم إذا ما وقع آمنتم به آلآن وقد كنتم به تستعجلون

translation: Then it was said to those who did wrong, 'Taste the punishment of eternity. Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice and retribution in the afterlife, specifically addressing those who engaged in wrongful actions during their earthly lives. It conveys that the punishment they face is a direct consequence of their deeds. The phrase 'punishment of eternity' underscores the permanence and severity of the consequences for wrongdoing, intended to serve both as a retribution for injustice and a deterrent for others. The rhetorical question at the end reinforces the principle that one only receives what they have rightfully earned through their actions, highlighting the fairness and accountability inherent in divine judgement.
orig: ثم قيل للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب الخلد هل تجزون إلا بما كنتم تكسبون

translation: And they ask you, is it true? Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, indeed it is true; and you cannot escape it.'
interpretation: This verse addresses skepticism amongst people regarding the truthfulness of the messages delivered by the Prophet. The affirmation, 'Yes, by my Lord,' emphasizes the certainty and irrefutability of the divine truth being conveyed. The phrase 'indeed it is true' reinforces the unchangeable and factual nature of God's words. Lastly, 'and you cannot escape it' signifies that the reality of divine decrees is inescapable and beyond human manipulation or denial, highlighting the ultimate authority of divine will.
orig: ويستنبئونك أحق هو قل إي وربي إنه لحق وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: And if every soul that had wronged had whatever is on the earth, it would offer it as ransom; and they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment, and the matters will be judged among them with justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound remorse and desperation that individuals will experience on the Day of Judgment. It underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the fact that no material wealth can compensate for wrongful deeds. The mention of every soul being judged fairly implies that ultimate accountability rests with each individual, regardless of their earthly status or possessions. This serves as a solemn reminder of the ethical and moral responsibilities held by each person in their lifetime, urging adherence to righteous behavior in anticipation of a fair, divine assessment.
orig: ولو أن لكل نفس ظلمت ما في الأرض لافتدت به وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب وقضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all that exists in the universe, both in the heavens and on the earth. It underlines the truthfulness and certainty of Allah's promises, implying that His plans and decrees are inevitable and reliable. However, it also points to a widespread lack of awareness or acknowledgment among people regarding these truths. The verse calls on individuals to recognize and reflect on Allah's omnipotence and the authenticity of His commitments, encouraging a deeper understanding and faith among the believers.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض ألا إن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of God over life and death, underscoring His omnipotence and authority over all creation. It reminds human beings of the transient nature of earthly existence and the ultimate return to God for judgment and recompense. This return is not just physical but also spiritual, reflecting on accountability and the eternal consequences of one’s actions in this world.
orig: هو يحيي ويميت وإليه ترجعون

translation: O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord and healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal and comprehensive message of the Qur'an, highlighting its role not only as a source of spiritual guidance but also as a healing agent for emotional and psychological distress. It underscores the Qur'an's capacity to clear doubts, purify intentions, and provide solace and clarity to the human heart. Moreover, the verse particularly extends this message of guidance and mercy towards believers, indicating that those who embrace the faith with sincerity will find in the Qur'an a deep source of mercy and a clear path to follow.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءتكم موعظة من ربكم وشفاء لما في الصدور وهدى ورحمة للمؤمنين

translation: Say, 'In the bounty of Allah and in His Mercy - in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and valuing the spiritual blessings and mercy granted by Allah above materialistic acquisitions. The genuine joy and contentment come not from amassing wealth or worldly possessions but in appreciating and celebrating Allah's spiritual gifts and mercy, which provide true fulfillment and are far superior to temporal gains.
orig: قل بفضل الله وبرحمته فبذلك فليفرحوا هو خير مما يجمعون

translation: Say, have you considered what Allah has provided for you of sustenance, yet you have deemed some of it unlawful and some lawful? Say, did Allah permit you, or do you fabricate [lies] against Allah?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah in declaring what is permissible (halal) and what is forbidden (haram) regarding provisions and sustenance. It criticizes those who arbitrarily assign such statuses based on their desires or cultural practices rather than divine injunction. The rhetorical questions posed by Allah through the Prophet (peace be upon him) challenge the believers to reflect on the authority and source of such religious commands, underscoring the grave sin of falsely attributing religious laws to God without any legitimate basis. This verse thus serves as a reminder of the necessity to adhere strictly to divine guidance and to avoid introducing personal or cultural biases into religious practices.
orig: قل أرأيتم ما أنزل الله لكم من رزق فجعلتم منه حراما وحلالا قل آلله أذن لكم أم على الله تفترون

translation: And what do those who fabricate lies against Allah think of the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, Allah is full of grace towards mankind, but most of them do not give thanks.
interpretation: This verse highlights the misguided actions of those who falsely attribute lies to Allah, questioning their awareness or understanding of the consequences they will face on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the disconnect between Allah's boundless generosity and grace toward humanity and the ingratitude shown by the majority of people. The verse serves as a critique of human ungratefulness in the face of divine benevolence, and a warning about the reckoning that awaits those who deceive and mislead regarding Allah’s teachings and attributes.
orig: وما ظن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب يوم القيامة إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون

translation: And whatever situation you [Muhammad] may be in, and whatever portion of the Quran you recite, and whatever deed you [believers] may do, We are witnesses over you when you are engaged in it. And nothing is hidden from your Lord, so much as the weight of an atom on the earth or in the heaven, not smaller than that nor larger, but is in a clear record.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah. It serves as a reminder that Allah is a constant witness to all human actions and thoughts, regardless of their perceived significance. Every detail of human life, down to the minutest particulars, is known to Allah and recorded. The verse underscores the accountability of all beings to their Creator, and that every aspect of human existence is under divine surveillance. This awareness of constant divine oversight is meant to guide individuals towards ethical behavior and consciousness of their duties to Allah.
orig: وما تكون في شأن وما تتلو منه من قرآن ولا تعملون من عمل إلا كنا عليكم شهودا إذ تفيضون فيه وما يعزب عن ربك من مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: Behold, indeed the allies of Allah have no fear upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual security and emotional peace granted to those who are close to Allah, often referred to as His 'allies' or 'friends'. These individuals, who live in alignment with divine guidance, enjoy a unique protection from fear and sorrow. The absence of fear refers to freedom from anxieties about the future, while the absence of grief pertains to the burdens of the past. This state of tranquility is a direct consequence of their trust and reliance on Allah's wisdom and His plans for them, marking a deep spiritual connection and divine favor.
orig: ألا إن أولياء الله لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who believed and were God-fearing
interpretation: This phrase highlights the characteristics of true believers. It underscores not only the importance of having faith but also of embodying taqwa, which means being conscious and mindful of God. This mindfulness is reflected in one's obedience and adherence to God's commands and avoidance of sinful actions. Essentially, this description emphasizes that true belief is complemented by a lifestyle that respects divine guidance and maintains moral integrity.
orig: الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: For them are glad tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter. No change can there be in the words of Allah. That is the great success.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the enduring truth and unchangeable nature of God's words, highlighting the unique stability and reliability that divine revelations offer to believers. It reassures those who follow divine guidance that they will receive blessings both in their earthly existence and in the eternal hereafter. The mention of 'glad tidings' signifies a spiritual and possibly material reward for piety and steadfast faith, while 'the great success' refers to the ultimate achievement of eternal salvation and divine favor, transcending the transient pleasures and accomplishments of the mortal world.
orig: لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة لا تبديل لكلمات الله ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: And let not their words grieve you. Indeed, all honor belongs to Allah; He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing
interpretation: This verse provides comfort and reassurance by emphasizing that ultimate authority and respect belong only to Allah, who is aware of everything and understands all circumstances completely. The suggestion is that human opinions or criticisms should not cause distress, as the divine perspective transcends human judgment and encompasses all wisdom.
orig: ولا يحزنك قولهم إن العزة لله جميعا هو السميع العليم

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth. And those who invoke other than Allah do not follow [anything but] conjecture, and they are only guessing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and sole divine authority of Allah over all creation, both in the heavens and on earth. It critiques those who worship or invoke others beside Allah, highlighting that such actions are based merely on speculative assumptions rather than divine truth. The verse underscores the futility and misguided nature of idolatry or polytheism, emphasizing that true guidance and knowledge come only from Allah, not through the unfounded beliefs or the conjectural worship of other entities.
orig: ألا إن لله من في السماوات ومن في الأرض وما يتبع الذين يدعون من دون الله شركاء إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: It is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein and the day giving sight. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom in the creation and alternation of night and day, serving specific purposes beneficial to human life. The night is a time for rest and recuperation, a period of calm and tranquility to restore energy. The day, filled with light, provides the ability to see and carry out activities, prompting productivity and interaction. The emphasis on 'a people who listen' suggests that understanding and appreciating these signs requires mindful reflection and a willingness to perceive the underlying order and purpose established by God in the natural world.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: They say, 'Allah has taken a son.' Exalted is He! He is the Self-Sufficient. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Have you any authority for this statement? Do you say about Allah what you do not know?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and uniqueness of Allah, rejecting any anthropomorphic attributes or likenesses to His creation. It strongly criticizes those who attribute offspring or human qualities to Allah, highlighting His complete self-sufficiency and ownership of all that exists. The verse also confronts the baselessness of such claims about Allah, urging people to refrain from making statements about the divine that are not backed by revelation or true knowledge, hence promoting a reverence for the sanctity of divine attributes and the careful consideration of religious assertions.
orig: قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا سبحانه هو الغني له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض إن عندكم من سلطان بهذا أتقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will not succeed.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the inherent futility and ultimate failure awaiting those who deliberately attribute falsehoods to God. It serves as a warning about the severe spiritual and possibly worldly consequences of spreading untruths concerning the divine. The emphasis on 'not succeeding' highlights both the temporal and eternal dimensions of their failure, indicating that such actions not only defy divine commandments but also erode the individual's moral and spiritual integrity.
orig: قل إن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب لا يفلحون

translation: A provision in this world, then to Us is their return, then We shall make them taste severe punishment because of their disbelief.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient nature of worldly life and possessions, hinting that whatever comfort and luxury the disbelievers enjoy are temporary. The ultimate reality is their return to God, who holds absolute authority over the hereafter. The severe punishment mentioned in the verse serves as a warning and a consequence of their disbelief and denial of divine truths. It illustrates the principle of accountability in the afterlife, where actions in the worldly life directly influence one's fate in the eternal life.
orig: متاع في الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعهم ثم نذيقهم العذاب الشديد بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: And recite to them the news of Noah, when he said to his people, 'O my people, if my stay and my reminding of the signs of Allah is hard on you then I have relied on Allah. So gather your affair and your partners, and let not your affair be an indictment upon you, then decide upon me and do not wait.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound trust and reliance that Prophet Noah (Nuh) placed in God under severe opposition and rejection from his community. His declaration reflects a challenge to his people, urging them to proceed with whatever decision they intend against him without delay, demonstrating his unwavering faith in God's plan and protection. It serves as an instruction on the importance of patience, steadfastness in one's mission, and full reliance on God when faced with adversarial circumstances.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ نوح إذ قال لقومه يا قوم إن كان كبر عليكم مقامي وتذكيري بآيات الله فعلى الله توكلت فأجمعوا أمركم وشركاءكم ثم لا يكن أمركم عليكم غمة ثم اقضوا إلي ولا تنظرون

translation: But if you turn away, then I have not asked you for any reward; my reward is only from Allah, and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the selflessness of the prophet's mission, underscoring that his work is solely for the sake of God, not expecting any material reward from the people. The reference to being commanded to 'be among the Muslims' reflects a submission to Allah's will and an embodiment of the values and principles of Islam, aiming to provide a pure example of devotion without any worldly distractions or compensation.
orig: فإن توليتم فما سألتكم من أجر إن أجري إلا على الله وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the Ark, and We made them successors, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. So see how was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine retribution and reward. It illustrates how God protects and saves those who believe and follow His guidance, exemplified by the salvation of Noah and his companions. Conversely, it depicts the destruction of those who reject divine messages, emphasizing the grave consequences of disbelief and disobedience. The reference to making Noah and his companions 'successors' highlights the idea of righteous individuals inheriting the earth after the unrighteous are removed. This narrative serves as a cautionary tale, urging adherence to divine guidance and warning of the severe outcomes for those who ignore or reject prophetic warnings.
orig: فكذبوه فنجيناه ومن معه في الفلك وجعلناهم خلائف وأغرقنا الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين
