translation: Then, after him, We sent messengers to their people, and they brought them clear signs. But they were not to believe what they had previously denied. Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine practice of sending prophets and messengers with clear signs and evidence to guide the people. However, it also highlights the notion of psychological consistency where people often refuse to accept truths they had earlier denied, even when faced with clear evidence. The sealing of the hearts of the transgressors serves as both a consequence of their actions and a divine retribution for their persistent disobedience and injustice. This reflects the recurring theme in the Qur'an of accountability and the inescapable reality of divine justice.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعده رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا به من قبل كذلك نطبع على قلوب المعتدين

translation: Then after them We sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs, but they acted arrogantly and were a people of criminals.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurrent theme of divine messengers confronting tyranny and disbelief with signs of divine authority. Moses and Aaron's mission to Pharaoh, a symbol of arrogance and oppression, underscores the resistance faced by truth when it challenges entrenched power and corrupt elites. The verse also reflects on the moral and spiritual decay inherent in arrogance and criminal behavior, illustrating how they lead to the rejection of truth even when it is substantiated by clear signs. It serves as a cautionary tale about the consequences of hubris and the rejection of divine guidance.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعدهم موسى وهارون إلى فرعون وملئه بآياتنا فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما مجرمين

translation: So when the truth came to them from Us, they said, 'Indeed, this is evident magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the refusal and denial faced by the prophets when they presented divine revelations to their people. The verse captures the reaction of skepticism and outright dismissal, where the miracles or the truths brought by the prophets were mistaken as mere magic or deceit. It underscores the theme of human resistance to accepting unfamiliar truths, especially when it challenges established beliefs or ideas. The use of 'evident magic' reflects the intensity of their denial, illustrating how the clarity of the truth, rather than ensuring acceptance, can sometimes provoke a stronger reaction of denial and opposition.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا إن هذا لسحر مبين

translation: Moses said: Do you say about the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' And the magicians will not succeed.
interpretation: In this verse, Moses confronts the skepticism and denial of those who question the authenticity of the divine message he delivers, equating it to magic. It emphasizes the recurrent theme of opposition faced by prophets when they present the truth to people entrenched in their disbelief. By stating that 'the magicians will not succeed,' the verse underscores the ultimate failure of deception and falsehood, reinforcing the idea that truth, as ordained by God, will invariably prevail despite initial resistance or misinterpretation.
orig: قال موسى أتقولون للحق لما جاءكم أسحر هذا ولا يفلح الساحرون

translation: They said, 'Have you come to turn us away from what our fathers followed and to have supremacy in the land? We do not believe in you.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the resistance faced by prophets when they challenged the prevailing belief systems and societal norms. The accusation of seeking worldly supremacy reflects a common skepticism towards change-makers, suggesting that their intentions might be driven by personal gain rather than divine mandate. The response encapsulates a typical human apprehension towards abandoning ancestral traditions and the fear of the unknown that new teachings represent. It underscores the challenge of spiritual and social transformation, particularly when it confronts deeply ingrained practices and beliefs.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لتلفتنا عما وجدنا عليه آباءنا وتكون لكما الكبرياء في الأرض وما نحن لكما بمؤمنين

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'Bring to me every learned magician.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge posed by Pharaoh in the face of a perceived threat from divine signs, as presented by Prophet Moses. It illustrates Pharaoh's reliance on his own worldly power and knowledge, symbolized by the magicians, to counteract what he perceives as a challenge to his authority. His call for 'every learned magician' underscores a desperate attempt to consolidate all available human resources to maintain control and counteract the divine message. This reflects a broader theme of the struggle between divine truth and human arrogance or authority.
orig: وقال فرعون ائتوني بكل ساحر عليم

translation: So when the magicians arrived, Moses said to them, 'Throw down whatever you are going to throw.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a moment of confrontation where Moses, representing divine authority and truth, challenges the magicians, who symbolize illusion and deception. By instructing them to proceed with their display, Moses is not just confronting their physical actions but also challenging the underlying beliefs and the societal norms that empower such deceptions. The command 'Throw down whatever you are going to throw' reveals a deep confidence in the superiority of divine power over human trickery, indicating that truth has no fear of falsehood, as falsehood is bound to ultimately reveal its own weakness and defeat.
orig: فلما جاء السحرة قال لهم موسى ألقوا ما أنتم ملقون

translation: So when they threw, Moses said, 'What you have brought is magic. Indeed, Allah will invalidate it. Indeed, Allah does not allow the work of the corrupt to succeed.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of truth triumphing over falsehood and the divine justice that prevails against deceit and corruption. Moses's response to the magicians' actions underlines the principle that any efforts rooted in deceit, such as sorcery or manipulation, are ultimately doomed to failure by divine decree. It highlights the futility of relying on dishonest means to achieve success and asserts that corrupt actions, no matter how seemingly powerful, will not flourish under the watch of a just and omnipotent deity.
orig: فلما ألقوا قال موسى ما جئتم به السحر إن الله سيبطله إن الله لا يصلح عمل المفسدين

translation: And Allah establishes the truth with His words, even if the criminals dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supremacy and the unwavering nature of divine truth in contrast to human falsehood and dissent. It asserts that God's truth is irrefutable and prevails regardless of resistance from those who commit offenses against divine laws. It highlights a universal truth that persists even in the face of opposition from people with malicious intents or those engaged in wrongdoings. The sovereignty of divine will over human desires and misdeeds is underscored, indicating that the ultimate judgment and reality stem from God’s immutable words.
orig: ويحق الله الحق بكلماته ولو كره المجرمون

translation: But none believed in Moses except [some] offspring of his people, out of fear of Pharaoh and his chiefs, lest they should persecute them; and indeed, Pharaoh was haughty in the land and he was indeed among the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense challenge Moses faced in persuading his people to embrace faith and divine guidance due to the oppressive environment created by Pharaoh's tyranny. The reference to only a few from Moses’ lineage believing in him underscores the difficulty of maintaining faith under persecution and fear. Pharaoh’s mention as being haughty and a transgressor reveals the Quranic critique of arrogant leadership and misuse of power, showing how such rulers sow fear and hinder spiritual growth among their subjects.
orig: فما آمن لموسى إلا ذرية من قومه على خوف من فرعون وملئهم أن يفتنهم وإن فرعون لعال في الأرض وإنه لمن المسرفين

translation: And Moses said, 'O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then put your trust in Him, if you are Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust in God's plan and surrender to His will, emphasizing that true belief in Allah naturally leads to reliance on Him. It underscores the notion that faith and trust are inseparable qualities of a Muslim’s spiritual life, encouraging the believers to practice unconditional dependence on God, especially after professing their faith.
orig: وقال موسى يا قوم إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا إن كنتم مسلمين

translation: And they said, 'Upon Allah we have relied. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the believers' reliance on Allah's guidance and protection amidst adversity. By invoking Allah and expressing their dependence, the believers seek to distance themselves from actions or situations that might cause or exacerbate oppression or injustice. The supplication to not become a 'trial' for wrongdoers highlights a deep concern for not being a means or catalyst for furthering injustice, either through provocation or by becoming victims whose plight could be manipulated or misunderstood. It underscores the integrity and moral responsibility of not contributing to a cycle of wrongdoing, while also seeking divine support to uphold justice and righteousness in challenging circumstances.
orig: فقالوا على الله توكلنا ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للقوم الظالمين

translation: And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God, seeking His divine mercy to be rescued from the influences and harms associated with those who deny the truth or have disbelief. It underlines a dependency on divine grace for spiritual and perhaps physical salvation from environments or communities that do not uphold faith. The plea highlights the believers' acknowledgment of their vulnerability and the necessity of divine intervention to maintain righteousness and guidance in a world that may sometimes be antagonistic to spiritual and moral values.
orig: ونجنا برحمتك من القوم الكافرين

translation: And We inspired Moses and his brother, [saying], 'Settle your people in Egypt in homes, and make your homes a place of prayer, establish the prayer, and give good news to the believers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of creating a community centered around faith and worship, even in adverse circumstances. By instructing Moses and his brother to establish their community in Egypt, a place historically associated with trials for the Israelites, the verse underscores the resilience of faith. The directive to make homes a place of prayer conveys that worship and the remembrance of God should permeate every part of a believer's life, transforming personal spaces into sanctuaries of spirituality. Additionally, the call to establish prayer and give good news symbolizes the continuous nurturing and encouragement of faith amongst believers, fostering a supportive spiritual community.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى وأخيه أن تبوآ لقومكما بمصر بيوتا واجعلوا بيوتكم قبلة وأقيموا الصلاة وبشر المؤمنين

translation: And Moses said, 'Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs splendor and wealth in the worldly life, our Lord, that they may lead [people] astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a poignant appeal from Moses to God, highlighting the misuse of wealth and power by Pharaoh and his elites to lead people astray from divine guidance. Moses perceives their material prosperity not as a benign blessing, but as a facilitation of their tyranny and misguidance. His prayer for the obliteration of their wealth and the hardening of their hearts is a plea for divine intervention to prevent them from further leading others away from the path of righteousness. The request for their hearts to be hardened until they witness divine punishment underscores a theme of inevitable divine justice and the consequences of persistent disbelief and tyranny.
orig: وقال موسى ربنا إنك آتيت فرعون وملأه زينة وأموالا في الحياة الدنيا ربنا ليضلوا عن سبيلك ربنا اطمس على أموالهم واشدد على قلوبهم فلا يؤمنوا حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: He said, 'Your prayer has been answered, so remain steadfast and do not follow the path of those who do not know.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and guidance post-acceptance of one's prayers by God. It underscores a spiritual and moral alignment in one's actions and beliefs, cautioning against the influence of ignorance. The verse instills a sense of responsibility to uphold ethical conduct and wisdom in following the rightful path, highlighting the pitfalls of veering towards patterns set by those lacking true knowledge or understanding. Ultimately, it reflects on the divine acknowledgment of sincere supplications and the need for continual righteousness in one's life journey.
orig: قال قد أجيبت دعوتكما فاستقيما ولا تتبعان سبيل الذين لا يعلمون

translation: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea; then Pharaoh and his troops followed them in oppression and enmity until, when drowning overtook him, he said, 'I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of true faith and the consequences of arrogance and denial of truth until facing inevitable demise. Pharaoh, who had been a tyrant, only declared his belief in the one true God at the moment of his death, highlighting the insincerity of his conversion, intended as a last resort to save himself from drowning. It serves as a profound reminder of the importance of sincere faith and the futility of acknowledging truth only when faced with dire consequences, rather than as a genuine recognition and submission to divine guidance throughout one's life.
orig: وجاوزنا ببني إسرائيل البحر فأتبعهم فرعون وجنوده بغيا وعدوا حتى إذا أدركه الغرق قال آمنت أنه لا إله إلا الذي آمنت به بنو إسرائيل وأنا من المسلمين

translation: Now, after you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters
interpretation: This verse highlights the themes of accountability and redemption. It addresses an individual who has previously engaged in disobedience and corruption, emphasizing the past actions and their recognition in the present moment. The tone serves as a reminder that previous misdeeds are acknowledged but also suggests a pivotal moment for change. The verse can be seen as a call to self-awareness and transformation, urging an individual to reflect on their past in order to reform and seek a righteous path moving forward.
orig: آلآن وقد عصيت قبل وكنت من المفسدين

translation: So today We will save your body so that you may be a sign for those after you, and indeed many people are heedless of Our signs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine signs and warnings meant for contemplation and learning. It underscores the preservation of a significant figure's body as a stark reminder and lesson for future generations. The reference to people being 'heedless of Our signs' serves as a critical admonishment, highlighting the enduring human tendency to overlook or dismiss divine signals and lessons, underscoring the need for reflection and awareness in understanding and appreciating the signs of God in one's life and environment.
orig: فاليوم ننجيك ببدنك لتكون لمن خلفك آية وإن كثيرا من الناس عن آياتنا لغافلون

translation: And indeed, We settled the Children of Israel in an honorable place and provided them with good things; and they differed not until after knowledge had come to them. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's grace and favor upon the Children of Israel by granting them a dignified settlement and sustenance. However, the benevolence of God also brings a test; the knowledge presented to them became a source of division once they received it. The verse points out the human tendency to dispute and diverge once endowed with knowledge, even when bestowed with numerous blessings. The ultimate resolution of these disputes will occur in the divine justice of the Day of Judgment, reminding believers of the temporary nature of earthly disagreements and the finality of God’s judgment. This serves as a caution against the misuse of knowledge and the futility of disagreements that can detract from gratitude and unity.
orig: ولقد بوأنا بني إسرائيل مبوأ صدق ورزقناهم من الطيبات فما اختلفوا حتى جاءهم العلم إن ربك يقضي بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: So if you are in doubt concerning what We have sent down to you, ask those who read the Scripture before you. The truth has indeed come to you from your Lord, so be not among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and confirmation when faced with doubts, particularly regarding spiritual or religious matters. It advises the seeker of truth to consult those who have prior knowledge or experience with divine scriptures. This process is viewed as a means to affirm the truth and the guidance received from God, underscoring the connection between past revelations and the current message. Additionally, it advocates for a steadfast faith, cautioning against falling into skepticism or doubt once the truth from God is clear. This reflects the broader theme in the Qur'an of continuity and consistency in the divine message across different prophets and scriptures.
orig: فإن كنت في شك مما أنزلنا إليك فاسأل الذين يقرءون الكتاب من قبلك لقد جاءك الحق من ربك فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And do not be among those who deny the signs of Allah, lest you be among the losers
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against the denial of God's revelations and signs, emphasizing the dire consequences of such actions. It underscores the principle that rejecting divine guidance leads one down a path of spiritual and moral loss. This loss is not merely worldly but profound in its scope, impacting one's ultimate standing in the hereafter. The verse calls for reflection and adherence to faith, urging individuals to recognize and accept the signs of God as a means to spiritual success and salvation.
orig: ولا تكونن من الذين كذبوا بآيات الله فتكون من الخاسرين

translation: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine decree and the immutability of certain outcomes as determined by God. It suggests that there are individuals who, despite the evidence of the truth or the communication of divine messages, are destined not to believe. This destiny is tied to the fulfillment of God's word or His decrees. The verse highlights the limits of human influence on belief and stresses the sovereignty of God over guidance and misguidance.
orig: إن الذين حقت عليهم كلمت ربك لا يؤمنون

translation: And even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stubbornness and denial of some people who, despite being shown numerous signs and evidences of truth, continue to reject it until they face severe consequences. It illustrates the extent of disbelief and the hardness of some hearts, which do not relent or recognize the truth until they are directly confronted with the dire outcomes of their denial—symbolized here by the 'painful punishment'. This serves as a warning about the perils of persistent disbelief and the eventual reality of divine justice.
orig: ولو جاءتهم كل آية حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: So why was there not a single town that believed so its faith could have benefited them, except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in worldly life and provided for them for a while.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exceptionality of the people of Jonah amongst the communities to whom prophets were sent. Unlike other communities that faced divine retribution due to their disbelief, the people of Jonah are singled out for their collective acceptance of faith upon receiving a warning. Their timely belief averted the impending divine punishment, illustrating Allah's mercy and the transformative power of genuine faith in altering one's destiny. The verse serves as both an encouragement towards faith and a reminder of the temporal grace that can be granted in this life as a result of sincere belief and repentance.
orig: فلولا كانت قرية آمنت فنفعها إيمانها إلا قوم يونس لما آمنوا كشفنا عنهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ومتعناهم إلى حين

translation: And if your Lord had willed, everyone on Earth would have believed altogether. So, would you compel people until they become believers?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's supreme authority and the notion of free will in human belief. It suggests that although God has the power to make all humans believers, He has chosen to give them the freedom to believe or not. The rhetorical question posed to the Prophet Muhammad, or by extension to the reader, underscores the futility and inappropriateness of attempting to coerce belief, emphasizing that faith must be a personal and voluntary decision.
orig: ولو شاء ربك لآمن من في الأرض كلهم جميعا أفأنت تكره الناس حتى يكونوا مؤمنين

translation: And it is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah, and He places defilement upon those who do not reason
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah over human belief and guidance. It suggests that faith is not simply a personal choice or effort, but a grace that is bestowed by Allah upon whom He wills. The verse also highlights the consequence of neglecting reason and intellect in discerning truth, suggesting that those who forsake rational thinking are subject to spiritual and moral impurity. This underscores the importance of using one's cognitive abilities in understanding and accepting divine truths.
orig: وما كان لنفس أن تؤمن إلا بإذن الله ويجعل الرجس على الذين لا يعقلون

translation: Say, 'Observe what is in the heavens and the earth.' But neither signs nor warnings avail a people who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipresence of signs in the universe that point to the existence and supremacy of God. However, it also emphasizes the futility of such signs and warnings in guiding those who are adamant in their disbelief. The verse underscores the intrinsic nature of faith, suggesting it cannot be instilled merely through rational evidence or forewarnings, but is deeply interconnected with the will and openness of an individual's heart towards belief.
orig: قل انظروا ماذا في السماوات والأرض وما تغني الآيات والنذر عن قوم لا يؤمنون

translation: So do they await except [the likes of] days of those who passed before them? Say, 'Then wait; I am with you among those who wait.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical query and a warning, challenging individuals who hesitate to believe or reflect on the consequences that befell previous peoples due to their  disbelief or misdeeds. It emphasizes the certainty of divine reckoning and encourages the Prophet Muhammad to declare his resolve to patiently await alongside his detractors for the ultimate unfolding of God's plan. It asserts the inevitability of divine judgment and the preparedness to face the consequences, reinforcing the theme of accountability and the prophetic role in reminding and enduring.
orig: فهل ينتظرون إلا مثل أيام الذين خلوا من قبلهم قل فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: Then We save Our messengers and those who have believed. Thus, indeed, it is incumbent upon Us to save the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine commitment to protect and deliver the prophets and their followers from adversity, as a fulfillment of God’s promise. It underscores the principle that faith is intrinsically linked to divine support and salvation. The phrase 'indeed, it is incumbent upon Us' highlights that it is God’s deliberate responsibility and decision to rescue those who maintain their faith amidst trials. This acts as both a reassurance to believers and a reminder of the rewards of steadfast faith.
orig: ثم ننجي رسلنا والذين آمنوا كذلك حقا علينا ننج المؤمنين

translation: Say, 'O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those whom you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah, who causes you to die, and I have been commanded to be among the believers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinctiveness and steadfastness in the belief of monotheism. It underscores the resolve of the speaker, presumed to be the Prophet Muhammad, in rejecting polytheism and maintaining an unwavering commitment to worship the singular God, Allah, who holds sovereignty over life and death. Furthermore, it highlights a directive imbued upon the speaker to persist in faith amidst disbelief, asserting a clear distinction between the beliefs of the monotheistic and polytheistic communities. The verse calls on believers to remain resolute and steadfast in their faith, particularly when confronted with skepticism or opposition regarding their monotheistic practices.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في شك من ديني فلا أعبد الذين تعبدون من دون الله ولكن أعبد الله الذي يتوفاكم وأمرت أن أكون من المؤمنين

translation: And set your face towards the religion as a Hanif, and do not be among the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of dedicating oneself purely and sincerely to monotheism, steering clear of any form of idolatry or polytheism. It advocates for a focused and unwavering commitment to God's path, encouraging an individual to maintain a straight and true faith, devoid of any deviations influenced by associating partners with God.
orig: وأن أقم وجهك للدين حنيفا ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: And do not invoke besides Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you do, then indeed you are among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of directing worship and reliance solely towards Allah, rejecting idolatry and the invocation of any other entities or deities. It underscores that turning to anything other than Allah is not only futile, as these things neither bring benefit nor inflict harm, but also a grave mistake that aligns an individual with injustice and wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder of the inherent powerlessness of false gods and the spiritual and moral implications of idolatry.
orig: ولا تدع من دون الله ما لا ينفعك ولا يضرك فإن فعلت فإنك إذا من الظالمين

translation: And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none who can remove it but Him; and if He intends good for you, there is none who can repel His favor. He bestows it upon whom He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and control of Allah over every aspect of human experience. It illustrates that both hardship and prosperity come by the will of Allah and that He alone has the power to alter our conditions. The attributes of Allah as 'the Forgiving, the Merciful' at the end of the verse serve to reassure believers that, despite the trials they may face, Allah's overarching compassion and mercy are ever-present. This can encourage believers to maintain their faith and trust in Allah's wisdom and benevolence, regardless of current circumstances.
orig: وإن يمسسك الله بضر فلا كاشف له إلا هو وإن يردك بخير فلا راد لفضله يصيب به من يشاء من عباده وهو الغفور الرحيم

translation: Say, 'O people, the truth has indeed come to you from your Lord. So whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his own soul, and whoever goes astray, only goes astray [to the detriment] of it. And I am not a guardian over you.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual responsibility in accepting or rejecting the truth that comes from God. It underscores that guidance and misguidance are personal paths that directly affect the individual's own soul. While the truth is revealed for all, its acceptance is an individual choice, and each person bears the consequences of their choice. The role of the Prophet is conveyed as a deliverer of the message, not as one who has control over people's acceptance or rejection of the message.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الحق من ربكم فمن اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها وما أنا عليكم بوكيل

translation: And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah passes judgment, and He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to divine revelation and the virtue of patience. It encourages believers to steadfastly follow the guidance they receive through revelation, which is believed to be a direct communication from God. The verse also calls for patience in awaiting God's judgment, suggesting that divine judgments are carried out in God's timing and wisdom. Believers are reassured that God's decisions are the most just and fair, surpassing any human judgment, thereby instilling a sense of trust and serenity in facing life's challenges and uncertainties.
orig: واتبع ما يوحى إليك واصبر حتى يحكم الله وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: Alif-Lam-Ra. [This is] a Book whose verses have been perfected and then detailed from One who is Wise and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and meticulous composition of the Qur'an. It emphasizes that the verses are not only perfected but also elaborated in detail, ensuring clarity and precision in guidance. The descriptors 'Wise' and 'Acquainted' attribute comprehensive knowledge and profound wisdom to God, highlighting His capability to provide guidance that is both insightful and relevant to all aspects of human existence. This serves to reassure the reader of the reliability and relevance of the Qur'anic text as a source of spiritual and moral guidance.
orig: الر كتاب أحكمت آياته ثم فصلت من لدن حكيم خبير

translation: Worship none but Allah. Verily, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the foundational Islamic principle of Tawhid, the oneness of Allah, urging adherence to monotheism. It underscores the role of the speaker as a messenger, who not only warns the community of the consequences of neglecting this divine mandate but also brings hopeful news of the blessings and rewards associated with true faith and worship of one God. The dual aspect of the message highlights the balance between fear and hope, designed to guide the community towards spiritual purity and ethical conduct.
orig: ألا تعبدوا إلا الله إنني لكم منه نذير وبشير

translation: And [saying], 'Seek the forgiveness of your Lord and then turn to Him in repentance. He will provide you enjoyment for a goodly period and grant grace to each one who merits grace. But if you turn away, then I fear for you the punishment of a great Day.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness and repentance in one's relationship with God. It highlights the compassionate and merciful aspects of God, who rewards genuine repentance with blessings and an extension of good in this life. The reference to God granting 'grace to each one who merits grace' signifies that divine rewards are tailored to individuals based on their virtues and actions. It also carries a warning about the severe consequences of turning away from God's path, indicating that such actions lead to facing divine retribution on a significant and frightening day, symbolically referred to as 'a great Day' likely alluding to the Day of Judgment.
orig: وأن استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه يمتعكم متاعا حسنا إلى أجل مسمى ويؤت كل ذي فضل فضله وإن تولوا فإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم كبير

translation: To Allah is your return and He is capable of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence of Allah and the inevitable return of all creation to Him. It highlights the concept of accountability and the ultimate control of Allah over all affairs, suggesting that human beings, along with all other entities, are transient and will eventually return to their Creator, who possesses absolute power over every aspect of existence.
orig: إلى الله مرجعكم وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: Unquestionably, they fold their breasts to conceal themselves from Him. Behold, when they cover themselves with their clothes, He knows what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omniscience of God, emphasizing that no aspect of human thoughts or actions can be hidden from Him. The act of folding their breasts metaphorically signifies individuals attempting to hide their intentions or feelings. Covering with clothes further represents efforts to conceal one's inner states through outward appearances. Yet, these physical and metaphorical covers do not prevent God from understanding the true nature of their thoughts and emotions. The verse serves as a reminder of the futility of trying to hide from God, reinforcing His absolute knowledge and awareness that extends even to the concealed sentiments of the heart.
orig: ألا إنهم يثنون صدورهم ليستخفوا منه ألا حين يستغشون ثيابهم يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And there is no creature on Earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its resting place and its deposit; all is in a clear record.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah in the governance of all creation. It reassures believers that every creature's sustenance is under Allah's care, highlighting His providential role and meticulous knowledge of every aspect of their existence, including their habitats and destinies. The reference to 'a clear record' signifies that everything is precisely documented and nothing escapes Allah’s comprehensive wisdom and control. This serves to comfort believers, reaffirming their faith in Allah's perfect management of the universe and encouraging them to trust in His plans and provisions for all beings.
orig: وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها ويعلم مستقرها ومستودعها كل في كتاب مبين

translation: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His throne was upon the water, to test which of you is best in deed. And if you say, 'You will indeed be raised after death,' those who disbelieved will surely say, 'This is nothing but obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and strategic purpose of God's creation. Creating the universe in six days signifies God's deliberate and measured approach to creation, highlighting divine wisdom and power. The mention of God's throne over water symbolizes His authority and control over all existence, both seen and unseen. The reference to the test through deeds underlines the importance of moral accountability and the divine evaluation of human actions based on righteousness. The skepticism of the disbelievers towards resurrection as 'obvious magic' showcases the common human tendency to doubt and dismiss supernatural elements of faith when they contradict empirical understanding or when they challenge existing beliefs. This verse, therefore, speaks to the themes of divine authority, human accountability, and the conflict between belief and disbelief.
orig: وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام وكان عرشه على الماء ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا ولئن قلت إنكم مبعوثون من بعد الموت ليقولن الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And if We delay the punishment for them until a counted nation, they will surely say, 'What holds it back?' Indeed, on the day it comes to them, it will not be diverted from them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to mock.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine retribution and highlights human impatience and skepticism about the unseen consequences of their actions. The delay in punishment serves as a test of faith and character, revealing true dispositions towards belief and accountability. When the punishment eventually manifests, it serves as both a fulfillment of divine promise and a stark reminder of the folly of mocking or disregarding spiritual warnings. The verse teaches that divine justice is inescapable and mocks no one but the mocker themselves, fulfilling the natural law of cause and effect in moral and spiritual realms.
orig: ولئن أخرنا عنهم العذاب إلى أمة معدودة ليقولن ما يحبسه ألا يوم يأتيهم ليس مصروفا عنهم وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And if We let man taste mercy from Us and then withdraw it from him, indeed, he is despairing, ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fluctuating nature of human emotions and responses to the changes in their circumstances, particularly in relation to divine gifts and trials. When humans experience blessings, they often revel in them, but their true character is revealed when these blessings are taken away. The verse points out a tendency towards despair and ingratitude when faced with loss or hardship, highlighting a warning against such negative reactions. It calls for consistent faith and gratitude regardless of one’s transient worldly state, encouraging individuals to recognize and appreciate the divine wisdom in all situations—both ease and hardship.
orig: ولئن أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة ثم نزعناها منه إنه ليئوس كفور

translation: And if We let him taste mercy after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, 'My misfortunes have gone away.' Indeed, he is exultant, boastful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to quickly forget past hardships upon experiencing ease or blessings. It reflects the impulsive joy and pride that often accompany the relief from suffering, indicating a lack of depth in acknowledging the continuous nature of divine tests and blessings. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining humility and gratitude, not only in times of difficulty but also in times of ease.
orig: ولئن أذقناه نعماء بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن ذهب السيئات عني إنه لفرح فخور

translation: Except those who have patience and have done righteous deeds, those will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and righteous actions in the sight of God. It suggests that enduring hardships with patience and consistently performing good deeds are key virtues that lead to divine forgiveness and substantial spiritual rewards. The mention of 'great reward' highlights the significant value that these attributes hold in spiritual growth and redemption.
orig: إلا الذين صبروا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: Perhaps you would leave some of what is revealed to you, and your heart is constricted by it because they say, 'Why has not a treasure been sent down to him, or an angel come with him?' You are only a warner, and Allah is over all things a Trustee.
interpretation: This verse addresses the emotional and psychological burden that the Prophet Muhammad may have felt due to the skepticism and demands from his contemporaries for miraculous signs to prove his prophethood. It acknowledges his potential feelings of distress and hesitation in delivering a message that was met with skepticism and unrealistic demands. The verse reassures him of his role as a mere warner of God's message, not a wielder of supernatural powers to appease the demands of disbelief. It emphasizes that the responsibility of ensuring outcomes rests with Allah, who is the ultimate guardian and trustee, thus relieving the Prophet from carrying the weight of the people’s response or the outcomes of his message.
orig: فلعلك تارك بعض ما يوحى إليك وضائق به صدرك أن يقولوا لولا أنزل عليه كنز أو جاء معه ملك إنما أنت نذير والله على كل شيء وكيل

translation: Or do they say, 'He has forged it'? Say, 'Bring then ten chapters like it that have been forged and call upon whoever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse challenges the skeptics who accuse the Prophet Muhammad of fabricating the Qur'an. It throws down a gauntlet to produce ten chapters of similar literary excellence and spiritual depth, using their own resources, and without divine help, to validate their claim. The challenge underscores the inimitability of the Qur'an and is intended to underscore the impossibility of replicating its composition by human effort alone, thereby affirming its divine origin.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بعشر سور مثله مفتريات وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But if they do not respond to you, then know that it was revealed with the knowledge of Allah and that there is no deity except Him; so are you [then] Muslims?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and accepting the divine origin of the message of Islam, which is revealed through the knowledge and will of Allah alone. It challenges the audience to reflect on the authenticity and exclusivity of Allah as the sole deity worthy of worship. The question posed at the end, 'so are you [then] Muslims?', serves as a call for self-assessment and encourages individuals to embrace Islam fully, acknowledging Allah's sovereignty and submitting to His divine will as true believers.
orig: فإلم يستجيبوا لكم فاعلموا أنما أنزل بعلم الله وأن لا إله إلا هو فهل أنتم مسلمون

translation: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments, We fully compensate them for their deeds therein, and they are not shortchanged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea of divine justice and the impartial fulfillment of desires based on human intentions. It suggests that those who prioritize worldly gains and materialistic pursuits receive their due rewards entirely within the realm of this life, with nothing to be diminished. Allah's fairness ensures that everyone reaps the consequences of their choices, whether they seek transient worldly pleasures or eternal spiritual rewards. The verse invites reflection on the ultimate focus and values one chooses to pursue, highlighting the transient nature of worldly adornments compared to everlasting spiritual fulfillment.
orig: من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها نوف إليهم أعمالهم فيها وهم فيها لا يبخسون

translation: Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire; whatever they did there is nullified, and worthless is what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the stark consequences faced by those who deny the truth and lead sinful lives, emphasizing the nullity and futility of their worldly actions in the context of the eternal life. It highlights the concept of divine justice in the Hereafter, where the values and deeds of one's earthly existence are re-evaluated, rendering any achievements or deeds that are not aligned with divine guidance as void and without merit. It serves as a reminder of the impermanence of worldly gains and the ultimate importance of living a life in accordance with divine will to achieve salvation.
orig: أولئك الذين ليس لهم في الآخرة إلا النار وحبط ما صنعوا فيها وباطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Is one who stands on clear evidence from his Lord, with a witness from Him reciting it, and before him, the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy, the same as one who disbelieves? Those believe in it, and whoever disbelieves in it among the factions, the Fire is their appointed place. So do not be in doubt about it; it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction between those who are guided and informed by divine revelation and those who actively choose to reject it. The clear 'evidence' and the 'witness' refer to the divine scriptures and their affirmations, underscoring the continuity and reinforcement of guidance provided throughout different prophets' teachings, exemplified here by the reference to Moses’s scripture. It stresses that divine truth is consistent and available, serving as both a guide and a mercy to those who accept it. The consequence for disbelieving despite clear signs indicates a self-chosen path away from divine mercy, leading to spiritual ruin symbolized by the 'Fire'. The verse also underlines a recurring theme of human tendency towards disbelief, despite evident truth, urging reflection on the steadfastness of one's own faith.
orig: أفمن كان على بينة من ربه ويتلوه شاهد منه ومن قبله كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة أولئك يؤمنون به ومن يكفر به من الأحزاب فالنار موعده فلا تك في مرية منه إنه الحق من ربك ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, 'These are the ones who lied against their Lord.' Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of falsely attributing lies to Allah, marking it as one of the gravest injustices. It underscores the accountability in the hereafter, where the culprits will be confronted by witnesses in the presence of their Lord, thus being directly accountable for their deception. The consequence of such wrongdoing is severe, invoking the curse of Allah, which signifies divine disfavor and exclusion from His mercy. This serves as a stern warning against deceit in matters of faith and a reminder of the moral and spiritual obligations that humans hold towards truthfulness in their belief and conduct.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أولئك يعرضون على ربهم ويقول الأشهاد هؤلاء الذين كذبوا على ربهم ألا لعنة الله على الظالمين

translation: Those who hinder (others) from the path of Allah and seek to make it crooked, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse addresses the behaviors and attitudes of individuals who actively work against the spiritual and moral guidance offered by Allah. It highlights two primary actions: obstructing others from following Allah's path and attempting to distort the truth of this path. Such actions are indicative of a deeper disbelief in the concept of the Hereafter, which fundamentally undermines the accountability and moral rectitude that belief in an afterlife promotes. This verse serves as a warning against deception and the conscious choice to lead oneself and others away from divine truth, underscoring the inherent dangers of such actions for one's spiritual state.
orig: الذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: Those were not ones to escape [the punishment] on earth, nor did they have protectors besides Allah. The punishment will be doubled for them. They were unable to hear, nor did they see.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inescapable nature of divine justice for those who reject truth and fail to heed God’s guidance. It emphasizes that such individuals will find no refuge or allies besides Allah when facing consequences. The 'doubling of the punishment' implies intensified recompense for their deliberate ignorance and denial of guidance. The description of them being unable to hear or see metaphorically suggests their willful rejection to acknowledge and understand the truth, indicative of spiritual blindness and deafness that led to their suffering.
orig: أولئك لم يكونوا معجزين في الأرض وما كان لهم من دون الله من أولياء يضاعف لهم العذاب ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع وما كانوا يبصرون

translation: Those are the ones who have lost themselves, and what they used to fabricate has strayed from them.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the ultimate consequence of those who engage in deceit and falsehood. It emphasizes the profound loss of one's true purpose and identity when one persists in creating and believing in falsehoods. The 'losing of themselves' signifies a deep spiritual and moral decline, where individuals diverge from the path of truth and righteousness. The verse also highlights that the falsehoods people create eventually abandon them, leaving them devoid of any real support or truth, resulting in a complete spiritual abandonment.
orig: أولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, they will, in the Hereafter, be the greatest losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the theme of ultimate accountability and consequence in the afterlife. It suggests that those who deny truth, justice, or behave unjustly, despite temporal gains or successes, will face severe losses in the eternally significant realm of the Hereafter. It serves as a warning and a reminder of the moral and spiritual stakes at play in human choices and actions.
orig: لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون

translation: Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds and humbled themselves to their Lord - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of faith accompanied by righteous actions and humility towards God as the fundamental criteria for attaining eternal paradise. It underscores the interconnected nature of belief, moral conduct, and humility, presenting them as inseparable qualities of the truly devout who will be rewarded with everlasting life in paradise. The repetition of 'those' at both the beginning and in the middle of the verse highlights their distinguished status, directly connecting their characteristics with their eternal reward.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأخبتوا إلى ربهم أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: The example of the two parties is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Then do you not remember?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark differences in perception and understanding between those who are spiritually aware and those who are not. By comparing one group to the blind and deaf and the other to the seeing and hearing, it emphasizes that spiritual enlightenment and ignorance are vastly different states. The rhetorical question at the end serves to challenge the listener to reflect on their own spiritual state and the importance of seeking true understanding and awareness, suggesting that remembering and mindful reflection are crucial in recognizing the disparities and choosing the path of enlightenment.
orig: مثل الفريقين كالأعمى والأصم والبصير والسميع هل يستويان مثلا أفلا تذكرون

translation: And indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], 'Indeed, I am to you a clear warner'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the paramount role of prophets in delivering divine messages to their communities. The emphasis on Noah being a 'clear warner' underlines the clarity and unmistakability of the warnings provided by the prophets, tasked with guiding their people away from wrongful paths and towards righteousness and obedience to God. It reflects the mercy of God in sending messengers to forewarn and guide communities, giving them opportunities to amend their ways before facing divine reckoning.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه إني لكم نذير مبين

translation: Worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the central Islamic tenet of monotheism, urging devotion exclusively to Allah to avoid the severe consequences of polytheism or idolatry. It reflects the prophet's concern for his community, highlighting that deviating from this principle could lead them to face dire, painful consequences on the Day of Judgment, a time when divine justice will be manifest.
orig: أن لا تعبدوا إلا الله إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم أليم

translation: And the leaders who disbelieved among his people said, 'We see you as nothing but a human like us, and we see none follow you but the lowest of us, immature in judgment. And we see no superiority in you over us; rather, we think you are liars.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenges faced by prophets when their messages challenge existing power structures and norms. The leaders' dismissal of the prophet and his followers as being of lower social status and immature judgment reflects a common human tendency to resist change that threatens established hierarchies and to discredit sources of challenge by attacking their credibility and social standing. This resistance is rooted in a protective stance towards familiar belief systems and social orders, rather than an objective evaluation of the truth of the new message being presented.
orig: فقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه ما نراك إلا بشرا مثلنا وما نراك اتبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا بادي الرأي وما نرى لكم علينا من فضل بل نظنكم كاذبين

translation: He said, 'O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear proof from my Lord and He has bestowed a mercy upon me from Himself, but it has been made obscure to you, do we compel you to accept it while you dislike it?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine guidance and human free will. It suggests that even when a prophet presents clear evidence of divine truth, the reception of this message can be clouded by the spiritual blindness or predispositions of the people. The rhetorical question posed underscores the ethical dilemma of imposing belief on others, emphasizing that faith must be embraced willingly and cannot be coerced, aligning with the principle that guidance is ultimately in the hands of God, not humans.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي وآتاني رحمة من عنده فعميت عليكم أنلزمكموها وأنتم لها كارهون

translation: O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return for it; my reward is only from Allah. And I will not drive away those who have believed, for they will meet their Lord, but I see that you are a people acting in ignorance.
interpretation: The verse highlights the integrity and selflessness of a prophet who does not seek any material compensation from his people for delivering God’s message. His responsibility and rewards are solely tied to the divine, emphasizing his dedication and trust in God alone. By refusing to ostracize the believers, he underscores the inclusive and compassionate nature of his mission, rejecting societal pressures or prejudices. His admonition of his people's ignorance reflects not just a lack of knowledge, but an ethical and spiritual failing to recognize and embrace the truth he brings. This verse calls for a faithful dedication to truth and righteousness, free from materialistic motives and inclusive of all believers, while also serving as a critique of misguided societal values.
orig: ويا قوم لا أسألكم عليه مالا إن أجري إلا على الله وما أنا بطارد الذين آمنوا إنهم ملاقو ربهم ولكني أراكم قوما تجهلون

translation: O my people! Who will help me against Allah if I drive them away? Will you not then remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of opposing God's will and the consequences of rejecting divine guidance. It underscores the speaker's awareness of the dependence on Allah's mercy and the importance of aligning with divine commands. The rhetorical question serves to remind the community of their vulnerability without God's support, urging them to reflect on the wisdom of adhering to spiritual truths and moral values ordained by Allah.
orig: ويا قوم من ينصرني من الله إن طردتهم أفلا تذكرون

translation: And I do not say to you that I possess the treasures of Allah, nor do I claim to know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel, nor do I say to those whom your eyes hold in contempt that Allah will not grant them goodness. Allah knows best what is within their souls. Indeed, if I did, I would surely be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and limitations of human beings in claiming divine attributes or knowledge. It emphasizes the importance of avoiding judgments about others' worth or future blessings based on superficial perceptions. The speaker rejects claims of having special divine powers or knowledge, recognizing that such assertions would align him with injustice. The verse teaches that God alone possesses ultimate knowledge and authority over the unseen and human hearts, and it warns against the sin of arrogance and the presumption to judge others unfairly.
orig: ولا أقول لكم عندي خزائن الله ولا أعلم الغيب ولا أقول إني ملك ولا أقول للذين تزدري أعينكم لن يؤتيهم الله خيرا الله أعلم بما في أنفسهم إني إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: They said, 'O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied the dispute. So bring us what you promise us, if you are of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse depicts a moment of challenge and skepticism directed towards Prophet Noah by his people. After extensive conversation and attempts at persuasion regarding the message of monotheism and righteousness, his people express their fatigue and impatience with the ongoing debate. They confront Noah with a demand for immediate proof of his claims and divine backing. This reflects a common human tendency to resist transformative messages, especially those requiring profound changes in belief and lifestyle, essentially testing the veracity and patience of messengers. The demand for signs as a proof of truth highlights the deep-rooted skepticism and the challenging conditions prophets often face in their efforts to guide their communities.
orig: قالوا يا نوح قد جادلتنا فأكثرت جدالنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, 'Only Allah will bring it to you if He wills, and you cannot escape.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and will of Allah in the events that befall individuals and communities. It highlights human limitations and the inability to evade or alter divine decrees. The statement underscores reliance on God’s will and the acceptance that human efforts are bounded by divine intervention. It serves as a reminder of humility and the need to trust in God’s greater plan, acknowledging that ultimate control rests with Him alone.
orig: قال إنما يأتيكم به الله إن شاء وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: And my advice will not benefit you, even if I wished to advise you, if Allah intends to lead you astray. He is your Lord, and to Him you will return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme authority and will of Allah over human affairs. It indicates that divine will is the ultimate determinant of human destiny. Even the most sincere advice or guidance from a well-wisher has no effect if it conflicts with what Allah has ordained. The statement underscores the notion of submission to Allah's will and the importance of recognizing Him as the ultimate authority to whom everyone is accountable.
orig: ولا ينفعكم نصحي إن أردت أن أنصح لكم إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم هو ربكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Or do they say, 'He has fabricated it'? Say, 'If I have fabricated it, then the guilt is upon me, and I am innocent of what you commit.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusations of falsehood directed at the Prophet Muhammad by skeptics, asserting that if the Prophet were to concoct the message of the Qur'an, the sin of such an action would solely be upon him. However, he firmly disassociates himself from the sins that the accusers themselves commit. The verse underlines the personal accountability for one's actions and emphasizes the clear distinction between the Prophet's responsibility for his own deeds and his detachment from the misdeeds of others. It reinforces the principle that each individual is responsible for their own actions, and not for the actions of others.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل إن افتريته فعلي إجرامي وأنا بريء مما تجرمون

translation: And it was revealed to Noah that none of his people would believe except those who already had believed, so do not be distressed by what they had been doing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine revelation to the Prophet Noah, highlighting the predestination of belief among his people. It underscores the immutability of divine decree — that those who were to believe had already done so. Furthermore, it provides consolation to Noah, instructing him not to grieve over the continuing disbelief and sinful behaviors of his people, as their fate was already sealed. This guidance helps prophets and believers alike to place their trust in God’s wisdom and to remain steadfast, without despair, despite the disbelief that surrounds them.
orig: وأوحي إلى نوح أنه لن يؤمن من قومك إلا من قد آمن فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يفعلون

translation: And construct the ark under Our observation and Our inspiration, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine guidance and oversight in the construction of the ark by Noah. It signifies that God's instructions are to be followed precisely and with complete trust. The command to not plead for the wrongdoers indicates a firm divine decree against those who persist in their wrongdoing and reinforces the notion of inevitable divine justice. It highlights the themes of obedience to divine commands, the consequences of moral deviation, and the assurance of divine retribution and redemption.
orig: واصنع الفلك بأعيننا ووحينا ولا تخاطبني في الذين ظلموا إنهم مغرقون

translation: And he constructed the ark, and whenever the elders of his people passed by, they ridiculed him. He said, 'If you mock us, then we will mock you, just as you mock.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of perseverance and faith under ridicule and opposition. It demonstrates the resolve and steadfastness of a prophetic figure, who, despite being mocked by his people for his actions and beliefs, remains committed to his divinely ordained mission. The response of the prophet to his mockers is not just a retort but a declaration of moral and spiritual resilience. This serves as a lesson that true commitment to one's faith and responsibilities should remain unwavering, even in the face of adversity and derision.
orig: ويصنع الفلك وكلما مر عليه ملأ من قومه سخروا منه قال إن تسخروا منا فإنا نسخر منكم كما تسخرون

translation: Soon you will know who will be afflicted with a humiliating punishment and upon whom an everlasting punishment will descend.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and a reminder of the accountability in the hereafter. It emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice and highlights the fate that awaits those who persist in wrongdoing or disbelief. The reference to a 'humiliating punishment' and an 'everlasting punishment' underscores the severity of the consequences for certain actions and beliefs. It prompts believers to reflect on their own actions and to strive for righteousness to avoid such a dire fate.
orig: فسوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم

translation: Until, when Our command came and the oven overflowed, We said, 'Load on it two of every kind, and your family, except those upon whom the word has already passed, and those who believe.' And none had believed with him, except a few.
interpretation: This verse refers to divine intervention and the critical moments of making moral and survival decisions under divine guidance. The reference to the oven overflowing symbolizes a sign of impending disaster, prompting the need to preserve life through specific instructed actions. The command to take 'two of every kind' indicates an effort to ensure the continuation of life. The exclusion of certain individuals based on prior divine judgments and the limited number who believed highlight themes of divine justice and the often-lonely path of true faithfulness and obedience to God's commands. Thus, the verse underscores the importance of readiness to respond to God’s commandments, the consequences of disbelief, and the preservation of the righteous.
orig: حتى إذا جاء أمرنا وفار التنور قلنا احمل فيها من كل زوجين اثنين وأهلك إلا من سبق عليه القول ومن آمن وما آمن معه إلا قليل

translation: And he said: 'Embark therein; in the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage. Surely, my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the notion of reliance on God's will and divine guidance in all actions, particularly when embarking on a journey or undertaking a significant task. Mentioning the name of Allah during both the journey's commencement and its conclusion signifies entrusting the whole process to divine protection and beneficence. The terms used for movement and rest ('its course and its anchorage') imply that all phases of an endeavor, be they dynamic or stationary, are under God’s care. Furthermore, recognizing God as 'Forgiving' and 'Merciful' reassures the individual of divine mercy and forgiveness, alleviating the fear of potential faults committed along the way. This dual attribute of God underscores the nurturing and compassionate nature of divine oversight in human activities.
orig: وقال اركبوا فيها بسم الله مجراها ومرساها إن ربي لغفور رحيم

translation: And it sailed with them amidst waves like mountains, and Noah called to his son, who was apart, 'O my son, embark with us and do not be with the disbelievers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the emotional and spiritual turmoil faced during the time of Prophet Noah, emphasizing the stark choice between faith and disbelief. Noah's plea to his son embodies the desperation and hope of a father for redemption and guidance of his child within the overarching context of divine command and the struggles of faithfulness against overwhelming disbelief. It illustrates the broader theme of isolation experienced by believers when surrounded by a disbelieving society, and the profound personal choices that define one's spiritual destiny.
orig: وهي تجري بهم في موج كالجبال ونادى نوح ابنه وكان في معزل يا بني اركب معنا ولا تكن مع الكافرين

translation: He said, 'I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me from the water.' He was told, 'There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for those upon whom He has mercy.' And the waves came between them, so he was among the drowned.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitable nature of divine decree and the futility of relying solely on one's own efforts or reasoning in escaping God’s destiny. Even the perceived strongholds or refuges, like a mountain in this context, are powerless against God’s command. The statement underscores the importance of divine mercy as the only true source of salvation and protection against overwhelming calamities. It serves as a profound reminder of human vulnerability and the absolute sovereignty of God in all affairs.
orig: قال سآوي إلى جبل يعصمني من الماء قال لا عاصم اليوم من أمر الله إلا من رحم وحال بينهما الموج فكان من المغرقين

translation: And it was said, 'O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold.' And the water subsided, and the matter was concluded, and it [the ark] rested on [Mount] Judi. And it was said, 'Away with the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse describes the cessation of the Deluge (Great Flood) and signifies the divine command that brought an end to this catastrophe as a manifestation of God's mercy and justice. By addressing both the earth and the sky, the verse emphasizes the comprehensive control of God over all elements of creation. The resting of the ark on Mount Judi symbolizes safety, salvation, and a new beginning for the righteous, while the phrase directed at the 'wrongdoing people' underscores the consequences of transgressing divine laws. This narrative highlights themes of divine retribution paired with mercy, the renewal of life, and the stark distinction between the fates of the righteous versus the wrongdoers.
orig: وقيل يا أرض ابلعي ماءك ويا سماء أقلعي وغيض الماء وقضي الأمر واستوت على الجودي وقيل بعدا للقوم الظالمين

translation: And Noah called upon his Lord and said, 'My Lord, indeed my son is of my family; and indeed, Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound confusion and distress experienced by Prophet Noah when confronting the contradiction between God’s promise and the impending divine punishment during the flood. Despite his son's disobedience and disbelief, Noah's paternal instincts led him to plead for his son’s safety, asserting his familial ties and faith in God's justice. This verse underscores the complexity of divine justice, illustrating that divine decrees are not always aligned with human expectations or desires, and highlights the absolute wisdom and fairness of God in making decisions beyond human understanding.
orig: ونادى نوح ربه فقال رب إن ابني من أهلي وإن وعدك الحق وأنت أحكم الحاكمين

translation: He said, 'O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous, so do not ask about what you have no knowledge of. Indeed, I advise you lest you be among the ignorant.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and wisdom of God in determining the fate and rightful association of individuals based on their actions rather than merely their familial ties. It underscores the notion that true kinship in the divine perspective is aligned with righteousness and moral conduct, not just blood relations. The advice to Noah to refrain from questioning divine decisions reinforces the teaching of surrendering to God’s wisdom and acknowledges the limits of human understanding. It is a reminder that human judgment should not interfere with divine decree and that ignorance lies in challenging the wisdom of the divine.
orig: قال يا نوح إنه ليس من أهلك إنه عمل غير صالح فلا تسألن ما ليس لك به علم إني أعظك أن تكون من الجاهلين

translation: My Lord, indeed I seek refuge in You from asking You that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse expresses a deep awareness of human limitations and the humility required in supplication to God. It highlights the significance of seeking God’s forgiveness and mercy, acknowledging that without divine grace and compassion, one is at risk of spiritual loss and failure. The plea for refuge from ignorance in questioning implies the necessity of mindfulness in one's inquiries and prayers, advocating for a conscious relationship with God that is based on knowledge, reverence, and the acknowledgment of one's own limited understanding.
orig: قال رب إني أعوذ بك أن أسألك ما ليس لي به علم وإلا تغفر لي وترحمني أكن من الخاسرين

translation: It was said, 'O Noah, disembark in peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations [to come] from those with you and [other] nations whom We will grant enjoyment, then a painful punishment will touch them from Us.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine grace and retribution in the life cycle of human communities. The command to Noah to disembark signifies the end of a trial and the beginning of a period of peace and blessing, reflecting God’s mercy. However, the reference to future nations who will enjoy blessings followed by a subsequent punishment serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly pleasures and the inevitability of divine justice. The verse emphasizes that God's blessings are accompanied by responsibilities, and that failing to uphold divine commands can lead to severe consequences.
orig: قيل يا نوح اهبط بسلام منا وبركات عليك وعلى أمم ممن معك وأمم سنمتعهم ثم يمسهم منا عذاب أليم

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. You did not know it, nor did your people before this. So be patient; indeed, the outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special role of divine revelation in conveying previously unknown truths to the Prophet Muhammad and, through him, to his community. The reference to 'news of the unseen' underlines the notion that God communicates knowledge inaccessible to humans through ordinary means. The verse further instills a sense of responsibility and privilege in receiving such knowledge. It also serves as a reassurance and encouragement for patience and steadfastness, highlighting that adherence to God’s guidance, embodied in the practice of righteousness, will lead to a favorable outcome. This conveys a broader spiritual principle that divine wisdom and following the path of righteousness ultimately lead to success and salvation.
orig: تلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيها إليك ما كنت تعلمها أنت ولا قومك من قبل هذا فاصبر إن العاقبة للمتقين

translation: And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. You are merely fabricating lies.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the monotheistic message that Prophet Hud conveyed to his people, the tribe of 'Ad. Hud's proclamation to his people stresses the sole worship of Allah and denounces the worship of any other entities, which he declares as mere fabrications and falsehoods. The implication here is that deviating from the worship of the one true God leads to the construction of falsehoods that mislead communities and individuals from the truth. Hud’s role as a messenger is to rectify such beliefs and guide his people back to the rightful worship of Allah alone.
orig: وإلى عاد أخاهم هودا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره إن أنتم إلا مفترون

translation: O my people, I do not ask of you any reward for it; my reward is only from the One who created me, will you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes selfless devotion and the conveyance of truth without seeking personal gain. The speaker highlights that their efforts are purely for the sake of righteousness and guidance, anchored by their accountability solely to God, the Creator. It also serves as a call to reflection and wisdom, urging others to recognize the authenticity and sincerity behind actions not motivated by worldly compensation but driven by spiritual and moral obligations.
orig: يا قوم لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إن أجري إلا على الذي فطرني أفلا تعقلون

translation: O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord, then repent to Him; He will send abundant rain to you from the sky and add strength to your strength, and do not turn away as criminals.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the necessity of repentance and seeking forgiveness from God as a means to usher in divine blessings and enhancement in one's life. It underscores the concept that repentance can lead to both spiritual and material gain. The abundant rain symbolizes prosperity and the enhancement of strength, suggesting that turning towards God and adhering to His commands contributes to empowerment and prevents moral and societal decline, embodied by the warning against turning away like criminals.
orig: ويا قوم استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا ويزدكم قوة إلى قوتكم ولا تتولوا مجرمين

translation: They said, 'O Hud, you have not brought us any clear evidence, and we are not going to abandon our gods just because of your word, and we are not believers in you.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between the Prophet Hud and his people, who were deeply entrenched in idolatry. It reflects their skepticism and outright dismissal of the new monotheistic message Hud was tasked with delivering. Their response underscores a common human resistance to abandon traditional beliefs or practices, even when faced with new revelations or evidence suggesting a need for change. This resistance is not merely due to the lack of evidence, but also a deep-seated allegiance to their cultural and religious identity, which they are not willing to forsake based on the preaching of Hud. The verse thus serves as a reflection on the challenges of confronting and changing entrenched beliefs and how such challenges are a recurrent theme in the paths of many prophets.
orig: قالوا يا هود ما جئتنا ببينة وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا عن قولك وما نحن لك بمؤمنين

translation: They said, 'We say nothing except that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil.' He replied, 'Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and you also bear witness that I am free from what you associate with Him.'
interpretation: This verse confronts the challenge of polytheism and the persecution faced by those who advocate for monotheism. The protagonist's response highlights a strong, unyielding repudiation of idolatry and associates himself solely with the worship of Allah, emphasizing a clear dissociation from the beliefs and practices of polytheists. It also underscores the importance of maintaining a steadfast position in one's faith, even when faced with accusations or adversity from others who do not share the same belief in monotheism. This declaration of innocence and disassociation from polytheism serves as a profound assertion of one’s commitment to divine unity and a rejection of all forms of associating partners with God.
orig: إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء قال إني أشهد الله واشهدوا أني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Plan against me all together; then give me no respite.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a challenge or defiance against those plotting harm, expressing confidence and readiness to face whatever schemes are devised without fear or need for delay. It reflects a strong stance of confronting adversity head-on, emphasizing the futility of conspiracies and the resolve to counteract them immediately.
orig: من دونه فكيدوني جميعا ثم لا تنظرون

translation: Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He has grasp of its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound reliance and trust in Allah, acknowledging His supreme authority and control over all creatures. The reference to Allah holding the forelock of every creature symbolizes His omnipotence and pervasive influence in the destiny of all living beings. The affirmation that the speaker's Lord is on a 'straight path' signifies adherence to truth and justice, guiding believers towards righteousness and moral integrity.
orig: إني توكلت على الله ربي وربكم ما من دابة إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم

translation: But if you turn away, I have conveyed to you what I was sent with to you, and my Lord will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability and responsibility of the recipients of the divine message. If they choose to ignore or reject the message, they have been adequately warned, and their refusal will not harm God in the slightest. Instead, God's plan is unchangeable and His sovereignty extends over all things. He can easily replace them with others who are more receptive and appreciative of the guidance. This serves as a reminder of God's ultimate control and oversight, and that human rebellion against divine guidance does not impede God's will but rather affects one's own spiritual destiny.
orig: فإن تولوا فقد أبلغتكم ما أرسلت به إليكم ويستخلف ربي قوما غيركم ولا تضرونه شيئا إن ربي على كل شيء حفيظ

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us, and We saved them from a harsh punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine intervention and mercy of God towards His prophets and followers in times of trials.
