translation: He said, 'That is settled between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, let there be no injustice against me. And Allah is Witness over what we say.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of mutual agreements and the adherence to fairness and justice in fulfilling commitments. The speaker insists on a clear understanding to prevent any future disputes and appeals to Allah as a guardian of their words and actions, highlighting the spiritual and moral responsibility to uphold one's promises. It reflects the principle that ethical conduct and trustworthiness are foundational in interpersonal dealings, with God as the overseer of all agreements, ensuring that commitments are honoured.
orig: قال ذلك بيني وبينك أيما الأجلين قضيت فلا عدوان علي والله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: So when Moses had completed the term and was traveling with his family, he perceived a fire on the side of the Mount. He said to his family, 'Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I will bring you from there some information or a burning brand from the fire that you may warm yourselves.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine guidance and providence. Moses's sighting of the fire represents moments of divine intervention that guide individuals towards their destinies. His decision to leave his family temporarily to explore the fire indicates a commitment to seeking knowledge and guidance, even at the cost of personal comfort or certainty. The potential outcomes of 'bringing information' or 'a burning brand' suggest benefits ranging from gaining wisdom to addressing immediate physical needs. This serves as a metaphor for spiritual enlightenment and practical assistance that divine guidance can provide in navigating life's journeys.
orig: فلما قضى موسى الأجل وسار بأهله آنس من جانب الطور نارا قال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر أو جذوة من النار لعلكم تصطلون

translation: So when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot from the tree, 'O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound moment of divine communication between God and Moses, symbolizing God's omnipresence and His ability to engage directly with His chosen prophets. The 'blessed spot' and the 'right side of the valley' emphasize the sanctity and special designation of the location as a place of divine revelation. The call from the tree, an unexpected source, signifies the miraculous and transcendent nature of God's messages, affirming His sovereignty and uniqueness as the Creator and Sustainer of all existence, thereby instilling in Moses a mission rooted in divine authority.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي من شاطئ الواد الأيمن في البقعة المباركة من الشجرة أن يا موسى إني أنا الله رب العالمين

translation: And [it was said], 'Throw down your staff.' But when he saw it moving as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not return. 'O Moses, approach and fear not. Indeed, you are of the secure.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine support and protection granted to Moses, highlighting the theme of overcoming fear with faith. The miraculous transformation of the staff serves as a physical manifestation of divine power, meant to strengthen Moses's trust in God. His initial fear and subsequent reassurance underscore a spiritual journey from fear to faith, illustrating that with divine assurance, one can confront and overcome even the most daunting challenges.
orig: وأن ألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب يا موسى أقبل ولا تخف إنك من الآمنين

translation: Insert your hand into your pocket; it will come out white without any harm. And draw your wing close to you to guard against fear. Those are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs; indeed, they were a transgressing people.
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous signs given to Prophet Moses by God as evidence of the divine support and mission to confront Pharaoh and his authorities, who were known for their tyranny and disobedience to God's commands. The miracles were meant to serve as undeniable proofs, convincing Pharaoh and his council of the truth of Moses's message, seeking their submission to divine authority. The transformation of Moses’s hand and his ability to control fear symbolize the power and protection offered by faith in God, while also highlighting the importance of divine signs in aiding the righteous amidst adversities and oppressions.
orig: اسلك يدك في جيبك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء واضمم إليك جناحك من الرهب فذانك برهانان من ربك إلى فرعون وملئه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed I have killed one of them, so I fear that they will kill me.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the fear and remorse expressed by Moses after unintentionally killing an Egyptian. It highlights the vulnerability and accountability of human beings, even prophets, in their actions. Moses appeals to God, acknowledging his mistake and expressing the genuine fear for his life, which portrays the concept of divine forgiveness and the human need for divine protection and guidance.
orig: قال رب إني قتلت منهم نفسا فأخاف أن يقتلون

translation: And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent than I in speech, so send him with me as a helper to confirm me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me.
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and strategic foresight of a prophet, acknowledging his own limitations in eloquence and proposing a complementary partnership to enhance the effectiveness of his mission. It emphasizes the importance of collaborative support in facing significant challenges, particularly when confronting scepticism and opposition. The prophet's request for his more articulate brother to accompany him as a supportive verifier stresses the value of leveraging individual strengths for a unified, impactful message. This scenario teaches the value of self-awareness, humility, and the strategic use of personal resources in leadership and communication.
orig: وأخي هارون هو أفصح مني لسانا فأرسله معي ردءا يصدقني إني أخاف أن يكذبون

translation: He said, 'We will strengthen your arm through your brother, and We will give both of you authority so they will not reach you. With Our signs, you and those who follow you will be the victors.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine support and empowerment provided to the prophets in fulfilling their missions. The strengthening 'through your brother' suggests a theme of solidarity and cooperation in facing challenges. The granting of 'authority' indicates the provision of divine protection and capability to overcome opposition. The assurance that adversaries 'will not reach you' along with the signs from God emphasizes the notion of invincibility granted by steadfast faith and adherence to divine guidance. Ultimately, this verse promises victory and success to those who faithfully follow the divinely appointed leaders, reinforcing the value of unity and righteous leadership in overcoming adversities.
orig: قال سنشد عضدك بأخيك ونجعل لكما سلطانا فلا يصلون إليكما بآياتنا أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون

translation: So when Moses came to them with Our clear signs, they said, 'This is nothing but invented magic, and we have never heard of this among our forefathers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and denial often faced by prophets when they present divine signs and messages to their communities. The response of Moses' people, dismissing the signs as mere magic and citing their lack of historical precedent, illustrates a common theme in the Quran: the challenge prophets encounter from their communities who are entrenched in their ways and unwilling to accept new truths. This verse serves as a reflection on how tradition and skepticism can blind individuals to spiritual truths and divine messages, reinforcing the need for openness and humility when encountering revelations that challenge established beliefs.
orig: فلما جاءهم موسى بآياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا سحر مفترى وما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين

translation: And Moses said, 'My Lord is more knowledgeable about who brings guidance from Him, and to whom the ultimate abode will belong. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the reliance of Moses on the omniscience and justice of God. It reflects the belief that true guidance is from God and that He alone knows who truly follows His path and who will ultimately inherit the eternal dwelling, suggesting that success in this life or the hereafter is determined by adherence to divine guidance. The statement confirms that those who commit injustice or wrongdoing are ultimately destined for failure, underscoring the view that temporal power or success does not equate to divine favor or eternal success.
orig: وقال موسى ربي أعلم بمن جاء بالهدى من عنده ومن تكون له عاقبة الدار إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'O chiefs, I know not that you have a god other than me. So kindle for me (a fire), O Haman, upon the clay and make for me a tower that I may look upon the God of Moses. And indeed, I think he is among the liars.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates Pharaoh's arrogance and denial of any divine authority other than himself, showcasing his extreme disbelief and delusion of grandeur. His command to build a tower to supposedly seek out the God of Moses signifies his mocking challenge to the divine message brought by Moses, reinforcing his stature and defiance. The statement reveals Pharaoh's manipulative control over his people and his insistence on rejecting the truth, portraying his skepticism and eventual downfall due to his arrogant disbelief.
orig: وقال فرعون يا أيها الملأ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين فاجعل لي صرحا لعلي أطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه من الكاذبين

translation: And he and his soldiers were arrogant upon the earth without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dangers of arrogance and unchecked power. It addresses individuals and rulers who exercise authority and dominion over others with injustice and without rightful grounds. Their arrogance leads them to forget accountability and the eventual return to their Creator, where their actions and decisions will be judged. This verse serves as a reminder of the moral and spiritual consequences of such attitudes and behaviors and emphasizes the inevitability of divine reckoning.
orig: واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق وظنوا أنهم إلينا لا يرجعون

translation: So We seized him and his troops and threw them into the sea. So observe how was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of divine justice and the inevitable downfall of those who commit tyranny and oppression. It underscores the principle that wrongful actions lead to dire consequences, illustrating that divine retribution can manifest dramatically and decisively. By referring to the destruction of a tyrant and his forces, the verse emphasizes the power and authority of divine will over human arrogance and injustice. It also serves as a cautionary tale, urging individuals and communities to uphold justice and righteousness to avoid such a devastating fate.
orig: فأخذناه وجنوده فنبذناهم في اليم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection, they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of leading others astray. Those who guide people away from righteousness and towards sinful paths are positioned as leaders towards destruction, specifically the Hellfire. Such leaders bear not just personal accountability but also the burden of leading others to doom. Moreover, their leadership in the world translates to utter helplessness and abandonment in the Hereafter, reflecting divine justice and the importance of responsible and truthful leadership.
orig: وجعلناهم أئمة يدعون إلى النار ويوم القيامة لا ينصرون

translation: And We made them followed in this world with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of persistently deviating from divine guidance. The 'curse' mentioned is a metaphor for the social, moral, or natural repercussions that follow their misdeeds during their earthly life. It serves as a deterrent and reminder that wrongful actions have implications not only in the present world but also in the hereafter. The 'Day of Resurrection' being highlighted as a time when such individuals will be publicly reproached serves as a stern warning about the eternal state of disgrace awaiting those who indulge in corrupt and unethical practices and turn away from the path advocated by divine revelations.
orig: وأتبعناهم في هذه الدنيا لعنة ويوم القيامة هم من المقبوحين

translation: And indeed, We gave Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the former generations as insights for mankind, and as guidance and mercy, so that they might remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of divine revelation in guiding humanity and providing mercy. By mentioning the destruction of previous nations, it highlights the consequences of disregarding divine guidance. The provision of the Scripture to Moses is a means to enlighten and guide the people, encouraging them to reflect on their actions and adhere to righteous paths to avoid the fate of their predecessors. The phrase 'so that they might remember' underscores the importance of memory and reflection in learning from past mistakes and fostering spiritual and moral growth.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب من بعد ما أهلكنا القرون الأولى بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command, and you were not among the witnesses.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and asserts the prophethood of Muhammad. By stating that Muhammad was neither physically present nor a witness to the historical events of Moses, the verse highlights that the knowledge of such events in the Qur'an comes directly from divine revelation rather than from human sources or eyewitness testimony. This serves as a validation of the divine origin of the Qur'an and the authenticity of Muhammad's prophecy, as he relays information that he could not have known through natural means.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الغربي إذ قضينا إلى موسى الأمر وما كنت من الشاهدين

translation: But We raised up generations, and time prolonged for them. You were not dwelling among the people of Madyan, reciting Our signs to them, but We were the senders.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and continuous guidance of Allah across generations and people. It conveys that historical communities have risen and declined over extended periods under God's oversight. By mentioning that Prophet Muhammad was not physically present among every past community, like the people of Madyan, to share divine messages, the verse highlights that the transmission of divine guidance does not depend on any single prophet’s direct intervention. Instead, it underscores the idea that God perpetually sends His guidance through various prophets and means, affirming His omnipresence and the perpetuity of His message to humanity.
orig: ولكنا أنشأنا قرونا فتطاول عليهم العمر وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين تتلو عليهم آياتنا ولكنا كنا مرسلين

translation: And you were not at the side of the Mount when We called, but [it was] a mercy from your Lord to warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that perhaps they might remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of divine selection and the unique role of Prophets in guiding humanity. Although the Prophet Muhammad was not present at the historical event of the divine call at Mount Sinai, he is linked through the mercy of God, who chose him to deliver a message to a people previously unreached by a prophet. The phrase highlights both the continuity and the renewal of divine communication, underscoring God's mercy in ensuring all communities receive guidance and a chance for remembrance and reflection on divine laws and principles.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الطور إذ نادينا ولكن رحمة من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And if a disaster had not struck them for what their hands had sent forth, they would say, 'Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could follow Your signs and be among the believers?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the human tendency to recognize the need for divine guidance primarily in times of distress and calamity. It highlights the excuse people might make for their disbelief or misguidance, blaming the absence of a clear messenger or signs from God. The verse serves as a critique of such attitudes, pointing out that people often ignore or forget divine signs and guidance in their prosperity and only seek them in adversity. Additionally, it underscores the accountability of individuals for their actions ('what their hands had sent forth'), suggesting that human beings are often forewarned but may neglect the signs until they face consequences.
orig: ولولا أن تصيبهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم فيقولوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك ونكون من المؤمنين

translation: So when the truth came to them from Us, they said, 'Why was he not given the same as Moses was given?' Did they not disbelieve in what Moses was given before? They said, 'Two kinds of magic that support each other.' And they said, 'Indeed, we disbelieve in all of it.'
interpretation: This verse highlights human nature's resistance to accepting divine revelations when they differ from expectations or past experiences. It underscores the recurrence of skepticism and dismissiveness towards prophets across different eras, where people not only reject new guidance but also contradict their previous beliefs. The mention of 'magic' represents a misunderstanding or intentional mischaracterization of divine signs as mere trickery, reflecting a deep-rooted denial and obstinacy against faith. The final declaration of disbelief in 'all of it' signifies a comprehensive rejection of divine truth, illustrating the extent of their defiance and the closure of their hearts to guidance.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا لولا أوتي مثل ما أوتي موسى أولم يكفروا بما أوتي موسى من قبل قالوا سحران تظاهرا وقالوا إنا بكل كافرون

translation: Say, 'Then bring a scripture from Allah that is more guiding than these two that I may follow it, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the challenge posed to the skeptics who doubt the guidance provided by the divine scriptures. It asserts the supremacy of the Quranic guidance by inviting critics to produce a text superior in guidance if they claim truthfulness. The verse underscores a foundational aspect of Islamic belief regarding the irrefutable and unmatched guidance offered by the Quran, pointing towards the ultimate accountability of statements made against divine revelations.
orig: قل فأتوا بكتاب من عند الله هو أهدى منهما أتبعه إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desires without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dangers of following one's capricious desires over divine guidance. It underscores that individuals who dismiss prophetic messages and instead pursue their personal whims are severely misguided. The mention of 'without guidance from Allah' highlights that true direction and morality come from adherence to divine instructions. The categorization of such individuals among the 'wrongdoing people' whom Allah does not guide further illustrates the grave spiritual consequences of opting for self-indulgence over righteousness. This verse serves as a stern warning against the perils of moral waywardness and the importance of seeking and following divine guidance.
orig: فإن لم يستجيبوا لك فاعلم أنما يتبعون أهواءهم ومن أضل ممن اتبع هواه بغير هدى من الله إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And indeed, We have conveyed the message to them so that they may remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of communicating divine guidance clearly and effectively to people. It reflects God's mercy and commitment to ensure that every person has ample opportunity to receive and reflect upon His words. The phrase 'so that they may remember' suggests that the ultimate goal of delivering the message is to remind and stimulate an intrinsic understanding, potentially leading to spiritual awakening and adherence to moral and ethical truths. It underscores the importance of remembrance as a means to spiritually connect with God and maintain a life in accordance with His commandments.
orig: ولقد وصلنا لهم القول لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it, they are believers in it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the affirmation and continuation of faith among those who had received divine revelations prior to the Qur'an. It underscores the shared spiritual and monotheistic heritage between the followers of previous scriptures and the Qur'an, emphasizing a unity of belief among the people of the Book. The verse also underlines a profound respect for those earlier recipients who recognize and embrace the truth of subsequent revelations, showcasing the interconnectedness of divine messages throughout human history.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب من قبله هم به يؤمنون

translation: And when it is recited to them, they say, 'We believe in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were, before it, Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the affirmation and recognition of truth by those who were already predisposed towards faith. The statement underscores a continuity and consistency in their belief system, signifying that their acceptance of the revealed words is not a sudden shift but a reaffirmation of an already existing faith. It points to the deep-rootedness of faith in the believers' hearts, implying that true belief reinforces itself when confronted with divine truth.
orig: وإذا يتلى عليهم قالوا آمنا به إنه الحق من ربنا إنا كنا من قبله مسلمين

translation: Those will be given their reward twice for their patience, and they repel evil with good, and from what We have provided them, they spend.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtues of patience, good conduct, and generosity. It highlights that individuals who demonstrate patience in the face of adversity, who respond to negative actions with positive actions, and who generously contribute from their own resources to support others, are highly esteemed in the eyes of God. Their ethical behavior and resilience not only yield a direct immediate reward but also promise an additional reward, underscoring the concept of multiplied blessings for righteous deeds. This serves as an encouragement for believers to adopt a moral disposition, ensuring peace and positivity in their interactions and contributing to the well-being of their community.
orig: أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين بما صبروا ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it and say: 'To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you. We seek not the ignorant.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining dignity and disengaging from pointless or harmful discourse. It advocates for a peaceful response over conflict, signaling a preference for respectful boundaries over entanglement in unproductive arguments. By focusing on personal accountability and avoiding those who indulge in ignorance, it advises believers to uphold a standard of behavior that fosters peace and understanding rather than strife.
orig: وإذا سمعوا اللغو أعرضوا عنه وقالوا لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم سلام عليكم لا نبتغي الجاهلين

translation: Indeed, you cannot guide those you love, but Allah guides whom He wills, and He is most knowing of the rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse underscores the limitations of human influence and the supremacy of divine will in guiding individuals towards the right path. It teaches that guidance ultimately belongs to Allah and cannot be enforced by personal desires or affections. This serves as a reminder to maintain humility, acknowledging that while one can convey the message, the actual turning of hearts is in the hands of Allah. It also emphasizes Allah's omniscience, as He knows best who is truly guided and deserving of His guidance.
orig: إنك لا تهدي من أحببت ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And they say, 'If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land. Have we not established for them a sanctuary of safety to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the resistance and fears expressed by some people who worried that adhering to divine guidance and truth would result in their displacement or loss of their homeland. The response to their concern highlights God’s grace in providing a secure sanctuary that not only offers protection but also ensures the provision of sustenance. The verse criticizes the ignorance that prevails among many; despite the clear signs of safety and provision, they fail to recognize or appreciate divine protection and sustenance that accompanies true faith and guidance.
orig: وقالوا إن نتبع الهدى معك نتخطف من أرضنا أولم نمكن لهم حرما آمنا يجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء رزقا من لدنا ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed that was insolent in its way of living. So those are their homes, not inhabited after them except briefly, and We were the inheritors.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and a reminder of the consequences of arrogance and excess in one's way of life. It emphasizes the transient nature of worldly success and the ultimate dominance of divine authority. By mentioning destroyed towns whose thriving dwellings became uninhabited ruins, the verse underlines the futility of materialism without regard to ethical and spiritual values. It also highlights that everything eventually returns to God, reinforcing the concept of divine ownership and control over all creation.
orig: وكم أهلكنا من قرية بطرت معيشتها فتلك مساكنهم لم تسكن من بعدهم إلا قليلا وكنا نحن الوارثين

translation: And your Lord would not destroy the towns until He had sent to their mother-town a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not destroy the towns except while their people were oppressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's justice and mercy, highlighting that He does not punish or destroy any community without first giving them a fair chance to reform. It underscores the principle that divine punishment is a consequence of persistent oppression and wrongdoing by the people, after they have been clearly warned and given the opportunity to repent by a messenger who recites God's communications. Thus, it highlights the importance of accountability and the avoidance of injustice.
orig: وما كان ربك مهلك القرى حتى يبعث في أمها رسولا يتلو عليهم آياتنا وما كنا مهلكي القرى إلا وأهلها ظالمون

translation: And whatever you have been given is merely the enjoyment and adornment of this worldly life. But what is with Allah is better and more lasting. Do you then not reason?
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly possessions and pleasures, emphasizing that they are temporary and merely superficial. It contrasts these with the eternal and superior blessings that await believers with Allah, urging individuals to prioritize spiritual values over materialistic gains. The rhetorical question at the end challenges the reader to use their intellect and discernment to recognize the greater value of divine rewards over worldly ones, thus encouraging a focus on long-term and everlasting benefits rather than short-lived gratifications.
orig: وما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها وما عند الله خير وأبقى أفلا تعقلون

translation: Is the one to whom We have promised a good promise, and he will meet it, the same as the one whom We have allowed to enjoy the pleasures of worldly life, but then he will be among those presented [for punishment] on the Day of Resurrection?
interpretation: This verse contrasts the outcomes between those who are promised paradise due to their faith and righteous deeds with those who are engrossed in the indulgence of worldly life without regard for the hereafter. It emphasizes the transient nature of worldly enjoyment compared to the everlasting rewards in the hereafter for the believers. This disparity highlights the importance of prioritizing spiritual obligations and moral conduct over fleeting worldly gains. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability in the hereafter, where each individual's choices and actions in the worldly life will determine their final standing.
orig: أفمن وعدناه وعدا حسنا فهو لاقيه كمن متعناه متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم هو يوم القيامة من المحضرين

translation: And the Day He will call them and say, 'Where are My partners whom you used to claim?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a significant moment of accountability in the Hereafter, where God confronts those who associated partners with Him, challenging the baseless claims and beliefs they held in the worldly life. It serves as a stark reminder of the futility of ascribing divine qualities to others beside God and underscores the truth of monotheism. The verse emphasizes God’s sole sovereignty and the reckoning that awaits those who deviate from this truth.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: Those against whom the word will be fulfilled will say, 'Our Lord, these are the ones we led astray. We led them astray as we were astray ourselves; we declare our innocence before You. They did not worship us.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability and consequences of leading others astray through misguidance. It portrays a dialogue wherein the leaders or influencers who misguided others admit to their wrongdoings, recognizing their misguided actions were a result of their own deviation. They attempt to absolve themselves of responsibility by stating that their followers worshipped them under false pretenses, not as divine entities. It underscores the principle that each individual is responsible for their actions and beliefs, and that blaming others will not absolve one of the ultimate accountability before God.
orig: قال الذين حق عليهم القول ربنا هؤلاء الذين أغوينا أغويناهم كما غوينا تبرأنا إليك ما كانوا إيانا يعبدون

translation: And it was said, 'Call upon your 'partners' (false gods), so they called them but they did not respond to them. And they saw the punishment; if only they had been rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility and failure of relying on false deities or idols as protectors or intercessors instead of the One True God (Allah). When the disbelievers finally faced the consequences of their disbelief—symbolized here as punishment—they attempted to call upon their so-called partners, which proved ineffective. This scenario demonstrates that these 'partners' are unable to offer guidance, help, or salvation, especially when faced with divine retribution. This scenario serves as a warning and a lesson about the importance of seeking true guidance and adhering to the path of righteousness stipulated through genuine divine revelation.
orig: وقيل ادعوا شركاءكم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم ورأوا العذاب لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون

translation: And the Day He will call them and say: 'What answer did you give to the messengers?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the moment of accountability in the hereafter, where individuals will be directly questioned by God about their responses to the divine messages delivered through prophets. It emphasizes the importance of how humans respond to divine guidance in their earthly lives, highlighting the concept of accountability and the consequences of one's choices concerning following or ignoring the truth presented by messengers of God.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول ماذا أجبتم المرسلين

translation: So the news was blinded to them that day, so they do not ask each other.
interpretation: This verse suggests a state of bewilderment or loss of understanding among people on a significant day, likely referring to the Day of Judgment. The phrase 'the news was blinded to them' metaphorically portrays the idea that crucial information or truth is inaccessible or incomprehensible to them at that critical moment. Consequently, their inability to inquire or communicate with one another signifies a deeper spiritual or intellectual paralysis, emphasizing the severity of their situation where they are overwhelmed or rendered unable to function normally in seeking or sharing knowledge.
orig: فعميت عليهم الأنباء يومئذ فهم لا يتساءلون

translation: But as for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds, perhaps they will be among the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of repentance, faith, and good deeds in Islam. It suggests that divine forgiveness and success in the hereafter are achievable for those who turn away from their wrongdoings, truly embrace belief in God, and commit to performing virtuous actions. The conditional phrase 'perhaps they will be among the successful' indicates that while these actions set a path towards salvation, ultimate success remains in the domain of divine judgment and grace. This reinforces the humility and continual striving in the believer's life.
orig: فأما من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فعسى أن يكون من المفلحين

translation: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; they have no choice. Glorified and Exalted is He above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and authority of God in creation and in the exercise of divine choice. It highlights human limitations in influencing or dictating the divine will, reinforcing the notion that God's decisions are beyond human jurisdiction and are always aligned with a wisdom that transcends human understanding. The verse also serves as a reminder of God's transcendence and purity, dismissing any associations of partners or equals with Him, which is a form of idolatry strictly condemned in Islam.
orig: وربك يخلق ما يشاء ويختار ما كان لهم الخيرة سبحان الله وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And your Lord knows what their chests conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of God, highlighting that nothing is hidden from Him, whether thoughts or actions. It serves as a reminder of God's intimate awareness of all inward sentiments and outward expressions, suggesting accountability for both hidden intentions and visible behaviors.
orig: وربك يعلم ما تكن صدورهم وما يعلنون

translation: And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs all praise in the former and the latter (life), and His is the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah, highlighting that He alone is worthy of worship and praise throughout all phases of existence, both in this world and the hereafter. It reinforces the concept that ultimate authority and judgment belong to Allah alone, and that everyone is accountable to Him, ultimately returning to Him in the afterlife where their fate will be decided based on His just judgment.
orig: وهو الله لا إله إلا هو له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة وله الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, is there any deity other than Allah who could bring you light? Will you not then hear?'
interpretation: This verse invites people to reflect on their dependence on God's mercy and power. It uses the hypothetical scenario of a never-ending night to emphasize that no one besides Allah can alter the natural order or bring about change. The challenge to find another deity capable of bringing light serves as both a rhetorical question and a call to recognize the uniqueness and sovereignty of Allah. The appeal to 'hear' at the end of the verse underscores the importance of understanding and acknowledging these truths about divine power and the human condition.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم الليل سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بضياء أفلا تسمعون

translation: Say, have you considered: if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, who other than Allah could bring you night in which you could rest? Will you not then see?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dependence of human beings on the divine balance that Allah has established in nature, particularly in the alternation of night and day. The rhetorical question posed highlights the unique power and authority of Allah in regulating the universe, underscoring that no other deity can manipulate these natural phenomena. The mention of night as a time of rest also alludes to Allah's mercy and consideration for human needs. The query 'Will you not then see?' serves as a call to recognize and reflect on the evidence of Allah's sovereignty and beneficence manifest in the world around us.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم النهار سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بليل تسكنون فيه أفلا تبصرون

translation: And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein, and that you may seek from His bounty, and that perhaps you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy manifested in the creation of night and day, each serving a distinct purpose beneficial to human beings. The night is a time for rest and rejuvenation, allowing humans to recover from the day's activities. The day provides an opportunity to pursue livelihood and engage in activities that earn divine favor. The provision of both night and day is designed to enable humans to reflect on God's bounties, fostering a sense of gratitude towards the creator. This gratitude is integral to spiritual awareness and growth, suggesting that recognizing and appreciating divine favours can lead to a more fulfilling and consciously lived life.
orig: ومن رحمته جعل لكم الليل والنهار لتسكنوا فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And the Day He will call them and say, 'Where are My 'partners' whom you used to claim?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the Day of Judgment, where God challenges the notions of idolatry and polytheism directly. It highlights the helplessness of false deities and the regret of those who worshipped them. The rhetorical question posed by God serves to emphasize the futility of associating partners with Him and is a means to remind people of the importance of monotheism and accountability in the hereafter.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: And We will bring forth a witness from every nation and say, 'Produce your proof.' Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and what they used to fabricate will fade away from them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the events of the Day of Judgment, where every community will be required to present evidence for their beliefs and actions. The mention of a witness from each nation suggests that no one will be able to escape accountability. The revelation of the ultimate truth that belongs only to Allah underscores the futility of human falsehoods and the falsehoods that people crafted in life. This serves as a reminder of the inevitable reality where truth prevails and falsehood perishes, emphasizing the importance of adhering to the truth in one's earthly life.
orig: ونزعنا من كل أمة شهيدا فقلنا هاتوا برهانكم فعلموا أن الحق لله وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he acted tyrannically towards them. And We had given him such treasures that their very keys would burden a band of strong men. When his people said to him, 'Do not exult; indeed, Allah does not like the exultant.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the dangers of arrogance and excessive pride in worldly wealth. Qarun, despite being among Moses' community, succumbed to greed and tyranny, exploiting his immense treasures. His community's warning against exultation emphasizes humility and the divine dislike for those who revel boastfully in their possessions. The narrative serves as a moral caution against the corrupting power of wealth when it leads to haughtiness and contempt for others, reminding believers to seek a balance between worldly success and spiritual humility.
orig: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم وآتيناه من الكنوز ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة أولي القوة إذ قال له قومه لا تفرح إن الله لا يحب الفرحين

translation: And seek, through that which Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and do not forget your portion of this world; and do good as Allah has done good to you; and do not seek corruption in the earth; indeed, Allah does not like the corruptors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of balancing worldly life and the hereafter. It encourages the believers to utilize the bounties bestowed by Allah not only for earthly comforts but significantly for preparing for the eternal life after death. It also reminds believers of their responsibility to contribute positively to society and refrain from engaging in destructive behaviors. Essentially, it underscores the values of moderation, gratitude, benevolence, and ethical conduct.
orig: وابتغ فيما آتاك الله الدار الآخرة ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك ولا تبغ الفساد في الأرض إن الله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: He said, 'I was given it only because of the knowledge I possess. Did he not know that God had destroyed before him generations who were stronger than him in power and greater in accumulation? And the criminals are not asked about their sins.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the folly of arrogance and the delusion of attributing one's success solely to one's own knowledge or effort, without recognizing the grace and decree of God. It serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly power and wealth, drawing attention to past nations that were mightier and wealthier, yet were ultimately destroyed due to their transgressions. The rhetorical question about the ignorance of past destructions serves to criticize those who are heedless of history and divine warnings, highlighting that material success does not equate to righteousness or impunity. The mention of criminals not being questioned about their sins underscores the inevitability of divine justice, where the ultimate accountability lies beyond mundane inquiries and cannot be escaped by mere power or accumulation.
orig: قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندي أولم يعلم أن الله قد أهلك من قبله من القرون من هو أشد منه قوة وأكثر جمعا ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون

translation: So he came out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, 'Would that we had like what Qarun has been given! Indeed, he is one of great fortune.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the dangers of materialism and envy. It reflects how people often prioritize worldly gains and material wealth, admiring and envying those who possess them without considering the moral or spiritual consequences. The emphasis on Qarun's opulence and the people's reaction serves as a caution against the allure of wealth and the superficial judgments based on it. It teaches that true value and success are not measured by material possessions but by one's righteousness and standing with God.
orig: فخرج على قومه في زينته قال الذين يريدون الحياة الدنيا يا ليت لنا مثل ما أوتي قارون إنه لذو حظ عظيم

translation: And those endowed with knowledge said: 'Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and none shall receive it except the patient.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the value of true knowledge in understanding and appreciating the divine rewards promised by Allah. It highlights that the rewards from Allah are superior to worldly gains and are reserved for those who not only have faith but also commit to righteous actions. Critically, it points out that such rewards require patience, implying that perseverance in face of trials and steadfastness in one’s faith and good deeds are crucial for achieving spiritual success.
orig: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا ولا يلقاها إلا الصابرون

translation: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. There was no group to help him against Allah, nor was he among those who could defend themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power of Allah and the consequences of defying divine commands. It serves as a warning that reliance on earthly power and resources, whether it be through wealth, status, or social groups, is futile when opposing divine will. The swallowing of the individual and his home by the earth represents the definitive and inescapable nature of divine justice, highlighting the ultimate vulnerability of humans when they arrogantly challenge or disregard divine guidance. The phrase also underscores the isolation that accompanies defiance of divine commands; ultimately, no earthly allies or personal capabilities can prevail against the decrees of Allah.
orig: فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان من المنتصرين

translation: And those who had desired his position the day before began to say, 'Indeed, it is as if God expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. Had it not been for God’s grace upon us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us. Indeed, it appears that the disbelievers do not prosper.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the sudden shift in human perception based on their circumstances. It emphasizes the fickleness of human desire and the shortsightedness in understanding God's distribution of sustenance and mercy. Those who envied others' fortunes one day are grateful for their own safety the next, recognizing that worldly positions are transient and entirely under God's control. The mention of disbelievers not prospering serves as a reminder that true success is in recognizing and submitting to God's will, and that rejecting faith can lead to ruin, both spiritually and materially.
orig: وأصبح الذين تمنوا مكانه بالأمس يقولون ويكأن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر لولا أن من الله علينا لخسف بنا ويكأنه لا يفلح الكافرون

translation: That home of the Hereafter, We assign it to those who do not desire high rank on the Earth nor corruption, and the result [is] for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Islamic ethical principle of humility and righteousness, suggesting that the eternal abode in the Hereafter is reserved for those who shun worldly arrogance and corruption. It highlights the Islamic value of modesty and the denunciation of disruptive and unethical behaviors on earth, underscoring that success and ultimate salvation in the afterlife are the rewards for those who live a life characterized by fear of God, moral integrity, and justice.
orig: تلك الدار الآخرة نجعلها للذين لا يريدون علوا في الأرض ولا فسادا والعاقبة للمتقين

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it, and whoever comes with an evil deed, those who have committed evil deeds will not be recompensed except for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principles of divine justice and recompense in Islam. It asserts that good deeds will not only be rewarded but rewarded with something greater, highlighting the generous and merciful nature of God. Conversely, it states that the punishment for evil deeds will be no more than the equivalent of the actions committed, reflecting the just and fair character of divine judgment. The verse reassures believers that God's system of reward and punishment is meticulously balanced and encourages adhering to righteous conduct while deterring malevolence.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى الذين عملوا السيئات إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Indeed, He who imposed the Qur'an upon you will take you back to a place of return. Say, 'My Lord is most knowing of who brings guidance and who is in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of return to God, highlighting that the same Divine authority who revealed the Qur'an is also guiding the believer through life's journey and will eventually lead them back to the ultimate destiny. It underscores the all-encompassing knowledge of God in distinguishing between those who are guided and those who stray. Thus, it serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and the accountability that each individual holds in terms of their response to divine guidance and error.
orig: إن الذي فرض عليك القرآن لرادك إلى معاد قل ربي أعلم من جاء بالهدى ومن هو في ضلال مبين

translation: And you did not expect that the Book would be cast to you, but [it is] a mercy from your Lord, so do not be an assistant to the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the unexpected nature of the prophetic mission bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad and emphasizes the divine origin of the revelation as an act of mercy from Allah. The admonition to not support the disbelievers underlines the importance of maintaining fidelity to the divine message and the spiritual responsibility to uphold and propagate faith in the face of denial or opposition.
orig: وما كنت ترجو أن يلقى إليك الكتاب إلا رحمة من ربك فلا تكونن ظهيرا للكافرين

translation: And do not let them deter you from the signs of Allah after they have been revealed to you, and invite [people] to your Lord and do not be among the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes steadfastness and integrity in the face of opposition or distraction. It underscores the importance of holding onto divine guidance, particularly when one has received clear signs or revelations from Allah. The call to invite others to Allah signifies a duty towards conveying the message of monotheism and righteousness. The warning against joining polytheists highlights the critical importance of maintaining pure monotheistic beliefs and practices, avoiding any form of association or actions that might compromise one's devotion exclusively to Allah.
orig: ولا يصدنك عن آيات الله بعد إذ أنزلت إليك وادع إلى ربك ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face. His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the core Islamic principle of Tawhid, the absolute oneness of God. It warns against associating any partners with Allah, affirming that He is the sole deity deserving of worship. The passage also reflects on the transient nature of the universe, where everything is temporal and doomed to destruction except for the divine essence of Allah, symbolized by 'His Face.' This suggests the eternal, unchanging, and continuous presence of God. Additionally, the verse underlines that all judgment belongs exclusively to Allah and that ultimately, every individual's fate will be decided by Him, reinforcing the concept of accountability in the afterlife.
orig: ولا تدع مع الله إلها آخر لا إله إلا هو كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه له الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem
interpretation: These letters are one of the mysteries of the Quran. Known as the Muqatta'at, or disjointed letters, they appear at the beginning of some surahs. Scholars and interpreters have offered various views on their significance. Some consider them to be secret codes, others see them as challenges to the listeners or readers to contemplate the uniqueness and miraculous nature of the Quran's language, suggesting that although they are written in the familiar Arabic script, the Quran's depth and meaning are not easily imitable or fully comprehensible by humans.
orig: الم

translation: Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, 'We believe,' and will not be tested?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept that professing faith is not sufficient without being tested. It underscores the idea that true belief is demonstrated through resilience and perseverance during trials and challenges. The verse suggests that tests serve to validate and strengthen a believer's faith, separating those who possess genuine conviction from those who may merely pay lip service to their beliefs.
orig: أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون

translation: And indeed, We tested those before them, so that Allah will certainly know those who are truthful and will certainly know the liars.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the recurrent theme of divine testing in human life, which serves as a mechanism to distinguish the sincere believers from those who are deceitful. It underscores the notion that God uses trials to reveal the true characters and intentions of people, affirming that nothing is hidden from God. The testing acts as both a purifier and an identifier, segregating the truthful from the deceitful based on their reactions to challenges and temptations.
orig: ولقد فتنا الذين من قبلهم فليعلمن الله الذين صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين

translation: Or do those who commit evil deeds think they can outrun Us? Evil is what they judge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the misconception held by those who commit sins, thinking they can escape or outmaneuver divine justice. It points to the flawed judgment and false sense of security harbored by wrongdoers. Ultimately, it serves as a warning that no one can evade accountability before God, stressing His omnipresence and omnipotence.
orig: أم حسب الذين يعملون السيئات أن يسبقونا ساء ما يحكمون

translation: Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, indeed Allah's appointed time is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and proximity of the Day of Judgment or ultimate accountability before Allah for those who look forward to this event with hope and reverence. It reassures the believers of the inevitable reality of meeting their Creator and underscores Allah’s omniscience and omnipotence, reminding that Allah is aware of all actions and intentions, and His divine wisdom encompasses all. The verse serves both as a comfort to those who are pious and a warning to those who may neglect the weight of such a meeting.
orig: من كان يرجو لقاء الله فإن أجل الله لآت وهو السميع العليم

translation: And whoever strives, indeed he strives only for himself. Indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the personal nature of spiritual striving or jihad. It suggests that the pursuit of self-improvement and spiritual growth is ultimately for one's own benefit. Allah, being self-sufficient, does not need our efforts or worship to sustain Him. Thus, the act of striving is portrayed as a purely personal endeavor aimed at self-betterment, aligning oneself more closely with divine will, and fostering spiritual development.
orig: ومن جاهد فإنما يجاهد لنفسه إن الله لغني عن العالمين

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely blot out their bad deeds and reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of God towards those who have faith and engage in virtuous actions. It highlights the transformative power of redemption and the divine promise that good deeds will not only erase bad deeds but will also be compensated by the greatest reward. This underscores a fundamental principle in Islamic theology about the balance between justice and grace, where God's benevolence predominates as He rewards the faithful based on the best of their actions, rather than their missteps.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم ولنجزينهم أحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment. And if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of treating one's parents with kindness and respect, highlighting it as a divine commandment. However, it also establishes a clear boundary: obedience to parents does not extend to compromising one’s monotheistic belief in God. The verse underlines the individual's accountability to God and emphasizes that ultimate judgment and guidance resides with Him. It is a reminder that while parental respect is crucial, allegiance to God's command surpasses all other loyalties, urging a balance between societal duties and spiritual integrity.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حسنا وإن جاهداك لتشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely admit them among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine reward for faith and good deeds. It reassures believers that their commitment to faith and moral conduct will lead to their inclusion among those who are deemed righteous in the sight of God. It highlights the importance of both belief and action in the spiritual journey, suggesting that it is not merely faith alone, or deeds alone, that garners divine favor, but the combination of both. This can be seen as an encouragement for believers to persist in their righteous deeds and maintain their faith, assuring them of a cherished status in the hereafter.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لندخلنهم في الصالحين

translation: And among the people is he who says, 'We believe in Allah,' but if he is harmed in the cause of Allah, he considers the trial of the people as the punishment of Allah. And if help comes from your Lord, he will surely say, 'Indeed, we were with you.' Is not Allah most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds?
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who profess faith in God superficially, but their commitment wavers under hardship or persecution. Their faith is conditional, dependent on circumstances being favorable, revealing a lack of true spiritual depth. Contrarily, their readiness to realign with believers upon sensing victory or support showcases opportunism and insincerity. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes God's omniscience, particularly in understanding the true intentions and convictions hidden within people's hearts, highlighting a divine awareness that surpasses human perception and judgment.
orig: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله فإذا أوذي في الله جعل فتنة الناس كعذاب الله ولئن جاء نصر من ربك ليقولن إنا كنا معكم أوليس الله بأعلم بما في صدور العالمين

translation: And Allah will surely make evident those who believe and surely make evident the hypocrites.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine knowledge and judgment of Allah, highlighting His omniscience in distinguishing between the true believers and the hypocrites. It serves as a reminder that genuine faith and deceitful pretense cannot remain hidden from Allah, and that ultimately, everyone will be recognized for their true intentions and actions.
orig: وليعلمن الله الذين آمنوا وليعلمن المنافقين

translation: And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, 'Follow our way, and we will bear your sins.' But they will not bear any of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceitful tactics employed by those who reject faith, attempting to sway the believers by promising to bear the consequences of their sins if they abandon their faith. It warns the believers of the empty promises made by the disbelievers, emphasizing that such claims are fundamentally lies, as each individual is responsible for their own actions and sins. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of steadfastness in one’s faith and the dangers of being misled by false promises.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا اتبعوا سبيلنا ولنحمل خطاياكم وما هم بحاملين من خطاياهم من شيء إنهم لكاذبون

translation: And they will surely bear their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual accountability in the hereafter, where each person will not only bear the consequences of their own actions but also the repercussions of any additional misguided deeds they influenced others to commit. It highlights the severity of fabricating falsehoods, particularly in matters of faith, and underscores that such actions will be subject to intense scrutiny on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a stern warning about the serious consequences of leading oneself and others astray through falsehood and deception.
orig: وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم وليسألن يوم القيامة عما كانوا يفترون

translation: And indeed, We sent Noah to his people, and he stayed among them a thousand years less fifty years; then the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extent of patience and persistence demonstrated by Noah in his mission to guide his people toward righteousness under the command of God. Despite his prolonged efforts spanning 950 years, his people persisted in their wrongdoing and injustice. The reference to the flood underscores the inevitable consequence of persistent moral transgression and divine justice that befalls a community that refuses to heed the warnings of their prophet. It serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding divine guidance and the potential consequences of disregarding it.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فلبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما فأخذهم الطوفان وهم ظالمون

translation: So We saved him and the companions of the ship, and made it a sign for the worlds
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy and power in delivering Noah and his companions from the flood, emphasizing the event as a significant sign for all peoples and epochs to ponder the consequences of disobedience and the rewards of faithfulness. The reference to the ark and its inhabitants as 'a sign for the worlds' underlines the universal and enduring lessons to be learned from this episode, serving as a reminder of divine justice and the importance of adhering to God's guidance.
orig: فأنجيناه وأصحاب السفينة وجعلناها آية للعالمين

translation: And [mention] Abraham when he said to his people, 'Worship Allah and fear Him; that is better for you, if you should know.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of monotheism and piety as taught by Prophet Abraham to his people. It emphasizes worshiping only Allah and maintaining a consciousness of Allah's omnipresence and omnipotence, which leads to moral and ethical living. Abraham's call to his people serves as a reminder that true wisdom and benefit lie in recognizing and obeying the divine command, which not only ensures spiritual well-being but also promotes societal harmony and individual peace.
orig: وإبراهيم إذ قال لقومه اعبدوا الله واتقوه ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: You only worship idols besides Allah and fabricate falsehood. Indeed, those whom you worship besides Allah do not possess any provision for you. So seek sustenance from Allah, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of idol worship and the fabrication of lies in contrast to the worship of Allah, who is the sole provider of sustenance and to whom all accountability returns. It encourages turning to Allah for needs, recognizing His sovereignty, and expressing gratitude for His provisions, reinforcing the concept of monotheism and reliance on the divine.
orig: إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له إليه ترجعون

translation: And if you deny, indeed, nations before you have denied, and upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the recurring human tendency to reject divine guidance, pointing out that such denial is not unique to the current audience but has been a common pattern throughout history. It serves both as a warning and a consolation to the Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that his duty is not to ensure acceptance of his message, but merely to deliver it clearly and truthfully. The focus here is on the fulfillment of duty and reliance on God for the outcomes, reinforcing the prophetic responsibility regardless of the people's reaction.
orig: وإن تكذبوا فقد كذب أمم من قبلكم وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: Have they not seen how Allah begins creation and then repeats it? Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and absolute control of Allah over the cycle of life and creation. It invites individuals to reflect on the natural world and the renewal processes within it as signs of Allah's endless power and capability. By illustrating the ease with which Allah can initiate and replicate creation, the verse serves as a reminder of the divine authority and the transient nature of earthly existence, encouraging believers to acknowledge and submit to the divine will.
orig: أولم يروا كيف يبدئ الله الخلق ثم يعيده إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: Say, 'Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allah will bring forth the final creation. Indeed, Allah has power over all things.'
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on the origins and the continuous cycle of life as a sign of Allah's omnipotence and meticulous craftsmanship in creating the universe. It points to the importance of travel and observation as means to gain knowledge and insight. By studying how creation started, we can develop an appreciation and understanding of Allah's capabilities, reaffirming our faith in His ability to resurrect and transform life for the hereafter. Thus, it highlights both Allah's supreme power and the continuity of life as part of a divine plan.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف بدأ الخلق ثم الله ينشئ النشأة الآخرة إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: He punishes whom He wills and shows mercy to whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and sovereignty of God over His creation, highlighting His absolute authority to dispense both punishment and mercy according to His own will. It serves as a reminder of the final return of all beings to God, where they will be accountable for their actions. The phrase underscores the dual aspects of God's interaction with humanity—His justice in punishing those who do wrong and His compassion in forgiving those who seek forgiveness. It calls believers to be conscious of their deeds, keeping in mind the ultimate return to their Creator.
orig: يعذب من يشاء ويرحم من يشاء وإليه تقلبون

translation: And you are not frustrating [God] on the earth or in the heaven, nor have you any protector or helper besides Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence of Allah and the limitations of human beings. It serves as a reminder that in all spheres of existence, whether earthly or celestial, humans cannot escape the will and the encompassing knowledge of Allah. It underscores the reliance on the divine, as without Allah, humans lack any true protector or supporter to help them against adversities. The verse ultimately stresses the importance of placing trust and faith in Allah alone, acknowledging His supreme authority over all aspects of life.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض ولا في السماء وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and His meeting, those have despaired of My mercy, and for them there is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual consequences for those who reject the divine revelations and the concept of meeting Allah. It emphasizes the state of despair that such disbelief leads to, specifically regarding the hope of receiving Allah's mercy. The mention of 'painful punishment' serves as a stern warning about the severe repercussions in the hereafter for those who persist in their disbelief, illustrating the spiritual and eventual existential peril that comes from turning away from divine guidance and truth.
orig: والذين كفروا بآيات الله ولقائه أولئك يئسوا من رحمتي وأولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: And the answer of his people was nothing but that they said, 'Kill him or burn him.' But Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the theme of divine intervention and protection bestowed upon believers who face persecution for their faith. The response of his people—calling for his death or to burn him—illustrates the extreme hostility and opposition faced by those who stand firm in their beliefs. However, the key message here is Allah's power to save and the miraculous survival of the believer from an apparently inescapable death, symbolizing that faithfulness in divine promise can deliver one from even the most dire of circumstances. This occurrence serves as a profound sign to those who have faith, reinforcing that belief in God encompasses trust in His protection and justice, and that ultimately, righteousness is rewarded even in the face of severe trials.
orig: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا اقتلوه أو حرقوه فأنجاه الله من النار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And he said, 'You have taken idols besides Allah out of mutual love in this worldly life, then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will deny each other and curse each other, and your abode will be the fire, and you will have no helpers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient and ultimately destructive nature of forming attachments or alliances based on idolatry or materialism, rather than on true spiritual principles advocated by God. It points out that while such attachments may provide comfort or seem beneficial in the worldly life, they lead to discord, betrayal, and spiritual ruin in the hereafter. The reference to fire as the abode emphasizes the severe consequences of idolatry and turning away from divine guidance, underscoring the importance of loyalty to God and the values He promotes. The lack of helpers on the Day of Judgment conveys the idea that each individual is accountable for their actions and decisions, particularly those concerning faith and allegiance.
orig: وقال إنما اتخذتم من دون الله أوثانا مودة بينكم في الحياة الدنيا ثم يوم القيامة يكفر بعضكم ببعض ويلعن بعضكم بعضا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين

translation: So Lot believed him, and said, 'Indeed, I will emigrate to my Lord. Indeed, He is the Almighty, the Wise.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the profound faith and resolve of Prophet Lot in the face of adversity. It highlights his decision to leave his homeland and people in obedience to God's command, trusting in God's wisdom and strength. The verse exemplifies the theme of migration in the path of righteousness and submission to divine will, emphasizing that true strength and wisdom lie in reliance on the Almighty.
orig: فآمن له لوط وقال إني مهاجر إلى ربي إنه هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and placed in his descendants prophethood and scripture, and We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine favor granted to a revered prophet by bestowing upon him not only offspring but also continuing the lineage of prophethood through them. It highlights the continuity of divine guidance via prophethood and scriptures entrusted to his descendants. The mention of a worldly reward signifies divine recognition and blessings in the earthly life, which complements the ultimate spiritual reward in the afterlife, affirming the balance between immediate and eternal blessings. Being among the 'righteous' in the afterlife underscores the ultimate success and spiritual fulfillment granted to those who adhere to divine guidance and lead a life of righteousness.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وجعلنا في ذريته النبوة والكتاب وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, 'Indeed, you commit such lewdness as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the admonition by the Prophet Lot to his people concerning their engagement in unprecedented and abominable sexual behaviors, which were not only morally reprehensible but also uniquely grievous in their nature. The emphasis on 'no one has preceded you' underlines the severity and the unprecedented aspect of their actions, suggesting a deep deviation from the natural and moral order established by God. Lot's reproach serves as a divine warning against following desires that lead to actions which cut off from the ethical path endorsed by God and disrupt the social and moral fabric of humanity.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه إنكم لتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: Do you indeed approach men, and cut off the highway, and commit evil in your assemblies? But the response of his people was nothing but that they said, 'Bring us the punishment of Allah if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral degradation and rebellious nature of the people addressed, who not only engaged in acts that were socially and morally reprehensible, such as homosexuality and banditry, but also defiantly rejected the warnings of their prophet. Their audacity extends to not just dismissing the admonitions but also to daringly challenge the prophet to bring about divine retribution as proof of his truthfulness. This scenario encapsulates the themes of human defiance against moral law, the test of prophetic truth, and the consequences of transgression as forewarned by divine messengers.
orig: أئنكم لتأتون الرجال وتقطعون السبيل وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said: 'My Lord, help me against the corrupting people.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a plea for divine assistance in overcoming and resisting the influence and actions of those who spread corruption and disorder in society. It emphasizes the reliance on spiritual support from God when facing challenges posed by individuals or groups whose actions disrupt social and moral harmony. The supplicant recognizes the superiority of divine intervention in rectifying situations that human capabilities alone may struggle to amend. This invocation also reflects a moral alignment and commitment to righteousness, seeking divine backing to uphold justice and moral order against corruption.
orig: قال رب انصرني على القوم المفسدين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good news, they said, 'Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this town, for its people have been unjust.'
interpretation: This passage reflects on divine justice and the consequence of collective wrongdoing. The visitors, who are divine messengers, inform Abraham not only of good tidings but also deliver a grave message concerning the imminent destruction of a town due to the oppressive and unjust actions of its residents. This serves as a reminder of the moral and ethical responsibilities communities hold, and underscores the principle that persistent injustice can lead to divine retribution. It also highlights the role of prophets and messengers as bearers of both good and difficult news, emphasizing their duty to convey the divine decree without alteration.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا إنا مهلكو أهل هذه القرية إن أهلها كانوا ظالمين

translation: He said, 'Indeed, Lot is in there.' They said, 'We know better who is in there. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she was of those who remained behind.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine intervention and providence in saving the righteous individuals from imminent destruction while delivering punishment upon those who have chosen to remain in disbelief. In this context, Lot's family, except his wife, who chose to stay morally and spiritually aligned with the corrupt society, were designated for salvation. The angels’ assertion of their knowledge reflects God’s omniscience and the meticulous execution of His will, emphasizing that divine judgment distinguishes between the righteous and the wrongdoers even within a single household.
orig: قال إن فيها لوطا قالوا نحن أعلم بمن فيها لننجينه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed by their arrival and felt constrained by their presence. They said, 'Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except for your wife; she will be of those who remain behind.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine protection extended to the righteous and their families, except those who choose to disregard the warning and remain in sin. It illustrates the tension between divine mercy and justice. While divine agents deliver salvation and reassurance to the faithful, there is also a clear demarcation of consequences for those who reject the truth. The verse conveys that divine deliverance often comes with trials, testing the believer's faith and commitment, and that ultimate outcomes are determined by individual choices aligned with or against divine guidance.
orig: ولما أن جاءت رسلنا لوطا سيء بهم وضاق بهم ذرعا وقالوا لا تخف ولا تحزن إنا منجوك وأهلك إلا امرأتك كانت من الغابرين

translation: Indeed, We are sending down upon the people of this town a punishment from the sky because of their defiant disobedience.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and exemplifies divine retribution for immoral and defiant behavior. It underscores the concept of accountability in the spiritual and moral law that governs human actions. The specific mention of a punishment from the sky implies a sudden and unavoidable consequence for collective transgression, reinforcing the idea that divine justice can manifest in powerful and decisive ways to restore order and ethical conduct.
orig: إنا منزلون على أهل هذه القرية رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And indeed, We left therein a clear sign for people who understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and understanding in recognizing the signs left by God in the world. It suggests that the divine signs are evident, but only those who apply their intellect and seek deeper insight will be able to appreciate and learn from them. The verse points to a universal message that transcends time and space, serving as a reminder of God's presence and the need for thoughtful contemplation to grasp the spiritual and moral lessons embedded in the universe.
orig: ولقد تركنا منها آية بينة لقوم يعقلون

translation: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah and hope for the Last Day, and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.'
